# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > Old > Chanukah Menorahs > Public Menorah] Giant Menorah - Comprehensive Resource Guide

## Table of Contents

1. Permission Letter Templates
2. Proposal Examples
3. Letters from the Rebbe on Public Lighting
4. Lighting Methods
5. Power Source Options
6. Spotlight Recommendations
7. DIY Construction Resources

---

## 1. Permission Letter for Mall/City

### Template Letter for Mall Management

**[Title] [First name] [Last name]**
[Position]
[Name of mall or company]
[Street address]
[City, State, ZIP]
[Date]

Dear [Title] [Last name]:

For many years now, the Chabad-Lubavitch movement has been displaying the joys of Chanukah in malls, shopping centers and other such public places throughout the country. Chabad has attracted thousands of people to these holiday celebrations. These events have received immense press coverage, have featured appearances from government officials and Hollywood stars and have also brought many newcomers to participating malls.

**Over 150 such lightings have taken place coast to coast.**

---

### Historical and Cultural Significance

The Jewish holiday of Chanukah commemorates the rededication of the Temple in Jerusalem following the Jews' victory over the ancient Syrian Empire, who had sought to coerce them into replacing their faith with Hellenism.

Today, Chanukah is celebrated by lighting the Menorah candles for eight days, to remind us of the ancient victory and as a symbolic reconfirmation of faith and hope.

However, the large-scale public Menorah lightings, begun in America but now conducted throughout the world, have come to proclaim the **universal message of religious freedom**, particularly the basic beliefs of America's first settlers, themselves victims of religious persecution.

---

### Our Proposal

This year we are pleased to inform you that we have chosen the [name of mall here] as a potential site for a Chanukah celebration.

**We propose to:**
- Set up an electric Menorah
- Ceremonial lighting of one light each night
- Produce a celebration with live entertainment
- Provide our own refreshments

**Anticipated Benefits:**
- Participation of local personalities
- Widespread media coverage
- Obvious benefit for the mall
- Unique holiday experience for patrons

---

### Event Details

**Proposed Date:** [date here]
- Scheduled to avoid conflict with rest of holiday season

**Advance Publicity:**
- Will be submitted to mall for approval

**Supporting Materials:**
- Enclosed: Copies of publicity and pictures from lightings elsewhere around country
- Examples show how successful these mall events have been

---

### Call to Action

I'm sure the [name of mall here] will want to take advantage of this opportunity to provide patrons and local residents with an experience unique, yet quite appropriate, to this holiday season.

I look forward to meeting with you to go over any details and finalize arrangements, so that together we may extend the warm holiday feelings to all.

Sincerely,

Rabbi [First name] [Last name]

---

## 2. Proposal for Bank/Public Space

### Example: City of Stonnington Proposal

**From Forum:** http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/forum/viewtopic.php?t=19604

**Context:** Writing a proposal to erect menorahs in different branches of a bank

**Should Include:**
- How it would benefit the bank and attract more customers
- How the menorah is a universal sign of peace and light, not just a religious symbol

---

### Sample Proposal

**To Whom It May Concern,**

I am writing to seek the involvement of The City of Stonnington in the Jewish festival of Chanukah, which commences this year on the evening of Friday, 19th December and ends at sunset on Saturday, 26th December.

**Universal Message:**
Chanukah is an extremely joyous holiday, commemorating the universal message of the victory of good over evil. It is celebrated in particular by lighting the Menorah, an eight-branched candelabra, in a public place in order to publicise this victory.

**Symbolism:**
An extra candle is lit every night, one the first night, two the second night, and so on. Light symbolises good, the dispelling of darkness. By the final night, all eight candles are blazing, signifying the total eradication of evil.

---

### Reasons for Partnership

**1. Cultural Diversity:**
I believe it will be a tangible illustration of Stonnington's well-known commitment to cultural diversity.

**2. Festive Season:**
It will be a beautiful expression of the festive season.

**3. Statement Against Terror:**
Last, and by no means least, its message of comfort in the battle against evil will be a profound statement of Australia's principled stance against terror.

---

### Specific Requests

**Permission Sought:**
To light a Menorah in a prominent position outside the municipal buildings at the corner of Glenferrie and High Streets, Malvern on the eight evenings commencing on 19th December.

**Specifications:**
- Menorah will be lit electrically
- Size: Approximately ten feet tall

**Additional Requests:**
- City institutionalise the commemoration of Chanukah
- Provide storage of the Menorah
- One-off grant of $1,000.00 to help defray costs

**Contact:**
Please call me on [REDACTED-PHONE] if you have any questions.

I look forward to your favourable response.

Yours truly
Rabbi [REDACTED-NAME]

---

## 3. Legalities and Letters from the Rebbe

### Legal Resources

**Google Drive Folder:**
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aLSk2xYJBhAO7xhXyN4C3nFMdX_PfpdD?usp=share_link

**Contents:**
- Legal precedents
- Supreme Court decisions
- Sample legal documents
- Constitutional arguments

---

### Letters from the Rebbe on Public Lighting

**Resource Links:**
- http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/article.html?h=483&o=114314
- http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/forum/viewtopic.php?t=58658

---

### Key Lessons from Rebbe's Letters

**SITUATION ONE: Teaneck Menorah**

**The Rebbe's Strong Defense:**
The Rebbe publicly put himself on the line defending this public Menorah.

**But Also Wrote:**
"Bitchila kosavti lo shelo lehadlik eish hamachlokes" - "At the very outset, I wrote to him (the local Shliach involved with this Menorah dispute) not to ignite the fire of Machlokes."

**When Senator Advised Backing Off:**
Beside the Senator's words (to back off for this year), the Rebbe wrote:
"V'harei boze hatzedek itoy" - "For in this (the Senator's alarm at Lubavitch's actions), he is correct."

**Result:**
- Lubavitch backed off that year
- Next year, Senator helped arrange Menorah in Trenton and spoke at event
- Ultimately helped with Teaneck situation as well

---

**SITUATION TWO: Mayor Koch in New York**

**Situation:**
Rabbi Butman approached Mayor Koch for permission to erect Menorah in certain location. Mayor said no.

**Rabbi Butman's Response:**
Wrote to Rebbe that "we will stand strong for the Menorah at that location."

**Rebbe's Response:**
Don't start a Machlokes with him.

**Result:**
Mayor Koch gave different public space for the Menorah, where it stands until today.

---

### Clear Principle

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME], S. José, Costa Rica

> "Clearly, while the Rebbe defends the right to put up a public Menorah, **he doesn't want us to pick fights about them.**"

---

## 4. What to Use to Light a Public Menorah

### Outdoor Option: Tiki Torch

**Best for:** Outdoor public menorahs

**Features:**
- Pretty powerful
- Works well in wind
- Large wick

**Fuel Options:**
1. Tiki brand torch fuel (Home Depot/Lowe's)
2. Paraffin

**Important Notes:**
- Tiki torch only has 1 wick (big but 1)
- Good for menorah
- Not good for havdala

**How to Find:**
Go into local Home Depot with the insert and find best fit for the torch

---

### Lighting the Menorah

**Best Method:**
Blow torch or butane torch taped to a stick or pole

**Why NOT Tiki Torch for Lighting:**
- Very difficult to use tiki torch to light other candles
- Tiki cover gets in the way
- Tilting makes fuel spill
- Takes people like 60 seconds to light one candle
- Oil spills all over

---

### Indoor Option: Candle Conversion Kit

**Product:** Paraffin with Glass Chimney

**Best for:** Indoor public menorahs

---

### Alternative: Gas Lantern

**IMPORTANT:** Make sure it is ONE Mantel (wick) not two

**Product Example:**
Coleman One-Mantle Compact Propane Lantern
[Amazon Link](http://www.amazon.com/Coleman-One-Mantle-Compact-Propane-Lantern/dp/B0009PUR54/)

**Runtime:** One propane can lasts about 4 hours on high

---

### If You Don't Have Conversion Kit

**Question:** "Don't have the tiki conversion set for a Klar Menorah, what's the best and easiest way to do lighting?"

**Solution:** Tape and big candles

---

## 5. Public Menorah Power Source Ideas

### Option 1: LED Rechargeable or Solar

**Products:**
- LED chargeable bulbs
- TomCare solar lights

**Availability:**
Shlichus market will be selling

**Advantages:**
- No power source needed
- Environmentally friendly
- No ongoing electricity costs

---

### Option 2: Car Battery

**How It Works:**
Car batteries sound the most shayech (appropriate)

**Requirements:**
- Low watt LED light bulbs (Walmart has 4W ones)
- Inverter (car batteries operate at 12V, most menorahs are 120V)
- Electrician to install (merge cables, ensure outdoor safe)

**Maintenance:**
You might need to switch out battery a few times over Chanukah

---

#### Advanced 12V System

**From:** Rabbi [REDACTED-NAME], Chabad of Sunnyvale

**Their Solution:**
Someone rigged menorah and changed it from 115V to 12V system that ran off a marine battery.

**Components Created:**
- LED spotlights fit into regular light fixtures with adaptors
- Lenses for all eight bulbs (weatherproofed with 3D printer)
- Regular 115 wiring plug wired directly into battery
- Batteries in outdoor plastic protectors, chained down (doubled as weights)

**Maintenance:**
Trickle charge batteries two times over Chanukah (had two batteries they swapped)

**Additional Feature:**
Second plug wire to battery for 12V garden spotlight to light up the menorah

**Photos:**
- https://www.chabadsunnyvale.com/templates/photogallery_cdo/aid/3544769/jewish/Chanukah-2016.htm#photoid=9940324
- https://www.chabadsunnyvale.com/templates/photogallery_cdo/aid/3544769/jewish/Chanukah-2016.htm#photoid=9940322

**Note:** Major investment of time, modest investment of money by handy community member

**Contact for Details:**
Rabbi [REDACTED-NAME]
[REDACTED-PHONE]

---

### Option 3: Generator

**Pros:**
- Heavy but worth its weight in gold in some places
- Reliable power source

**Important Considerations:**

**Power Calculation:**
- All 9 bulbs (at 75 watts each) = 675 watts
- Add any spotlights
- Ensure generator provides good amount more than needed
- Advertised number is highest it gets to, not idle level

**Noise:**
- Generators make a lot of noise
- Put it far away during events
- Use extension cord (at least for events)
- Alternative: Electric generators that are almost inaudible

**Security:**
- Chain it to something that won't move

**Fuel:**
- Buy gas cans big enough to fill it
- You'll probably/certainly need to refill each night

**Green Option:**
- Solar generator
- Expensive initial investment
- Can promote as "green Menorah"
- Good pitch for green-minded balebatim

---

### Option 4: Street Lamps

**Hidden Resource:**
In several places there have been outlets in street lamps, either exposed or under a screwed panel.

**How to Use:**
- Look around to see if it's there
- If you see it and use it, usually no one will ask questions
- If under panel and someone working there: Ask with breitkeit (openness): "Are you the one who knows how to open this? We need to use it for our menorah display"

**CRITICAL WARNING:**
K'muvan (obviously), every such breitkeit has a risk. If a friend politician arranged the permit for you, **don't risk stabbing him in the back** by doing it.

---

### Municipal Challenge: Power Yes, Menorah No

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME]

**Issue:**
Some municipalities throwing wrenches: "menorah yes, power no"

**Their Solution (See Option 2 above):**
12V system with marine battery - detailed above

**Note:** Too late for this year when posted, but sharing for future

---

## 6. Spotlight - CRITICALLY IMPORTANT

### Annual Reminder

**Forum Post:** http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/forum/viewtopic.php?t=543473

**Subject:** Very important for anyone with a menorah for the public (annual message)

---

### The Visibility Problem

**Test Right Now:**
If you are reading this message at night, please look out your window. Try to make out the design of anything outdoors that doesn't have any spotlight on it.

**You can't. Plain and simple.**

Now look at something that has a light shining on it. It is super visible, and it stands out from everything around it.

**PLEASE GET A SPOTLIGHT TO SHINE ON YOUR MENORAH!!**

---

### The Pirsumei Nisa Difference

**From [REDACTED-NAME]:**
> "Just try to remember how long it takes on Chanukah, while driving down the street, to 'find' the menorah. Now, compare that to anything that you see outside that is lit up. **The difference in pirsumei nisa is incomparable.**"

---

### Recommended Setup

**Lights (2 pack) - $32:**
Powerful, water/weather proof LED light kit
35W (200W equivalent) two piece

[Amazon Link](https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07M5WRRWW/)

**Coverage:**
- Each light might be enough for one mid-size menorah
- Two lights set up on big (12 or 18 foot) outdoor menorah
- Lit up menorah very brightly
- Also lit entire front of Chabad House

---

**Waterproof Timer with Photo Cell - $12:**
Automatically turns on at night

[Amazon Link](https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07GZH9R43/)

---

**50ft, 3 Head Extension Cord - $24:**
[Amazon Link](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07M7PXDHV/)

---

**Electrical Tape - $3:**
[Amazon Link](https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B001B19JLS/)

---

### The Impact

**Before Spotlight:**
Takes 30+ seconds while driving to locate menorah (if you find it at all)

**With Spotlight:**
Instantly visible from blocks away, impossible to miss

**Result:**
Exponentially greater pirsumei nisa for minimal cost ($71 total for complete setup)

---

## 7. DIY Construction Resources

### PVC Menorah Design

**Resource:**
http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/article.html?h=1832&o=2894591

**Materials:**
- PVC pipe
- Connectors
- End caps
- Lights
- Wiring

**Advantages:**
- Lightweight
- Inexpensive
- Easy to work with
- Customizable

---

### Wood Menorah Diagram and Resources

**Resource:**
http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/article.html?h=785&o=2834849

**What's Included:**
- Technical diagrams
- Measurements
- Materials list
- Construction instructions

**Options:**
- Car menorah
- 6-foot public menorah
- Giant menorahs for events

---

## Complete Setup Checklist

### For Public Menorah Success

**Before You Start:**
- [ ] Permission from property owner/city
- [ ] Legal review if needed
- [ ] Insurance coverage verified
- [ ] Budget approved

**Equipment:**
- [ ] Menorah (purchased or DIY)
- [ ] Power source selected and tested
- [ ] Lighting method (tiki torch/conversion kit/gas lantern)
- [ ] Lighter (blow torch on pole)
- [ ] Spotlight setup (CRITICAL!)
- [ ] Timer for automatic operation
- [ ] Extension cords as needed
- [ ] Security (chains, locks)

**Logistics:**
- [ ] Storage location secured
- [ ] Installation crew arranged
- [ ] Daily maintenance plan
- [ ] Fuel/power replenishment schedule
- [ ] Weather protection plan

**Publicity:**
- [ ] Permission letter sent
- [ ] Press releases drafted
- [ ] Media invited
- [ ] Photos from previous years
- [ ] Social media plan

**Safety:**
- [ ] Fire extinguisher on site
- [ ] Safe distance from traffic
- [ ] Proper electrical setup
- [ ] Emergency contacts posted

---

## Budget Planning

### Sample Costs

**Menorah:**
- Purchased: $800-$2,000
- DIY PVC: $200-$400
- DIY Wood: $400-$800

**Power:**
- Solar/LED: $300-$600
- Car battery + inverter: $150-$250
- Generator: $400-$1,000
- Street lamp: $0 (if available)

**Lighting:**
- Tiki torch fuel (8 nights): $30-$50
- Conversion kit: $100-$200
- Gas lantern + propane: $80-$120

**Spotlight (ESSENTIAL):**
- Complete setup: $71
- Don't skip this!

**Miscellaneous:**
- Chains/locks: $50
- Storage box: $100
- Extension cords: $50

**Total Range:** $1,200-$5,000 depending on choices

---

## Final Thoughts

A successful public menorah combines:

1. **Proper permissions** - Legal and relationship-based
2. **Reliable power** - Appropriate to your situation
3. **Quality lighting method** - Safe and halachically sound
4. **SPOTLIGHT** - Non-negotiable for pirsumei nisa
5. **Security** - Chains, monitoring
6. **Maintenance plan** - Daily checks, fuel/power
7. **Weather readiness** - Backup plans
8. **Professional appearance** - Clean, straight, impressive

The investment in a quality public menorah setup pays dividends in:
- Pirsumei nisa (primary goal)
- Community visibility
- Media coverage
- Jewish pride
- Annual tradition

Most importantly: Remember the Rebbe's guidance to defend the right to public menorahs while avoiding unnecessary machlokes. Work strategically, build relationships, and create beautiful, prominent displays that bring light to the world.

**Hatzlacha Rabba!**

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > Old > Chanukah Menorahs > Public Menorah] City Wants to Copy Public Lighting Event

## Forum Discussion

**Source:** http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/forum/viewtopic.php?t=467823

**Topic:** Time sensitive - need advice for meeting with city who wants to copy public lighting event, replacing ours

---

## Situation

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME]

We are planning the first public menorah lighting in our city. We confirmed the place we will be doing it and got the Mayor's confirmation that he will be joining.

**The Problem:**
Then someone from the Mayor's office contacted me and told me that:
- The Mayor is only available on a different day
- The city likes the idea (of a public menorah lighting) so much that they are planning to do it (with our menorah in the place that we arranged) every day that we are not doing it
- They will have the mayor attend on a different day than our event
- They plan to do their own publicity for a community event on that day

**Meeting:** Tomorrow IYH to talk about this

**Question:** Has anyone else dealt with this (or something similar) or have any advice?

---

## Response 1: One Big Community Event

**Key Arguments to Present:**

### Strength in Numbers
"You might want to point out that you will bring your community and it is more effective to combine efforts for one big night"

### Professional Event Management
"Plus... we in Chabad are good marketers and can bring people that wouldn't come otherwise plus you'll make it more fun with party kids entertainment etc which they won't do"

### People Care About the Party
"People care more about a good community Chanukah party than the lighting itself (the lighting gets old after a year or 2 I've noticed)"

### Community Building
"You can tell them the reason you want this to be one coordination is because in a small town it is important that people get to know other people in the Jewish community so the more the merrier"

### Avoid Duplication
"It would be silly to have 2 parties for a smallish Jewish community"

### Mayor Substitute
"If the mayor can't be there on that day have him send other city representative on his behalf - it works just fine"

### Quality Over Bureaucracy
"Bottom line: with you involved it will be on a much grander scale and they will look strange doing their own thing (besides that your party will be better etc)"

### Bring Support
"Maybe bring another community member with you to share their perspective like yours"

---

## Response 2: Clarify and Accommodate

**Questions to Ask:**

**Lighting Every Night:**
> "But you are lighting it every night, aren't you?"

**Accommodation Option:**
> "Maybe change the date of your 'big event' to accommodate mayor."

**Community Event vs. Chabad Event:**
> "Also explain to them that its not 'your' event but its The Community event."

**Facilitate City's Participation:**
> "You are thrilled that they want there to be a lighting event each night and you will be happy to facilitate."

---

## Strategy Framework

### Option 1: Partner with City

**Approach:**
- Frame as "community event" not "Chabad event"
- Offer to facilitate/organize city's desired daily lightings
- Coordinate one major event on a date mayor can attend
- Leverage city's resources and publicity

**Benefits:**
- Official city backing
- Mayor's participation
- City publicity machine
- Broader community reach

**Risks:**
- Loss of control
- Diluted messaging
- Potential for religious neutralization

---

### Option 2: Maintain Independence

**Approach:**
- Keep your event on your date
- Explain superior programming and community draw
- Position as established community tradition
- Offer to assist city separately if they insist

**Benefits:**
- Control over content and messaging
- Authentic Chabad event
- Clear Jewish identity
- Professional execution

**Risks:**
- Competing events split crowd
- City does own thing anyway
- Mayor attends theirs, not yours

---

### Option 3: Flexible Accommodation

**Approach:**
- Willing to change date to accommodate mayor
- But maintain control of programming
- Partner with city for publicity
- Make it "official" city event organized by Chabad

**Benefits:**
- Mayor attendance
- City support
- Maintained control
- Best of both worlds

---

## Key Negotiation Points

### What to Emphasize

**1. Your Expertise:**
- "We know how to make this successful"
- "We have the connections and resources"
- "We understand how to engage the Jewish community"

**2. Community Unity:**
- "Small town needs one unified event"
- "Splitting the community is counterproductive"
- "More Jews together is better"

**3. Quality Programming:**
- "Entertainment, food, activities for kids"
- "Professional organization"
- "Proven track record"

**4. Flexibility:**
- "Happy to accommodate mayor's schedule"
- "Open to partnership with city"
- "Want to make this work for everyone"

**5. Win-Win Scenario:**
- "City gets credit"
- "Mayor gets positive publicity"
- "Community gets great event"
- "Jewish community gets meaningful celebration"

---

## What to Avoid

**Don't Say:**
- "This is our event" (sounds territorial)
- "You can't do this" (sounds confrontational)
- "We did all the work" (sounds whiny)
- "It's a religious event" (triggers church/state concerns)

**Do Say:**
- "Community event"
- "Partnership"
- "Accommodate"
- "Coordinate"
- "Cultural celebration"

---

## Preparation for Meeting

### Bring With You

**1. Community Support:**
- Another community member
- Letters from community leaders
- List of expected attendees

**2. Professional Materials:**
- Past event photos/videos
- Publicity materials
- Program outline
- Budget (if appropriate)

**3. Flexibility:**
- Alternative dates
- Partnership proposals
- Accommodation options

---

### Meeting Goals

**Primary:** Maintain control of event programming while getting city/mayor support

**Acceptable:** Partnership where Chabad organizes, city promotes

**Fallback:** Separate events on different days (less ideal)

**Worst Case:** City does their own thing (avoid this)

---

## Long-Term Considerations

### Building Relationship

**This Year:**
- Focus on successful partnership
- Exceed expectations
- Create positive experience

**Future Years:**
- Established tradition
- City comes to you
- Smoother coordination
- Automatic mayor participation

### Political Capital

**Use Wisely:**
- This situation creates obligation
- City will "owe you one"
- Builds relationship with mayor's office
- Opens doors for other initiatives

---

## Final Thoughts

**The Situation:**
City wants to hijack your event → Turn into opportunity for partnership

**The Strategy:**
Emphasize community unity, professional execution, and flexibility

**The Goal:**
One great event with city backing and mayor attendance, under your control

**The Key:**
Frame it as "us helping them" not "them taking over"

**Remember:**
You bring expertise, community connections, and programming. They bring official backing and the mayor. Both sides need each other for maximum success.

Good luck with the meeting!


---
**End of Document 36**
---

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > Old > Chanukah Menorahs > Public Menorah] Ideas to Jazz Up Small Town Menorah Lighting

## Forum Discussion

**Source:** http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/forum/viewtopic.php?t=465938

---

## The Problem

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME], Pittsford, NY

We have been doing a public menorah in our small and cold town. Have done a juggler, magician at a free party we host right after.

**But:** It's getting boring though and people are taking for granted (smaller numbers etc)

**Question:** Any ideas to make it exciting for adults and kids who stopped coming to want to come again?

---

## Ideas Suggested

### 1. Light Show

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME], Fountain Hills, AZ

Simple suggestion: **Light show**

---

### 2. Fire Dancers

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME], Munster, IN

**Suggestion:** Fire dancers

**WARNING from [REDACTED-NAME], S. Barbara, CA:**
> "BH - Fire Dancers warning. We had a mix up and the female dancer that showed up was not dressed for the right event."

**Response from [REDACTED-NAME], Munster, IN:**
> "Outside of California and Florida that shouldn't be a problem for a Chanukah (winter) event."

---

### 3. Comprehensive Approach

**From:** Rabbi [REDACTED-NAME], Norfolk, VA

**Their Experience:**
> "Experiencing the same problem and a very dwindled crowd (and never using these mentioned entertainers yet) we added the following. Over the years (each year adding something else, and BH the last few years has been successful)"

---

#### Elements That Worked:

**Day of the Week:**
- **Sunday to be best**

**Dreidel Mascot:**
- Had ours made locally
- Shluchim Services now has a blow-up one

**Special Gift:**
- One year: Light up menorah necklace
- One year: Light up dreidel glasses
- Both from Shluchim Services

**Doughnut Decorating Station:**
- Doughnuts bought from bakery
- Station had:
  - Icing (large bucket bought at Sam's Club)
  - Sprinkles
  - Chocolate chips
  - Other toppings

**Real Chanukah Gelt:**
- Got crisp one dollar bills from bank
- **Tip:** Make sure to ask bank in advance

---

### 4. Give Kibudim (Honors)

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME], Rome, Italy

> "Just one eitza on top of all these, give kibudim, they will bring their family and friends, children could sing a song so all their families will come..."

**Strategy:**
- Honor community members
- Ask children to sing
- Families come to watch their kids
- Creates personal investment

---

### 5. Fireworks Show

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME], Lake Mary, FL

**Suggestion:** Fireworks show

**Note:** Could be expensive

---

### 6. Comprehensive Strategy from Santa Fe

**From:** Rabbi [REDACTED-NAME], Santa Fe, NM

**Reality Check:**
> "Big challenge. Here are some things we tried"

---

#### Practical Tips:

**1. Change the Event Name:**
- From "menorah lighting"
- To **"Chanukah Celebration"**

**Why:** Broadens appeal, focuses on festive atmosphere

---

**2. Ice Menorah:**
- **Big hit when possible**

---

**3. Realistic Expectations:**
> "Keep in mind that years vary and have ups and downs. Weather and vacation times make a difference."

**Don't panic** if one year is down - it's often external factors

---

**4. Search for Entertainers:**
> "Search and search for entertainers. We just found a fire eater and performers whom we didn't know about by asking and asking and asking."

**Strategy:**
- Keep asking different people
- Network extensively
- Look beyond obvious sources
- Local talent often hidden

---

**5. Hot Chocolate:**
- **Big hit**
- Especially in cold climates
- Warms people up
- Keeps them longer

---

**6. The Real Work - Personal Outreach:**
> "As with every event: calls, calls, text, calls, emails, calls, negotiations ('I think I would rather hang out in Starbucks' 'I have to pack for my trip in two weeks'), and rsvp list (for yourself to know)."

**Reality:**
Event success = personal outreach effort

---

### 7. Shluchim Services Resources

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME], Fort Lauderdale, FL

**Resource:** www.ShluchimServices.com

**Available Items:**
- Light up LED Menorah Necklaces
- Dreidel Glasses
- Many Chanukah crafts
- Etc.

**Kinus Pickup:**
Most items available for free pickup in NY during Kinus with preorders

**WARNING:** Don't wait until last minute when it's sold out

---

## Comprehensive Strategy Summary

### Core Elements for Success

**1. Reframe the Event**
- Name: "Chanukah Celebration" not just "Menorah Lighting"
- Focus: Party/celebration, not just ceremony

**2. Interactive Elements**
- Doughnut decorating station
- Craft activities
- Photo opportunities with mascot
- Hands-on experiences

**3. Giveaways**
- Real money (crisp dollar bills as gelt)
- Light-up items (menorah necklaces, dreidel glasses)
- Take-home crafts
- Memorable souvenirs

**4. Entertainment**
- Fire dancers (vet carefully)
- Fire eaters
- Juggler
- Magician
- Light show
- Fireworks (if budget allows)
- Ice menorah

**5. Food**
- Hot chocolate (essential in cold climates)
- Doughnuts
- Latkes
- Warm refreshments

**6. Community Involvement**
- Give kibudim (honors)
- Children sing
- Community members light
- Personal investment

**7. Timing**
- **Sunday works best**
- Avoid major vacation conflicts
- Check local calendar

**8. Personal Outreach**
- Calls, texts, emails
- RSVP tracking
- Negotiate ("No I really think you should come")
- Persistent follow-up

---

## What Doesn't Work Long-Term

### The Problem with Same Old Same Old

**From original question:**
> "Have done a juggler, magician... But it's getting boring though and people are taking for granted"

**Lesson:**
Need to refresh and vary elements year to year

### Need for Innovation

**Solutions:**
- Add new elements each year
- Rotate entertainment types
- Try new interactive activities
- Keep it fresh

---

## Budget Considerations

### Lower Cost Options:
- Hot chocolate
- Dollar bill gelt
- Local entertainers
- DIY decorating stations
- Mascot costume (one-time investment)

### Medium Cost Options:
- Light-up giveaways ($2-5 per person)
- Professional entertainer
- Ice menorah
- Sound/light equipment rental

### Higher Cost Options:
- Fireworks
- Multiple professional acts
- Elaborate food spreads
- Premium giveaways for everyone

---

## Implementation Plan

### 6 Weeks Before:
- Book entertainer
- Order giveaways from Shluchim Services
- Plan interactive elements
- Set date (Sunday if possible)

### 3-4 Weeks Before:
- Get crisp bills from bank
- Order doughnuts/food supplies
- Prepare decorating station materials
- Start personal outreach

### 2 Weeks Before:
- Intensify personal outreach
- Track RSVPs
- Confirm all vendors
- Test equipment

### Week Of:
- Final calls/texts
- Pick up supplies
- Prepare setup
- Charge mascot costume (if inflatable)

### Day Of:
- Set up decorating station
- Prepare hot chocolate
- Test sound system
- Have giveaways ready
- Enjoy!

---

## Measuring Success

### Beyond Attendance Numbers

**Quality Indicators:**
- People stay longer
- More engagement/participation
- Social media posts
- Word of mouth
- Requests to help next year
- Donations/sponsorships

**Remember:**
> "Keep in mind that years vary and have ups and downs" - Rabbi [REDACTED-NAME]

One down year doesn't mean failure. Weather, vacation schedules, and other external factors play a role.

---

## Final Thoughts

**The Challenge:**
Small town menorah lightings can become routine

**The Solution:**
- Constant innovation
- Multiple engaging elements
- Personal outreach (most important!)
- Community ownership
- Focus on celebration, not just ceremony

**The Work:**
Success requires significant personal effort - calls, texts, negotiations, persistence

**The Reward:**
Vibrant community Chanukah celebration that people look forward to

**Key Insight:**
> "People care more about a good community Chanukah party than the lighting itself (the lighting gets old after a year or 2)"

Focus on creating a memorable, fun, community-building experience, not just a lighting ceremony.


---
**End of Document 37**
---

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > Old > Chanukah Menorahs > Public Menorah] Fire Truck Giving Gelt

## An Idea for Future Chanukahs

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME]

**Note:** This content is also covered in detail in File 020 (Car Menorah Parade Compilation - Fire Truck Menorah Parade section)

---

## The Concept

### Background

In our area, the firemen go around to neighborhoods before December 25 giving out candy canes.

We have in our Chabad House a Fire Chief who asked if we could do something for Chanukah.

---

## Implementation

**Setup:**
- Put a Menorah on a Fire Truck
- Go around to neighborhoods giving out Chanukah Gelt and Dreidels

**Coordination:**
- Told people that we were coming around
- Set up a route
- Had people get their neighbors to come out to meet us

**Time:**
- Had two hours on the Fire Truck
- Able to visit six neighborhoods

---

## Results

**Attendance:**
> "In some neighborhoods we had over 100 people waiting for us to come."

**Impact:**
- Impressive sight with lights flashing
- Chanukah music playing over the loudspeakers
- Kiddush Hashem
- People loved it (who previously had only seen something like this for Dec. 25)

**Firemen Response:**
> "The firemen loved it and said that for next year we need to plan on doing it for more than one night"

**Outreach:**
> "It got us to meet a bunch of people we never would have met."

---

## Recommendation

**For Other Communities:**

If you have a similar system with firemen going around before December 25, **ask them if they would be willing to do something for Chanukah as well.**

---

## Additional Note from Sicha

**Important Halachic Point:**

> "I saw this in a sicha today, where the Rebbe says that an announcement should be made by the public lighting, that one is not yotze!"

**Meaning:**
At public menorah lightings, announce that this public lighting does not fulfill one's personal obligation to light at home.

**Why This Matters:**
- Ensures people understand they must light at home
- Prevents confusion about fulfilling mitzvah
- Educates about proper observance
- Maintains halachic integrity

---

## See Comprehensive Guide

For full details on fire truck menorah parades including:
- Detailed how-to guide
- Equipment needs
- Timing and logistics
- Stop coordination
- Music setup
- Community engagement
- Interview with experienced Shliach

**Refer to:** File 020 - Car Menorah Parade Compilation (Fire Truck Menorah Parade section)

---

## Key Takeaways

**What Worked:**
1. Fire department partnership
2. Neighborhood route planning
3. Advance notice to residents
4. Visual/audio impact (lights, music)
5. Giveaways (gelt, dreidels)
6. Meeting people in their neighborhoods

**Success Factors:**
- Fire Chief relationship
- Piggybacking on existing tradition (candy cane distribution)
- Community loved seeing familiar trucks for Chanukah
- Firemen wanted to do more next year
- Reached unaffiliated Jews where they live

**Halachic Responsibility:**
- Make announcement that public lighting doesn't fulfill personal obligation
- Educate about home lighting requirements
- Maintain proper halachic standards


---
**End of Document 38**
---

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > Old > Chanukah Menorahs > Public Menorah] Reform Wants to Join Event

## Forum Discussion

**Source:** http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/forum/viewtopic.php?t=218979

---

## Question

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME]

**Situation:**
I received a phone call from the president of the JCC (reform). He wanted to know if we could do a public menorah lighting together.

**Context:**
This is my first year being on Shlichus here in this small town.

**Questions:**
- How do I go about this?
- Is this a situation that I should take advantage of and do it together with him?
- Is it not good to join such a project with the reform?
- Any advice would be appreciated

---

## Response 1: Get Proper Guidance

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME]

**Critical Advice:**

> "You need to get a rov who you will be comfortable asking these questions to, and who can find the best solution for you. I doubt anyone on this forum is going to give you a clear yes or no."

> "This is why you have a head Shliach and your local Shliach. Between them and a rov you'll find your answer."

---

## Response 2: JCC vs. Reform Distinction

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME]

**Important Clarification:**

> "The jcc is not officially a single organization. We did a lighting at the jcc one year and never had any repercussions."

---

### When There IS a Problem

**Sanctioning Positions:**
> "It is only if by your presence you might be sanctioning their position as rabbis by doing panels together etc.. and only with rabbis getting perspectives of the so called three branches. By doing so you are tacitly agreeing that there can be a different peirush to the Torah than the Halacha."

**Where the Problem Lies:**
- Doing panels with Reform rabbis
- Being on programs about "three branches"
- Any format that legitimizes Reform rabbinic authority
- Tacit agreement to "different interpretations" of Torah

---

### When There's NO Problem

**This Case:**
> "Here there is none of that."

**Why It's Different:**
- Just a public menorah lighting
- Not a panel or discussion
- Not presenting "three perspectives"
- Not legitimizing Reform rabbinate
- Simple community event

---

## Response 3: Check JCC Affiliation

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME], CA

**Verification:**
> "JCC's as a rule are not affiliated with the Reform movement, if that is true there should be no problem, you can check out if they are at www.uahc.org"

---

## Key Distinctions

### JCC is NOT Reform

**Important Understanding:**
- JCCs are generally not Reform-affiliated organizations
- Community centers, not synagogues
- Neutral communal space
- Different from Reform temple

**Verification:**
Check www.uahc.org to see if specific JCC is Reform-affiliated

---

### Event Type Matters

**Problematic:**
- Panel discussions on "Jewish perspectives"
- Three branches of Judaism programs
- Anything implying equal validity of movements
- Legitimizing Reform clergy as "rabbis"

**Generally Acceptable:**
- Community menorah lighting
- Cultural event
- Holiday celebration
- Neutral communal gathering

---

## Decision Framework

### Questions to Ask

**1. Who is Involved?**
- JCC president (lay person) ✓ Generally OK
- Reform rabbi ⚠️ Requires careful assessment

**2. What is the Format?**
- Community menorah lighting ✓ Generally OK
- Panel/discussion with Reform clergy ✗ Problematic

**3. How is it Framed?**
- Community holiday event ✓ OK
- "Three branches perspective" ✗ Not OK
- Your menorah, they attend ✓ OK
- Joint program with equal billing ⚠️ Depends

**4. What's the Message?**
- Celebrating Chanukah together ✓ OK
- Legitimizing different Torah interpretations ✗ Not OK

---

## Practical Considerations

### Benefits of Partnership

**Outreach:**
- Reach Reform-affiliated Jews
- Bigger crowd
- Community unity
- Neutral ground

**Resources:**
- Shared costs
- JCC space
- Wider publicity
- Combined efforts

---

### Risks of Partnership

**Perception:**
- Legitimizing Reform
- Confusing community
- Appearing to endorse Reform
- Setting precedent

**Control:**
- Loss of message control
- Compromise on content
- Future expectations
- Precedent for other collaborations

---

## Guidance from Experienced Shluchim

### Consult Authority

**Critical Step:**
> "You need to get a rov who you will be comfortable asking these questions to"

**Who to Consult:**
1. Head Shliach
2. Local mashpia/rov
3. Merkos/Aguch if needed

**Why:**
- Situation-specific factors
- Halachic considerations
- Long-term implications
- Local dynamics

---

### Historical Precedents

**What Others Have Done:**
> "We did a lighting at the jcc one year and never had any repercussions"

**But Remember:**
Each situation is different:
- Community size
- JCC vs. Reform temple
- Who's involved
- How it's framed

---

## Possible Approaches

### Option 1: Yes, With Parameters

**If You Partner:**
- You lead/organize
- Your menorah, your rabbi
- They attend and help promote
- Clear it's a community (not Reform) event
- No joint billing with Reform rabbi
- Avoid language of "partnership between movements"

---

### Option 2: Polite Decline

**If You Don't Partner:**
- Thank them for interest
- Invite them to attend your event
- Offer to help them separately
- Maintain cordial relations
- Don't burn bridges

---

### Option 3: Alternative Collaboration

**Middle Ground:**
- They promote your event
- Use their mailing list
- JCC space (if appropriate)
- They attend, you organize
- No official "partnership"

---

## Red Flags to Avoid

**Never:**
- Joint program with Reform rabbi as co-equal
- Panel on "perspectives on Chanukah"
- Anything implying Reform is legitimate stream
- Format that legitimizes Reform clergy
- Language of "three branches"

**Warning Signs:**
- They want their rabbi to speak
- Suggest "different perspectives"
- Want equal billing
- Frame as interfaith/inter-movement dialogue

---

## Final Thoughts

**The Situation:**
JCC president (not Reform rabbi) wants to do menorah lighting together

**The Assessment:**
- Probably OK (JCC generally not Reform-affiliated)
- Verify JCC is not Reform organization
- Ensure format is simple community event
- No Reform clergy involvement as "rabbi"

**The Process:**
**MUST consult with:**
1. Head Shliach
2. Rov/mashpia
3. Get clear guidance for YOUR situation

**The Principle:**
Community menorah lighting together = generally OK

Joint program legitimizing Reform = not OK

**The Key:**
How it's framed and who's involved makes all the difference

**Remember:**
> "I doubt anyone on this forum is going to give you a clear yes or no" - [REDACTED-NAME]

Get proper rabbinic guidance for your specific situation!


---
**End of Document 39**
---

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > Old > Chanukah Menorahs > Public Menorah] Menorah on City Ground - Fees

## Forum Discussion

**Topic:** Menorah on city ground - Fees and permissions

---

## Question

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME]

Can you please share if you pay a fee or not? Also how much do you pay?

**Their Situation:**
The city here wants to charge me **$150 a day**....

---

## Response

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME]

**Key Point:**
> "I assume every single city is different, kol sheken state."

---

### Their City's Arrangement

**Booking Process:**
- No permission needed
- Just need to book the spot from parks department

**Cost:**
- Close to **$800** (presumably for the entire Chanukah period)

**Additional Benefit:**
> "On the other hand, the event is usually the first night and they have no problem with me leaving the menorah for the entire Chanukah."

---

## Analysis

### Fee Structures Vary Widely

**Example 1: Daily Fee**
- $150 per day
- For 8 nights = $1,200 total
- More expensive option

**Example 2: Event Booking**
- ~$800 for entire period
- Book the spot once
- Leave menorah up all Chanukah
- More cost-effective

---

## Considerations

### What Affects Fees

**Location Type:**
- City plaza vs. park
- High-traffic vs. low-traffic area
- Monument/landmark location vs. standard space

**City Size:**
- Major metropolitan area (higher fees)
- Suburban city (moderate fees)
- Small town (lower or no fees)

**Event Classification:**
- "Event permit" (one-time fee)
- "Temporary installation" (daily fee)
- "Public gathering" (different fee structure)

**Insurance Requirements:**
- May affect total cost
- Some cities require proof of insurance
- Additional insured designation

---

## Negotiation Strategies

### Option 1: Event Permit vs. Daily Fee

**Argue:**
- Main event is one night (first night or specific date)
- Menorah left up for religious observance
- Not 8 separate events
- Request event permit rate, not daily rate

**Example:**
If you have major event first night with mayor, etc., that's "the event." Menorah remaining is religious display, not separate daily events.

---

### Option 2: Religious Accommodation

**Frame As:**
- Religious observance requiring 8-night display
- Requesting accommodation for religious practice
- Not commercial event
- Educational/cultural purpose

**May Result In:**
- Reduced fees
- Waived fees
- Different classification

---

### Option 3: Community Partnership

**Propose:**
- City co-sponsor
- Free or reduced fee in exchange for city recognition
- Media coverage benefiting city
- Community service event

---

### Option 4: Compare to Other Holidays

**Research:**
- What does city charge for Christmas displays?
- Are religious displays given different treatment?
- Equal protection argument
- Precedent from other holidays

---

## Budget Planning

### Typical Fee Ranges

**Major Cities:**
- $500-$1,500 for entire Chanukah
- Higher for premium locations

**Mid-Size Cities:**
- $200-$800 for entire Chanukah
- Varies by location

**Small Towns:**
- Often free
- Or nominal fee $50-$200
- May waive for religious/community events

---

## Questions to Ask City

**Before Agreeing:**

1. **What's included in the fee?**
   - Just the space?
   - Electricity?
   - Security?
   - Insurance coverage?

2. **Is this daily or total?**
   - $150/day × 8 = $1,200
   - Or $150 total?
   - Clarify before committing

3. **Can we book as single event?**
   - Reduces paperwork
   - May reduce cost
   - Simpler process

4. **Are there alternative locations?**
   - Different fee structures?
   - Different departments?
   - Park vs. city hall vs. town square?

5. **Is negotiation possible?**
   - Religious accommodation?
   - Community partnership?
   - Sponsorship model?

---

## Alternative Approaches

### Private Property

**Instead of City Ground:**
- Mall parking lot
- Business plaza
- Private property with permission
- May be free or cheaper

**Benefits:**
- Avoid city fees
- Easier permission
- More control
- Flexible arrangements

---

### Shared Costs

**If Fee is High:**
- Find sponsors to cover city fee
- Community fundraiser
- Business sponsorship
- Grant/foundation funding

---

## Documentation

**Get in Writing:**
- Exact fee amount
- What it covers
- Duration (1 event or 8 days)
- Any restrictions
- Insurance requirements
- Setup/removal deadlines

**Avoid:**
- Verbal agreements
- Unclear fee structures
- Hidden costs
- Last-minute fee increases

---

## Final Thoughts

**Key Takeaways:**

1. **Fees vary dramatically** - $0 to $1,200+
2. **City policies differ** - No standard approach
3. **Classification matters** - Event vs. installation vs. display
4. **Negotiation is possible** - Religious accommodation, community partnership
5. **Get clarity upfront** - Understand exactly what you're paying for

**Strategy:**
- Research what others pay in your area
- Understand your city's classification system
- Negotiate for event permit vs. daily fee
- Consider religious accommodation angle
- Document everything in writing

**Bottom Line:**
$150/day ($1,200 total) seems high compared to other examples. Worth negotiating for event permit rate or religious accommodation.


---
**End of Document 46**
---

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > Old > Chanukah Menorahs > Public Menorah] Invitation for Balebatim

## Sample Invitation Letter

**Forum Source:** http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/forum/viewtopic.php?t=21040

---

## Template

**Dear Mr. & Mrs. [Last Name],**

This Chanukah, for the **fifth time**, we will be having a Public Menorah lighting ceremony in Liverpool City Centre. The **20-foot menorah** will be erected outside St. George's Hall and lighting will take place every evening at 6:00.

As a **friend and long-time supporter** of Lubavitch Foundation Liverpool, please accept this **personal invitation** to attend the special communal lighting ceremony, which will take place at **6:00 on Tuesday evening, December 3, the 5th candle of Chanukah**, in the presence of the **Lord Mayor of Liverpool**.

This will be an event for the entire community, young and old, **not to be missed**.

Wishing you a very joyous Chanukah,

Rabbi [REDACTED-NAME]
Lubavitch Liverpool

---

## Key Elements of Effective Invitation

### 1. Establish Tradition

> "for the fifth time"

**Why This Works:**
- Shows this is established event
- Not first-time experiment
- Proven track record
- Annual tradition they shouldn't miss

---

### 2. Impressive Details

> "20-foot menorah"

**Specificity Matters:**
- Exact height creates visual
- Impressive scale
- Professional execution
- Worth attending

> "erected outside St. George's Hall"

**Prestigious Location:**
- Well-known landmark
- Central location
- Public prominence
- Easy to find

---

### 3. Personal Touch

> "As a friend and long-time supporter"

**Recognition:**
- Acknowledges relationship
- Appreciates their support
- Makes them feel valued
- Not mass mailing (even if it is)

> "please accept this personal invitation"

**Exclusivity:**
- Special invitation
- VIP treatment
- Personally selected
- Privileged access

---

### 4. Specific Time and Date

> "6:00 on Tuesday evening, December 3, the 5th candle of Chanukah"

**Complete Information:**
- Exact time
- Day of week
- Secular date
- Which night of Chanukah
- No confusion

---

### 5. Highlight Special Guest

> "in the presence of the Lord Mayor of Liverpool"

**VIP Element:**
- Important dignitary
- Official recognition
- Photo opportunity
- Civic importance
- Social status

---

### 6. Broad Appeal

> "This will be an event for the entire community, young and old"

**Inclusive:**
- Bring whole family
- All ages welcome
- Community gathering
- Not exclusive or limited

---

### 7. Urgency/FOMO

> "not to be missed"

**Creates:**
- Sense of importance
- Fear of missing out
- Compelling attendance
- Social expectation

---

## Customization Guide

### Adapt This Template

**Replace These Elements:**

**Location:**
- Your city/landmark
- Specific venue
- Recognizable location

**Scale:**
- Your menorah size
- Unique features
- Impressive details

**Timing:**
- Your specific date/time
- Which night chosen
- Daily lighting times

**VIP Guest:**
- Your mayor
- Governor
- Celebrity
- Community leader
- Or omit if not applicable

**Year/Tradition:**
- First annual
- Fifth time
- Tenth anniversary
- Growing tradition

---

## When to Send

### Timing Strategy

**3 Weeks Before:**
- Save the date
- Initial invitation
- Build anticipation

**1 Week Before:**
- Reminder
- Final details
- RSVP request

**Day Before:**
- Final reminder
- Weather update
- Parking info

---

## Distribution Methods

### Personal Invitation

**Best For:**
- Major donors
- Community leaders
- Close supporters
- Board members

**Method:**
- Printed letter
- Hand-delivered or mailed
- Personal phone call follow-up

---

### Digital Invitation

**Broader Community:**
- Email
- E-vite
- Facebook event
- WhatsApp groups

**Advantages:**
- Reaches more people
- Easy RSVP tracking
- Reminder functionality
- Share-able

---

## Additional Enhancements

### What You Can Add

**RSVP Request:**
"Please RSVP by [date] to [contact info]"

**Parking Information:**
"Parking available at [location]"

**Weather Contingency:**
"Rain date: [alternative date]" or "Event rain or shine"

**What to Expect:**
- Program length
- Entertainment
- Refreshments
- Children's activities

**Dress Code:**
"Dress warmly - outdoor event"

**Photo Opportunity:**
"Photo with Lord Mayor available"

**Media Coverage:**
"Expected media attendance"

---

## Sample Variations

### Version for First Year

"This Chanukah, we are **excited to introduce** our inaugural Public Menorah lighting ceremony..."

### Version for Milestone

"This Chanukah marks our **10th anniversary** of bringing the light of Chanukah to Liverpool City Centre..."

### Version Emphasizing Community

"Join hundreds of community members for our annual Public Menorah lighting..."

### Version for Smaller Event

"You are personally invited to an intimate lighting ceremony with [notable guest]..."

---

## Follow-Up

### After the Event

**Thank You Note:**
"Thank you for joining us at this year's Public Menorah Lighting. Your presence contributed to the success of this meaningful community celebration."

**Photo Share:**
"Enclosed is a photo from the event. We hope to see you again next year!"

**Impact Report:**
"Thanks to your support, over 500 community members attended this year's lighting..."

---

## Final Thoughts

**This Invitation Works Because:**

1. **Personal** - Acknowledges recipient specifically
2. **Detailed** - All necessary information included
3. **Impressive** - Highlights scale and importance
4. **Prestigious** - VIP guest mentioned
5. **Inclusive** - Everyone welcome
6. **Urgent** - "Not to be missed"
7. **Professional** - Well-written and clear

**Result:**
Higher attendance from key community members and supporters

**Use this template** as basis for your own personalized invitations to ensure strong turnout from your balebatim and community leaders.


---
**End of Document 47**
---

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > Old > Chanukah Menorahs > Public Menorah] Letters from the Rebbe on Public Lighting

**Note:** This is a duplicate of content in Files 034 and 035. See those files for comprehensive guidance.

---

## Content Summary

**Forum Sources:**
- http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/article.html?h=483&o=114314
- http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/forum/viewtopic.php?t=58658

**Topic:** The Rebbe's letters regarding public menorah lightings and avoiding machlokes

---

## Key Situations Covered

**Situation One: Teaneck Menorah**
- Rebbe's instruction: "Bitchila kosavti lo shelo lehadlik eish hamachlokes"
- Senator's advice to back off
- Rebbe's response: "V'harei boze hatzedek itoy"
- Result: Backed off, worked it out next year

**Situation Two: Mayor Koch in New York**
- Rabbi Butman wanted to stand strong
- Rebbe wrote back: Don't start a Machlokes
- Result: Got different public space

**Key Principle:**
> "Clearly, while the Rebbe defends the right to put up a public Menorah, he doesn't want us to pick fights about them."

---

For complete details, cross-references, and practical application of the Rebbe's guidance on public menorahs and avoiding machlokes.

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Chanukah Facebook Contest

## Viral Photo Tagging Contest

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME]

**Description:** Another good Facebook Chanukah idea... not too late for this year

---

## The Concept

### How It Works

**Origins:**
> "Last year we started an idea at the Home Depot workshop and this year we extended it to every Chanukah event that we do..."

**Core Mechanism:**
Have people tag you or your wife or your Chabad with a picture of them lighting the menorah.

**Raffle System:**
- Every person who tags is entered into a raffle
- **8 nights, eight raffles**
- Different winner each night

**Daily Posts:**
Each morning post:
- A picture of a prize
- The name of the person who won

---

## Why This Works

### Engagement Benefits

**Direct Engagement:**
> "The people are loving it"

**Visual Proof:**
> "We get the Nachas (and the PR) of watching people actually lighting the menorahs"

**Bonus Nachas:**
> "The bonus is the extra nachas when members of other temples and their rabbi's are forced to like pictures (with you tagged in them) of them lighting."

---

### Viral Growth

**Organic Spread:**
> "Locally it has gone viral, people we don't even know are tagging us so they can be part of the contest"

**Why It Goes Viral:**
- Everyone wants to win
- Easy to participate
- Social proof (see others doing it)
- Fun and interactive
- Low barrier to entry
- Daily winners create urgency

---

## Implementation Guide

### Setup Requirements

**1. Decide on Prizes**
- 8 prizes (one per night)
- Varying value to keep interest
- Chanukah-themed or general prizes
- Post photo of each prize daily

**2. Create Contest Rules**
Post clear rules:
- Must tag [Your Chabad Name] in photo
- Photo must show menorah lighting
- One entry per night
- Winner announced each morning
- Must follow page to win

**3. Promote the Contest**
- Announce at every Chanukah event
- Post on Facebook before Chanukah
- Include in emails
- Mention at Home Depot workshop
- Tell everyone you give menorahs to

---

### Daily Process

**Night Of:**
- People light menorahs at home
- Take photos
- Tag your Chabad page
- Automatic entry

**Next Morning:**
- Review all tagged photos
- Select random winner (or judge on creativity)
- Post winner announcement with:
  - Winner's name
  - Their photo
  - Today's prize photo
  - Encouragement for tonight's lighting

---

## Sample Posts

### Launch Announcement

"🕎 CHANUKAH PHOTO CONTEST! 🕎

This Chanukah, share your menorah lighting with us!

**How to enter:**
1. Light your menorah each night
2. Take a photo
3. Tag @[YourChabadPage] in your post
4. You're entered to win!

**8 nights = 8 chances to win!**

Winners announced each morning. Tonight's prize: [Prize description]

Let the lights shine! 💫"

---

### Daily Winner Post

"🎉 NIGHT 3 WINNER! 🎉

Congratulations to [Winner Name] for winning tonight's prize: [Prize description]!

Thank you for sharing your beautiful menorah lighting with us! 🕎

**TONIGHT'S PRIZE:** [Show new prize photo]

Light your menorah tonight and tag us for your chance to win!

[Include winner's photo]"

---

### Engagement Post

"We are SO INSPIRED seeing all your menorah lightings! 😍

Over 50 families have already tagged us with their photos!

Don't forget to tag us tonight for your chance to win [Tonight's prize]

Keep the light shining! 💡"

---

## Prize Ideas

### Budget-Friendly Options

**Night 1-2:** $10-15 prizes
- Chanukah book
- Menorah set
- Dreidel game
- Chanukah music CD

**Night 3-5:** $20-30 prizes
- Restaurant gift card
- Judaica item
- Children's Chanukah toy
- Art supplies

**Night 6-7:** $40-50 prizes
- Larger gift card
- Quality menorah
- Shabbos candlesticks
- Jewish book set

**Night 8:** Grand Prize $75-100+
- Major gift card
- Premium Judaica
- Shabbaton sponsorship
- Family event tickets

---

### Sponsored Prizes

**Better Option:**
Get local businesses to donate prizes:
- Restaurant gift cards
- Retail merchandise
- Services (car wash, etc.)
- Product donations

**Benefits:**
- Free or low cost to you
- Promotes local businesses
- Community partnership
- Can mention sponsor in daily post

---

## Maximizing Participation

### Key Strategies

**1. Start Early**
- Announce contest before Chanukah
- Build anticipation
- Give menorahs with contest info attached

**2. Make It Easy**
- Clear, simple instructions
- Demonstrate at events
- Help people understand tagging

**3. Show Examples**
- Post your own family lighting
- Share early entries
- Model desired behavior

**4. Daily Reminders**
- Post each morning (winner)
- Post each afternoon (reminder for tonight)
- Keep it top of mind

**5. Celebrate All Entries**
- Like every tagged photo
- Comment on creative posts
- Share favorites to your page
- Make people feel seen

---

## The "Forced Like" Phenomenon

### Unexpected Benefit

**As Reported:**
> "The extra nachas when members of other temples and their rabbi's are forced to like pictures (with you tagged in them) of them lighting."

**Why This Happens:**
- Person tags you in their photo
- Their friends see the photo
- Their rabbi/temple friends like it to support them
- Facebook algorithm shows rabbi that Chabad is tagged
- Creates awareness in other communities
- Soft outreach to unaffiliated

**Strategic Value:**
- Extends your reach
- Non-confrontational visibility
- Social proof
- Algorithm boost

---

## Variations

### Alternative Implementations

**Video Contest:**
- Short video of lighting
- Brachot recitation
- Family singing

**Creativity Contest:**
- Most creative menorah
- Best decorated space
- Unique lighting location

**Story Contest:**
- Share Chanukah story with photo
- Best caption
- Family tradition description

**Kids Category:**
- Separate prizes for children
- Child-friendly prizes
- Encourages family participation

---

## Success Metrics

### What to Track

**Participation:**
- Number of tagged photos per night
- Total unique participants
- Repeat participants

**Engagement:**
- Likes per post
- Comments
- Shares
- Page follows gained

**Reach:**
- Post reach
- People talking about this
- Viral coefficient

**Real Impact:**
- People actually lighting
- New connections made
- Photos saved for future use

---

## Post-Chanukah Follow-Up

### Continue the Relationship

**Winner Thank You:**
- Personal message to each winner
- Invite to next event
- Add to special list

**Participant Recognition:**
- Create photo album with all entries
- "Thank you for sharing your light"
- Special appreciation post

**Database Growth:**
- Follow up with new taggers
- Invite to upcoming programs
- Personal welcome message

**Content Repurposing:**
- Save photos (with permission)
- Use in next year's promotion
- "Last year's contest" highlights
- Marketing materials

---

## Troubleshooting

### Common Issues

**Q: What if same people win repeatedly?**
A: Limit to one win per family, or weight selection toward new participants

**Q: What if no one tags us?**
A: Seed it with your own volunteers/staff/family. Once a few do it, others follow.

**Q: How do we verify they actually lit?**
A: Trust and assume good faith. Contest is about engagement, not policing.

**Q: What about privacy concerns?**
A: People choose to participate. They control what they post. You're not creating content, just receiving tags.

---

## Budget Planning

### Cost Breakdown

**Minimal Budget:** $200-300
- Mix of small items and donated prizes
- Focus on participation over prizes
- Community donations

**Moderate Budget:** $400-500
- Better quality prizes
- Gift cards more appealing
- Higher participation likely

**Generous Budget:** $700-1000
- Substantial prizes
- High-value grand prize
- Maximum participation
- Major buzz

**ROI:**
- Photos for future marketing (priceless)
- Engagement with dozens/hundreds (priceless)
- Watching people actually light (priceless)
- Viral spread (priceless)
- $50-100 per night in prizes = excellent value

---

## Final Thoughts

**Why This Works:**

1. **Low Barrier** - Take photo, tag, done
2. **Daily Engagement** - 8 nights, 8 chances
3. **Social Proof** - See others participating
4. **Fun** - Raffle element adds excitement
5. **Authentic** - People actually lighting menorahs
6. **Viral** - Spreads organically
7. **Cross-Community** - Reaches other temples' members

**The Genius:**
You're not asking people to come to an event or commit time. You're asking them to share something they're already doing (hopefully). The contest gives them extra motivation to actually light AND to share publicly.

**Result:**
> "Locally it has gone viral, people we don't even know are tagging us so they can be part of the contest"

**Bottom Line:**
For a few hundred dollars in prizes, you get massive engagement, visual proof of impact, viral spread, and the nachas of watching your community light menorahs. Highly recommended!

**Go for it!**


---
**End of Document 50**
---

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Chanukah Tips and Tricks

## Practical Field-Tested Tips Collection

**Forum Source:** http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/article.html?h=1824&o=2084457

**From:** [REDACTED-NAME]

> "While it is still fresh in our memory, perhaps we can put together some tips to make Chanukah easier for all of us."

---

## Maintenance & Setup Tips

### 1. WD40 for Menorah Sockets

**Prevents Rust and Stuck Bulbs**

**After Chanukah:**
- Before putting away your menorah (both car and large)
- Spray the light sockets with WD40
- Prevents rust during storage
- Next year's bulbs will install easily

**Before Chanukah:**
- Spray sockets BEFORE inserting bulbs
- Makes bulb removal much easier later
- "You would be having a much easier time getting the bulbs out :-)"

**Application:**
- Light spray in each socket
- Let dry before installing bulbs
- Works for both indoor and outdoor menorahs

---

### 2. Paraffin Candle Preparation

**For Souvenir Shop Candles**

**Pre-Event Wick Pulling:**
- Take tweezers (or do by hand)
- Pull wicks out a drop - not too much
- Creates easier lighting
- Produces larger flame

**Pre-Light New Candles:**
> "Pre light them - especially new ones, will save you alot of tzoros..."

**Why This Works:**
- New candles often have stiff wicks
- Pre-lighting creates carbon tip
- Much easier to relight at event
- First flame "primes" the wick

**Fuel Squirt Technique:**
> "Right before you light each candle... turn the candle upside-down and squeeze. It will squirt out some fuel. It should make it easier to light."

**Application:**
- Just before lighting (or during setup)
- Turn candle upside down
- Gentle squeeze
- Fuel spreads on top
- Dramatically easier ignition

---

## Fresh Latke Frying at Events

### Equipment Setup

**The Game-Changer:**
> "We bought a camping grill (double flame with a wind guard). They also sold a griddle in the same outdoor items area. We brought it to the menorah lighting and fried fresh latkes."

**Why Camping Grill vs Electric:**
> "The electric ones are not really hot enough."

**Equipment List:**
1. **Camping grill** - double flame with wind guard
2. **Griddle** - sold in outdoor items area (same section)
3. **Extra fuel** - one bottle sufficient for one lighting, but bring backup
4. **Different fuel types** available:
   - Home Depot: Multiple fuel types (different color bottles)
   - Target: Regular camping type only

**For Cold Climates:**
> "If you are in a very cold area, consider using a hotter burning fuel."

---

### Capacity and Timing

**Production:**
- One setup serves 20-25 people
- More if you prep in advance
- "Still better than sterno latkes"
- Creates authentic "Chanukah smell"

**Batter Timing:**
> "You can't make the batter too much in advance, because the potatoes will become watery, but your wife already knows that..."

**Setup Considerations:**
- Fresh frying creates major draw
- Smell attracts people
- Authentic experience
- Professional appearance
- Much better than pre-made

---

## Lighting & Illumination

### Halogen Spotlight System

**For Large Outdoor Menorahs:**
- Halogen lights illuminating the menorah
- Creates visibility from distance
- Professional appearance
- Pirsumei nisa enhancement

**Setup:**
- Position before event
- Test angles and brightness
- Ensure power source
- Creates dramatic effect

---

### DIY Lighting Torch

**Problem:** Need to reach tall menorah flames safely

**Solution:** Homemade torch

**Construction:**

**Materials:**
- Wire hanger
- Paint stick (or broomstick)
- Cotton cloth (or cotton rope, strip of old undershirt/towel)
- Lighter fluid

**Assembly:**
1. Straighten out hanger
2. Fold it a few times (for strength)
3. Attach to end of paint stick/broomstick
4. Tie cotton cloth to the end

**Critical Safety Note:**
> "Make sure that it's cotton. Burn some dry and see if it burns or melts. Don't use it if it melts."

**Usage:**
- Dip in lighter fluid
- Light the torch
- Use to reach menorah lights
- Replace cotton almost every night

**Benefits:**
- Long reach for tall menorahs
- Safe distance
- Reusable
- Inexpensive
- Professional appearance

---

## Outdoor Menorah Bulbs

### Year-Round Display Bulbs

**Question from [REDACTED-NAME], Wellesley Hills, MA:**
> "We keep our menorah up all year. Anyone know which is the best looking OUTDOOR bulbs to use and where we can get them at a decent price?"

**Answer from [REDACTED-NAME], Baltimore, MD:**

**Recommended Bulb:**

## Advanced Tips

### Combining Strategies

**Maximum Impact Setup:**
1. **Arrival:** Halogen spotlights already positioned
2. **Setup:** Start latke frying 20 minutes before lighting
3. **Preparation:** Pre-squirt candles 10 minutes before
4. **Lighting:** Use DIY torch for safe, professional lighting
5. **Throughout:** Fresh latkes create authentic atmosphere
6. **Visibility:** WD40-maintained bulbs shine bright all winter

**Creates:**
- Visual impact (spotlights)
- Sensory draw (latke smell)
- Professional execution (torch)
- Smooth operation (maintained equipment)
- Year-round presence (quality bulbs)

## Safety Considerations

### Fire Safety

**DIY Torch:**
- Test cotton material first
- Keep lighter fluid away from flames until ready
- Replace worn cotton immediately
- Have fire extinguisher nearby
- Don't over-soak torch

**Latke Frying:**
- Stable surface for camping grill
- Wind guard properly positioned
- Keep children at safe distance
- Have burn kit available
- Extra fuel stored safely away from heat

**Electrical:**
- Weather-rated bulbs for outdoor use
- Proper outdoor-rated extension cords
- GFCI protection if available
- Keep connections dry
- Regular inspection of wiring

---

**Original Post Invitation:**
> "Few tips for Chanukah, please add your own. Perhaps someone can compile them and resend them for next year."

- Various forum contributors

**Why These Tips Matter:**

1. **WD40 maintenance** - Saves hours of frustration next year
2. **Candle prep** - Prevents lighting failures at critical moments
3. **Fresh latkes** - Creates authentic, engaging experience

Small preparations make huge differences. Spending 5 minutes with WD40 saves 30 minutes of struggling next year. Investing $50 in a camping grill creates an experience worth hundreds in engagement.

Compile these tips with your own additions and improvements. Share with other Shluchim. Build on collective wisdom.

**Bottom Line:**
These are real solutions from Shluchim who learned the hard way. Use them to avoid the same struggles and create better experiences for your community.

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Menorah Lighting Instructions for Balebatim

## Step-by-Step Guide for Home Menorah Lighting

**Purpose:** Clear, simple instructions to send to community members for lighting at home

**Resource Links:**
- Detailed blessings and transliterations: [Link in original document]
- Menorah Brochos Instructions and Songs: [Google Drive link in original]

---

## Daily Reminder Message

### Sample Email/Text Template

**Subject:** Light your Menorah - Today

**Message:**
> "Don't Forget to light your Menorah today in your home before [CANDLE LIGHTING TIME]."

**Timing Guidance:**
- Send daily reminder in morning or early afternoon
- Include specific time for your location
- Example: "before 4:26pm" (adjust for your time zone)

---

## Complete Lighting Instructions

### Step 1: Prepare the Menorah

**Arrange the Lights:**

Set up oil or candles ensuring they will burn for at least:
- **Half hour after nightfall** (if lighting before nightfall)
- **One half hour** (if lighting after nightfall)

**Placement Pattern:**

**First Night:**
- Set one candle to the **far right** of the menorah

**Second Night:**
- Add second light to the **left of the first one**

**Each Subsequent Night:**
- Add one light each night
- Continue adding from **right to left**

**Visual Guide:**
```
Night 1:  [shamash]  . . . . . . . *
Night 2:  [shamash]  . . . . . . * *
Night 3:  [shamash]  . . . . . * * *
Night 8:  [shamash]  * * * * * * * *
```

---

### Step 2: Gather the Family

**Before Lighting:**
- Gather everyone in the house around the menorah
- Creates family unity
- Shared experience
- Children witness the mitzvah

**Why This Matters:**
- Educational moment
- Family bonding
- Pirsumei nisa within home
- Creates lasting memories

---

### Step 3: Light the Shamash

**Preparation:**
- Light the shamash candle first
- Hold it in your **right hand** (unless you are left-handed)
- Stand while reciting blessings
- Ready to light the menorah candles

---

### Step 4: Recite the Blessings

**While Standing:**

#### First Blessing (All Nights)

**Transliteration:**
> Ba-ruch A-tah Ado-nai E-lo-he-nu Me-lech ha-olam a-sher ki-de-sha-nu be-mitz-vo-tav ve-tzi-va-nu le-had-lik ner Cha-nu-kah.

**Translation:**
Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who has sanctified us with His commandments, and commanded us to kindle the Chanukah light.

---

#### Second Blessing (All Nights)

**Transliteration:**
> Ba-ruch A-tah Ado-nai E-lo-he-nu Me-lech Ha-olam she-a-sa ni-sim la-avo-te-nu ba-ya-mim ha-hem bi-zman ha-zeh.

**Translation:**
Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who performed miracles for our forefathers in those days, at this time.

---

#### Third Blessing (First Night Only)

**Transliteration:**
> Ba-ruch A-tah Ado-nai E-lo-he-nu Me-lech Ha-olam she-heche-ya-nu ve-ki-yi-ma-nu ve-higi-a-nu liz-man ha-zeh.

**Translation:**
Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who has granted us life, sustained us, and enabled us to reach this occasion.

**Important Note:**
> "The 3rd Blessing is only recited on the first night of Chanukah."

---

### Step 5: Light the Candles

**Direction:**
- Each night, light the **newest (left-most) candle first**
- Continue lighting from **left to right**

**Pattern:**
- **Add candles:** Right to left
- **Light candles:** Left to right

**Why This Order:**
- Honors the new mitzvah first
- Light the fresh candle before the others
- Traditional order

**Example for Night 3:**
```
Setup order:     →  →  →
                * * * [shamash]

Lighting order:  ←  ←  ←
                1st 2nd 3rd [shamash]
```

---

## Quick Reference Card Format

### For Printing/Distribution

**One-Page Format:**

---

**CHANUKAH MENORAH LIGHTING**

**1. ARRANGE LIGHTS**
- Right to left
- Enough oil/wax for 30+ minutes

**2. GATHER FAMILY**
- Everyone around menorah

**3. LIGHT SHAMASH**
- Hold in right hand
- Stand for blessings

**4. RECITE BLESSINGS**

*All nights:*
1. Baruch... lehadlik ner Chanukah
2. Baruch... she'asa nisim

*First night only:*
3. Baruch... shehecheyanu

**5. LIGHT CANDLES**
- Start with newest (left)
- Light left to right

**TIMING:** Before [LOCAL TIME]

**RESOURCES:**
[Your website]/chanukah
[Phone number]

---

## Digital Distribution Options

### Email Template

**Subject Line Options:**
- "Light Your Menorah Tonight! 🕎"
- "Chanukah Lighting - Night [#]"
- "Don't Forget: Menorah Lighting Tonight Before [TIME]"

**Email Body:**

```
Dear [Name],

Don't forget to light your Menorah tonight before [TIME]!

Tonight is Night [#] of Chanukah.

QUICK GUIDE:
1. Place [#] candle(s) from right to left
2. Gather family
3. Light shamash
4. Say blessings (see link below)
5. Light candles left to right

BLESSINGS & SONGS:
[Link to your resources page]

Need a menorah or candles? Call us: [PHONE]

Wishing you a bright and joyous Chanukah!

Rabbi [Your Name]
[Your Chabad House]
```

---

**Short Version:**

```

Night [#] of Chanukah.

```

```
Tonight: [#] candles

Step-by-step guide: [LINK]

#Chanukah #MenorahLighting #JewishHolidays #ChabadOf[YourCity]
```

## Supporting Materials Reference

### Detailed Resources Available

**Menorah Brochos Instructions and Songs:**
- Full transliteration with vowels
- Audio pronunciation guides
- Traditional Chanukah songs
- Extended family activities

**Available At:**
- Website: [Your Chabad website]/chanukah
- Google Drive: [Link in original document]
- Printed copies available at Chabad House

---

## Timing Guidelines

### When to Send

**Morning Reminder:**
- 9:00 AM - "Tonight is Chanukah lighting"
- Gives people all day to prepare

**Afternoon Reminder:**
- 2:00 PM - "Don't forget - tonight before [TIME]"
- Final reminder with specific time

**Just-in-Time:**
- 1 hour before lighting time - "Lighting time in one hour!"
- For those who need last-minute reminder

### Frequency

**Daily Throughout Chanukah:**
- Consistency is key
- Don't assume people remember
- Each night is fresh mitzvah
- Some people forget which night it is

---

## Common Questions to Address

### FAQ to Include in Full Instructions

**Q: What if I miss the lighting time?**
A: You can light later in the evening as long as people are still awake. Don't say the blessings after sunrise.

**Q: Where should I place my menorah?**
A: Near a window or doorway for pirsumei nisa (publicizing the miracle). Make sure it's visible from outside.

**Q: Can I use candles one night and oil another?**
A: Yes, both are perfectly acceptable. Use whatever is convenient each night.

**Q: How long must the lights burn?**
A: At least 30 minutes after nightfall. If you lit early, they should burn until 30 minutes after sunset.

**Q: What if my candles blow out?**
A: You fulfilled the mitzvah. You don't need to relight them, but you may if you wish.

---

## Follow-Up Resources

### What to Send After Initial Instructions

**Night 2-8:**
- Brief reminder of which night
- Link back to full instructions
- Encourage sharing photos
- Daily Chanukah thought/inspiration

**Photo Sharing Encouragement:**
"Share your menorah lighting photos! Tag us @[YourChabadHandle] or send via WhatsApp: [PHONE]"

---

## Accessibility Considerations

### For Different Audiences

**Families with Young Children:**
- Emphasize safety (adult supervision)
- Suggest children help set up candles
- Sing songs after lighting
- Make it fun and engaging

**Elderly or Solo Individuals:**
- Offer to bring menorahs/supplies
- Suggest lighting with family via video call
- Provide larger-print instructions
- Follow up with personal calls

**New to Mitzvah:**
- Offer in-person demonstration
- Video tutorial available
- "No question is too simple"
- Encourage calling with any confusion

**Hebrew Challenged:**
- Full transliteration provided
- "Do your best with pronunciation"
- "G-d understands your intent"
- Audio recordings available

---

## Tracking and Engagement

### Measuring Impact

**Ways to Track:**
- RSVP/confirmation responses
- Photo shares on social media
- Follow-up calls to select families
- Menorah kit distribution numbers
- Website resource page views

**Engagement Opportunities:**
- Daily photo contest (see File 050)
- "Share your candle count" social posts
- Video compilation at end of Chanukah
- Thank you post with community photos

---

## Materials Checklist

### What to Prepare Before Chanukah

**Digital:**
- [ ] Email template with local times
- [ ] SMS template ready
- [ ] Social media graphics
- [ ] Website instructions page updated
- [ ] Audio/video tutorials if using

**Print:**

- [ ] Full-page guides
