## The Grammen Themes

### Patterns to Note

**Chanukah Connections:**
- Matityahu and Maccabees
- Temple restoration
- Oil miracle
- Light overcoming darkness
- Dreidel game

**Light Metaphors:**
- Candle of G-d = soul
- Light from darkness
- One candle makes difference
- Inspiring others
- Keeping flame alive

**Gratitude Expressions:**
- "You made Chanukah bright"
- "We thank you"
- "Keeping Chabad alive"
- "Your kindness is like Manna from Heaven"
- "You made our evening"

**Community Pride:**
- "Over sixteen years" (Chabad presence)
- "Countless lives touched"
- "Chabad couldn't produce programs like these" (without you)
- Flying performer from Israel
- Everyone knows you

---

## The Invitation Letter

### Full Text

```
December 5, 2006
14 Kislev, 5767

Dr. Ross & Dani Clevens

Dear Dr. Ross & Dani,

As you have probably already heard, we are planning a sensational program that will put Chanukah in Brevard this year on a different plateau. This event, sponsored by Chabad of the Space & Treasure Coasts is open to the entire community and promises to be a dynamic evening of first class entertainment as well as a great way to celebrate the fourth night of Chanukah for the whole family.

World renowned Latino-Chassidic-Rock Sensation Yehudah Glantz from Israel will perform Live in Concert at the King Center for The Performing Arts Monday, December, 18 2006. A special children's program titled "A Kid's Paradise" featuring Judah Maccabee Stilt Walker, Chanukah crafts and contests will precede the program followed by a grand Menorah Lighting & ceremony.

Here's where you come into the picture:

We have selected 8 friends, representing the Chanukah candles, to be honored with the kindling of the Menorah. We would like to honor you, Ross & Dani, to come up to the stage during the ceremony and light a candle. The actual ceremony will be held approximately 6:15 PM.

We would also like to ask you to be a sponsor for this event with a donation of $1000.

This sponsorship, along with the merit of doing a great mitzvah, entitles you to 10 complimentary tickets to the concert.

Chabad Lubavitch has made great inroads in it endeavors to bring a little bit of light into the darkness of our times. Without sacrificial support of people such as yourself, we are unable to accomplish our goal. It is dedicated people like you that enable us to touch the lives of thousands in a positive sense.

I will be calling you shortly about this. We hope you will accept this honor and assist in bringing more light into our community.

Your sponsorship will make this Chanukah so special and wonderful; for so many. Your contribution will enable us to bring joy, and spiritual warmth to Jews throughout Brevard and Indian River Counties.

[Signature]
```

---

### Letter Analysis

#### Opening: Build Excitement

**"Sensational program"**
**"Different plateau"**
**"First class entertainment"**

- Sets high expectations
- Major event framing
- Worth their investment

---

#### The Event Description

**Venue:** King Center for The Performing Arts (prestigious)
**Performer:** World renowned Latino-Chassidic-Rock Sensation from Israel
**For Families:** Children's program ("Kid's Paradise")
**Entertainment:** Stilt walker, crafts, contests
**Main Event:** Grand Menorah Lighting ceremony

**Shows:** Professional, comprehensive, worth attending

---

#### The Personal Ask

**"Here's where you come into the picture:"**

- Direct transition
- Makes it personal
- You're part of this

**The Honor:**
- "We have selected 8 friends"
- "Representing the Chanukah candles"
- "To be honored"
- "Come up to the stage"
- "Light a candle"

**The Amount:**
- Clear: $1,000
- Called "sponsorship" not "donation"
- Tied to honor

---

#### The Value Proposition

**10 Complimentary Tickets:**
- Worth significant value
- Can bring family/friends
- Tangible benefit
- Share the experience

**Merit of Mitzvah:**
- Spiritual benefit
- Part of mission
- Making difference

**Public Honor:**
- Stage recognition
- Everyone sees
- Immortalized in program
- Social capital

---

#### Mission Framing

**Not Just Event:**
> "Chabad Lubavitch has made great inroads in it endeavors to bring a little bit of light into the darkness of our times."

**Impact:**
> "Enable us to touch the lives of thousands in a positive sense"

**Scope:**
> "Throughout Brevard and Indian River Counties"

**Shows:** Part of something bigger, lasting impact

---

#### Closing Strategy

**Follow-Up:**
> "I will be calling you shortly about this."

- Not waiting for response
- Personal follow-up
- Serious ask
- Makes it harder to ignore

**Hope Language:**
> "We hope you will accept this honor"

- Honor, not just donation
- Invitation
- Selective

---

## Why This Works

### Psychological Elements

**1. Scarcity**
- Only 8 spots
- Limited opportunity
- Exclusive group
- First-come basis

**2. Public Recognition**
- On stage
- Everyone sees
- Photos in newspaper
- Program listing
- Social status

**3. Elegant Experience**
- Music
- Spotlight
- White tablecloth
- Young girl handing candle
- Like wedding processional

**4. Peer Pressure**
- Other prominent people
- "Everyone who's anyone"
- FOMO for those who say no
- Social proof

**5. Fair Exchange**
- $1,000 gets:
  - Public honor
  - 10 tickets
  - Program listing
  - Recognition
  - Photos
- Not just donation

**6. Personalized Grammen**
- Your name in rhyme
- Tailored compliment
- Creative effort
- Memorable
- Shareable

---

## Implementation Guide

### Step 1: Select Prospects (Week 1)

**Identify 15-20 prospects for 8 spots:**
- Major donors
- Community leaders
- Successful professionals
- Those who value recognition
- Can afford $1,000
- Will attend event

**Why 15-20 for 8:**
- Not everyone will say yes
- Some not available that night
- Over-subscription is fine (add candles!)
- Competition for spots

---

### Step 2: Send Letters (Week 2)

**Personalize Each:**
- Hand-address envelope
- Real signature
- Personal salutation
- Date it

**Include:**
- Event details
- The honor
- The ask
- Response method
- Follow-up notice

---

### Step 3: Follow-Up Calls (Week 3)

**As Promised:**
> "I will be calling you shortly about this"

**Script:**
"Hi [Name], Rabbi [X] calling. I wanted to follow up on the letter I sent about our Chanukah event. Did you have a chance to review it? We'd be honored to have you and [spouse] light one of the candles..."

**Be Ready For:**
- "I need to think about it" → "I understand. Can I answer any questions?"
- "That's a lot" → "It includes 10 tickets, and you'll be honored on stage"
- "Who else is doing this?" → Name 2-3 who committed
- "I'll get back to you" → "Great! I'll check in [specific day]"

---

### Step 4: Write Grammen (Week 4-5)

**For Each Sponsor:**
- Research them
- Find unique angle
- Personal compliment
- Connection to Chanukah theme
- Rhyme with their name (challenging!)

**Tips:**
- Start early (takes time)
- Keep meter consistent
- Test reading aloud
- Make sure names clear
- Practice pronunciation

---

### Step 5: Prepare Ceremony (Week 6)

**Logistics:**
- Choose girl to read grammen
- Practice reading (emotion, timing)
- Choose girl for candle table
- Set up table with white cloth
- Have candles ready
- Test sound system
- Cue music tracks
- Practice lighting timing
- Have printed grammen as backup

---

### Step 6: Execute (Event Night)

**Before Ceremony:**
- Greet all sponsors
- Confirm they're present
- Brief them on process
- "When your name called, come to stage"
- Make sure they feel special

**During Ceremony:**
- Clear audio
- Good lighting
- Spotlight on stage
- Music cued and ready
- Smooth transitions

**After:**
- Thank them personally
- Photo opportunities
- Newspaper/photographer get shots
- Recognition in program

---

## Adaptations

### For Smaller Event

**4 Candles at $500 Each:**
- First 4 nights
- More accessible price
- Still exclusive
- Total: $2,000

---

### For Larger Event

**8 at $1,800 Each (Chai):**
- More prestigious
- Jewish number
- Total: $14,400

---

### For Very Established Community

**8 at $5,000 Each:**
- Major donors only
- Very exclusive
- Ultra-professional production
- Total: $40,000

---

### For Multiple Nights

**8 Sponsors Per Night:**
- Night 1: 8 sponsors
- Night 2: 8 different sponsors
- Etc.
- Spreads opportunity
- More revenue

---

## Additional Resources

### Corporate Sponsorship Proposals

**Initial Question from Forum:**
> "Does anyone have a proposal that they made for an event at a JCC or asking a Foundation to sponsor an event? I would like to see how it is formatted and the language used."

**Available:**
Chanukah Event Corporate Sponsorship Proposal Example
http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/article.html?h=751&o=2893636

---

### Joint Community Events

**Also Asked:**
> "In addition, has anyone had experience making a joint community Chanukah event? (e.g. different communities making a branch on a menorah)"

**Interesting Concept:**
- Multiple Chabad houses
- Each lights branch
- Unity theme
- Shared resources

---

### Full Materials Package

**8 Sponsors - Candle Lighting Idea - PDFs and Files**
http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/article.html?h=1821&o=2084085

**Includes:**
- Sample letters
- Complete grammen
- Program handouts
- Audio tracks
- Photos

---

## Financial Analysis

### Revenue

**8 Sponsors at $1,000:** $8,000

**If Oversubscribed (13 sponsors as in example):** $13,000

---

### Costs Against This

**10 Tickets per Sponsor:**
- 8 sponsors × 10 tickets = 80 tickets
- If tickets are $20: $1,600 in lost revenue
- But tickets to your own event = minimal real cost

**Candles/Setup:**
- Minimal
- Candles: $50
- Table setup: nominal
- Printing grammen: $10

**Staff Time:**
- Writing grammen: significant but one-time
- Recruiting sponsors: would do anyway
- Setup: minimal incremental

---

### Net Impact

**Financial:**
- $8,000-13,000 revenue
- Minus ~$2,000 in ticket value
- Minus ~$100 in direct costs
- Net: $6,000-11,000

**Plus Intangibles:**
- Donor cultivation
- Prestige of event
- Community buzz
- Future major gifts
- Those who wished they sponsored

---

## Keys to Success

### 1. Make It Special

**Not just:**
- "Come light a candle for $1,000"

**But:**
- Prestigious event
- Professional production
- Music and spotlight
- Personal grammen
- Elegant presentation
- Feel like royalty

---

### 2. Fair Value Exchange

**$1,000 Gets:**
- Public honor
- 10 tickets ($200+ value)
- Recognition
- Photos
- Personal grammen
- Part of major event

---

### 3. Social Proof

**"Who else is doing this?"**
- Name respected community members
- Show it's prestigious
- Create FOMO
- Peer influence

---

### 4. Limited Availability

**Only 8 Spots:**
- Creates urgency
- Makes it exclusive
- Selective honor
- First-come basis

---

### 5. Professional Execution

**Don't Cut Corners:**
- Good music system
- Spotlight
- Printed program
- Girl elegantly dressed
- Practice the ceremony
- Smooth production

**Worth Investment:**
- People paid $1,000
- Expect professional
- Can't look cheap
- They're watching

---

**Bottom Line:**
This elegant 8-candle sponsorship program raised $13,000+ for Chanukah concert by honoring donors with stage candle-lighting ceremony featuring personalized rhyming grammen, spotlight, music ("There's a Light" and "Candles"), and refined presentation with young girl elegantly handing candles from white-tableclothed table. The result: "couples felt like a million bucks...walked like going down aisle to their wedding" and crucially "first time balebatim who didn't respond really felt left out"—creating powerful FOMO for future years. The winning invitation letter frames $1,000 as "sponsorship" (not donation) honoring them as one of "8 friends representing Chanukah candles" plus 10 complimentary concert tickets and "merit of great mitzvah." Grammen structure: 4-6 rhyming lines connecting Chanukah themes (Maccabees, light from darkness, miracles) to personal compliments, ending with couple's names and call to stage. Success psychology: scarcity (only 8 spots), public recognition, fair value exchange ($1,000 = honor + tickets + recognition), social proof (prominent community members), and professional execution (music, spotlight, elegant touches). Implementation: identify 15-20 prospects for 8 spots, send personalized letters, follow-up calls as promised, write tailored grammen (most time-consuming), practice ceremony, execute flawlessly. Adaptable: 4 candles at $500 for smaller events, 8 at $1,800 (chai) for established communities, or multiple nights with 8 sponsors each. Net revenue $6-11K after ticket value, plus intangible donor cultivation. Complete materials package with sample letters, full grammen, audio tracks available on Shluchim Exchange.

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Menorah Purchasing and Power Sources Guide

## Vendor Comparison and Power Solutions for Public Menorahs

**Purpose:** Practical guide for purchasing menorahs and solving power challenges

**Sources:** Shluchim Exchange forum discussions and vendor comparisons

---

## Menorah Vendors

### Main Suppliers

**1. Light Up Menorah**
- Website: https://lightupmenorah.com/
- Features: Aluminum holder + tiki torch canister

**2. Public Menorahs**
- Website: https://www.publicmenorahs.com/
- Features: Tiki torch compatible, steel construction

**3. Corporate Menorah**
- Website: http://www.corporatemenorah.com/
- Features: 9 switches (individual control)

**4. Menorah.net**
- Website: https://www.menorah.net/
- Features: Aluminum construction, automated controller, tiki torch conversion kit

---

## Vendor Comparison

### Price Question

**Forum Discussion:**
> "Why are 6' menorahs on menorah.net *double the price* of publicmenorah.com ??"

---

### Material Differences

**Menorah.net:**
- Material: Aluminum
- Lighter weight
- More compact
- Easier to move around

**PublicMenorahs.com:**
- Material: Steel
- Stronger construction
- Heavier
- More difficult to move
- Tiki torch compatible

> "Menorah.net is aluminum and publicmenorahs.com is steel"

---

### Feature Comparison

**Menorah.net Advantages:**
- Lighter weight
- More portable
- Compact storage
- **Menorah Controller** (automatic/manual control)
  - Can manually set number of bulbs lit
  - Auto function available
  - Set time, next bulb turns on after 24 hours
- Tiki torch conversion kit available

**PublicMenorahs.com Advantages:**
- Stronger construction
- More durable
- Tiki torch compatible (direct)
- Lower price point
- BUT: 6ft model **doesn't have individual switches** for each night
  - Can manually add new bulb each night

**Corporate Menorah:**
- **9 switches** (full individual control)
- One switch per candle + shamash
- Maximum flexibility

---

### Shaliach Experience

> "We have some from each. Menorah.net ones are lighter, more compact and easier to move around. The ones from public menorahs seem to be stronger but are a little heavier and more difficult to move around."

**Decision Factors:**
- Portability vs. durability
- Need for individual switches
- Price sensitivity
- Storage constraints
- Transportation method

---

## Power Source Options

### Overview

**Four Main Solutions:**
1. LED/Solar (rechargeable)
2. Battery (car batteries)
3. Generator
4. Street lamps (existing infrastructure)

---

## Option 1: LED Rechargeable or Solar

### Modern Solution

**Types:**
- LED chargeable bulbs
- TomCare solar lights
- Solar generator system

**Availability:**
> "Shlichus market will be selling"

**Advantages:**
- No fuel needed
- Environmentally friendly
- "Green menorah" marketing angle
- No noise
- Low maintenance

**Marketing:**
> "A solar generator is also cool and you can promote that is a green Menorah"

**Pitch:**
> "It's an expense tho, but if you have a green baalhabotim can be a good pitch :)"

**Considerations:**
- Initial expense higher
- Solar requires sun exposure
- Rechargeable needs daily charging
- Weather dependent (solar)

---

## Option 2: Car Batteries

### Popular Choice

**Why Car Batteries:**
> "Car batteries sound the most shayech"

**Requirements:**

**A. Low-Watt LED Bulbs**
- Get from Walmart
- 4W LED bulbs available
- Essential for battery life

**B. Voltage Conversion**
- Car batteries: 12V
- Most menorahs: 120V
- **Need an inverter**

**C. Professional Installation**
> "Get an electrician to do it"

**Electrical Work Needed:**
- Merge cables
- Ensure outdoor-safe
- Proper weatherproofing
- Safety considerations

**Maintenance:**
> "You might need to switch out the battery a few times over Chanukah"

**Planning:**
- Multiple batteries
- Charging rotation
- Replacement schedule
- Monitoring system

---

## Option 3: Generator

### Reliable But Noisy

**Advantages:**
> "A generator is heavy but it is worth it's weight in gold in some places"

---

### Sizing the Generator

**Calculate Wattage:**
- 9 bulbs at 75 watts each = 675 watts
- Add any spotlights
- Get generator with **significantly more capacity**
- Advertised number = peak, not idle
- Build in safety margin

**Example:**
- 675 watts for bulbs
- 200 watts for spotlights
- Total: 875 watts
- **Get 1500-2000 watt generator** (safety margin)

---

### Noise Management

**The Problem:**
> "It makes a lot of noise"

**Solution:**
- Place far from event area
- Use long extension cord
- At least during actual ceremony
- Distance reduces noise

**Alternative:**
> "You can get electric generators that are almost inaudible"

**Investment Worth It:**
- Quieter models more expensive
- But worth it for events
- Professional atmosphere
- Can hear speakers/music

---

### Security

**Critical:**
> "Make sure to chain it to something that won't move"

**Why:**
- Expensive equipment
- Theft target
- Public location
- Overnight exposure

**How:**
- Heavy chain
- Lock to immovable object
- Visible security
- Consider enclosure

---

### Fuel Management

**Buy Adequate Gas Cans:**
> "Buy gas cans big enough to fill it (you'll probably/certainly need to refill each night)"

**Planning:**
- Check tank capacity
- Calculate burn rate
- Buy sufficient cans
- Know nearby gas stations
- Schedule refueling
- Never let it run out

**Storage:**
- Safe fuel storage
- Away from flames
- Proper containers
- Fire code compliance

---

## Option 4: Street Lamps

### Hidden Power Source

**Surprising Discovery:**
> "In several places I've been there have been outlets in the street lamps, either exposed, or under a screwed panel."

**Where to Look:**
- Street lamp bases
- Exposed outlets
- Screwed panels
- Maintenance access points

---

### How to Use

**The Approach:**
> "I don't know if this will help you, but just putting it out there, look around to see if it's there."

**If You Find It:**
> "If you see it and use it, usually no one will ask questions"

**If Under Panel:**
- Someone working there nearby
- Ask with "breitkeit" (casualness)
- "Are you the one who knows how to open this?"
- "We need to use it for our menorah display"
- "Uchedomeh" (and so on - friendly approach)

---

### Legitimacy

**When on Public Property:**
- City/county menorah
- Public display
- Minimal electricity use
- Community benefit
- Usually okay

**Best Practice:**
- Ask permission if possible
- Know who to contact
- Have approval in writing
- Offer to pay minimal fee

---

## Power Source Decision Matrix

### Choose Based On:

**For Portable/Temporary:**
- Battery or solar (lightweight)
- Move between locations
- No infrastructure

**For Established Location:**
- Generator (reliable)
- Can secure properly
- Don't mind noise
- Or find street lamp outlet

**For Professional Events:**
- Quiet generator
- Or street lamp if available
- Battery backup
- Professional appearance

**For "Green" Marketing:**
- Solar generator
- Environmentally friendly
- Appeals to certain donors
- Modern image

**For Budget-Conscious:**
- Car batteries + inverter
- Street lamp (if available)
- Initial investment lower
- DIY approach

---

## Additional Components

### Giant Menorah Conversion Kit

**For Adding Flames to Electric:**
- Available from Shlichus Market
- Converts electric menorah to flame-capable
- Maintains both options

**Link:**
https://www.shlichusmarket.com/holiday-supplies/chanukah/candle-lighting-kit.html

---

### Menorah Sign

**Branding/Identification:**
- Professional signage
- Chabad identification
- Event information

**Available:**
https://www.shlichusmarket.com/holiday-supplies/chanukah/menorahsign.html

---

## Construction Resources

### DIY Building Plans

**For Custom Builds:**
- Car menorah drawings
- 6ft menorah from wood plans
- Step-by-step instructions

**Link:**
http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/article.html?h=785&o=2834849#

---

## Buying Checklist

### Before Purchasing

**Determine Needs:**
- [ ] Size required (height)
- [ ] Material preference (aluminum vs. steel)
- [ ] Portability requirements
- [ ] Storage space available
- [ ] Individual switch control needed?
- [ ] Indoor or outdoor?
- [ ] Budget constraints

---

### Compare Options

**Features to Compare:**
- [ ] Price
- [ ] Weight
- [ ] Material (durability)
- [ ] Switch configuration
- [ ] Flame/electric/both
- [ ] Assembly required
- [ ] Warranty
- [ ] Shipping costs

---

### Power Planning

**Before Event:**
- [ ] Power source identified
- [ ] Backup power available
- [ ] Testing completed
- [ ] Fuel/batteries purchased
- [ ] Extension cords adequate
- [ ] Weather protection planned
- [ ] Security measures in place

---

## Pro Tips from Forum

### Individual Switches Matter

**If No Individual Switches:**
> "The 6ft from public menorahs doesn't have individual switches for each night...You could have someone add a new bulb each night if you want though"

**Considerations:**
- Manual bulb changes
- Access to menorah
- Daily maintenance
- Consistency challenge

**Alternative:**
- Get model with switches
- Or automated controller
- Worth extra cost if remote location

---

### Weight vs. Strength Trade-Off

**Experience:**
- Aluminum: easier setup/takedown
- Steel: better for permanent/semi-permanent
- If moving daily: aluminum
- If staying put: steel's strength worth it

---

### Controller Technology

**Menorah.net Controller:**
- Auto-advance feature
- Set it and forget it
- 24-hour timer
- Reduces daily visits
- Worth investment for remote locations

**WiFi Smart Switches:**
> "If there is wifi available, I think Home Depot has now lights that you can turn on and off from your smart phone anywhere"

**Modern Solution:**
- Remote control
- From anywhere
- Monitor status
- Troubleshoot remotely
- Multiple locations manageable

---

## Budget Examples

### Low Budget Setup

**Equipment:**
- Used menorah or DIY build: $200-500
- Car battery + inverter: $100-200
- LED bulbs (4W): $30
- Extension cord: $20
- **Total: $350-750**

---

### Mid-Range Setup

**Equipment:**
- PublicMenorahs.com 6ft steel: $800-1200
- Small generator: $300-500
- Gas cans + fuel: $50-100
- Security chain: $30
- **Total: $1,180-1,830**

---

### Premium Setup

**Equipment:**
- Menorah.net aluminum with controller: $1,500-2,500
- Quiet generator: $800-1,200
- Professional installation: $200-500
- Solar/battery backup: $500-800
- **Total: $3,000-5,000**

---

### Green/Solar Setup

**Equipment:**
- Menorah with LED: $1,000-1,500
- Solar generator system: $1,500-3,000
- Solar panels: $500-1,000
- Battery bank: $300-600
- **Total: $3,300-6,100**

**But:** Marketing value, donor appeal, modern image

---

## Maintenance Considerations

### Daily Checks

**Essential:**
- Power source functioning
- Bulbs all working
- Security intact
- Weather protection adequate
- Fuel level (if generator)
- Battery charge (if battery)

---

### Weather Protection

**All Power Sources:**
- Waterproof connections
- Covered generator
- Battery protection
- Extension cord safety
- GFCI outlets

---

### End of Season

**Storage:**
- Clean menorah
- Store in dry place
- Drain generator
- Charge batteries fully before storage
- Document any issues
- Note for next year

---

## Safety First

### Electrical Safety

**Requirements:**
- Outdoor-rated components
- GFCI protection
- Proper grounding
- No frayed wires
- Professional installation for complex setups

---

### Fire Safety

**Considerations:**
- No combustibles near menorah
- Generator ventilation
- Fuel storage safety
- Fire extinguisher nearby
- Emergency contacts posted

---

### Security

**Protect Investment:**
- Chain generator
- Lock menorah if removable
- Lighting for visibility
- Check regularly
- Insurance coverage

---

## Vendor Contact Strategy

### Before Ordering

**Questions to Ask:**
1. Warranty coverage?
2. Return policy?
3. Shipping time/cost?
4. Assembly required?
5. Replacement parts availability?
6. Volume discount?
7. Payment terms?
8. Previous Chabad customers (references)?

---

### Multiple Menorahs

**If Buying Several:**
- Negotiate volume discount
- Coordinate delivery
- Stagger sizes/types
- Share shipping
- Bulk replacement parts

---

## Decision Helper

### Quick Assessment

**Answer These:**
1. How far from power source? → Affects cable/generator choice
2. How often accessed? → Affects automation need
3. Budget limit? → Narrows options
4. Portability need? → Aluminum vs. steel
5. Noise sensitivity? → Quiet generator or battery
6. Environmental messaging? → Solar option
7. Technical capability? → DIY vs. turnkey

---

**Bottom Line:**
Four main menorah vendors serve different needs: Menorah.net offers lightweight aluminum with automated controller (double price but premium features), PublicMenorahs.com provides durable steel construction at lower cost (but 6ft model lacks individual switches), Corporate Menorah has 9 individual switches for maximum control, and Light Up Menorah specializes in aluminum holder + tiki torch combinations. Power solutions include: (1) LED rechargeable/solar for green marketing and quiet operation ("if you have green baalhabotim can be good pitch"); (2) car batteries with inverter (12V to 120V conversion, use 4W LED bulbs from Walmart, need electrician for outdoor-safe installation, swap batteries periodically); (3) generator for reliability (calculate 675W for 9x75W bulbs plus spotlights, get significantly higher capacity, chain to immovable object, buy large gas cans for nightly refills, place far away due to noise or invest in "almost inaudible" models); (4) street lamp outlets as hidden power source ("usually no one will ask questions," look for exposed or panel-covered outlets, ask worker "are you the one who knows how to open this?"). Material trade-off: aluminum lighter/more portable but steel stronger/more durable. Key features: Menorah.net controller auto-advances bulbs every 24 hours (worth it for remote locations), WiFi smart switches enable smartphone control from anywhere, individual night switches critical unless manually changing bulbs daily. Budget range $350 (DIY + car battery) to $6,100 (solar generator system). Choose based on portability needs, noise sensitivity, budget, technical capability, and environmental messaging goals.

## What to Expect in Plans

**Bottom Line:**
Free DIY building plans available on Shluchim Exchange for both car menorah (mobile/parade use) and 6-foot wooden menorah (permanent/semi-permanent installation). Building your own offers significant cost savings ($250-500 materials vs. $800-2,500 commercial), complete customization (size, style, materials), and community engagement opportunity (volunteer build day, skill sharing, team bonding). Wood menorah requires basic carpentry skills (measuring, cutting, drilling, finishing) and takes 3-4 days including finishing/drying time. Car menorah needs mechanical and electrical skills for secure vehicle mounting, wind-resistant design, and safe attachment that won't shift while driving. Typical materials for wood version: 4x4 posts, 2x4 boards, plywood, hardware, paint/sealant ($250-400 total). Safety critical for both construction (eye protection, proper tools) and installation (stable base, weather resistance, public codes). Consider group build project for faster completion, shared skills/costs, and educational value. Document with photos and notes for improvements next year. Alternative if DIY not feasible: borrow, rent, buy used, or start small and upgrade later—but DIY investment pays off in subsequent years through reuse with only minor repairs needed.

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Electric Public Menorah: All 8 Lights vs. Progressive Lighting

## Major Halachic and Practical Debate Among Shluchim

**Question:** Do you keep all 8 menorah lights on for all 8 days, or turn on additional light each night?

**Forum Topic:** Surprisingly contentious discussion revealing deep philosophical differences

---

## The Original Question

> "I would like to see a consensus from shluchim if they keep all 8 lights on for all the nights of Chanukah or do they make a point of turning an additional light on for each night."

**Simple question, complex answers**

---

## Perspective 1: MUST Light Correct Number Each Night

### The Confusion Argument

**Real-World Problem:**
> "I missed flicking the switch one night, and someone contacted me all confused about which night it was and how many candles to light, because they saw our menorah....hopefully this helps answer your question."

**Impact:**
- People rely on public menorah
- Use it to know which night
- How many to light at home
- Wrong number = confusion

---

### The Educational Role

**Clarity Required:**
> "When you have a Menorah with four lights on the fifth night of Chanukah you are confusing people."

**Responsibility:**
- Public menorah teaches
- Shows correct practice
- Models behavior
- Educational tool

---

### Strong Reactions

**Response to Question:**
> "Personally this question is very surprising."

**Implication:** Should be obvious that correct number each night

---

### The Carter Story

**Referenced Multiple Times:**
> "What the Rebbe told Avremel when President Carter asked him to light all the candles before the last night of Chanukah!!!"

**Rebbe's Position:**
- Asked to light all 8 for Carter
- **Rebbe was upset**
- Even for President
- Even on small menorah
- Not many would see
- **Still wrong**

**Conclusion:** If Rebbe opposed even in that scenario, certainly for public menorahs

---

## Perspective 2: All 8 Lights Always Acceptable

### The Decoration Distinction

**Different Purpose:**
> "When you have a Menorah which from a week before Chanukah is on the outside ledge of a bank overlooking a big intersection but you cant access it every night of Chanukah, so from a week before it just has all eight light bulbs lit for Pirsumei Nisa no one is getting confused."

**Key Points:**
- Inaccessible locations
- Up before Chanukah starts
- Clearly decoration
- Pirsumei nisa (publicity)
- Context makes it clear

---

### Not Confusing in All Contexts

**Manhattan Example:**
> "Every storefront in Manhattan has it already and no one is lighting Menorah on tes kislev because of it."

**Argument:**
- All 8 lit before Chanukah
- No one confused
- Context matters
- People understand decoration

---

### Practical Limitations

**Shaliach's Challenge:**
> "If you have multiple menorahs around town with a long travel time between them, how do you ensure that every Jew that sees the different Menorahs will be up to date on the correct night?"

**Questions:**
- Multiple locations
- Long travel times
- Can't reach all nightly
- No volunteers available
- No fancy timer system

**Follow-Up:**
> "If you cannot ensure that the lights are up to date on the proper night - and therefore resort to having all eight on for the duration of Chanukah - should you not put up those menorahs?"

**Implication:** Better some pirsumei nisa than none?

---

### The Decoration Theory

**Motti Wilhelm's Suggestion:**
> "Perhaps there is an advantage to lighting all eighth bulbs of a electric menorah to show that it is only for decoration but not a fulfillment of the mitzvah."

**Logic:**
- All 8 lit = clearly not real lighting
- Shows it's symbolic
- No one thinks they're yotzei
- Avoids confusion about obligation

---

## Technology Solutions

### Automated Controllers

**Klar Menorah Feature:**
> "The new klar menorahs have an option to have the lights go on every night"

**Link:** http://www.menorah.net/home

**Capabilities:**
- Automatic progression
- Timer-based
- 24-hour cycles
- Set and forget

**Retrofit Question:**
> "I asked him if it is possible to retrofit and he said he cant, but someone did buy from him the mother board and had someone do it"

**Note:** Possible but requires technical work

---

### WiFi Smart Switches

> "If there is wifi available, I think Home Depot has now lights that you can turn on and off from your smart phone anywhere"

**Modern Solution:**
- Remote control
- From anywhere
- Multiple locations manageable
- Real-time adjustments
- Check status remotely

---

### Alternative Solutions

> "Also, you can appoint a cheresh koton or nochri to switch it on if you cant make it....  *they will be honored*"

**Delegation:**
- Minor (cheresh koton)
- Non-Jew (nochri)
- They feel honored
- Solves access problem
- Halachically acceptable

---

## The Real Menorah Debate

### Deeper Question: Electric vs. Real Flames

**Historical Context:**
> "Lgufo shel inyan of electric Menorahs I wonder if there were electric Menoras before 3 Tamuz and if they were approved."

---

### Geographic Variation

**New York vs. Texas:**
> "It is interesting that when we grew up in NY all windows had electric Menorahs, when I came on shlichus to Texas I didn't see any, if people lit they lit at home inside -real candles"

**Cultural Differences:**
- NY: electric window displays common
- Texas: real candles only
- Regional practices vary
- Community expectations differ

---

### Fire Safety Reality

**Modern Challenges:**
> "Today everyone is concerned with fire hazards and it is very hard to light indoors public candles"

**City Hall Example:**
> "I was told by those in charge of our city hall that the sensors inside are so sensitive that if I would light a candle it will pick up (put on sprinklers? ver vaist)"

**Practical Reality:**
- Insurance issues
- Fire codes
- Sensor sensitivity
- Sprinkler systems
- Indoor real flames often impossible

---

### The Fundamental Question

> "Does anyone remember the first car Menorahs???? they were not electric...."

> "So back to the original question... is electric public menorahs pirsumei nisa and really part of the Rebbes campaign? If you will say yes, then you need to do it right, if not you are not bound."

**Core Issue:**
- Are electric menorahs legitimate?
- Part of Rebbe's campaign?
- If yes: do it correctly (progressive lighting)
- If no: not obligated

---

## The "Real Flames Only" Position

### Rabbi Levitansky's Father's Approach

**Strict Standards:**
> "My father A''H was very makpid that ALL of the public Menorahs should have a flame and should be lit with a Brocho every night."

**Implementation:**
- Bank chain agreement
- Special candle lanterns
- Fire proof tape
- Safety lid (extinguishes if tips)
- Real flames only

**Scale:**
> "As of today I believe my siblings already light sixty+ Menorahs throughout Santa Monica, in supermarkets or on street corners etc."

**Logistics Challenge:**
> "As you can imagine it is not easy to run around every night lighting 40/50 Menorahs and we needed a lot of extra bochurim and volunteers from the community"

---

### The Philosophy

**Father's Argument:**
> "His main argument was that especially now when people think you can be 'yotze' with electric we need to show them the correct way to do it."

**Concern:**
- Electric menorahs mislead people
- Think they fulfill obligation
- Need to model real flames
- Educational imperative

---

### The Michshol Concern

**Model Matzah Bakery:**
> "(BTW he felt the same way about the Model Matza bakery because he would get calls from people asking for the recipe etc. and he felt that it a 'michshol')."

**Principle:**
- Educational programs can mislead
- People might do it wrong at home
- Better not to do than to cause michshol
- Applies to electric menorahs too

---

### Continuous Expansion

> "In the spirit of 'malin bakodesh' he would find at least one new place to light a Menorah every year."

**Growth Philosophy:**
- Add locations annually
- Never reduce
- Constantly expanding
- "Malin bakodesh" (ascend in holiness)

---

## Counter-Arguments

### Context is Everything

**Response to Strict View:**
> "Mah Hakesher as an answer to the question? When you have a Menorah with four lights on the fifth night of Chanukah you are confusing people. When you have a Menorah which from a week before Chanukah is on the outside ledge of a bank...for Pirsumei Nisa no one is getting confused."

**Distinction:**
- Wrong number during Chanukah = confusing
- All 8 before/after or inaccessible = decoration
- Context makes it clear
- Not comparable situations

---

### Questioning the Standard

> "Most poskim hold electricity (incandescent and not fluorescent, obviously) is fine for any candle mitzvah, even with a brachah, like for shabbos candles. Check with your Rov."

**Halachic View:**
- Many poskim permit electric
- With bracha even
- Shabbos candles example
- Not fringe position

---

### Model Matzah Challenge

> "Did your father not do ANY Model Matzah Bakeries because of the chashash that someone might think they can bake matzah at home?"

**Question:**
- Consistent application?
- Many Shluchim do model bakeries
- Similar michshol concern
- Why different?

---

## Technical Issues

### Klar Menorah with Power Interruptions

**Real Problem:**
> "I have one displayed at my city hall where the electricity shuts off during the day. When this happens the programming on the menorah resets it self making the settings useless."

**Solution Attempt:**
> "This year I will try to attach the menorah to car battery that is hooked up to an outlet."

**Lesson:**
- Technology not always reliable
- Power interruptions reset
- Need constant power
- Battery backup essential
- Test before relying on automation

---

## Summary of Positions

### Position A: Progressive Lighting Required

**Advocates:**
- Must show correct number each night
- Educational responsibility
- People get confused otherwise
- Rebbe opposed all-8 for Carter
- If doing it, do it right

**Best For:**
- Accessible locations
- Daily visits feasible
- Main community menorah
- Where people watch to learn

---

### Position B: All 8 Acceptable

**Advocates:**
- Inaccessible locations justify
- Clearly decoration if all lit
- Practical limitations real
- Some pirsumei nisa better than none
- Context prevents confusion

**Best For:**
- Remote locations
- Multiple menorahs can't all visit
- Pre-Chanukah displays
- Clearly decorative contexts

---

### Position C: Real Flames Only

**Advocates:**
- Electric misleads people
- Need to model correct way
- Extra effort worth it
- Educational imperative
- Halachic preference

**Challenges:**
- Extremely labor-intensive
- Fire safety issues
- Insurance problems
- Indoor limitations
- Need many volunteers

---

## Practical Recommendations

### Decision Framework

**Ask Yourself:**

**1. Can you access daily?**
- Yes → Progressive lighting
- No → Consider all 8 or don't do

**2. Is it main community menorah?**
- Yes → Progressive lighting essential
- No → More flexibility

**3. Do people watch to learn?**
- Yes → Correct number matters
- No → Less critical

**4. Fire safety allows real flames?**
- Yes → Consider real flames
- No → Electric only option

**5. Have volunteers/technology?**
- Yes → Progressive possible
- No → All 8 or automation

---

### Best Practices

**For Progressive Lighting:**
- Visit daily without fail
- Have backup person
- Use automation if available
- Check it's working
- Monitor remotely if possible

**For All-8 Display:**
- Put up before Chanukah
- Clearly decorative
- Don't call it "menorah lighting"
- Maybe add sign: "Chanukah decoration"
- Consider not doing if confusing

**For Real Flames:**
- Recruit volunteers
- Safety equipment
- Insurance coverage
- Fire department notification
- Backup plan for bad weather

---

## Unanswered Questions from Thread

**When to Light Electric Menorah Each Night:**
> "If you have an electric public menorah, and you are lighting a new bulb every night - by what time should you light it and it will not confuse people? Plag? Shkia? Tzeis?"

**No consensus reached**

**Multiple Menorahs Coordination:**
- How ensure all updated?
- Long travel times
- Timing considerations
- Best practices?

**Still debated**

---

## Tone of Discussion

### Contentious

**Notable:**
> "However, unfortunately we wont be finding out if anyone does differently as some on this forum feel this question is out of line even to be discussed and thus prevent others from sharing their views. Shame"

**Indication:**
- Strong feelings
- Some feel shouldn't even discuss
- Others frustrated by this
- No easy consensus
- Personal practices vary

---

### Respectful Disagreement

**But Also:**
- Multiple perspectives shared
- Stories from different approaches
- Learning from each other
- Acknowledging practical challenges
- Seeking to understand

---

**Bottom Line:**
Major unresolved debate among Shluchim about electric public menorahs: progressive lighting (correct number each night) vs. all 8 lights continuously. Progressive camp argues people rely on public menorah to know which night ("someone contacted me all confused"), educational responsibility requires correct display, and Rebbe opposed lighting all 8 for President Carter even on small menorah few would see—if wrong then, certainly wrong for public displays. All-8 camp counters that inaccessible locations (bank window, multiple remote sites) with all lights before Chanukah starts creates decorative context where "no one is lighting menorah on tes kislev"—people understand it's symbolic, and practical reality of multiple locations with long travel times makes daily visits impossible without many volunteers. Technology solutions include Klar menorah automated controller (advances every 24 hours) and WiFi smart switches (control from smartphone anywhere), but power interruptions reset programming. Deeper debate: are electric menorahs legitimate at all? Rabbi Levitansky's father insisted ALL public menorahs use real flames with bracha ("especially now when people think you can be yotzei with electric we need to show correct way"), requiring 60+ nightly visits across Santa Monica with many volunteers. Modern reality: fire codes, insurance, sensitive sprinkler sensors make indoor real flames often impossible. No consensus reached. Decision framework: if daily access feasible and main community menorah where people watch to learn, progressive lighting essential; if remote/inaccessible with clearly decorative context, all-8 more defensible; if fire safety permits, real flames preferable but extremely labor-intensive. Thread tone contentious with some feeling question "out of line even to be discussed," others frustrated by this suppression of dialogue.


---
**End of Document 92**

ACLU case), 077 (secular vs. religious framing debate), 078 (Nathan Lewin letter samples), 079 (quotable Supreme Court excerpts), 081 (real-time county vote advice). Organize your own local legal kit with court ruling, key excerpts, attorney letter templates, case summaries, and your city's approval documents. Share strategically with officials—start with one-page summary, provide details if requested, don't overwhelm. Get professional attorney help if facing litigation, high-stakes precedent-setting case, or unclear legal ground; Nathan Lewin is specialist frequently mentioned, plus Becket Fund, First Liberty, ACLJ. Document everything (requests, responses, correspondence, notes) to build case history and help future efforts. Remember distinction between legal right (constitutional protection, theoretical permission) and practical reality (community relationships, long-term presence)—assert rights when necessary but preserve relationships and think strategically. Access this emergency resource if sudden crisis arises, but better to review materials now during preparation phase for confidence and quick response capability when challenged.

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Menorah Lighting at Chanukah Wedding

## Halachic and Practical Guidance for Chanukah Weddings

**Forum Thread:** http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/forum/viewtopic.php?t=57997

**Scenario:** Wedding during Chanukah with mixed Orthodox and not-yet-religious guests

**Questions:** Halacha, timing, and logistics of menorah lighting at wedding

---

## The Question

### From Rabbi Mendy Kivman (Milford, MA)

**Situation:**
- Wedding during Chanukah
- Mixed guests (Modern Orthodox & not-yet-religious)
- Chosson & Kallah want to light menorah at wedding
- Appropriate time during event?

**Three Specific Questions:**

**1. Halachic Permissibility:**
> "Is there any reason (Halacha) not to do it?"

**2. Timing:**
> "When's a good time?"

**3. Under Chupah:**
> "They thought to do it under the Chupah but 'someone' told them that it wasn't good to 'mix one Mitzvah with another'. Any legitimacy to that?"

---

## Response: Halachic Analysis

### From Rabbi Menachem Mendel Greisman (Rogers, AR)

**His Research:**
> "I've done some research about it, as it was noig'ai'a l'maiseh [relevant to actual practice]."

**Assuming:** L'chatchila (ideal situation)

---

## For Guests: Primary Obligation

### Where to Light

**The Rule:**
> "The menorah needs to be lit in your place of 'kvi'us' i.e. your home, and after shkia."

**Kvi'us = Fixed location**
- Your home
- Where you're staying
- Not wedding hall

**Timing:**
- After shkia (sunset)
- Not at hall during day

---

### Timing Question for Guests

**Specific Psak Received:**

**Scenario:**
- Going to wedding after plag (hamincha)
- But before shkia
- Not coming home till very late
- Close to Alos (dawn)

**Psak:**
> "It is better to do it then [close to Alos] (and get some b'nai bayis to be present) rather than after plag."

**Principle:**
- Better late at night at home
- With household members present
- Than early not at home
- Kvi'us (fixed location) matters

---

## For Chosson: Special Status

### Yichud Room as Kvi'us

**What the Chosson Was Told:**

**Psak from 2 Rabbonim:**
> "He should light in the yichud room as that is his 'kvius' for that evening."

**Reasoning:**
- Yichud room = his "place" that evening
- First moments of married life
- Establishes location
- Fulfills obligation properly

**Uncertainty:**
> "I am not sure if he will be in his apartment or not that night, or even if that makes a difference regarding the chosson."

**Questions Remain:**
- If going to apartment after: still yichud room?
- Does chosson's status change the rule?
- Need more clarification

---

### Proper Timing for Chosson

**The Rule:**
> "The proper time to do it is right after shkia, or anytime thereafter, like everyone else."

**No Special Time:**
- Same as everyone
- After sunset
- Standard halacha applies
- No wedding-specific exemption

---

## Lighting in the Wedding Hall

### The "Public Menorah" Question

**Parallel to Shul:**
> "To light a menorah in the hall, is probably also an inyan [worthy thing], I guess it is no worse than a shul where we light l'pirsumai nissa [to publicize the miracle]"

**Especially If:**
> "Certainly if some present will not light in their homes"

**Purpose:**
- Pirsumei nisa (publicizing miracle)
- For those who won't light at home
- Educational moment
- Communal celebration

---

### Can Guests Be Yotzei?

**The Critical Question:**
> "But you should ask a rov if one can be yotze from such a lighting."

**Rabbi's Doubt:**
> "It is very difficult for me to believe that it has more strength then a shul lighting or public lighting."

**Comparison:**
- Shul lighting: don't fulfill obligation
- Public lighting: don't fulfill obligation
- Wedding hall: likely same status

**Request:**
> "If someone got a psak otherwise, I would like to hear that."

**Implication:** Probably NOT yotzei, but confirm with Rov

---

## Under the Chupah Question

### "Mixing Mitzvos" Concern

**The Claim:**
> "'Someone' told them that it wasn't good to 'mix one Mitzvah with another'. Any legitimacy to that?"

**No Direct Answer in Thread**

**But Implied:**
- Timing issue more significant
- Chupah during day usually
- Menorah after shkia
- Timing doesn't work anyway

**Possible Concerns:**
- Focus on wedding mitzvah
- Dilutes each simcha
- Logistical complexity
- Halachic timing conflicts

---

## Other Solutions Mentioned

### Additional Options

**Rabbi Greisman's Note:**
> "There were other solutions that rabbonim offered, you can contact me privately if you wish. Those were complicated some what."

**Indication:**
- Multiple approaches exist
- Some complex
- Case-by-case basis
- Private consultation needed

---

## Practical Recommendations

### Based on This Discussion

**For the Chosson:**
1. Light in yichud room
2. After shkia (sunset)
3. Get psak for your specific situation
4. If going to apartment: clarify with Rov

**For Guests:**
1. Light at home (where staying)
2. After shkia
3. Better very late at home than early elsewhere
4. Don't rely on hall lighting

**In the Wedding Hall:**
1. Can light for pirsumei nisa
2. Good for those not lighting at home
3. Educational moment
4. But guests NOT yotzei
5. Make announcement: must light at home

---

## Timing Scenarios

### Wedding Schedule Options

**Scenario 1: Evening Wedding (After Shkia)**

**Works Well:**
- Chosson lights in yichud room (after shkia)
- Hall menorah during reception (pirsumei nisa)
- Guests go home, light there
- Timing aligns naturally

---

**Scenario 2: Afternoon Wedding (Before Shkia)**

**Challenges:**
- Chupah during day
- Can't light then (before shkia)
- Chosson lights in yichud room later
- Hall lighting during reception (if after shkia)
- Guests must light when get home

---

**Scenario 3: Very Late Wedding**

**Special Case:**
- Wedding goes very late
- Guests staying locally
- Light at accommodation after wedding
- Even if very late (better than not at home)

---

## Under Chupah: Analysis

### Why Probably Not Ideal

**Timing Issues:**
- Chupah often before shkia
- Can't light menorah before shkia
- Would need to wait
- Disrupts flow

**Focus Issues:**
- Each mitzvah deserves focus
- Mixing could diminish both
- Wedding is main simcha
- Menorah separate moment

**Logistical Issues:**
- Chupah already has elements
- Adding more complexity
- Fire safety under chupah?
- Practical concerns

---

### Better Alternatives

**Option 1: Yichud Room**
- Private moment
- Chosson & Kallah together
- First mitzvah as married couple
- Intimate and meaningful
- After shkia timing works

**Option 2: During Reception**
- After shkia
- During dancing or meal
- Brief ceremony
- Emcee announcement
- Educational moment
- Pirsumei nisa for all

**Option 3: Pre-Reception (Cocktail Hour)**
- If after shkia
- Before seated meal
- Guests gathered
- Still casual
- Good timing

---

## Announcements to Make

### If Lighting at Wedding Hall

**Critical Communication:**

> "This menorah lighting is for pirsumei nisa - publicizing the miracle of Chanukah. It does NOT fulfill each person's individual obligation to light menorah at home. Everyone must still light menorah at their place of lodging tonight after sunset."

**Why Important:**
- People might think they're yotzei
- Could skip lighting at home
- Educational responsibility
- Halachic clarity

---

## Special Wedding Considerations

### Making It Meaningful

**For Chosson & Kallah:**
- First Chanukah as married couple
- New home, new menorah
- Symbolic beginning
- Jewish home established
- Beautiful moment

**For Guests:**
- Witness their first lighting
- Share in simcha
- Connect to tradition
- Remember this wedding
- Unique experience

**Photography:**
- Beautiful photo opportunity
- Yichud room moment
- Or reception lighting
- Capture the mitzvah
- Album keepsake

---

## Vendor Coordination

### If Lighting at Reception

**Venue Needs to Know:**
- Fire safety approval
- Location for menorah
- Timing in schedule
- Electrical if needed
- Insurance implications

**Caterer Coordination:**
- Pause service briefly
- Lights dimmed?
- Music stopped
- Respect for moment

**Band/DJ:**
- Cue music after
- Appropriate song
- "Maoz Tzur"?
- Chanukah medley
- Simcha continues

**Photographer:**
- Alert to timing
- Position for good shots
- Close-up and wide
- Candid reactions
- Family photos with menorah

---

## Checklist for Chanukah Wedding

### Planning Considerations

**Months Before:**
- [ ] Consult with Rov
- [ ] Decide: yichud room, reception, or both
- [ ] Get specific psak for chosson
- [ ] Venue fire safety approval
- [ ] Contract includes menorah time

**Weeks Before:**
- [ ] Menorah purchased/arranged
- [ ] Oil/candles ready
- [ ] Timing confirmed in schedule
- [ ] Vendors all notified
- [ ] Announcement script prepared

**Day Of:**
- [ ] Menorah set up in yichud room
- [ ] Oil/candles there
- [ ] Matches/lighter
- [ ] Reception menorah ready (if doing)
- [ ] Emcee has announcement

**After Shkia:**
- [ ] Chosson lights in yichud room
- [ ] Hall lighting (if doing)
- [ ] Announcement made
- [ ] Guests reminded to light at home

---

## For Different Guest Profiles

### Modern Orthodox Guests

**Likely:**
- Understand obligation
- Will light at home
- Appreciate hall lighting
- Educational value less critical

---

### Not-Yet-Religious Guests

**Opportunity:**
- May not light at home
- Hall lighting might be only exposure
- Extra important for pirsumei nisa
- Explanation valuable
- Could inspire them
- Beautiful first impression

**Provide:**
- Brief explanation
- Why we light
- Chanukah story
- Miracle message
- Invitation to try at home

---

## Alternative: Chanukah Theme Throughout

### Beyond Just Lighting

**Enhance Wedding with Chanukah:**
- Dreidels as party favors
- Blue and silver color scheme
- Chanukah gelt at each place
- Menorah centerpieces (LED for safety)
- Chanukah songs in medley
- Doughnut desserts (sufganiyot)
- Latke station
- Theme integrated beautifully

**Benefits:**
- Guests remember it's Chanukah
- More likely to light at home
- Festive atmosphere
- Photos show the season
- Unique wedding
- Double simcha

---

## Regional Considerations

### Vary by Community

**Different Minhagim:**
- Chasidish vs. Litvish
- American vs. Israeli
- Different Chabad communities
- Family traditions

**Consult Local Rov:**
- Know your kehilla's practice
- Follow mesorah
- Ask specific shailos
- Don't assume

---

## Contact for Questions

### From Original Thread

**Rabbi Menachem Mendel Greisman**
- Chabad of Northwest Arkansas
- Website: www.JewishNWA.org
- Phone: 479-631-6770
- Email: Rabbi@JewishNWA.org
- Researched this issue extensively
- Offered additional solutions privately

**Rabbi Mendy Kivman**
- Chabad Center, Milford, MA
- Website: www.LiveKabbalah.com
- Phone: 508-473-1299
- Email: Rabbi@LiveKabbalah.com
- Asked original question

---

## Bottom Line Summary

### The Essentials

**Chosson's Obligation:**
- Light in yichud room
- After shkia
- That's his kvi'us for the evening
- Get specific psak

**Guests' Obligation:**
- Light at their lodging
- After shkia
- NOT yotzei from hall lighting
- Even if late is better than wrong place

**Hall Lighting:**
- Permitted for pirsumei nisa
- Especially for non-observers
- Must announce NOT fulfilling obligation
- Educational moment

**Under Chupah:**
- Not addressed directly
- Timing problems (usually before shkia)
- Focus issues
- Better alternatives exist

**When to Do Hall Lighting:**
- During reception
- After shkia
- Brief ceremony
- Announce clearly
- Then continue simcha

---

**Bottom Line:**
Chanukah wedding menorah lighting requires careful halachic consideration: chosson should light in yichud room (his "kvi'us" that evening per psak from 2 rabbonim) after shkia like everyone else; guests must light at their lodging after shkia—better very late at home than early elsewhere—and are NOT yotzei from hall lighting even though hall lighting permitted for pirsumei nisa especially for those who won't light at home. Lighting under chupah not directly addressed but timing problematic (chupah usually before shkia, can't light menorah before sunset) plus "mixing mitzvos" concern. Best practice: chosson lights privately in yichud room fulfilling obligation, then optional hall lighting during reception after shkia for pirsumei nisa with critical announcement that guests must still light at home. Hall lighting serves educational purpose for not-yet-religious guests ("some present will not light in their homes") but Rabbi Greisman doubts it "has more strength than shul lighting or public lighting" for fulfilling obligation—get specific psak if relying on it. Coordinate with venue for fire safety, vendors for timing, photographer for moment, and prepare announcement script emphasizing individual home lighting obligation. Consider enhancing entire wedding with Chanukah theme (dreidels, doughnut station, blue/silver decor, gelt favors) to inspire guests and create double simcha atmosphere. Consult local Rov for specific situation as "there were other solutions that rabbonim offered...complicated somewhat" requiring case-by-case guidance.

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Purim Video Resources - Quick Reference Links

## Note: Purim Content (Not Chanukah)

**Resource Type:** Collection of online Purim video and activity links

**Format:** WhatsApp message thread

**Date:** March 16, 2022

**Shared by:** [REDACTED-NAME]

---

## Resource Links

### Virtual Purim Megillah

**Link:** http://www.jewishchildren.com/purim/virtual.php

**Description:** Interactive virtual Purim experience for children

**Use Case:**
- Remote learning
- Individual home use
- Classroom supplement
- Technology-based engagement
- Children's program resource

---

### Animated Purim Story

**Link:** https://www.chabadofislip.com/templates/articlecco_cdo/aid/2826585/jewish/The-Animated-Purim-Story.htm

**Format:** zslides (animated slides)

**Source:** Chabad of Islip

**Description:** Complete Purim story in animated slide format

**Use Case:**
- Visual storytelling
- Children's presentation
- Educational program
- Megillah reading supplement
- Pre-school/elementary education
- Engaging young audiences

---

### Pantomime Megillah

**Contact:** sales@chabad.org.il

**Description:** Pantomime (silent dramatic) Megillah presentation

**Acquisition:** Available for purchase/licensing from Chabad Israel

**Use Case:**
- Visual performance art
- Children's theater
- Non-verbal storytelling
- International audiences (language-free)
- Special needs accommodation
- Dramatic interpretation

---

### Sand Art Purim Video

**Link:** http://pidyon.net/purim-video/en-index.html

**Description:** Purim story told through sand art animation

**Format:** Video

**Use Case:**
- Artistic presentation
- Visual engagement
- Mesmerizing storytelling
- Pre-Megillah introduction
- Children's entertainment
- Event screening
- Social media sharing

---

### Personalized Purim Cartoon

**Link:** http://purimvideopersonalized.blogspot.com/

**Description:** Personalized cartoon-style Purim video

**Format:** Custom video with personalized elements

**Use Case:**
- Individual gift
- Special recognition
- Children's engagement
- Unique mishloach manot addition
- Birthday/special occasion
- Fundraising incentive
- Community spotlight

---

## Applications for Shluchim

### Pre-Purim Programming

**Educational:**
- Show in Hebrew school
- CTeen meetings
- Children's programs
- Adult education intro
- Pre-Megillah preparation

**Engagement:**
- Social media content
- Email marketing
- Website resources
- Community outreach

---

### During Purim Events

**For Children:**
- Entertainment between activities
- Quiet activity station
- Individual device viewing
- Take-home links/QR codes

**For Adults:**
- Background display
- Artistic appreciation
- Novel presentation methods
- Discussion starters

---

### Remote/Virtual Programming

**Online Events:**
- Zoom backgrounds
- Screen sharing
- Breakout room activities
- Virtual party entertainment

**Individual Reach:**
- Email to homebound
- Hospital patients
- College students away
- Long-distance community members

---

## Resource Organization

### By Age Group

**Young Children (Ages 3-7):**
- Virtual Purim (jewishchildren.com)
- Animated story (Islip)
- Sand art video

**School Age (Ages 8-13):**
- All resources appropriate
- Personalized cartoon (special treat)

**Teens:**
- Sand art (artistic appreciation)
- Pantomime (performance art)
- Personalized (novelty)

**Adults:**
- Sand art (artistic/meditative)
- Pantomime (theatrical)
- All as educational tools

---

### By Program Type

**Classroom Setting:**
- Animated story
- Virtual Purim
- Sand art video

**Performance/Event:**
- Pantomime Megillah
- Sand art screening
- Combined presentation

**Individual/Gift:**
- Personalized cartoon
- Links in mishloach manot
- QR codes to resources

---

## Technical Requirements

### For Display

**Equipment Needed:**
- Internet connection
- Computer/tablet/phone
- Projector (for groups)
- Speakers
- HDMI cables

**Backup Plans:**
- Download videos beforehand
- Offline alternatives ready
- Technical support person
- Test all links before event

---

### For Sharing

## For Ba'alei Kriah (Megillah Readers)

### Preparation Timeline

**30 Days Before:**
- Begin daily practice
- Use Tikkun for practice
- Focus on difficult sections
- Record yourself reading
- Listen back for errors

**2 Weeks Before:**
- Increase practice frequency
- Practice entire Megillah without stopping
- Time yourself
- Work on speed vs clarity balance
- Review all challenging words

**Week Before:**
- Daily full read-through
- Practice with actual kosher Megillah if possible
- Minimize looking at Tikkun
- Focus on stamina
- Vocal rest when not practicing

**Days Before:**
- Light practice only
- Vocal care (warm liquids, rest)
- Mental preparation
- Review plan for graggers/noise
- Confirm scroll is kosher

---

### Practice Tips

**Using the Tikkun:**
1. Read from side with marks first
2. Cover marked side
3. Read from plain side
4. Check against marked side
5. Repeat problem areas
6. Practice transitioning

**Common Challenges:**
- Similar names (confusing characters)
- Long sentences
- Repeated phrases
- Uncommon words
- Physical stamina (standing, reading aloud)
- Audience noise/graggers

**Solutions:**
- Slow down deliberately
- Mark scroll mentally
- Take brief pauses
- Stay hydrated
- Practice standing up
- Simulate noisy environment

---

**Classes and Workshops:**
- "Understanding the Megillah" series

## Featured Content: "Hadassah and Esther" Class

### Source Information

**Teacher:** [REDACTED-NAME], [REDACTED-LOCATION]

**Posted:** Sun Feb 22, 2015 22:08 pm ET

**Subject:** Long-hand notes to Parsha Class for Tetzaveh - "The Story of Purim: Who is Hadassah and Who is Esther?"

**Based On:** Maamar "Vayehee Uman Es Hadassah," Purim (I), 5713 (1953)

---

### Audio and Notes

**Audio Recording:**
https://soundcloud.com/hachaim/13-the-story-of-purim-esther-and-haddasah

**Written Notes (PDF):**
https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/4614078/13.%20Tetzaveh%20%28Purim%29%205775%20-Parsha%20Class%20and%20Sermon.pdf

**Title:** Shabbos Tetzaveh (Purim) - 5775

---

## Class Content Overview

### Introduction: Two Names, One Person

**Biblical Text:**
> "And he [Mordechai] had brought up Hadassah, that is Esther..." (Esther 2:7)

**Central Question:**
- Why does Esther have two names?
- What is the significance of each name?
- How do these names reflect different aspects of her identity?

---

### Talmudic Interpretations

**Three Explanations (Megillah 13a):**

1. **"Esther was her proper name"**
   - Hadassah: Named after the myrtle
   - Righteous called myrtles
   - Reference: "He stood among the myrtle trees" (Zachariah 1:8)

2. **"Hadassah was her name" (R. Judah)**
   - Esther: From "astir" (concealed)
   - She concealed her identity
   - "Esther did not make known her people or her kindred" (Esther 2:20)

3. **"Hadassah was her name" (R. Nehemiah)**
   - Esther: Nations called her after Istahar (planet Jupiter)
   - Universal appeal
   - How gentiles perceived her

---

### Kabbalistic Framework

#### Sefirat Malchut - The Emanation of Kingship

**Unique Quality:**
- Only emanation that descends to lower world
- First nine emanations remain in their world
- Malchut bridges worlds
- Becomes inner essence of lower world's crown

**Two Dimensions:**
- **Ocean (Yam):** Kingship in its own world, hidden
- **Land (Yabasha):** Kingship revealed in lower world

**Parallel to Esther:**
- **Hadassah:** Kingship in righteous world (G-dliness)
- **Esther:** Kingship concealed in exile

---

### Application to the Soul

#### Israel and Jacob - Head and Heel

**Two Names for Jewish People:**

**Yisroel (Israel):**
- Letters: Yud-Shin-Reish-Aleph-Lamed
- Rearranged: "Li Rosh" = "My Head" / "Unto Me a Head"
- Essence of soul remaining above
- G-dly world connection

**Yaakov (Jacob):**
- From "okev" (heel)
- Ray of soul descending into body
- Physical world manifestation
- Lower level

**Parallel to Hadassah/Esther:**
- Hadassah = Israel = Head = Soul Essence
- Esther = Jacob = Heel = Soul's Ray in Body

---

### Key Message: Unity of Soul

**Biblical Teaching:**
> "Hadassah, that is Esther"

**Meaning:**
- The elevated soul essence (Hadassah)
- IS ONE WITH
- The soul's ray in the body (Esther)
- Not separate or disconnected
- Complete unity despite levels

**Practical Implication:**
- Even in lowest state (exile/body)
- Soul retains connection to essence
- G-dliness present always
- No true separation from G-d

---

## Three Loves of Shema

### Framework from "Shema Yisrael"

**"Love G-d with all your heart, soul, and might"**

Three types of love:

---

### 1. Love of the Heart

**Based On:**
- Understanding how G-d fills the world
- G-d is the life of creation
- Meditation on G-d as source of existence

**Result:**
- Love G-d for being my life
- Closeness through understanding
- G-d immanent in creation

**Level:** Light of Esther (revealed, based on creation)

---

### 2. Love of the Soul

**Based On:**
- Understanding G-d's infinite magnitude
- All creation is tiny ray of Infinite Light
- G-d infinitely transcends creation

**Result:**
- Willing to sacrifice physical life
- Love for Infinite transcends love for finite
- Mesirut nefesh (self-sacrifice)

**Level:** Still Light of Esther (related to creation)

---

### 3. Love "With All Your Might"

**Based On:**
- Focus transcends creation entirely
- Direct perception of G-d's Essence
- Core of G-dly Soul (Spark of Creator)
- Beyond understanding or meditation

**Result:**
- Pure love from soul's essence
- Not dependent on intellectual comprehension
- Innate connection to G-d

**Level:** Light of Hadassah (soul's essence)

---

## Exile and Concealment

### When Lights Are Extinguished

**In Times of Exile:**
- Light of G-d concealed
- Difficult to perceive G-dliness
- Both Love of Esther and Love of Hadassah seem unavailable
- Darkness magnified by indulgence in physical desires

**Human Condition:**
- Egocentric pleasure-seeking
- Disconnection from spirituality
- Loss of revealed love
- Spiritual darkness

---

### Beyond Light: Potency of Soul

**Deeper Than Light:**
- Light = Revealed, felt, experienced
- Potency = Latent, hidden, unfelt
- True Esther experience = Potency

**Potency of Soul:**
- Capacity for total self-sacrifice
- Not driven by understanding or love
- Comes from Spark of Creator within
- Activated specifically in darkest exile

**Five Names of Soul:**
1. Nefesh
2. Ruach
3. Neshama
4. Chaya
5. Yechidah (deepest - total unity with G-d)

**Beyond Yechidah:**
- Essence beyond names
- Spark of Creator (not created essence)
- Source of Potency

---

### Paradox of Darkness

**In Darkest Times:**
- Persecution or assimilation
- Complete concealment
- Essence Potency crushed out of soul
- Esther Potency in Esther Times!

**Result:**
- Greatest Hadassah Light emerges
- From deepest Esther Potency
- Hidden essence revealed through pressure

**Hence:** "Hadassah, that is Esther!"
- Esther (concealment/potency) produces greatest Hadassah (revelation/light)

---

## Torah as Empowerment

### The Word "Uman"

**Verse:** "And he [Mordechai] had brought up [uman] Hadassah, that is Esther..."

**"Uman" Meaning:**
- Nursling
- Refers to Torah
- Proverbs 8:30: "I was a 'uman' (nursling) beside Him..."

**Torah's Power:**
- Divinity of Torah-study
- Brings forth Esther Potency
- Activates Spark of Creator
- Especially in darkest exile times

**Mechanism:**
- "Strengthens G-dly Soul and weakens Animalistic Soul"
- Torah study empowers spiritual essence
- Simple Torah reading has profound effect

---

### Practical Application

**In Our Darkest Times:**
- Specifically during assimilation
- When spirituality seems distant
- Simple Torah study has power
- Reading Torah brings forth soul's essence

**Not Dependent On:**
- Deep understanding
- Emotional connection
- Spiritual feeling
- High level of observance

**Simply Through:**
- Opening a Jewish book
- Reading Torah text
- Studying any Jewish teaching
- Activates deepest potency

---

## Conclusion of Class

### Key Takeaways

**1. Two Dimensions of Soul:**
- Hadassah = Essence, Light, Israel, Head
- Esther = Ray, Potency, Jacob, Heel
- Both are one unified soul

**2. Beyond Revelation:**
- Potency deeper than Light
- Concealment can produce greatest revelation
- Esther's concealment is her power

**3. Power of Exile:**
- Specifically in darkest times
- Essence Potency activated
- Greatest light from greatest darkness

**4. Torah's Role:**
- Simple Torah study
- Brings forth Esther Potency
- Which reveals Hadassah Light
- "Uman" (Torah) connects Hadassah and Esther

---

## For Shluchim: Teaching Applications

### Adult Education

**Depth and Accessibility:**
- Complex Kabbalistic concepts
- Made relatable through soul analogy
- Practical application to daily life
- Relevant to contemporary challenges

**Class Structure:**
- Start with Biblical question
- Build through Talmudic sources
- Introduce Kabbalistic framework
- Apply to personal experience
- Conclude with practical takeaway

---

**Timing:**

- Built-in sermon opportunity
- Community interest high

**Thematic Links:**
- Concealment and revelation
- Light (Menorah) and darkness
- Priestly garments (external) vs essence
- Service of G-d in different modes

---

### Relevance to Modern Audience

**Struggles with Identity:**
- Public vs private self
- Jewish identity in secular world
- Inner essence vs outer presentation
- Hadassah/Esther in everyone

**Empowerment Message:**
- Darkest times hold greatest potential
- Concealment is not disconnection
- Simple acts have profound impact
- Torah study accessible to all

---

**Bottom Line:**

Purim educational class collection from Shluchim Exchange: Lunch N'Learn Book of Esther Part II (shluchimexchange.com/article.html?h=942&o=2922310) for adult education series with sequential in-depth textual analysis; Purim Overview Class (shluchimexchange.com/article.html?h=942&o=2918223) for comprehensive introduction to general audiences. **Featured class from [REDACTED-NAME], [REDACTED-LOCATION] (Feb 22, 2015):** "Who is Hadassah and Who is Esther?" for Shabbos Tetzaveh based on Rebbe's maamar "Vayehee Uman Es Hadassah" Purim 5713, with audio at soundcloud.com/hachaim/13-the-story-of-purim-esther-and-haddasah and PDF notes. **Core teaching:** Esther 2:7 "He brought up Hadassah, that is Esther" explores two names representing Sefirat Malchut (Emanation of Kingship) - Hadassah as kingship in righteous G-dly world (ocean hidden), Esther as kingship concealed in exile (land revealed); applied to soul with Yisroel/Israel ("Li Rosh" = my head, essence of soul above) and Yaakov/Jacob (okev = heel, ray of soul in body) showing Hadassah=Israel=Head=Soul Essence while Esther=Jacob=Heel=Soul's Ray, yet "Hadassah that is Esther" teaches unity - elevated soul essence IS ONE WITH soul's ray in body despite levels. **Three loves from Shema:** Love of heart (understand G-d fills world, love G-d as my life, Light of Esther revealed/based on creation), love of soul (understand G-d's infinite magnitude making all creation tiny ray, willing to sacrifice physical life for Infinite, mesirut nefesh, still Light of Esther), love "with all your might" (focus transcends creation entirely, direct perception of G-d's Essence from core G-dly Soul Spark of Creator beyond understanding, pure innate connection, Light of Hadassah from soul's essence). **Potency beyond Light:** In exile when lights extinguished, true Esther experience is Potency (latent/hidden/unfelt) not Light (revealed/felt) - capacity for total self-sacrifice not driven by understanding coming from Spark of Creator activated specifically in darkest exile (persecution or assimilation); paradoxically in darkest Esther Times the Essence Potency crushed from soul produces greatest Hadassah Light from deepest Esther Potency thus "Hadassah that is Esther!" **Torah empowerment:** Word "uman" (brought up) in verse means nursling referring to Torah (Proverbs 8:30), Torah-study brings forth Esther Potency activating Spark of Creator especially in darkest times by "strengthening G-dly Soul and weakening Animalistic Soul" - simple Torah reading/study (not dependent on deep understanding/emotional connection/high observance) brings forth soul's essence. **Teaching applications:** Complex Kabbalistic concepts made relatable through soul analogy with practical daily life application; Shabbat Tetzaveh near Purim provides natural thematic connection; modern relevance for struggles with public/private identity, Jewish identity in secular world (Hadassah/Esther in everyone), empowerment message that darkest times hold greatest potential with simple acts having profound impact. Additional classes in Google Drive folder (drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B0NzpGAq5H5XZF95XzRZRmRtN0E). Note: These Purim educational resources appear in Chanukah directory.
