# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Two Purim Sermons - Hadassah/Esther and Zachor

## Note: Purim Content (Not Chanukah)

**Author:** [REDACTED-NAME], [REDACTED-LOCATION]

**Posted:** Fri Feb 27, 2015 16:31 pm ET

**Subject:** Two Short-Hand Notes to Sermons for Tetzaveh/Zachor: (a) Haddasah is Esther (b) To Remember or To Not Know?

**Format:** Sermon notes/outlines

**Related:** File 1057 contains full detailed version of "Hadassah is Esther" teaching

---

## Sermon 1: Hadassah, She is Esther

### Biblical Source

**Verse:**
> "And he [Mordechai] brought up Hadassah, that is Esther." -Esther 2:7

**Date of Rebbe's Maamar:**
- Purim 1953 (5713)
- First delivered this teaching
- Explored two dimensions

---

### Talmudic Question

**Which Was Her Real Name?**
- Hadassah or Esther?
- Which was nickname?
- Talmud explores this

**Spiritual Significance:**
- Both quoted in Book of Esther
- Both exist in spiritual dimension
- Both within soul of every Jew
- Not just historical names
- Archetypal qualities

---

### Kabbalistic Framework: Ten Emanations

**World of Atzilut:**
- Ten Emanations (Sefirot)
- Made up of Light and Vessels
- Both absolutely transparent
- Unified with G-d
- No separation

**Tenth Emanation - Kingship (Malchut):**
- Has two dimensions
- Unlike other nine emanations

---

### Two Dimensions of Kingship

**Haddasah (Myrtle; Righteous):**
- As it is within its world of Atzilut
- Higher world
- Revealed G-dliness
- Times of Divine Revelation

**Esther (Hidden):**
- As it descends
- Hidden within lower world of Beriah (Creation; Ego)
- Concealment of G-d's presence
- Times of Exile

---

### Application to Soul

**Two Names for Jewish People:**

**Children of Israel:**
- Like Hadassah
- Soul in revelation
- Intellectual and emotional revelation
- Living within perception of G-d
- Living within love for G-d

**Word Analysis:**
- Yisroel (Hebrew for Israel)
- Letters form: "Lee Rosh"
- Means: "Unto Me a head"
- Head = higher level

**Children of Jacob:**
- Like Esther
- Soul in exile and concealment
- State of darkness

**Word Analysis:**
- Yaakov (Hebrew for Jacob)
- Named after holding Esau's heel at birth
- Akeiv = heel
- Heel = lower level

---

### Two Types of Exile/Concealment

**1. World's State:**
- Darkness and exile at large
- External circumstances
- Historical conditions

**2. Personal Exile:**
- "When we draw our power of desire and love into the indulgence of self-pleasuring egocentric desire"
- We deny soul its expression
- Love for G-d concealed
- Internal self-imposed exile

---

### Central Message of Verse

> "The verse in the Book of Esther is telling us that even the dimension of the soul that is in a state of Esther exile is still connected and contains within it all the divinity of the Hadassah dimension of the soul."

**Even More:**
> "When the Haddasdah dimension of the soul is extinguished, it is the Esther dimension of the soul that resurrects it!"

---

### Haddasah Dimension of Soul

**Characteristics:**
- All levels of soul's love
- Depends on being fueled by:
  - Soul's understanding
  - Concentrating on G-d
  - Meditating upon G-d's relationship with us
  - Meditating upon G-d's greatness

**In Exile:**
- G-d is concealed
- Higher sensitivities drowned
- Indulgence in lower egocentric pleasures
- Hadassah experience extinguished

---

### Esther Dimension of Soul - The Potency

**Remains Unaffected by Exile:**
- Potency of the Soul
- Power of self-sacrifice
- NOT based on perception
- NOT based on feelings
- Outcome of soul's nucleus being "Spark of Creator!"

**Greater Than Hadassah:**
- Esther (Hidden) Potency > Hadassah (Revealed) Love
- In essence, deeper level
- More fundamental

**In Darkest Times:**
- When Haddasah Love extinguished
- Esther (Hidden) Potency resurrects her
- Concealment produces revelation
- Darkness births light

---

### Activating the Potency

**The Seed:**
> "The seed that draws forth the Esther (Hidden) Potency of the soul are the words of Torah-study."

**Torah's Power:**
- Empowers Potency of Soul
- Reveals potency into action
- Transforms latent into active
- Brings forth essence

---

## Sermon 2: To Remember or To Not Know?!

### The Contradiction

**Shabbat Zachor:**
- Shabbat before Purim
- Called "Zachor" - Remember
- Read commandment to remember Amalek
- What Amalek did leaving Egypt
- First nation to attack Jews in desert
- Clear memory and identification

**Haman Connection:**
- Haman called "Haman H'Agogi"
- Agog = king of Amalek in times of Saul
- Agog impregnated woman night before death
- Haman = offspring of Agog
- Therefore: Amalekite

**Purpose:**
- Shabbat Zachor: Remember wickedness
- Remember commandment to eradicate
- Clear identification
- Intellectual understanding

**Then Comes Purim:**
- Completely different approach
- New directive

---

### Purim's Law

**Must Drink:**
> "Until he becomes too intoxicated to know the difference between, 'Blessed be Mordechai and Cursed be Haman!'"

**Apparent Contradiction:**
- Zachor: Clearly remember who Haman (Amalek) is
- Purim: Too intoxicated to know difference
- Which is it?
- Remember or forget?

---

### The Key: "Ad D'loh Yodah"

**Wording Analysis:**
- Does NOT use word "Shikor" (drunk)
- States: "Ad d'loh yodah"
- Means: "Until [he] doesn't know"
- Focus on "know" vs "not know"

---

### Parable: The Sinking Ship

**Scenario 1 - Forgot Friend:**
- Man on sinking ship
- Panic
- Forgot about friend
- Jumped ship to save himself

**Decent World's Reaction:**
- Eventually understand
- Would forgive
- Panic overrides logic

**Scenario 2 - Forgot Children:**
- Same man
- Same panic
- Forgot about children
- Jumped ship to save himself

**Decent World's Reaction:**
- Very difficult to understand
- Very difficult to forgive
- Never acceptable

**Why the Difference?**
- Panic overrides logic
- But panic does NOT override what lies deeper than logic
- In depths of heart
- Core essence
- No justification for forgetting children
- No matter how powerful the panic

---

### Two Levels of Remembrance

**Shabbat Zachor - "Know" Level:**
- Sitting in synagogue holiness
- Intellectually reading
- Understanding
- Absorbing who Amalek is
- What he did to us
- Logical relationship
- Between us and Amalekian War

**Problem:**
- Logic-based remembrance
- Won't necessarily withstand panic
- Won't withstand sinking ship
- Intellectual understanding insufficient

**Purim - "Not Know" Level:**
> "The deeper dimension of the words, 'Ad d'loh yodah -Until [he] doesn't know.' is to take the depths of, 'Blessed be Mordechai and Cursed be Haman!' beyond the 'Know' (logic) into the deeper essence of the heart and soul, transcending into the 'Not Know!'"

---

### Deeper Than Logic

**Some Concepts Require More:**
- Logical relationship not enough
- Must touch essence of soul
- Beyond intellectual understanding
- Core identity level

**Amalek:**
> "A people who stand up against Israel, bent on annihilating our people, G-d forbid, must touch the very essence of our soul!"

**In Deepest Intoxication:**
- Way beyond "Know"
- Into depths of soul's "Not Know"
- Jew must cry out:
- "Blessed be Mordechai and Cursed be Haman!"

---

### Contemporary Application

**Dangerous Approach:**
> "To negotiate within our minds with resolutions of the United Nation, Foreign Policy, and World Opinion about an outright Haman sworn to destroy our land and wipeout our people, is to not have celebrated Purim!"

**What It Means:**
- Not truly "Zachor" - Remembered
- Not remembered history
- Not remembered people's enemies
- Intellectual negotiation insufficient

---

### The Cry from Soul's Essence

**Must Passionately:**
- Remember
- Cry out
- To point of intoxication
- From depths of soul

**The Declaration:**
> "Blessed be Mordechai! Blessed be our people! Blessed be our Holy Land! Cursed be Haman! Cursed be those who want nothing but to destroy our People and destroy our Holy Land! Blessed be Mordechai and Cursed be Haman!"

**Not Intellectual:**
- Not debate
- Not negotiation
- Not analysis
- Soul-level certainty

---

### Conclusion

**Message:**
- Two levels of knowing
- Intellectual (Zachor)
- Essential ("Not Know" - beyond intellect)
- Both necessary
- But essence deeper
- Must reach soul's core
- Especially regarding enemies of Jewish people

**Closing:**
> "Have a happy Purim!"

---

## For Shluchim: Using These Sermons

### Shabbat Tetzaveh/Zachor

**Timing:**
- Often near Purim
- Built-in connection
- Community expecting Purim content
- Timely and relevant

**Audience:**
- Intellectually sophisticated
- Can handle Kabbalistic concepts
- Interested in deeper meaning
- Seeking personal application

---

### Sermon 1 Applications

**Hadassah and Esther in Daily Life:**
- Times we feel connected (Hadassah)
- Times we feel disconnected (Esther)
- Both are one soul
- Concealment contains revelation
- Torah study activates essence
- Hope in darkest times

**Personal Relevance:**
- Identity struggles
- Feeling distant from G-d
- Self-imposed exile
- Potency always present
- Never truly disconnected

---

### Sermon 2 Applications

**Current Events:**
- Israel and threats
- Enemies of Jewish people
- Not just intellectual issue
- Soul-level response required
- Beyond politics
- Core identity

**Personal Level:**
- What touches our essence?
- What only touches intellect?
- Some truths beyond debate
- Core convictions
- Non-negotiable values

---

## Related Resources

**In This Collection:**
- File 1057: Full detailed version of "Hadassah is Esther" class with extensive notes
- Files 1059-1062: Mivtza Purim guidelines
- File 1066: Another Purim sermon ("Divine Curveball")

---

**Bottom Line:**

Two Purim sermon outlines from [REDACTED-NAME], [REDACTED-LOCATION] (Feb 27, 2015) for Shabbat Tetzaveh/Zachor: **(1) Hadassah, She is Esther** based on Rebbe's Purim 1953 maamar exploring Esther 2:7 "He brought up Hadassah, that is Esther" - both names exist spiritually within every Jewish soul. **Kabbalistic framework:** Tenth Emanation (Malchut/Kingship) has two dimensions - Haddasah (Myrtle/Righteous) as it is within Atzilut higher world representing Divine Revelation times, Esther (Hidden) as it descends hidden within Beriah (Creation/Ego) representing Exile/Concealment times. **Applied to soul:** Children of Israel (like Hadassah) = soul in intellectual/emotional revelation living within perception/love for G-d (Yisroel letters form "Lee Rosh" = "Unto Me a head"), Children of Jacob (like Esther) = soul in exile/concealment state of darkness (Yaakov from akeiv = heel at birth); two types of exile are world's state of darkness and personal exile when "we draw power of desire into indulgence of self-pleasuring egocentric desire" denying soul's expression. **Central message:** "Even dimension of soul in Esther exile still connected and contains all divinity of Hadassah dimension" and "when Haddasah dimension extinguished, Esther dimension resurrects it!" Haddasah dimension (all soul's love levels depends on being fueled by understanding/concentrating/meditating upon G-d) becomes extinguished in exile when G-d concealed and higher sensitivities drowned in egocentric pleasures; Esther dimension (Potency of Soul, power of self-sacrifice NOT based on perception/feelings but outcome of soul's nucleus being "Spark of Creator") remains unaffected by exile with Esther (Hidden) Potency greater than Hadassah (Revealed) Love - in darkest times when Haddasah Love extinguished, Esther Potency resurrects her with concealment producing revelation; "seed that draws forth Esther Potency are words of Torah-study" empowering Potency into action. **(2) To Remember or To Not Know?!** addresses apparent contradiction: Shabbat Zachor commands "remember wickedness of Amalek" (Haman H'Agogi descended from Agog king of Amalek) with clear identification and intellectual understanding, but Purim law requires drinking "until intoxicated to not know difference between 'Blessed Mordechai and Cursed Haman'" - which is it, remember or forget? **Key insight:** Wording NOT "Shikor" (drunk) but "Ad d'loh yodah" (until doesn't know) focusing on "Know" vs "Not Know" levels. **Sinking ship parable:** Decent world eventually understands/forgives man in panic forgetting friend and jumping ship (panic overrides logic), but decent world very difficult to understand/forgive same man forgetting children (no justification no matter how powerful panic) because panic overrides logic but NOT what lies deeper than logic in depths of heart/core essence. **Two remembrance levels:** Shabbat Zachor "Know" level (sitting in synagogue holiness intellectually reading/understanding/absorbing who Amalek is creating logical relationship, but logic-based remembrance won't necessarily withstand panic/sinking ship); Purim "Not Know" level takes "Blessed Mordechai and Cursed Haman" beyond "Know" (logic) into deeper essence of heart/soul transcending into "Not Know" - some concepts require more than logical relationship must touch essence of soul beyond intellectual at core identity level. **Amalek application:** "People who stand up against Israel bent on annihilating our people must touch very essence of our soul" - in deepest intoxication way beyond "Know" into soul's "Not Know" depths Jew must cry "Blessed Mordechai and Cursed Haman!" **Contemporary warning:** "To negotiate within our minds with UN resolutions, Foreign Policy, World Opinion about outright Haman sworn to destroy our land and wipeout our people is to not have celebrated Purim" - not truly Zachor/Remembered history or people's enemies (intellectual negotiation insufficient); must passionately remember and cry from soul's depths "Blessed Mordechai! Blessed our people! Blessed our Holy Land! Cursed Haman! Cursed those who want destroy our People and Holy Land!" - not intellectual debate/negotiation/analysis but soul-level certainty. Related: File 1057 (full detailed Hadassah/Esther class), 1059-1062 (Mivtza Purim guidelines), 1066 (another sermon). Note: These Purim sermons appear in Chanukah directory.

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] "Purim: The Divine Curveball" - Sermon/Essay

## Note: Purim Content (Not Chanukah)

**Author:** [REDACTED-NAME], [REDACTED-LOCATION]

**Posted:** Fri Mar 25, 2016 10:52 am ET

**Subject:** Purim: The Divine Curveball

**Format:** Creative sermon/essay using baseball metaphor

**Style:** Engaging, contemporary, accessible

---

## Opening: Personal Baseball Anecdote

### The Curveball Challenge

**Personal Admission:**
> "Can you believe its almost April? With the baseball season only days away, my mind turns to my non existent curveball. You see, the curveball is one of the many reasons I will never be a pitcher. My curveball just doesn't curve. I can throw it straight, fast or slow, but I can't make it curve."

**The Mystery:**
- How do pitchers even do that?
- Can understand straight throw
- While ball in hand, control direction
- But control trajectory after it leaves hand?
- Never gets it right

**Humorous Image:**
> "I am reminded of the children who release their bowling ball and then twist their bodies to the right, hoping the ball will follow suit. Yes, that's me and the curveball."

---

## Purim as Curveball

### Life's Unexpected Challenges

**The Expression:**
- "Life threw you a curveball"
- No reason to expect challenge
- Arrives when off guard
- Caught completely by surprise

**Purim Fit:**
> "Well Purim was certainly one mean curveball."

---

### Jews' Comfortable Position

**Before Haman's Decree:**
- Not expecting annihilation threat
- Comfortable in Persia
- Wealthy
- Socially accepted
- Friends in high places
- Mordechai: respected minister in palace
- Esther: the queen

**Then:**
> "One day, out of the blue, G-d threw them a curveball by the name of Haman and the Jews were caught completely by surprise."

---

### Second Curveball: G-d's Silence

**Historical Pattern:**
- In every Jewish crisis until Purim
- Jews turned to G-d
- He intervened with direct miracle
- Rarely if ever failed
- Pattern: Sin → Punishment threat → Repentance → G-d's response

**G-d's Responses:**
- Either miracle saving them
- Or inform sins beyond salvation
- One thing G-d would definitely NOT do: sit idly by

**Purim Was Different:**
> "Purim was the first occasion, when G-d met the Jewish entreaty with silence."

**The Experience:**
> "Their heart rending pleas for help ascended to the heavens, but returned empty; their cadence bouncing back to earth, their echoes fading off distant hills with nary a response from above."

---

### Human Initiative

**Out of Desperation:**
- Jews decided to act on their own
- Mordechai appointed Esther to appeal
- Esther consented
- Appeared before king with impeccable timing

**Everything Fell Into Place:**
- With perfection
- Scene for dramatic salvation set
- Esther revealed identity
- Precision of maestro
- Haman fell off chair and out of favor

**Result:**
> "A looming crisis became a joyful holiday in the span of a moment."

---

### The Unexpected Nature

**How Unexpected:**
- No miraculous arm from above
- No wall of water descending
- No drowning Persians
- Heavens silent that night
- But grounds thundered with salvation

**Assessment:**
> "A most unusual spectacle. Another true curveball."

---

## The Greatest Curveball Pitcher

### G-d's Mastery

**Baseball Debate:**
> "The book is out on who is the greatest curveball pitcher of all time. Sandy Koufax or Dwight Gooden, your guess is as good as mine. But I can tell you one thing. Nobody's curveball is quite as good as G-d's."

---

### How a Curveball Works

**Mechanics:**
- Thrown high
- Somewhere between mound and plate
- Bottom drops out of ball
- Comes in low

**G-d's Execution:**
> "G-d is really good at it, and Purim was His shining moment."

**Purim Application:**
- Jews prayed
- Expected Him to come in high
- With heavenly miracle
- But He surprised them
- With curveball
- Let bottom drop out
- Came in low
- With earthly, non-miraculous solution

---

## The Fastball vs The Curveball

### The Fastball Pitcher

**Characteristics:**
- Comes in throwing heat
- No matter how fast batter swings
- Ball blows right by
- Open challenge
- Pitcher stares batter down
- Dares him to swing
- Everyone knows what's coming
- Blows it by anyway

**G-d's Fastball:**
> "When G-d comes in throwing heat, no one can stand up to Him."

**Examples:**
- Think you can hurt His children?
- Think you can annihilate His people?
- Think you have it figured out?
- G-d comes along and stares you down

**Historical Examples:**
- Walls of Jericho tumbling down
- Cruise of oil burns eight days
- First born of Egypt die
- Who can stop Him?
- Nature is putty in His hands

---

### When G-d Throws the Curveball

**The Scenario:**
- Jews in crisis
- Call to the bullpen
- Pray and fast
- Call on G-d for relief pitching
- G-d comes trotting in
- But refuses to throw fastball
- Refuses to bail us out

**Appearance:**
- Sluggers line up opposite side
- Swing away at will
- Appear to be in control
- Hitting long hard drives
- Flying over wall
- Just another inning or two
- Game will be lost
- G-d's children going down

**Then:**
> "Then in the bottom of the ninth, when you least expect it, G-d starts throwing curve balls and strikes out the side."

---

### What It Looks Like

**When G-d Overrules Nature:**
- Bread falls from sky
- You know He's in charge
- Clear divine intervention
- No question who's controlling

**When G-d Lets Nature Run:**
- Allows world's bullies upper-hand
- Seems nature slipped from control
- Enemies appear winning
- We appear losing
- To all intents and purposes
- As if He let go

---

## The Mystery of the Curveball

### Author's Fascination

**Recall Opening:**
> "Remember what I wrote at the beginning of this essay? I am fascinated by the curveball because the pitcher controls the ball though it is no longer in his hands?"

---

### G-d Does the Same

**With Nature:**
- Rather than taking control of patterns
- Lets it run loose
- But astoundingly
- Remains in control
- Even after He lets go

**The Mystery:**
> "In some inexplicable way, the randomness of nature ends up delivering the same result that G-d would have delivered had He intervened directly."

---

### Enemies Scratching Heads

**Their Confusion:**
- How did He do that?
- We had this one
- He wasn't interfering
- He had let go
- And He still won out
- How did He control what He already released?

---

### Historical Examples

**Nazi Germany:**
- Record incredible victories
- But allies discover bomb first

**Stalin:**
- Plan of annihilation against Soviet Jews
- Days before carrying out
- Stalin up and dies

**1948 Israel:**
- Five Arab armies converge
- Yet manage to lose the war

**The Question:**
> "How does G-d pull of these seemingly random conclusions?"

---

## Two Types of Miracles

### The Fastball Miracle

**Characteristics:**
- Bends nature to His will
- Doesn't surprise us
- Open intervention
- Direct control
- Hard hitting
- Everyone expects it
- No one can stop it

**Example:**
- Splitting of Red Sea
- Manna from heaven
- Clear supernatural events

---

### The Curveball Miracle

**Characteristics:**
- Hidden in nature
- Takes you by surprise
- Fast dropping
- Comes in through natural means
- Strikes out anyway
- Takes breath away
- By far more impressive

**Why More Impressive:**
> "When random patterns of nature save us from annihilation each time we are threatened, we are definitely surprised."

---

### The Greater Recognition

**When Nature Expresses G-d's Will:**
- We recognize no daylight
- Between G-d and His nature
- Unity revealed
- Hidden becomes manifest

**Comparison:**
> "The miracle that overrules nature is the hard hitting fastball – every one expects it and no one can stop it. The miracle hidden in nature is the fast dropping curveball. It takes you by surprise. It drops down to earth and strikes you out anyway. It takes your breath away and is by far the more impressive miracle."

---

### The Winning Pitch

**Final Assessment:**
> "The pitch that wins the game."

**Implication:**
- Curveball more effective
- More complete victory
- Demonstrates greater control
- Reveals deeper truth
- Nature itself expressing divine will

---

## For Shluchim: Using This Sermon

### Audience Appeal

**Who This Reaches:**
- Sports fans
- Contemporary mindset
- Those who relate to analogies
- Seeking accessible Torah
- Americans (baseball culture)
- Younger demographics

**Tone:**
- Light and engaging
- Self-deprecating humor
- Relatable personal anecdote
- Sophisticated theology in accessible packaging

---

### Key Messages

**1. Purim's Uniqueness:**
- Different from other miracles
- Hidden nature
- Human agency
- G-d's silent guidance

**2. Two Types of Divine Intervention:**
- Open miracles (fastball)
- Hidden miracles (curveball)
- Both demonstrate control
- Curveball more impressive

**3. Contemporary Application:**
- Modern Jewish survival
- Israel's victories
- Threats that don't materialize
- "Random" positive outcomes

**4. Faith Lesson:**
- When G-d seems silent
- Still in control
- Working through nature
- Ultimate victory assured

---

### Sermon Structure

**Opening:**
- Personal, humorous hook
- Baseball reference timely (March, season starting)
- Establishes credibility through vulnerability

**Development:**
- Purim story through lens of metaphor
- Historical examples
- Theological depth without jargon

**Climax:**
- Comparison of miracle types
- Curveball as superior
- Nature expressing divine will

**Conclusion:**
- "The pitch that wins the game"
- Memorable, punchy ending
- Leaves audience with image

---

### When to Deliver

**Ideal Times:**
- Purim seudah
- Pre-Purim classes
- Shabbat Zachor/Tetzaveh
- Adult education series

**Modifications:**
- Non-baseball culture: different sports metaphor
- Women's groups: same content, perhaps different sport
- Youth: could be even more developed with recent examples
- Scholarly: add source references

---

### Follow-Up Discussion

**Questions to Explore:**
- What are modern "curveballs"?
- When have you experienced hidden miracles?
- How does this change prayer expectations?
- What about when bad things happen?
- Nature vs supernatural intervention

---

## Related Resources

**In This Collection:**
- File 1065: Two sermons including "Remember or Not Know"
- File 1057: Detailed "Hadassah is Esther" class
- Files 1059-1062: Mivtza Purim operational guidelines

**Similar Themes:**
- Hidden miracles
- Purim's unique nature
- Divine providence
- Faith in difficult times

---

**Bottom Line:**

Creative Purim sermon "The Divine Curveball" from [REDACTED-NAME], [REDACTED-LOCATION] (Mar 25, 2016) using baseball metaphor to explain Purim's unique miracle. **Opening personal anecdote:** Author's "non existent curveball" that doesn't curve - can throw straight/fast/slow but can't make it curve, fascinated how pitchers control ball's trajectory after it leaves hand (like children releasing bowling ball then twisting bodies hoping ball follows). **Purim as curveball:** Expression "life threw you a curveball" (no reason expect challenge, caught off guard) fits Purim perfectly - Jews comfortable in Persia (wealthy, socially accepted, friends in high places, Mordechai respected minister, Esther queen) then "out of the blue G-d threw them curveball by name of Haman" catching completely by surprise. **Second curveball - G-d's silence:** Historical pattern every Jewish crisis until Purim (Jews turned to G-d, He intervened with direct miracle, rarely failed, pattern sin→punishment threat→repentance→G-d's response either miracle or inform sins beyond salvation, but definitely NOT sit idly); "Purim was first occasion when G-d met Jewish entreaty with silence" - "heart rending pleas ascended to heavens but returned empty, echoes fading off distant hills with nary response from above"; out of desperation Jews decided act on own (Mordechai appointed Esther to appeal, appeared before king with impeccable timing, everything fell into place with perfection, Esther revealed identity with precision of maestro, Haman fell off chair/out of favor, "looming crisis became joyful holiday in span of moment") - "heavens silent that night but grounds thundered with salvation, most unusual spectacle, another true curveball." **G-d as greatest curveball pitcher:** "Book out on who is greatest (Sandy Koufax or Dwight Gooden?) but nobody's curveball quite as good as G-d's" - curveball thrown high but somewhere between mound and plate bottom drops out comes in low; "G-d is really good at it, Purim was His shining moment" - Jews prayed expecting Him come in high with heavenly miracle but He surprised with curveball letting bottom drop out coming in low with earthly non-miraculous solution. **Fastball vs curveball:** Fastball pitcher comes in throwing heat (ball blows by no matter how fast batter swings, open challenge, everyone knows what's coming but blows by anyway) - when G-d comes throwing heat no one can stand up (walls of Jericho tumbling, oil burns eight days, firstborn of Egypt die, "Who can stop Him when nature putty in His hands?"); but when Jews in crisis call bullpen G-d sometimes refuses fastball/refuses bail out - sluggers appear in control hitting over wall game seems lost but "then in bottom of ninth when you least expect it G-d starts throwing curve balls and strikes out side" (when G-d overrules nature with bread from sky you know He's in charge, but when lets nature run loose and allows world's bullies upper-hand seems nature slipped from control with enemies appearing winning). **Mystery of curveball:** Author fascinated "pitcher controls ball though it is no longer in his hands" - G-d does same with nature: "rather than taking control of patterns lets it run loose but astoundingly remains in control even after lets go"; "in some inexplicable way randomness of nature ends up delivering same result G-d would have delivered had He intervened directly"; enemies scratching heads (Nazis record victories but allies discover bomb first, Stalin planning annihilation days before carrying out up and dies, five Arab armies converge on Israel yet manage to lose war) - "How does G-d pull off these seemingly random conclusions?" **Two miracle types:** Fastball miracle (bends nature to will, doesn't surprise, open intervention, hard hitting, everyone expects, no one stops like Red Sea splitting/manna) vs Curveball miracle (hidden in nature, takes by surprise, fast dropping through natural means, strikes out anyway, takes breath away, "by far more impressive") because "when random patterns of nature save us from annihilation each time threatened we definitely surprised" revealing "no daylight between G-d and His nature" - unity revealed, hidden becomes manifest. **Conclusion:** "Miracle overrules nature is hard hitting fastball everyone expects no one stops; miracle hidden in nature is fast dropping curveball takes by surprise, drops to earth, strikes out anyway, takes breath away, by far more impressive miracle - the pitch that wins the game." **Key messages:** Purim's uniqueness (hidden nature, human agency, G-d's silent guidance), two divine intervention types (open/hidden both demonstrate control but curveball more impressive), contemporary application (modern Jewish survival, Israel's victories, threats don't materialize, "random" positive outcomes), faith lesson (when G-d seems silent still in control working through nature with ultimate victory assured). Related resources: File 1065 (two sermons), 1057 (Hadassah/Esther class), 1059-1062 (Mivtza Purim guidelines). Note: This Purim sermon appears in Chanukah directory.

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] "Purim: Reversal of Assimilation" - Sermon Based on Likutei Diburim

## Note: Purim Content (Not Chanukah)

**Author:** [REDACTED-NAME], [REDACTED-LOCATION]

**Posted:** Sat Mar 04, 2017 23:11 pm ET

**Subject:** A Purim Thought based on Likutei Diburim

**Source:** Likutei Diburim 371b and other sources

**Theme:** Assimilation, forgetfulness, and return

---

## Section 1: Inadvertent Slide

### Core Message

**Central Teaching:**
> "Purim celebrates the reversal of assimilation."

**Not Sudden Fall:**
- Not deliberate abandonment
- Inadvertent process
- Gradual slide
- Little by little

---

### Historical Context: Jews in Persia

**Before Haman:**
- Talmud teaches slide began well before Haman
- Jews in highest enclaves
- Commerce and government
- Most exclusive social clubs
- When king gave party, Jews on guest list

**Accommodations:**
- Royal caterers served kosher food
- Jews free to observe dietary laws
- Surface-level observance maintained
- Appeared integrated successfully

---

### Mordechai's Warning

**His Reasoning:**
> "Natural social boundaries are important to foster pride in distinct cultural identities and these would erode at a one-hundred-eighty day party."

**Philosophy:**
- Minority populations must preserve identity
- Lest swallowed by majority
- Must interface with majority
- But never integrate fully

**Timeline:**
- Might take a year
- Might take decades
- Might take generations
- But unchecked long-term integration
- Leads inexorably to assimilation

---

### No One Intends It

**Reality:**
> "No one sets out to erode religious or cultural pride. No Jew seeks to deliberately stamp out our traditions. It occurs inadvertently. Little by little, boundaries fade, divisions disappear and identity is lost."

**Persian Jews' State:**
- By no means assimilated (yet)
- But process had begun
- But for Mordechai and handful of followers
- No one took notice

---

## Section 2: Forget

### Gematria Analysis of "Shushan"

**Exploration Method:**
- Explored name Shushan for message
- Tried numeric value of Hebrew letters
- Failed to decipher message
- Divided number by two
- Hit pay dirt

**Calculation:**
- Four letters of Shushan = 656
- 656 ÷ 2 = 328
- 328 in Hebrew letters: Shin, Chaf, Chet
- Spells: **Shachach** = "to forget"

**Message:**
> "In other words, if you forget two or more times, you reach the *Shushan state*."

---

### The Process of Forgetfulness

**How It Begins:**
- Set out to broaden horizons
- Establish contacts, friendships, familiarities
- With differing religions and cultures
- Don't intend to erode own heritage

**Immersed in Discovery:**
- Thrill of newness
- Might on occasion neglect single Shabbat
- Or Passover
- First time: feel guilty
- Second or third time: becomes habit

**Result:**
> "If we engage in the process of forgetfulness, we reach the state that our ancestors reached in Shushan."

---

### Responsibility for Forgetfulness

**Never Set Out to Reach That Stage:**
- Yet responsible for having reached it

**Talmudic Teaching:**
- We are responsible for Torah knowledge we forget
- Because forgetfulness results from idleness
- When choose to sit idly rather than study
- Responsible for consequences of choice

**Same Applies to Assimilation:**
> "When we choose to pursue foreign cultures, rather than our own, we are responsible for our resultant assimilation."

---

## Section 3: Return

### Meaning of "Responsible"

**Word Play:**
> "Responsible means response-able."

**Implication:**
- We are able to respond
- To reality of assimilation
- By reversing it
- Which is precisely what Mordechai set out to do

---

### Mordechai's Response to Haman

**After Haman's Announcement:**
- Rallied nation to renew commitment
- Throughout year of impending doom
- Despite continued contacts with Persian community
- No Jew, even inadvertently, slipped away
- From Jewish faith and practice

**Source:** Torah Ohr, Megilas Esther 91b

---

### When You Really Care, You Remember

**Analogy: Forgotten Birthday**
> "When a husband forgets his wife's birthday, she is justifiably upset. Though he didn't deliberately set out to forget, if he had really cared, he would have remembered."

**Application to Faith:**
- When strive to be true to faith
- Become intensely aware of behavior
- Don't trip up even by mistake
- Care creates vigilance

---

### Story: Rabbi Nochum from Chernobyl

**Decided to Allow Evil Inclination One Victory:**
- Set out to commit a sin
- Heard people gossiping
- Joined the group
- As approached, fellow shouted: "Don't gossip, it's a sin"

**Group's Response:**
- Someone retorted: speaking ill of this individual is actually a Mitzvah
- When Rabbi heard this
- Stepped away
- "He was in the business of committing a sin that day, not a Mitzvah"

**His Day:**
- From one sin opportunity to next
- Every time set out to commit sin
- Somehow recast in guise of Mitzvah
- Was spared each time

**Lesson:**
> "When one is truly attached, heart and soul, to G-d, one does not trip up even deliberately. How much more so inadvertently."

---

## Section 4: Response

### G-d Responds Measure for Measure

**Teaching:**
> "Our sages taught that G-d responds to our behavior measure for measure. He treats us precisely as we treat Him."

**In Case of Purim:**
> "This is astoundingly accurate."

**Source:** Babylonian Talmud, Megillah 12b

---

### Haman's Lottery

**The Process:**
- Chose date for annihilation by throwing lots
- Didn't set out to kill in month of Adar
- Lot just happened to fall on that month

**Haman's Joy:**
- Moses passed away in Adar
- Took it as sign he would succeed
- In terrible design

---

### The Parallel

**Jews' Assimilation:**
- Didn't deliberately set out to assimilate
- Allowed it to happen inadvertently

**Haman's Date Selection:**
- Didn't set out to choose auspicious day
- Found it inadvertently

**Measure for Measure:**
- Same pattern of inadvertence

---

### Haman's Miscalculation

**The Reversal:**
- Haman miscalculated
- Moses also **born** in month of Adar
- Month ostensibly bad for Jews
- Turned out to work in our favor

**Complete Reversal:**
- Ancestors reversed course
- From assimilation to enthusiastic faith
- So their misfortune reversed
- They worked to prevent inadvertent slip ups
- So G-d prevented inadvertent fortune of Haman's lottery
- Date Haman chose turned out to be good fortune and protection

---

## For Shluchim: Using This Sermon

### Themes to Emphasize

**1. Inadvertent Assimilation:**
- Most relevant to modern audience
- Many experiencing this
- Not deliberate rejection
- Gradual process
- Relatable struggle

**2. Responsibility and Response:**
- Not just guilty
- Response-able
- Can reverse the trend
- Empowering message

**3. Measure for Measure:**
- G-d's response mirrors ours
- When we commit fully
- Protection comes "inadvertently"
- Theological depth

---

### Contemporary Applications

**Modern "Shushan State":**
- Interfaith social circles
- Professional integration
- Cultural assimilation
- Gradual boundary erosion
- "Just this once" mentality

**Process of Forgetfulness:**
- Skipping Shabbat "occasionally"
- "Too busy" for Jewish events
- Children's activities on Jewish holidays
- Becomes habit over time

**Path to Return:**
- Renew commitment like Mordechai's generation
- Even without immediate crisis
- Proactive rather than reactive
- Reverse the trend now

---

### Teaching Points

**Gematria Hook:**
- Engaging for intellectual audience
- Shushan = 2x Forget
- Memorable teaching device
- Shows depth in text

**Stories Work:**
- Rabbi Nochum from Chernobyl
- Forgotten birthday analogy
- Make abstract concrete
- Help audience connect

**Historical Perspective:**
- Not first generation to face this
- Pattern throughout history
- Jews in Persia parallel to today
- Continuity and relevance

---

### Sermon Structure

**Opening:**
- Purim celebrates reversal of assimilation
- Set contemporary context
- Most Jews experiencing gradual slide

**Body:**
1. Inadvertent Slide (historical context)
2. Forget (gematria and responsibility)
3. Return (Mordechai's response)
4. Response (measure for measure)

**Conclusion:**
- We too can reverse course
- Before reaching full assimilation
- Mordechai's example for today
- Response-able = able to respond

---

### Target Audience

**Best For:**
- Assimilated or assimilating Jews
- Interfaith families
- Young professionals
- Those feeling disconnected
- Seeking return without guilt

**Why Effective:**
- Non-judgmental tone
- Acknowledges inadvertent nature
- Empowers rather than condemns
- Provides clear path forward
- Grounded in sources

---

## Sources Cited

**Primary Sources:**
1. Likutei Diburim: 371b (main source)
2. Babylonian Talmud, Megillah 12a (Achashverosh's party)
3. Ibid (Kosher food served)
4. Ethics of Our Fathers, 3:8 (responsibility for forgetfulness)
5. Torah Ohr, Megilas Esther: 91b (no inadvertent slips during crisis year)
6. Babylonian Talmud, Megillah: 12b (measure for measure)

**Note on Mordechai and Esther:**
- Their posts in government demonstrate integration level
- Yet Mordechai warned against party
- Leadership from within system

---

## Related Resources

**In This Collection:**
- File 1066: "Divine Curveball" sermon (another from same author)
- File 1070: "My Jewish Identity" (similar assimilation theme)
- Files 1065: "Remember or Not Know" sermon
- Files 1057: "Hadassah and Esther" detailed class

---

**Bottom Line:**

Purim sermon "Reversal of Assimilation" from [REDACTED-NAME], [REDACTED-LOCATION] (Mar 4, 2017) based on Likutei Diburim 371b teaching Purim celebrates reversal of assimilation - Talmud teaches Persian Jews' slide began well before Haman with Jews in highest enclaves of commerce/government, exclusive social clubs, king's party guest list; royal caterers served kosher allowing dietary observance but Mordechai warned "natural social boundaries important to foster pride in distinct cultural identities" that would erode at 180-day party, reasoning "minority populations must preserve identity lest swallowed by majority - must interface but never integrate" because "unchecked long-term integration leads inexorably to assimilation" over years/decades/generations. "No one sets out to erode religious/cultural pride, no Jew seeks deliberately stamp out traditions, occurs inadvertently - little by little boundaries fade, divisions disappear, identity lost"; Persian Jews by no means assimilated but process begun (but for Mordechai and handful no one noticed). **Gematria analysis "Shushan":** Four letters Shushan = 656, divided by 2 = 328 which in Hebrew letters Shin-Chaf-Chet spells "Shachach" (to forget) meaning "if you forget two or more times you reach Shushan state" - spiritual state of assimilation reached through forgetfulness process (set out broaden horizons establishing contacts/friendships/familiarities with differing religions/cultures not intending erode own heritage, but immersed in discovery thrill might occasionally neglect single Shabbat/Passover feeling guilty first time but by second/third becomes habit). **Responsibility:** We're responsible for Torah knowledge we forget because forgetfulness results from idleness - "when choose to sit idly rather than study responsible for consequences of choice"; same applies assimilation - "when choose pursue foreign cultures rather than our own responsible for resultant assimilation." **Return - "Responsible means response-able":** Able to respond to assimilation reality by reversing it (precisely what Mordechai did); after Haman's announcement rallied nation to renew commitment throughout year of impending doom - despite continued Persian contacts "no Jew even inadvertently slipped away from Jewish faith and practice" (Torah Ohr Megilas Esther 91b). **Analogy:** Husband forgets wife's birthday justifiably upsets her - "though didn't deliberately set out forget, if really cared would have remembered"; when strive be true to faith become intensely aware of behavior and don't trip up even by mistake. **Story Rabbi Nochum Chernobyl:** Decided allow evil inclination one victory to commit sin, heard gossiping and joined but fellow shouted "Don't gossip it's sin" then someone retorted speaking ill of this individual actually Mitzvah so Rabbi stepped away ("in business committing sin that day not Mitzvah") - went from one sin opportunity to next but every time set out commit sin somehow recast as Mitzvah and was spared, teaching "when truly attached heart and soul to G-d one does not trip up even deliberately, how much more so inadvertently." **G-d's response measure for measure (Megillah 12b):** Haman chose annihilation date by throwing lots (didn't set out kill in Adar, lot just happened fall on that month) and rejoiced because Moses died in Adar taking as sign would succeed; parallel to Jews who didn't deliberately assimilate but allowed inadvertently, Haman didn't set out choose auspicious day but found inadvertently (same pattern inadvertence). **Reversal:** Haman miscalculated because Moses also BORN in Adar so month ostensibly bad turned out work in Jews' favor - as ancestors reversed from assimilation to enthusiastic faith so misfortune reversed; as they worked prevent inadvertent slip ups so G-d prevented inadvertent fortune of Haman's lottery making chosen date good fortune/protection. Sources: Likutei Diburim 371b, Megillah 12a (party), Torah Ohr 91b (no slips), Ethics 3:8 (responsibility), Megillah 12b (measure for measure). # [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] "Haman's Gallows" - Ki Sisa Sermon

## Note: Purim Content (Not Chanukah)

**Title:** Ki Sisa Sermon: "Haman's Gallows"

**Parshat Connection:** Ki Sisa (contains account of Golden Calf and Abraham's tree)

**Theme:** Mystical significance of fifty cubits and Abraham's tree

---

## The Story: Haman's Growing Hatred

### Initial Plan

**Original Intention:**
- Have Mordechai killed with rest of Jewish people
- 11 months later
- After his plan executed

---

### Venom Grows

**Haman's Complaint to Zeresh:**
> "And Haman said, 'Esther did not even bring [anyone] to the party that she made, except me, and tomorrow, too, I am invited to her with the king. But all this is worth nothing to me, every time I see Mordechai the Jew sitting in the king's gate.'"

**Analysis:**
- Honored by queen exclusively
- Invited again tomorrow
- Yet all feels worthless
- Because sees Mordechai not bowing
- One thorn spoils entire bouquet

---

### Zeresh's Advice

**The Proposal:**
> "Let them make a gallows fifty cubits high, and in the morning say to the king that they should hang Mordechai on it, and go to the king to the banquet joyfully."

**Key Details:**
- Specific height: fifty cubits
- Act in morning (urgent)
- Then go joyfully to banquet
- Remove irritant immediately

---

## G-d's Response

### The Divine Reaction

**G-d's Statement:**
> "Said the Holy One, blessed be he, 'the tree [wood; gallows] shall not be, for Abraham already was first [with the tree] and said [to his guest, the three angels] "and you shall rest under the tree."'"

**Question:**
- "Under the tree?"
- Which tree?
- What's the reference?

---

## History of Abraham's Tree

### Abraham's Original Use

**At Beer Sheba:**
- Abraham brought tree with him
- Built guest house from it
- Called it "Eshel"

---

### Meaning of "Eshel"

**Acronym in Hebrew:**
- **Aleph:** Achila [a place to eat]
- **Shin:** Shtiya [a place to drink]
- **Lamed:** Linah [a place to sleep]

**Purpose:**
- Guest hospitality house
- Food, drink, lodging
- Service to travelers
- Acts of kindness

---

### Journey Through Generations

**Abraham to Jacob:**
- Abraham's grandson Jacob
- Brought tree to Egypt with him
- Told Jewish people
- Should bring tree when leave Egypt

**From Egypt to Wilderness:**
- Jews brought tree out of Egypt
- From this tree of Abraham
- Walls of Holy Temple built
- The Tabernacle in desert
- Mishkan structure

**Spiritual Continuity:**
- Abraham's kindness tree
- Becomes walls of G-d's dwelling
- Physical structure with spiritual heritage
- Hospitality becomes holiness

---

## G-d's Scoffing at Haman

### The Divine Argument

**G-d's Point:**
> "Thus, G-d scoffs at Haman, that long before Haman came to create a gallows with mystical powers, in order to be able to hang Mordechai, Abraham already utilized this mystical tree to serve G-d, with kindness to people, and from that Abraham's descendants built a House for G-d."

**Priority:**
- Abraham got there first
- Used tree for good
- Established pattern
- Kindness and holiness
- Haman too late

---

## Mystical Powers of Fifty Cubits

### The Question

**Why Fifty Cubits?**
- About seventy-five feet high!
- Absurdly tall for gallows
- Why does Zeresh advise this?
- Why does Haman listen?
- Why specifically fifty cubits?

---

### The Mystical Number Fifty

**Counting of Omer:**
- Jews commanded to prepare
- From when left Egypt
- For forty-nine days
- After which, on fiftieth day
- G-d revealed Himself
- Gave Ten Commandments
- Gave holy Torah

---

### Forty-Nine vs Fifty

**Forty-Nine:**
- 7 x 7
- Full measure of Finite Linear Light
- Manifesting through nature
- Of human psyche
- Clear description of right and wrong
- Good and evil defined

**On This Level:**
- Haman knows cannot obtain Heavenly permission
- For wicked to conquer righteous
- Clear moral categories
- Justice prevails

---

### The Fiftieth Gateway

**Transcendence:**
- Infinite Circular Light
- "G-d is everything and everything is G-d"
- All are equal
- No distinctions

**Haman's Strategy:**
> "Here, Haman provokes an Essence Light, beyond light and darkness, good and evil, and hopes to be able to conquer Mordechai."

**Haman's Hope:**
- Reach level beyond morality
- Where distinctions don't matter
- Where wicked equal to righteous
- Exploit divine transcendence
- Against divine justice

---

## Abraham's Preemptive Action

### G-d's Counter to Haman

**The Message:**
> "Thus, G-d tells Haman, that Haman is too late! For Abraham already evoked the magical Essence Light, and made sure to draw this light as well, into only Light and Goodness, cutting it off from Darkness and Evil."

**What Abraham Did:**
- Reached Fiftieth Gateway first
- Evoked Essence Light
- But channeled it exclusively
- Into Light and Goodness
- Cut off from Darkness and Evil
- Established precedent

**Implication:**
- Even transcendent level
- Serves only good
- Not available for evil
- Abraham's merit protects
- Haman cannot exploit it

---

## The Deepest Level

### Purim's Ultimate Lesson

**Summary:**
> "This is the story of Purim on its deepest level."

**The Challenge:**
> "We must reach into our depths, and even there where nothing matters anymore, we must make everything matter, with a commitment and conviction to Goodness, Kindness, and Light!"

---

### Understanding the Message

**Two Levels of Service:**

**Level of Forty-Nine:**
- Clear right and wrong
- Defined morality
- Obvious choices
- Natural service

**Level of Fifty:**
- Beyond definitions
- Transcendent realm
- Where distinctions blur
- "Nothing matters"

**Our Task:**
- Even at level where "nothing matters"
- Make everything matter
- Commitment remains
- Conviction to goodness
- Even in transcendence
- Choose light over darkness

---

## For Shluchim: Using This Sermon

### Audience

**Best For:**
- Intellectually sophisticated
- Interested in Kabbalah
- Seeking depth
- Comfortable with mysticism
- Advanced learners

**May Be Challenging For:**
- Beginners
- Those unfamiliar with Jewish concepts
- Literal thinkers
- Youth programs

---

### Key Teaching Points

**1. Abraham's Tree:**
- Physical object with spiritual history
- Kindness to holiness trajectory
- Multi-generational legacy
- Concrete symbol

**2. Fifty Cubits Significance:**
- Not random detail
- Deep mystical meaning
- Haman's strategy revealed
- Abraham's preemptive action

**3. Beyond Good and Evil:**
- Sophisticated concept
- Transcendent realm exists
- But must be channeled properly
- Cannot be exploited for evil

**4. Practical Application:**
- Even in our "beyond" moments
- When feel transcendent
- When normal rules seem irrelevant
- Must commit to goodness

---

### Sermon Structure

**Opening:**
- Tell story of Haman's growing hatred
- Zeresh's specific advice (fifty cubits - why?)
- Hook audience with mystery

**Development:**
- History of Abraham's tree
- Eshel and its meaning
- Journey through generations
- To Mishkan walls

**Climax:**
- Mystical significance of fifty
- Forty-nine vs fiftieth gateway
- Haman's strategy to exploit transcendence
- Abraham's preemptive channeling

**Conclusion:**
- We too must reach our depths
- Even where "nothing matters"
- Make everything matter
- Commitment to goodness, kindness, light

---

### Connections to Parshat Ki Sisa

**Why This Parsha?**
- Golden Calf episode
- Transcendent experience gone wrong
- Revelation without proper boundaries
- Resulted in idolatry

**Parallel:**
- Fiftieth gate improperly accessed
- Leads to spiritual danger
- Must be channeled correctly
- Abraham vs Haman example

**Moses' Role:**
- Brought them back from brink
- Re-established boundaries
- Like Abraham's precedent
- Goodness and holiness prevail

---

### Contemporary Application

**Modern "Fiftieth Gate" Experiences:**
- Spiritual transcendence
- Meditation states
- Flow experiences
- "Everything is one" feelings
- Beyond conventional morality feelings

**The Danger:**
- Thinking transcendence means
- Normal ethics don't apply
- "Anything goes" mentality
- Exploitation of spiritual states
- For selfish ends

**The Lesson:**
- Like Abraham
- Channel transcendence
- Into goodness and kindness
- Not moral relativism
- But moral absolutism at all levels

---

### Discussion Questions

**For Advanced Class:**
1. What does it mean that G-d is everything and everything is G-d?
2. How can transcendence be both true and dangerous?
3. Why did Abraham's use of the tree prevent Haman's?
4. What are modern equivalents of Haman's gallows?
5. How do we make "everything matter" when "nothing matters"?

---

## Related Resources

**In This Collection:**
- File 1057: "Hadassah and Esther" (detailed Kabbalistic class)
- File 1065: "Remember or Not Know" (depth of soul teaching)
- File 1066: "Divine Curveball" (hidden miracles)
- File 1067: "Reversal of Assimilation" (Likutei Diburim)

**Similar Themes:**
- Mystical dimensions of Purim
- Abraham's merit protecting Jews
- Fiftieth gate concepts
- Transcendence and morality

---

**Bottom Line:**

Ki Sisa sermon "Haman's Gallows" exploring mystical significance of fifty cubits height. **Story:** Haman initially planned kill Mordechai with all Jews 11 months later but venom grew - complained to wife Zeresh "Esther invited only me to party and tomorrow again but all this worth nothing to me every time I see Mordechai the Jew sitting in king's gate"; Zeresh advised "make gallows fifty cubits high, in morning say to king hang Mordechai on it, go to banquet joyfully" (specific height fifty cubits about 75 feet absurdly tall - why?). **G-d's response:** "Said Holy One blessed be He 'tree shall not be for Abraham already was first with tree and said to guests under the tree'" - which tree? **Abraham's tree history:** At Beer Sheba Abraham brought tree and built guest house called "Eshel" (acronym in Hebrew: Aleph=Achila place to eat, Shin=Shtiya place to drink, Lamed=Linah place to sleep) for hospitality service to travelers acts of kindness; Abraham's grandson Jacob brought tree to Egypt telling Jews should bring when leave Egypt, and from this tree of Abraham the walls of Holy Temple (Mishkan/Tabernacle) in desert were built (spiritual continuity from Abraham's kindness tree becoming walls of G-d's dwelling, hospitality becomes holiness). **G-d scoffs at Haman:** "Long before Haman came to create gallows with mystical powers to hang Mordechai, Abraham already utilized this mystical tree to serve G-d with kindness to people and from that Abraham's descendants built House for G-d" (Abraham got there first establishing pattern of kindness/holiness, Haman too late). **Mystical fifty:** Jews commanded prepare from leaving Egypt for 49 days then on 50th day G-d revealed Himself giving Ten Commandments and Torah; **49 = 7x7** full measure of Finite Linear Light manifesting through nature of human psyche with clear description right/wrong (on this level Haman knows cannot obtain Heavenly permission for wicked conquer righteous with clear moral categories where justice prevails); **50th Gateway** is Infinite Circular Light where "G-d is everything and everything is G-d" with all equal no distinctions - "here Haman provokes Essence Light beyond light/darkness good/evil and hopes to conquer Mordechai" by reaching level beyond morality where distinctions don't matter where wicked equal righteous exploiting divine transcendence against divine justice. **Abraham's preemptive action:** "G-d tells Haman that Haman too late! Abraham already evoked magical Essence Light and made sure to draw this light as well into only Light and Goodness cutting it off from Darkness and Evil" - Abraham reached 50th Gateway first evoking Essence Light but channeled exclusively into Light/Goodness cut off from Darkness/Evil establishing precedent (even transcendent level serves only good not available for evil, Abraham's merit protects, Haman cannot exploit). **Deepest level:** "This is story of Purim on its deepest level - we must reach into our depths and even there where nothing matters anymore we must make everything matter with commitment and conviction to Goodness, Kindness, and Light!" Teaching even at level 50 where "nothing matters" beyond definitions in transcendent realm where distinctions blur, we must make everything matter with commitment remaining and conviction to goodness - even in transcendence choose light over darkness. Related: File 1057 (Hadassah Kabbalistic class), 1065 (Remember soul depth), 1066 (Divine Curveball), 1067 (Assimilation reversal). Note: This Purim sermon appears in Chanukah directory.

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] "First Impressions" - Purim Teaching

## Note: Purim Content (Not Chanukah)

**Author:** [REDACTED-NAME], [REDACTED-LOCATION]

**Posted:** Thu Mar 14, 2019 22:31 pm ET

**Subject:** Purim - First Impressions

**Theme:** Identity, leadership, and living up to one's appearance

---

## Opening: Textual Question

### The Verse

**Biblical Text:**
> "There was a Jewish man in the capital city, Shushan, whose name was Mordechai the son of Yair, son of Shimi, son of Kish, a Benjamite, who had been exiled from Jerusalem" (Esther 2:5)

---

### The Writing Problem

**Structural Issue:**
> "If you were writing the Megilla and were about to introduce your leading man to the story, wouldn't you restructure that sentence?"

**Questions:**
- Was it really necessary to first inform of ethnicity and gender?
- And only then name?
- And only then pedigree?
- And only then where from?

**Normal Structure:**
- Introduce name
- Important bits of back-story
- Allow reader to infer identity
- Jewish male from context

---

## The Point: First Impressions

### What the Megilla Is Teaching

**The Message:**
> "But perhaps that's the point the Megilla is trying to make about this heroic character, responsible for saving his nation and transforming their sense of identity during this era of assimilation and anti-Semitism."

**Don't Assume:**
- Only reason he accomplished so much
- Was because of personal identity
- Family network
- Background

---

### What You Could See

**Before Knowing Specifics:**
> "When you first saw Mordechai walking the streets of Shushan you didn't know any specifics about him, but you could still tell who he was and exactly what he represented."

**Observable Identity:**
- He dressed like a Jew
- He acted like a Jew
- He strode the streets like a Jew
- He looked the part
- Lived up to expectations his appearance created

---

## Universal Leadership Principle

### Nobody Really Knows You

**Reality:**
> "Nobody really knows you. They don't understand your inner life or your innate abilities."

**How You're Judged:**
- They'll judge on results, eventually
- But first impression sets scene
- For tasks you'll be given
- For opportunities offered
- For respect accorded

---

### We Are All Called to Lead

**Opportunities:**
> "At times we are all called on to lead. There will be opportunities for every single one of us to serve."

**Resources We Draw On:**
- Faith will be useful
- Family will be useful
- Draw on reserves of strength
- Laid down in past

**The Uncertainty:**
> "But you never really know in advance when you'll be called."

---

### Can't Rely on Reputation

**The Challenge:**
> "You can't rely on your reputation and good name to get you through. You've got to walk the walk now so you can talk the talk when the time comes."

**Why:**
- Crisis comes unexpectedly
- No time to build reputation then
- Must already be established
- Through daily living

---

## The Call to Action

### Stand Straight

**The Directive:**
> "Stand straight. Walk proud. Act like a Jew and wait for the world to come calling."

**The Promise:**
> "The first impression you're making now will resonate in the memory of everyone who sees you out walking, so that when your time comes you'll be ready to step up to save your nation."

---

### Daily Preparation

**Constant State:**
- Not waiting for crisis
- Living identity daily
- Public and visible
- Consistent behavior

**Result:**
- When called
- Already known
- Already trusted
- Already respected
- Ready to lead

---

## Additional Articles Referenced

### Other Writings by Rabbi Greenbaum

**Listed:**
1. **Schmaltz** - "It wasn't always this way. Until relatively recently, fat was considered a delicacy."

2. **Never Say Sorry** - "There is a brewing political situation, which may or may not develop into a scandal. But it's the cover-up that sinks them every time..."

3. **Typesetting, Typecasting** - "The small *Alef* of our Parsha is counterpointed by another font change elsewhere in the Bible. The name 'Adam,' the first man and the personal handiwork of G-d, is written once with an oversize *Alef*"

4. **Hatred** - "Can Judaism condone hatred? Or perhaps the question really is -- does a failure to hate evil constitute a tacit approval of its existence?"

**Topic Range:**
- Vayikra topics
- Zachor topics
- Purim topics
- Various Jewish themes
- Contemporary issues

---

## For Shluchim: Using This Teaching

### Target Audience

**Ideal For:**
- Young professionals
- College students
- Those concerned with image
- Career-oriented individuals
- Modern Orthodox
- Baalei teshuva
- Anyone in public roles

**Why Effective:**
- Speaks to modern concerns
- Identity and authenticity
- Professional image
- Leadership development
- Practical application

---

### Key Messages

**1. Identity Is Visible:**
- Not just internal
- Observable to others
- First thing people notice
- Before knowing details

**2. Live It Daily:**
- Can't fake when crisis comes
- Must be authentic now
- Consistency matters
- Preparation is daily

**3. Everyone Is a Leader:**
- Not just rabbis
- Not just communal professionals
- Every Jew has moments
- To lead and influence

**4. First Impressions Count:**
- Create opportunities
- Or close doors
- Set expectations
- Determine trust level

---

### Contemporary Applications

**Professional Settings:**
- Wear kippah at work
- Keep kosher visibly
- Leave early Friday
- Shabbat observance known
- Jewish calendar respected

**Social Settings:**
- Don't hide identity
- Explain Jewish practices
- Invite to Jewish events
- Share Jewish values
- Model Jewish life

**Public Spaces:**
- Walk with pride
- Jewish symbols visible
- Carry yourself with dignity
- Represent community well

---

### Discussion Questions

**For Classes:**
1. What does "acting like a Jew" mean today?
2. How do you balance fitting in and standing out?
3. When have you been called to lead unexpectedly?
4. What first impression do you make?
5. How can we prepare daily for moments of leadership?

---

### Sermon Structure

**Opening:**
- Read verse about Mordechai
- Point out unusual structure
- "Wouldn't you restructure this?"
- Audience relates to question

**Development:**
- Explain Megilla's point
- Visible identity came first
- Before knowing specifics
- People could tell who he was

**Application:**
- Nobody knows your inner life
- First impressions set stage
- We're all called to lead
- Can't rely on reputation alone

**Call to Action:**
- Stand straight
- Walk proud
- Act like a Jew
- Wait for world to call
- When moment comes, be ready

---

### Variations for Different Audiences

**Youth:**
- Peer pressure context
- School and sports
- Dating and relationships
- Career choices

**Adults:**
- Professional integrity
- Family leadership
- Community involvement
- Public representation

**Seniors:**
- Legacy and example
- Grandchildren watching
- Lifetime consistency
- Passing torch

---

### Challenges to Address

**Common Objections:**

**"But I want to fit in"**
- Response: Standing out creates respect
- Those who hide invite contempt
- Authenticity attracts authentic relationships

**"It's not safe"**
- Response: Usually social pressure, not danger
- Mordechai faced actual death
- We face discomfort at most
- Context appropriate responses

**"I'm not a leader"**
- Response: Everyone leads sometimes
- Leading by example
- Small moments count
- Preparation for unexpected

---

### Related Themes

**From Megillah:**
- Esther's hidden identity (contrast)
- Mordechai's refusal to bow
- Public vs private observance
- Assimilation dangers

**From Other Sources:**
- Kiddush Hashem (sanctifying G-d's name)
- "Be a Jew at home and man on street" (critique)
- Pirsumei nisa (publicizing miracles)
- Light unto nations

---

## Related Resources

**In This Collection:**
- File 1067: "Reversal of Assimilation" (assimilation theme)
- File 1070: "My Jewish Identity" (similar identity theme by different author)
- Files 1059-1062: Mivtza Purim guidelines
- File 1057: "Hadassah and Esther" class

**External:**
- More Vayikra articles by Rabbi Greenbaum
- Zachor articles
- Purim teachings

---

**Bottom Line:**

"First Impressions" Purim teaching from [REDACTED-NAME], [REDACTED-LOCATION] (Mar 14, 2019) examining Esther 2:5 introduction of Mordechai: "There was a Jewish man in capital city Shushan whose name was Mordechai son of Yair son of Shimi son of Kish Benjamite who had been exiled from Jerusalem" - questioning unusual structure first informing ethnicity/gender then name/pedigree/origin when normal writing would introduce name and important back-story allowing reader infer Jewish male from context. **The Megilla's point:** Don't assume only reason he accomplished so much (saving nation, transforming identity during assimilation/anti-Semitism era) was because of personal identity/family network/background; "when you first saw Mordechai walking streets of Shushan you didn't know any specifics about him but could still tell who he was and exactly what he represented" - he dressed like Jew, acted like Jew, strode streets like Jew, looked the part, lived up to expectations his appearance created (observable identity before knowing details). **Universal leadership principle:** "Nobody really knows you, don't understand your inner life or innate abilities" - they'll judge on results eventually but first impression sets scene for tasks given/opportunities offered/respect accorded; "at times we are all called to lead, there will be opportunities for every single one of us to serve" drawing on faith/family/reserves of strength laid in past but "you never really know in advance when you'll be called" and "you can't rely on reputation and good name to get you through" because crisis comes unexpectedly with no time to build reputation then (must already be established through daily living). **Call to action:** "Stand straight, walk proud, act like a Jew and wait for world to come calling - first impression you're making now will resonate in memory of everyone who sees you out walking so when your time comes you'll be ready to step up to save your nation" (not waiting for crisis but living identity daily publicly/visibly with consistent behavior resulting in being already known/trusted/respected ready to lead when called). **Contemporary applications:** Professional settings (wear kippah at work, keep kosher visibly, leave early Friday, Shabbat observance known), social settings (don't hide identity, explain practices, invite to events, share values, model Jewish life), public spaces (walk with pride, Jewish symbols visible, carry with dignity, represent community well). Additional articles by Rabbi Greenbaum referenced: Schmaltz (fat as delicacy), Never Say Sorry (cover-up in scandal), Typesetting/Typecasting (small/oversize Alef), Hatred (can Judaism condone hatred). Related: File 1067 (assimilation reversal), 1070 (Jewish identity similar theme), 1059-1062 (Mivtza Purim guidelines), 1057 (Hadassah class). Note: This Purim teaching appears in Chanukah directory.
