# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Can You Have Your Chometz and Eat It? - Concise Study

## Note: Passover Content (Not Chanukah)

**Resource Type:** Condensed source study on mechiras chametz

**Purpose:** Shorter presentation format addressing selling chametz controversy

**Format:** Questions, sources, methods of acquisition

**Relationship:** Condensed version of comprehensive study (File 1093)

---

## Opening Question

**Title Question:**
> "Can you have your chometz and eat it?"

**Subtitle:**
> "Selling chometz, is it one big loophole?"

**Sets Up:**
- Direct, provocative question
- Common perception
- Need for answers

---

## The Controversy

**Five Objections:**

**1. Sale seems contrived**
- Are we dodging Torah directive?

**2. Doesn't leave residence**
- "The chametz does not leave the owner's residence"

**3. Purchaser uninterested**
- "The purchaser does not appear interested in actually taking possession of the chametz"

**4. No access required**
- "Rarely, if ever, does the seller have to open his doors and cabinets to the new owner of his food"

**5. Automatic reversion**
- "The chometz invariably reverts to its original ownership immediately after Pesach"

---

## Introduction: The Chametz Issue

### Torah Prohibitions

**Three Key Verses:**

> "For seven days fermented dough shall not be found in your homes..."
> — Shemos 12:19

> "For seven days you shall eat Matza, but on the first day you shall destroy fermented dough from your houses…"
> — Shemos 12:15

> "You shall eat matzos for seven days, and you may not see any chametz and you may not see any fermented dough in all your borders…"
> — Shemos 13:7

---

### Rambam: Severity of Violation

**Punishment:**
> "If one had chametz in one's possession before Pesach, and did not destroy it before Pesach, but left it in his possession… he is given lashes…"

**Permanent Prohibition:**
> "Chometz that remains in a Jew's possession over Pesach may never be used by a Jew for any beneficial purpose."
> — Rambam, Laws of Chometz & Matzah 1:3-4

**Shulchan Aruch:**
> "It is prohibited to benefit from chametz that belonged to a Jew over Pesach…"
> — Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 448:3

---

### A Non-Jew's Chometz - The Key

**Cannot Hide Your Own:**
> "It is written in the Torah: 'No leavened bread shall be seen with you' (Exodus 13:7). One might suppose that a man commits no transgression if he hides the cḥometz or deposits it with a non-Jew; the Torah therefore says plainly: 'No leaven shall be found in your houses' (Exodus 12:19), even if he has deposited or hidden it."

**Critical Exception:**
> "Chometz that… belonged to a non-Jew and was in a Jew's possession, even if it is in the Jew's house, is permitted because it doesn't belong to him."
> — Rambam, Laws of Chometz & Matzah 4:1-2

**Principle:**
- Ownership matters, not location
- Cannot merely deposit
- Non-Jew's chametz permitted in your house

---

## Questions for Consideration

**Six Key Questions:**

**1.** "If the Torah says we must rid our homes of chometz, can a Rabbinic loophole override it?"

**2.** "Can you retain chometz that you don't own on your property?"

**3.** "Is it considered a genuine transaction to 'sell' an item to someone who will never collect it from you/ take possession of it?"

**4.** "Is it practical to expect the non-Jew to come collect the chometz he has bought from all of us? Could that invalidate the process?"

**5.** "Is it legit to sell something that you really want back?"

**6.** "If the Torah prescribes a means of transaction that is not recognized by secular law, can we use that means of transaction to transact with a non-Jew, who is not bound by Torah law?"

---

## Precedent for the Chometz Sale

### Talmudic Permission

> "During the time that it is permitted to eat, one can… sell to the gentile."
> — Talmud, Pesachim 21a

> "If one gave the chometz to a gentile before noon [on erev Pesach], one need not destroy it."
> — Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 445:2

---

### The Yochanan Chakuka'a Incident

**Emergency Sale:**

Person deposited saddlebag with chametz with Yochanan Chakuka'a, mice bore hole, chametz spilling out.

Came to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi on erev Pesach morning:
- Hours 1-4: "Wait" (owner might return)
- Hour 5 (before prohibition): "Go and sell it in the market"

**Source:** Talmud, Pesachim 13a

---

### Tosefta: Travelers on Boat

> "If a Jew and gentile were traveling by boat [such that there is no means of replenishing one's food stock after the holiday] and there is chametz in the hands of the Jew: He may sell it to the gentile or give it as a gift, and subsequently repurchase it from him after Pesach."
> — Tosefta, Pesachim 2:12

---

### Shulchan Aruch: Even Knowing It Will Return

**Critical Ruling:**
> "If he sold it or gave it to a Jew outside of his home before Pesach, even though the Jewish seller knows that the gentile will not touch the chametz at all until after Pesach, and afterwards, he will return the chametz, it is permitted, so long as the Jew gave it as a complete gift without any stipulation."
> — Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 448:3

**Key:** Unconditional gift, even knowing it returns

---

### Kitzur Shulchan Aruch: Wholehearted Sale

> "…one who has much chometz, and cannot get rid of it all, needs to sell it to a gentile before Pesach…"

> "…this sale should not be simply by rote, rather one should have in mind to sell wholeheartedly… literally like a merchant (would)."
> — Kitzur Shulchan Aruch, 114:1

---

## Is It a Farce If You Expect to Get Your Chometz Back?

### Rabbi Yosef Caro

> "I don't understand his reservation, considering that [the Talmud] permits giving chometz to a gentile as a gift, when one will ask the gentile to re-gift it back after Pesach. Surely, this is blatantly deceitful [i.e. a major loophole], yet [the Talmud] permitted it, because he will remove the chometz from his possession."
> — Beis Yosef, Orach Chaim 445

**Talmud explicitly permits despite seeming like loophole**

---

### Vilna Gaon - Stricter View

> "One should not sell chometz, unless one intends for the sale to be permanent. After Pesach, one should not purchase baked goods from flour that was stored over Pesach or whiskey that was stored over Pesach, as the sale is unreliable…"
> — Ma'aseh Rav, Siddur of the Vilna Gaon 180-1

---

### Bechor Shor - Limited Scope

> "Selling chometz cannot override the Torah prohibition and, therefore, can only help with chometz that one has already nullified [which is only a Rabbinic prohibition]."
> — Rabbi Alexander Sender Shor, Bechor Shor on Pesachim 21b

---

### Rav Amram Gaon - Conditions

> "A Jew who sold his chometz to a gentile, or gave it to him as an unconditional gift, if the gentile [acquired the chometz as he] moved it and there is no intention to deceive and he would not do this during the rest of the year… the Jew may repurchase such chometz from the gentile after Pesach. The reason being that the gentile moved the chometz, so it is in his possession and chometz in a gentile's possession over Pesach is permitted to a Jew after Pesach."
> — Rav Amram Gaon, Otzar HaGeonim, Pesachim 48

---

### Evolution of Practice

**Terumas HaDeshen:**
> "One should instruct them to give the‎‏ ‏chametz to the non-‎Jew outside the‏ ‏house."
> — Terumas Hadeshen, 119

**Bach - Selling the Room:**
> "In this land, where most commerce is in‏ ‏whisky and one cannot sell it to a non- Jew outside the ‎home, and especially for‏ ‏those who hold a license for selling‏ ‏liquor, there is room to permit sale to ‎a‏ ‏non-Jew of all chametz in the room, as‏ ‏well as the room itself.‎"
> — Bach, Orach Chaim 448:2

**Kitzur Shulchan Aruch:**
> "The chometz that you sell to a gentile should not remain in the Jew's home… if the gentile is unable to take the chometz to his own home, the Jew must rent the room where the chometz is stored to the gentile."
> — Kitzur Shulchan Aruch 114:2

---

### Chasam Sofer - Full Legal Sale

> "The contrived sale [mentioned in the Tosefta] is completely permitted by Torah, without any qualms, because the Jew sells his chometz as a full legal sale to the gentile, despite them both knowing that the Jew wants to reclaim the chometz after Pesach. In spite of this, at the moment, the chometz is fully sold to the gentile, who may sell it, eat it, donate it or dispose of it without restraint. It is only because the gentile likes his Jewish friend that he retains the chometz until after Pesach."
> — Responsa, Chasam Sofer Orach Chaim 113

**At the moment: Full legal sale with complete rights**

---

## What Method of Sale Works?

### Torah Sources on Acquisition

**Biblical Verse:**
> "When you sell merchandise to your compatriot, or purchase from the hand of your compatriot, do not overcharge a man to his brother."
> — Vayikra 25:14

**Talmudic Debate:**
- Rabbi Yochanan: "Coins acquire according to Torah law"
- Reish Lakish: "Meshicha (pulling the item) is explicit in the Torah"
- Verse: "from the hand of your compatriot" - hand to hand transfer

**Source:** Bava Metzia 47b

---

### For Gentiles

> "If one wishes to sell an animal to a gentile in order to exempt it from the first-born obligations, the gentile must pay for it with money in addition to pulling it by hand."
> — Tosfos, Avodah Zarah 71a

**Requires both payment and physical transfer**

---

## Acquiring Through Property

**Kinyan Chatzer:**
> "A person's courtyard acquires for him (even) without his knowledge. Even if he is not standing there, as soon as a gift enters his property, it is as if someone else had claimed the gift on his behalf."
> — Rambam, Laws of Ownerless Property & Gifts 4:9

**The Problem:**
- One opinion: Chatzer extended from hand
- Other opinion: Chatzer functions like agent (shliach)
- But: "A gentile may not act as an agent for a Jew for any issue" (Rambam, Laws of Agents 2:1)

**Issue:** If chatzer works through agency, won't work for gentile

---

## Acquiring Through Exchange

**Biblical Source:**
> "And this was the custom in Israel regarding sale and exchange… a man shall take off his shoe and hand to his friend, and this was the proof in Israel."
> — Ruth 4:7

**The Problem:**
> "Acquiring through exchange is not binding for a gentile."
> — Sifsei Cohen, Choshen Mishpat 123:30

---

## The Situmta Method

**Talmudic Source:**
> "This Situmta acquires. For what purpose?... In a place where this is used to actually acquire, it acquires."
> — Bava Metzia 74a

**Two Explanations:**

**Rashi:**
> "Situmta means a label that was marked onto the wine merchant's barrels to indicate that a customer had purchased this part of his inventory."

**Rabbeinu Chananel:**
> "Situmta is a handshake (or any other locally recognised act) that merchants commonly do to indicate the closing of a deal."

**Question:**
> "Consider this: How have diamond dealers typically closed their deals? Is this relevant in other industries?"

---

## The Practical Method

### Kinyan Agav (Acquisition Via Land)

> "Rabba said: If the debtor transferred movable property to the creditor as liened property by means of an acquisition of land, the creditor acquires the land and acquires the movable property, i.e., a lien is created with regard to both."
> — Talmud, Bava Basra 44b

---

### Requirements

**Kitzur Shulchan Aruch:**
> "One must write the name of the buyer, the price, and that he acquires the chometz by way of renting the [section of the] property… one must discuss the contents of the sale agreement verbally as well, and the buyer must pay a down payment and the document must include a commitment that the buyer will pay the remainder of the purchase value."
> — Kitzur Shulchan Aruch, 114:2

**Mishneh Berurah:**
> "The chometz sale should conform to local (secular) law."
> — Mishneh Berurah 448:17/9

---

## But the Gentile Hasn't Paid in Full?

### Terumas HaDeshen

**Question:** Can give chometz to gentile knowing he won't touch it and will re-gift after Pesach?

**Response:**
> "It would seem that this is permitted, as long as he gives the chometz to the gentile wholeheartedly, without reservation or conditions or if he sells the chometz to the gentile for a nominal amount."
> — Responsa, Terumas HaDeshen 1:120

**Nominal amount sufficient**

---

### Talmudic Precedent

> "Consider a case where Reuven sold a field to Shimon with a guarantee that if it is repossessed he will compensate Shimon for his loss. Shimon did not pay for the purchase, and instead set up the value of the field as a loan by writing a promissory note for this amount."
> — Talmud, Kesuvos 92a

**Payment can be structured as loan**

---

## Important Considerations for the Sale

### Partitioning

> "If one needs to use any of the rooms where the chometz is housed, one must make a partition in front of the chometz and sell the partitioned section… and note in the sale agreement that the gentile has free access to the area where the chometz is housed and that he remains entitled to on-sell the chometz to another gentile over Pesach."
> — Kitzur Shulchan Aruch, 114:4

---

### No Re-Sale Condition

> "One may not include a clause, as a condition of sale, that the gentile must re-sell the chometz to its original owner after Pesach."
> — Kitzur Shulchan Aruch, 114:6

**Must be unconditional**

---

### Include Name and Address

> "The sale agreement should include the name of the seller and his address, so that the gentile could [theoretically] come claim his chometz over Pesach."
> — Mishneh Berurah 448:12

---

## Can You Sell Someone Else's Chometz?

> "One may sell chometz on behalf of someone who did not manage to sell theirs, because we are permitted to benefit someone without their knowledge."
> — Pischei Teshuvah, Yoreh Deah, 320:6, Siddur Pesach Kehilchoso, 11:7

---

## Can You Sell Your Chometz Online?

> "You don't sell your chometz online, you simply appoint the relevant rabbi as your agent to sell your chometz. This is essentially what we do when 'selling' our chometz 'to the rabbi'. The rabbi does not buy the chometz from the community, but acts as their agent to facilitate their sale of chometz."

> "One need not be in their presence to appoint someone as an agent."
> — Responsa, Rabbi Shmuel Eliyahu, Chief Rabbi of Tzfat

---

## Something to Think About

> "In 2006, the Chief Rabbi of the IDF landed up selling a few hundred dogs with the army's chometz. Any thoughts why he would have done this?"

**Reason:** Dog food contains chametz, must sell dogs with their food

---

## Do I Need Utensils to Mikveh?

> "Chometz that is in a container that would need to be immersed in the mikveh should not be sold to the gentile together with the container, because then one would need to immerse the container after buying the chometz back after Pesach."
> — Kitzur Shulchan Aruch, 114:2

**Solution:** Sell chametz only, not containers

---

- Quicker presentation

- File 1087: Common Passover questions

---

**Bottom Line:**

Condensed mechiras chametz source study with title question "Can you have your chometz and eat it? Selling chometz, is it one big loophole?" addressing five controversy objections: (1) Sale seems contrived dodging Torah directive; (2) Chametz doesn't leave owner's residence; (3) Purchaser not interested in taking possession; (4) Rarely if ever seller opens doors/cabinets to new owner; (5) Chometz invariably reverts to original ownership after Pesach. **Torah prohibitions:** Three verses (Shemos 12:19 "not be found in homes," 12:15 "destroy from houses," 13:7 "may not see in all borders"); Rambam teaches lashes for violation, chametz remaining in Jew's possession over Pesach may never be used for any beneficial purpose; critical exception: "Chometz that belonged to non-Jew and was in Jew's possession, even if in Jew's house, is permitted because doesn't belong to him" (Rambam Laws Chometz 4:1-2) - ownership matters not location. **Six key questions:** (1) Can Rabbinic loophole override Torah directive to rid homes; (2) Can retain chametz don't own on property; (3) Is it genuine transaction to sell item someone never collects/takes possession; (4) Is it practical expect non-Jew collect from all could that invalidate process; (5) Is it legit sell something really want back; (6) If Torah prescribes means of transaction not recognized by secular law can use with non-Jew not bound by Torah law. **Precedents:** Talmud Pesachim 21a "can sell to gentile," Yochanan Chakuka'a incident (emergency sale hour 5 before prohibition), Tosefta Pesachim 2:12 travelers on boat may sell/gift and repurchase after Pesach; **critical Shulchan Aruch ruling:** "If sold/gave to Jew outside home before Pesach, EVEN THOUGH Jewish seller knows gentile won't touch chametz at all until after Pesach and afterwards will return chametz, it is permitted, so long as Jew gave as complete gift without any stipulation" (OC 448:3) - unconditional gift even knowing it returns permitted. **Opinions on expecting chametz back:** Rabbi Yosef Caro defends "Talmud permits giving chametz to gentile as gift when will ask gentile re-gift back after Pesach, surely this blatantly deceitful yet Talmud permitted it because he will remove chometz from his possession" (Beis Yosef OC 445); Vilna Gaon stricter "should not sell chometz unless intends for sale to be permanent" (Ma'aseh Rav 180-1); Chasam Sofer "contrived sale completely permitted by Torah without any qualms because Jew sells as full legal sale to gentile despite both knowing Jew wants to reclaim, at the moment chometz is fully sold to gentile who may sell/eat/donate/dispose without restraint, only because gentile likes his Jewish friend retains until after Pesach" (Responsa OC 113) - full legal sale at moment with complete rights. **Evolution of practice:** Terumas HaDeshen give chametz to non-Jew outside house; Bach innovation "in this land where most commerce in whisky cannot sell outside home especially license holders, room to permit sale to non-Jew of all chametz in room as well as room itself" (OC 448:2); Kitzur SA "chometz you sell to gentile should not remain in Jew's home, if gentile unable to take to his home Jew must rent the room where chometz stored to gentile" (114:2). **Methods of acquisition (kinyan):** Torah debate whether coins (Rabbi Yochanan) or meshicha/pulling (Reish Lakish) acquires (Bava Metzia 47b); kinyan chatzer (courtyard acquires but problem: if works through agency won't work for gentile since gentile can't be agent per Rambam Laws Agents 2:1); kinyan chalipin/exchange not binding for gentile (Sifsei Cohen CM 123:30); kinyan situmta (customary mark/gesture like handshake that merchants do, Bava Metzia 74a - Rashi: label on wine barrels, Rabbeinu Chananel: handshake or locally recognized act, question: how diamond dealers close deals); **primary practical method:** Kinyan agav (Bava Basra 44b "if debtor transferred movable property to creditor by means of acquisition of land, creditor acquires land and acquires movable property") - acquire land/room and movable property/chametz acquired with it. **Requirements:** Kitzur SA 114:2 must write buyer's name/price/acquisition via renting property section, discuss verbally, buyer pay down payment, document includes commitment to pay remainder; Mishneh Berurah 448:17/9 "chometz sale should conform to local secular law." **Partial payment permitted:** Terumas HaDeshen 1:120 permits giving wholeheartedly without reservation/conditions or selling for nominal amount; Talmud Kesuvos 92a precedent of field sale where payment structured as loan with promissory note. **Important considerations:** If using room must partition chametz area noting gentile's free access and right to on-sell (Kitzur SA 114:4); cannot include clause as condition that gentile must re-sell to original owner after Pesach (Kitzur SA 114:6 - must be unconditional); sale agreement should include seller's name and address so gentile could theoretically come claim over Pesach (Mishneh Berurah 448:12). **Can sell someone else's chometz:** "One may sell on behalf of someone who did not manage to sell theirs because we are permitted to benefit someone without their knowledge" (Pischei Teshuvah YD 320:6). **Online sale:** "You don't sell chometz online, simply appoint relevant rabbi as your agent to sell - essentially what we do when 'selling' to the rabbi, rabbi does not buy from community but acts as their agent to facilitate their sale;" "one need not be in their presence to appoint agent" (Rabbi Shmuel Eliyahu Chief Rabbi Tzfat). **IDF dogs 2006:** Chief Rabbi sold few hundred dogs with army's chometz (dog food contains chametz must sell dogs with food). **Keilim/utensils:** "Chometz in container needing immersion in mikveh should not be sold to gentile together with container because then would need to immerse after buying back" (Kitzur SA 114:2) - solution: sell chametz only not containers. **Comparison to File 1093:** This version more condensed for quicker presentation with essential sources and key points highlighted (use for shorter classes, community presentations, quick reference, email/bulletin format); File 1093 comprehensive chavrusa guide with detailed historical development and extensive analysis for in-depth study/advanced learning/addressing detailed objections/scholarly presentations. Note: This Passover study appears in Chanukah directory.

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Passover Crash Course - Laws of Chametz

## Note: Passover Content (Not Chanukah)

**Resource Type:** Structured teaching outline

**Date:** Tuesday, April 2, 2019

**Purpose:** Systematic presentation of chametz laws

**Format:** Numbered outline with Torah sources

**Audience:** Classes, shiurim, community education

---

## Opening Framework

**Course Title:** Passover Crash Course

**Topic:** Laws of Chametz

**Eight Major Categories:**

1. Prohibition to eat
2. Prohibition to derive benefit from
3. Prohibition to own and possess
4. Obligation to dispose of
5. Obligation to check for
6. Obligation to negate
7. Selling Chametz to Non-Jew
8. Chametz after Pesach

---

## 1. Prohibition to Eat Chametz

### a. On the 7 Days of Pesach

**Source:** Exodus 13.3

**Duration:** All seven days of Passover

---

### b. After Noon of the Eve of Pesach

**Source:** Deuteronomy 16.3

**Biblical Prohibition:** From noon on erev Pesach

---

### c. Late Morning

**Status:** Rabbinical Prohibition

**Extends:** Beyond Biblical minimum

---

### d. After Pesach

**Status:** Rabbinical Prohibition

**Applies To:** Chametz that was in a Jew's possession over Pesach

**Reason:** Penalty for violation during Pesach

---

### e. As a Mixture with Other Foods

**Source:** Exodus 12.20

**Scope:** Even mixed with permitted foods

---

### f. Even a Minute Amount

**Standard:** No minimum quantity

**Strictness:** Any amount prohibited

---

## 2. Prohibition to Derive Benefit from Chametz

### a. Source

**Biblical Verse:** Exodus 13.3

**Derivation:** "It shall not be eaten"

**Expanded Meaning:** Not just eating, but all benefit

---

### b. On Pesach

**Applies:** Throughout Passover

---

### c. After Noon of the Eve of Pesach

**Biblical Level:** From noon onwards

---

### d. Late Morning

**Status:** Rabbinical Prohibition

**Earlier Restriction:** Before Biblical prohibition begins

---

## 3. Prohibition to Own or Possess Chametz During Passover

### a. First Source

**Verse:** Exodus 12.19

**Language:** "Shall not be found"

---

### b. Second Source

**Verse:** Exodus 13.7

**Language:** "Shall not be seen"

---

### c. Two Prohibitions

**Distinct Commandments:**
- Not to be found (bal yimatzei)
- Not to be seen (bal yeira'eh)

**Two separate negative commandments**

---

### d. Biblical Prohibition; Safeguard?

**Question:** Is this Biblical or Rabbinical safeguard?

**Status:** Biblical-level prohibition

---

### e. Yours, Not Others

**Key Distinction:** "Shall not be seen **of yours**"

**Implication:** Others' chametz permitted

**Application:** Non-Jew's chametz may be in your house

---

### f. Chametz, Not Non-Edible

**Scope:** Applies to edible chametz

**Non-edible:** Different status

---

## 4. Obligation to Dispose of Chametz Before Pesach

### a. Source

**Verse:** Exodus 12.15

**Command:** "Destroy fermented dough from your houses"

---

### b. When: When Prohibited or Before Prohibition?

**Question:** Timing of disposal obligation

**Options:**
- When chametz becomes prohibited
- Before prohibition begins

---

### c. How: Toss, Burn, etc.

**Methods:**
- Tossing
- Burning
- Other means of disposal

**Flexibility:** Various methods permitted

---

### d. Passive or Active

**Question:** Must one actively destroy?

**Or:** Can one passively abandon?

**Distinction:** Active disposal vs. passive removal

---

### e. Why Burn: Like Leftover Sacrifice

**Comparison:** Exodus 12.10

**Parallel:** Like leftover Pesach sacrifice

**Method:** Burning preferred like sacrifice remains

---

### f. What's Done Today

**Modern Practice:**
- Symbolic burning
- Sale to non-Jew
- Combination approach

---

## 5. Obligation to Check for Chametz - Bedikat Chametz

### a. Biblical Mitzvah as Part of Disposing

**Source:** Part of disposal obligation

**Level:** Biblical commandment

---

### b. Blessing on Checking: Disposing of Chametz

**Blessing Formula:** "...al biur chametz"

**Language:** On **disposing** of chametz (not on checking)

**Why:** Checking is means to disposal end

---

### c. When Only Rabbinically Required: Two Reasons

**Sometimes Reduced to Rabbinic Level**

**Two Possible Reasons:**
1. Already disposed of visible chametz
2. Sale makes possession Rabbinic issue

---

### d. When: Night Before Pesach

**Timing:** Night of 14th of Nissan

**Why Night:** Can search thoroughly with candle

---

### e. If One Leaves Their Home Before the Night Before Passover

**Early Departure:** Special procedures

**Timing Adjustment:** Search before leaving

**Considerations:** When to search if traveling

---

## 6. Obligation to Abandon Chametz - Bitul Chametz

### a. In Order Not to Possess

**Purpose:** Remove ownership status

**Effect:** "It's not mine" - mental abandonment

---

### b. In Case One Finds Good Chametz on Pesach

**Safeguard:** If valuable chametz discovered

**Human Nature:** Hard to destroy valuable food

**Solution:** Pre-nullified means no temptation

---

### c. As a Method of Disposing

**Alternative:** Instead of physical disposal

**Or Supplement:** In addition to disposal

---

### d. When: Night of Checking and When Burning

**Two Times:**
1. After bedikat chametz (night before)
2. After burning chametz (morning before)

**Two Declarations:** Different formulas

---

### e. How

**Method:** Verbal declaration

**Formula:** "All chametz in my possession..."

**Language:** Can be in any understood language

---

## 7. Selling Chametz to Non-Jew

### a. Talmud: Sell and Remove from Possession

**Source:** Talmudic permission

**Purpose:** Remove from possession

**Effect:** No longer "yours"

---

### b. Institutionalized to Sell: Approximately 600 Years Ago

**Historical Development:** Around 1400s

**Context:** European Jewish distilleries

**Economic Necessity:** Cannot destroy stock

**Timeline:** ~600 years of formal practice

---

### c. Communal Selling of Chametz via Rabbi: Last 250 Years

**Recent Development:** Last ~250 years

**Method:** Rabbi as community agent

**Terms:** Full price, debt structure

**Modern Form:** What we do today

---

## 8. Chametz After Passover

### a. Rabbinical Prohibition

**Status:** Chametz that was Jewish-owned over Pesach

**Level:** Rabbinic prohibition (not Biblical)

**Reason:** Penalty for violation

**Effect:** Permanently forbidden

---

### b. How It's Done Today

**Modern Practice:**
- Avoid purchasing from Jewish stores immediately after
- Check sources
- Rely on sale mechanism
- Community standards

---

## Maimonides Introduction

### Eight Mitzvot Framework

**Rambam's Count:**

**Three Positive Commandments:**
1. [Eat matzah]
2. [Tell the story]
3. [Dispose of chametz]

**Five Negative Commandments:**
1. Not to eat chametz
2. Not to eat mixtures with chametz
3. Not to see chametz
4. Not to find chametz
5. [One more negative]

**Total:** Eight mitzvot related to chametz and matzah

---

## Torah Sources - Full Text

### Exodus 12:15

**Hebrew:**
> טו שִׁבְעַ֤ת יָמִים֙ מַצּ֣וֹת תֹּאכֵ֔לוּ אַ֚ךְ בַּיּ֣וֹם הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן תַּשְׁבִּ֥יתוּ שְּׂאֹ֖ר מִבָּֽתֵּיכֶ֑ם כִּ֣י | כָּל־אֹכֵ֣ל חָמֵ֗ץ וְנִכְרְתָ֞ה הַנֶּ֤פֶשׁ הַהִוא֙ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִיּ֥וֹם הָֽרִאשֹׁ֖ן עַד־י֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִעִֽי:

**Translation:**
> "For seven days you shall eat unleavened cakes, but on the preceding day you shall clear away all leaven from your houses, for whoever eats leaven from the first day until the seventh day that soul shall be cut off from Israel"

**Key Points:**
- Seven days matzah
- Clear away leaven
- Punishment: Karet (spiritual excision)
- Timeframe: First through seventh day

---

### Exodus 12:17

**Hebrew:**
> יזוּשְׁמַרְתֶּם֘ אֶת־הַמַּצּוֹת֒ כִּ֗י בְּעֶ֨צֶם֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אֶת־צִבְאֽוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֞ם אֶת־הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֛ה לְדֹרֹֽתֵיכֶ֖ם חֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָֽם:

**Translation:**
> "And you shall watch over the unleavened cakes, for on this very day I have taken your legions out of the land of Egypt, and you shall observe this day throughout your generations, [as] an everlasting statute."

**Key Points:**
- Guard the matzot
- Commemorate the Exodus
- Eternal statute
- For all generations

---

### Exodus 12:19

**Hebrew:**
> יטשִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים שְׂאֹ֕ר לֹ֥א יִמָּצֵ֖א בְּבָֽתֵּיכֶ֑ם כִּ֣י | כָּל־אֹכֵ֣ל מַחְמֶ֗צֶת וְנִכְרְתָ֞ה הַנֶּ֤פֶשׁ הַהִוא֙ מֵֽעֲדַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּגֵּ֖ר וּבְאֶזְרַ֥ח הָאָֽרֶץ:

**Translation:**
> "For seven days, leavening shall not be found in your houses, for whoever eats leavening that soul shall be cut off from the community of Israel, both among the strangers and the native born of the land."

**Key Points:**
- Leaven not found (bal yimatzei)
- Seven days
- Punishment: Karet
- Applies to convert and native-born

---

### Exodus 12:20

**Hebrew:**
> ככָּל־מַחְמֶ֖צֶת לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֑לוּ בְּכֹל֙ מֽוֹשְׁבֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם תֹּֽאכְל֖וּ מַצּֽוֹת:

**Translation:**
> "You shall not eat any leavening; throughout all your dwellings you shall eat unleavened cakes."

**Key Points:**
- No leavening at all
- All your dwellings
- Positive: Eat matzot

---

### Exodus 13:3

**Hebrew:**
> גוַיֹּ֨אמֶר משֶׁ֜ה אֶל־הָעָ֗ם זָכ֞וֹר אֶת־הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְצָאתֶ֤ם מִמִּצְרַ֨יִם֙ מִבֵּ֣ית עֲבָדִ֔ים כִּ֚י בְּחֹ֣זֶק יָ֔ד הוֹצִ֧יא יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִזֶּ֑ה וְלֹ֥א יֵֽאָכֵ֖ל חָמֵֽץ:

**Translation:**
> "Moses said to the people, 'Remember this day, when you went out of Egypt, out of the house of bondage, for with a mighty hand, the Lord took you out of here, and [therefore] no leaven shall be eaten.'"

**Key Points:**
- Remember the Exodus
- From house of bondage
- With mighty hand
- Therefore: No chametz eaten

---

### Exodus 13:7

**Hebrew:**
> זמַצּוֹת֙ יֵֽאָכֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֑ים וְלֹא־יֵֽרָאֶ֨ה לְךָ֜ חָמֵ֗ץ וְלֹא־יֵֽרָאֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ שְׂאֹ֖ר בְּכָל־גְּבֻלֶֽךָ:

**Translation:**
> "Unleavened cakes shall be eaten during the seven days, and no leaven shall be seen of yours [in your possession], and no leavening shall be seen of yours throughout all of your borders"

**Key Points:**
- Matzot for seven days
- No chametz seen "of yours" (bal yeira'eh)
- No leavening seen "of yours"
- Throughout borders

---

### Deuteronomy 16:2

**Hebrew:**
> בוְזָבַ֥חְתָּ פֶּ֛סַח לַֽיהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ צֹ֣אן וּבָקָ֑ר בַּמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִבְחַ֣ר יְהֹוָ֔ה לְשַׁכֵּ֥ן שְׁמ֖וֹ שָֽׁם:

**Translation:**
> "You shall slaughter the Passover sacrifice to the Lord, your God, [of the] flock, and [the Festival sacrifices of the] cattle, in the place which the Lord will choose to establish His Name therein"

**Key Points:**
- Pesach sacrifice
- Flock and cattle
- Designated place
- Where Hashem's Name dwells

---

### Deuteronomy 16:3

**Hebrew:**
> גלֹֽא־תֹאכַ֤ל עָלָיו֙ חָמֵ֔ץ שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֛ים תֹּֽאכַל־עָלָ֥יו מַצּ֖וֹת לֶ֣חֶם עֹ֑נִי כִּ֣י בְחִפָּז֗וֹן יָצָ֨אתָ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לְמַ֣עַן תִּזְכֹּ֗ר אֶת־י֤וֹם צֵֽאתְךָ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיֶּֽיךָ:

**Translation:**
> "You shall not eat leaven with it; for seven days you shall eat with it matzoth, the bread of affliction, for in haste you went out of the land of Egypt, so that you shall remember the day when you went out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life."

**Key Points:**
- Don't eat chametz with it
- Seven days of matzah
- "Bread of affliction"
- Reason: Left in haste
- Remember all your life

---

### Deuteronomy 16:4

**Hebrew:**
> דוְלֹא־יֵֽרָאֶ֨ה לְךָ֥ שְׂאֹ֛ר בְּכָל־גְּבֻֽלְךָ֖ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים וְלֹֽא־יָלִ֣ין מִן־הַבָּשָׂ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּזְבַּ֥ח בָּעֶ֛רֶב בַּיּ֥וֹם הָֽרִאשׁ֖וֹן לַבֹּֽקֶר:

**Translation:**
> "And no leaven shall be seen with you within all your border for seven days; neither shall any of the flesh you slaughter on the preceding day in the afternoon, remain all night until the morning."

**Key Points:**
- No leaven throughout borders
- Seven days
- Pesach sacrifice meat
- Not left overnight

**Bottom Line:**

Passover Crash Course outline on Laws of Chametz dated Tuesday April 2, 2019, providing systematic presentation in eight major categories: **(1) Prohibition to eat chametz** covering (a) on 7 days of Pesach (Exodus 13.3), (b) after noon of eve of Pesach (Deuteronomy 16.3 Biblical prohibition), (c) late morning (Rabbinical prohibition), (d) after Pesach (Rabbinical prohibition for chametz that was in Jew's possession over Pesach as penalty), (e) as mixture with other foods (Exodus 12.20), (f) even minute amount (no minimum quantity any amount prohibited). **(2) Prohibition to derive benefit from chametz** with (a) source Exodus 13.3 "it shall not be eaten" expanded meaning not just eating but all benefit, (b) on Pesach, (c) after noon of eve of Pesach (Biblical level), (d) late morning (Rabbinical prohibition earlier restriction). **(3) Prohibition to own or possess chametz during Passover** with (a) Exodus 12.19 "shall not be found" (bal yimatzei), (b) Exodus 13.7 "shall not be seen" (bal yeira'eh), (c) two distinct negative commandments, (d) Biblical-level prohibition, (e) "of yours" not others (key distinction: others' chametz permitted, non-Jew's chametz may be in your house), (f) chametz not non-edible (applies to edible chametz). **(4) Obligation to dispose of chametz before Pesach** with (a) source Exodus 12.15 "destroy fermented dough from your houses," (b) timing question when prohibited or before prohibition, (c) methods: toss/burn etc with flexibility various methods permitted, (d) passive or active (active disposal vs passive removal distinction), (e) why burn: like leftover sacrifice (Exodus 12.10 burning preferred like sacrifice remains), (f) modern practice: symbolic burning, sale to non-Jew, combination approach. **(5) Obligation to check for chametz - Bedikat Chametz** with (a) Biblical mitzvah as part of disposing, (b) blessing on checking "al biur chametz" (on DISPOSING not on checking because checking is means to disposal end), (c) when only Rabbinically required two reasons (already disposed of visible chametz or sale makes possession Rabbinic issue), (d) timing night before Pesach (night of 14th Nissan why night: can search thoroughly with candle), (e) if one leaves home before night before Passover special procedures with timing adjustment search before leaving. **(6) Obligation to abandon chametz - Bitul Chametz** with (a) purpose to remove ownership status ("it's not mine" mental abandonment), (b) safeguard in case finds good/valuable chametz on Pesach (pre-nullified means no temptation), (c) as method of disposing (alternative or supplement), (d) two times: night of checking after bedikat chametz and when burning morning before (two declarations different formulas), (e) method: verbal declaration "all chametz in my possession" can be in any understood language. **(7) Selling Chametz to Non-Jew** with (a) Talmudic permission sell and remove from possession, (b) institutionalized to sell approximately 600 years ago (~1400s context: European Jewish distilleries economic necessity cannot destroy stock), (c) communal selling via rabbi last 250 years (recent development: rabbi as community agent, terms: full price debt structure, modern form what we do today). **(8) Chametz After Passover** (a) Rabbinical prohibition (chametz that was Jewish-owned over Pesach, Rabbinic level not Biblical, reason: penalty for violation, effect: permanently forbidden), (b) modern practice: avoid purchasing from Jewish stores immediately after, check sources, rely on sale mechanism, community standards. **Maimonides Introduction framework:** Eight mitzvot - three positive commandments and five negative commandments related to chametz and matzah. **Full Torah sources provided:** Exodus 12:15 ("seven days unleavened cakes, clear away leaven, punishment karet"), 12:17 ("watch over unleavened cakes, eternal statute for generations"), 12:19 ("leavening not found in houses seven days, applies to convert and native-born"), 12:20 ("not eat any leavening, all dwellings eat matzot"), 13:3 ("remember Exodus from house of bondage with mighty hand therefore no chametz eaten"), 13:7 ("matzot seven days, no chametz/leavening seen OF YOURS throughout borders"), Deuteronomy 16:2 (Pesach sacrifice flock/cattle at designated place), 16:3 ("don't eat chametz with it, seven days matzah bread of affliction, left in haste, remember all your life"), 16:4 ("no leaven throughout borders seven days, Pesach sacrifice meat not left overnight"). **For Shluchim teaching:** Eight clear categories numbered points with sub-points for detail in progressive complexity; course length options: single session 60-90 minutes overview, multi-session series (Session 1 prohibitions 1-3, Session 2 obligations 4-6, Session 3 practical 7-8), or in-depth one topic per session 8-week course; audience adaptations for beginners (focus main points skip complicated sub-questions practical emphasis), intermediate (all numbered points some sub-questions balance theory and practice), advanced (full outline with all questions, source texts in Hebrew, discuss ambiguities, Talmudic background); complement with Files 1093/1094 (mechiras chametz detail), 1091 (practical preparation), 1073 (resource links), 1087 (common questions) for sequential teaching. # [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Matzah Spiritual Significance - Teaching

## Note: Passover Content (Not Chanukah)

**Resource Type:** Spiritual/philosophical teaching on matzah

**Purpose:** Explain deeper meaning of matzah and Pesach

**Format:** Questions, concepts, included essay

**Audience:** Classes, divrei Torah, educational programming

---

## Opening Question from Haggadah

### The Text

> "This Matzah that we eat for what reason? Because the dough of our fathers did not have time to become leavened before the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself to them and redeemed them."

---

### The Problem

**It Seems So Insignificant:**
- Almost an accident?
- Just because they were rushing?
- We have Pesach because of this?

**The Question:**
> "There must be a spiritual idea behind the Matzah, something significant about it."

---

## Second Question: Bread of Affliction

### The Text

> "This is the bread of affliction that our fathers ate in the land of Egypt. Whoever is hungry, let him come and eat; whoever is in need, let him come and conduct the Seder of Passover. This year [we are] here; next year in the land of Israel. This year [we are] slaves; next year [we will be] free people."

---

### The Problem

**"This is the bread..."**
- This is not literally that bread
- Might taste like it
- But it's not physically the same

**The Question:**
> "Why are we saying it is? There must be something in common between our bread now, and theirs back then."

---

## Circular Nature of Time

**Principle:**
> "Each year is a circle, the event that happened back then, reoccurs on some level each year."

**Implication:**
- Not just remembering
- Spiritual energy returns
- Original event's power available
- Annual renewal of experience

---

## Core Concepts

### The Contrast

**Chometz = Ego**
- Puffed up
- Inflated
- Self-important
- Arrogance

**Matzah = Humility**
- Flat
- Simple
- Submission
- Letting go

---

### Pesach - The Concept

**Word Meaning:** "To leap"

**Not a Step:**
- Step: Still connected to previous space
- Leap: Both feet off the ground
- Totally new place
- Complete transition

---

### Egypt - The Limitation

**Mitzrayim = Limiting**
- Narrow straits (meitzarim)
- Constrictions
- Boundaries
- Restrictions

**Going Out of Egypt:**
- Breaking free of limitations
- Overcoming restrictions
- Transcending boundaries

---

## What Is Freedom?

**Not Negative Definition:**
- Not just "not enslaved"
- Not just "not restricted"
- Freedom is positive act

**True Freedom:**
> "Reaching within and realizing our true potential, that we are truly a piece of G-d, we can accomplish much more then we think"

**The Act:**
- Looking within
- Realizing who we are
- Not limiting ourselves to outer part
- Connecting to essence

---

## Being in the Place of Change

**Why Risky?**

### Risk 1: Amalek - Ego Can Set In

**The Danger:**
- Make real meaningful move
- Feel very proud of yourself
- Don't realize Hashem helped
- Conceit and arrogance
- Amalek comes right after Exodus

**What is Amalek?**
- Source of all negative traits
- Especially ego
- When making spiritual progress
- Threatens to make you conceited

---

### Risk 2: Foundational Stage Is Fragile

**The Problem:**
- Making new platform in Yiddishkeit
- New leap in spiritual self
- This is the foundation
- Don't want negativity mixed in
- Don't want chometz in foundation

**Therefore:**
> "Pesach we need to avoid chometz at all cost."

---

## How Do We Get Rid of All the Chometz?

### Method 1: Work Hard

**Our Effort:**
- Scrubbing
- Toiling
- Physical labor
- Removing chametz actively

---

### Method 2: Divine Revelation

**From Above:**
> "Hashem reveals himself in such an open way that we are naturally humbled."

**What Happened at Original Exodus:**
> "At the time of Mitzrayim that is what happened, Hashem was reveled in such an open way, that they were naturally humbled."

---

## Understanding the Haggadah Text

### The Question Repeated

> "This Matzah that we eat for what reason? Because the dough of our fathers did not have time to become leavened before the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself to them and redeemed them."

---

### The Deep Read

**Why do we eat the Matzah?**
- Because of "Ma"
- What is "Ma"?

**The Word "Ma":**

**In Hebrew:**
חכמה (Chochma - Wisdom)

**Broken Down:**
כח מה (Koach Ma)

**Meaning:**
- The power of "what"
- The power of the unknown
- Humility
- Subjection
- Lose self
- Nothingness

---

### Why We Eat Matzah

**Purpose:**
> "In order to achieve Ma - ability to lose self, to be totally submitted to Hashem, just like chochma, is undefined, just a spark of idea."

**The Mechanism:**
- Chochma is undefined
- Just a spark
- Not fully formed
- State of nullification before ego

---

## The Original Pesach Energy

**What Happened:**
> "During the original Pesach the dough was unable to rise, because Hashem was revealed, there was no space for ego."

**Not Because They Rushed:**
- Dough was **unable** to rise
- Not just didn't have time
- Couldn't rise
- No space for chometz
- Hashem revealed, so no space for ego

**Why We Think We Have Ego:**
- Because Hashem is hidden
- When Hashem revealed
- Naturally no ego
- No place for "who am I"

---

## Annual Energy

**Each Year:**
> "That energy is with us each year on the first night of Pesach. The energy to let go of ourselves and our ego."

**First Night:**
- Divine revelation energy
- Natural humility
- Let go of ego
- Foundation moment

---

## Last Night Different

**By Last Night:**
> "We lean a bit more toward chometz, we are not at foundational stage anymore, therefore we need the sense of self to come in, to build it up, we can't sit back and rely on Hashem to continue inspiring us."

**Why Chometz Allowed Later:**
- Not at foundation anymore
- Need to build yourself up
- Can't be total nobody
- Need Jewish pride
- Work with yourself piece by piece

**Gebrokts on Last Day:**
- First week of Omer is foundational (chesed)
- After foundation built, can let bit of chometz
- Need healthy build
- Chometz only threat at foundation

---

## Cleaning for Pesach

**Purpose:**
> "The cleaning for Pesach assists in the nullification, kind of feel like a shmate."

**Effect:**
- Humbling experience
- Physical humility
- Feel like a rag (shmate)
- Preparation for spiritual nullification

---

## Soul Scrubbing: A Passover Lesson

**Author:** Mimi Hecht (Notik)

**Context:** Student at Machon Alte in Tzfat, Israel

---

### Opening - The Physical Work

**The Experience:**
> "My right arm is officially a hundred times stronger than my left, still burning and smelling of bleach."

**The Job:**
- Day of cleaning before Passover
- Scrub the floor
- Scrub 30 refrigerator racks
- Scrub counters
- Scrub dishes

**Initial Reaction:**
- Removing layers of grime
- Mold and rotting food
- Overwhelmed by work

---

### Seeking Meaning

**The Question:**
> "As I was removing layers of grime, mold and rotting food from the surfaces of all the items I encountered, I struggled to use my overly-exposed-to-fumes brain to tap into the meaning and purpose of all the cleaning."

**Tzfat Lesson:**
> "Learning in Tzfat, the city where the study of Kabbalah originated in northern Israel, has taught me enough to expect more from the seemingly mundane in this world."

**Principle:**
- Nothing merely physical
- Everything has deeper meaning
- Mundane contains profound
- Tzfat teaches to look deeper

---

### The Alter Rebbe's Example

**The Story:**
> "The Alter Rebbe is known to have spent an enormous amount of time intensely cleaning his one-room house."

**The Standard:**
- Bedikat chametz takes ~20 minutes
- Alter Rebbe went all through the night
- Carefully guiding candle along floor
- Searching for crumbs

**The Question:**
> "Clearly, there is something here that goes beyond spring cleaning."

---

### The Insight

**Not Just House:**
> "The Alter Rebbe wasn't only searching his house. He was searching his soul."

**His Purpose:**
- Identifying proper motives for cleaning
- Checking for crumbs covering our soul
- Removing layers of dirt
- Stopping soul from shining full light

**Many Explanations Exist:**
> "There are many explanations for the much dreaded Passover cleaning. But for me, the Alter Rebbe's approach stands out."

---

### The Inner Dialogue

**While Scrubbing:**
> "So here I am scrubbing and scrubbing. I've got my soul on my mind. And I'm talking to myself. I'm saying, 'Mimi, scrub it away.'"

**The Mantra:**

> "Scrub away negativity. Let your soul shine."

> "Scrub away the suggestive powers of society. Let your soul shine."

> "Scrub away the barriers between your brothers and sisters. Let your soul shine."

> "Scrub away your silly insecurities. Let your soul shine."

> "Scrub away your ego. Let your soul shine."

> "Scrub away laziness. Let your soul shine."

> "Scrub away meaningless distractions. Let your soul shine."

---

### The Revelation

**Purpose:**
> "Scrub away all the layers. Reveal the light, the shine."

**What to Reveal:**
- Your mission
- Your powers
- The meaning
- The light inherent in the dark
- The G-dliness
- Redemption

---

### Universal Participation

**Personal and Cosmic:**
> "This little light of mine, I'm gonna let it shine. And the whole world, too, is with me."

**The Month:**
> "It is Nissan, the month of redemption, and Jews of every type and affiliation are cleaning away."

**The Activity:**
- Soul scrubbing
- World scrubbing
- Personal and universal
- Individual and collective

---

### The Result

**The Transformation:**
> "The world is starting to freshen and sparkle."

**The Anticipation:**
> "Passover is on its way."

**The Hope:**
> "I'll see you in Jerusalem."

---

### Multiple Audiences

- Chochma/koach ma analysis
- Etymology and language
- Philosophical depth
- Chassidic concepts

Because dough of our fathers did not have time to become leavened before King of kings Holy One blessed be He revealed Himself to them and redeemed them" asking **it seems so insignificant almost accident** just because rushing doesn't seem right, "there must be spiritual idea behind Matzah something significant about it." **Second question** from "this is the bread of affliction that our fathers ate in land of Egypt" - this is not literally that bread (might taste like it but it's not) so why are we saying it is, "there must be something in common between our bread now and theirs back then." **Principle:** "Each year is circle, event that happened back then reoccurs on some level each year" (not just remembering, spiritual energy returns, original event's power available, annual renewal). **Core concepts:** Chometz = ego (puffed up, inflated, self-important, arrogance), Matzah = humility (flat, simple, submission, letting go); Pesach word meaning "to leap" (not step still connected to previous space, but leap both feet off ground into totally new place complete transition); Mitzrayim/Egypt = limiting (narrow straits/meitzarim, constrictions, boundaries, restrictions), Going out of Egypt = breaking free of limitations/overcoming restrictions/transcending boundaries. **What is freedom:** Not negative definition (not just "not enslaved/not restricted"), but positive act: "Reaching within and realizing our true potential, that we are truly piece of G-d, we can accomplish much more than we think" (looking within, realizing who we are, not limiting ourselves to outer part, connecting to essence). **Being in place of change risky:** (1) Amalek-ego can set in (make real meaningful move, feel very proud, don't realize Hashem helped, conceit and arrogance - Amalek source of all negative traits especially ego comes right after Exodus); (2) Foundational stage is fragile (making new platform in Yiddishkeit, new leap in spiritual self, this is foundation, don't want negativity mixed in, don't want chometz in foundation, therefore "Pesach we need to avoid chometz at all cost"). **Two methods to get rid of chometz:** (1) Work hard scrubbing/toiling/physical labor/removing actively; (2) Divine revelation "Hashem reveals himself in such open way that we are naturally humbled" - "at time of Mitzrayim that is what happened, Hashem was revealed in such open way they were naturally humbled." **Deep read of Haggadah:** Why eat Matzah? Because of "Ma" - what is Ma? חכמה Chochma broken down כח מה Koach Ma meaning "power of what/power of unknown/humility/subjection/lose self/nothingness;" "in order to achieve Ma - ability to lose self, to be totally submitted to Hashem, just like chochma is undefined just a spark of idea" (chochma undefined, just spark, not fully formed, state of nullification before ego). **Original Pesach energy:** "During original Pesach dough was UNABLE to rise because Hashem was revealed there was no space for ego" (not because they rushed, dough couldn't rise, no space for chometz - we think we have ego because Hashem hidden, when Hashem revealed naturally no ego no place for "who am I"); **annual energy:** "That energy is with us each year on first night of Pesach, energy to let go of ourselves and our ego" (first night: divine revelation energy, natural humility, let go of ego, foundation moment). **Last night different:** "By last night we lean bit more toward chometz, we are not at foundational stage anymore therefore we need sense of self to come in to build it up, can't sit back and rely on Hashem to continue inspiring us" (why chometz allowed later: not at foundation, need to build yourself up, can't be total nobody, need Jewish pride, work with yourself piece by piece - gebrokts on last day: first week of Omer foundational/chesed, after foundation built can let bit of chometz, need healthy build, chometz only threat at foundation). **Soul Scrubbing essay by Mimi Hecht** (student at Machon Alte Tzfat Israel): Physical work cleaning day before Passover (scrub floor/30 refrigerator racks/counters/dishes, "my right arm officially hundred times stronger than left still burning and smelling of bleach"); # [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Chometz/Matzah Spiritual Class - Informal Notes

## Note: Passover Content (Not Chanukah)

**Resource Type:** Informal class notes / teaching outline

**Purpose:** Present spiritual significance of chometz and matzah

**Format:** Conversational, question-driven, stream of consciousness

**Relationship:** Similar themes to File 1097, different presentation style

**Note:** Raw teaching notes, not polished for distribution as-is

---

## Opening Examples

### Levi Yitzchok's Teaching

**The Comparison:**
> "Won't do Aveira Beshogeg if careful about chamets"

> "Levi yitzchok said after if the angle from shofer not good enough to bring brachas, then the cleaning and scrubbing for pesach should"

**Point:**
- If angel from shofar not perfect enough
- Then Pesach cleaning should certainly count
- Effort and kavanah matter
- Scrubbing has spiritual value

---

## The Haggadah Question

### What We Read

> "We read at Seder 'this matzah we eat cuz r father dough didn't rise, before hashem revealed himself and redeamed.'"

---

### Questions to Ask

**Question 1:**
> "We eat matza cuz dough didn't rise. So if dough would've risen we wouldn't eat matzah on pesach???"

**Seems incidental:**
- Because they rushing we eat matzah?
- Doesn't seem right
- Everything in Yiddishkeit has spiritual reason
- Why is Matzah so significant?

**Compare to Other Holidays:**
> "We don't say sukkos cuz ..."
- Other holidays have clear spiritual reasons
- Not presented as accidental
- Matzah seems different - why?

---

**Note:**
> "Matzah mitzvah is only the first night (first two in chutz laoretz) rest of pesach no obligation"

**Implication:**
- First night critical
- Rest of Pesach different status
- Timing significant

---

**Question 2:**
> "Reason eat it cuz didn't have time to rise, till hashem came to redeem them."

**Sequence Problem:**
> "We usually think it is hashem revealed then they packed and went not first they get ready then hashem reveal ??"

**Timeline Confusion:**
- Which came first?
- Did they pack, then Hashem revealed?
- Or Hashem revealed, then they packed?
- Affects understanding of matzah

---

**Question 3:**
> "What spiritual significant of chamatz and matzah. How it related back then and how it relates today"

**Seeking Connection:**
- Past and present
- Physical and spiritual
- Personal application

---

## Bread of Affliction Question

> "What we mean by saying 'this is the bread of affliction', this not that bread - might taste like it - but it's not it. So must b smtn the same about it"

**Analysis:**
- Not literally same bread
- But we say "this is"
- Something connects them
- What is it?

---

## Annual Cycle Concept

> "When yt come around, not only about remembering it, but spiritual effect that happens originally, happen again each yr"

---

### Alter Rebbe Story

**The Incident:**
> "Story of alter rebbe when he was in jail, they tell him it is night, he said no it's day, how he know each hr is a diff name of hashem shining."

**Lesson:**
- Each hour has different Divine name
- Spiritual reality beyond physical
- Alter Rebbe perceived spiritual truth
- Time has spiritual dimension

---

### The Circle

> "Each yr a circle, so u connect to the original pesach again on some level. The energy on that day shines again"

**Questions to Explore:**
- What is the energy of pesach?
- What does it mean on a personal level?
- What can we learn from it?

---

## Core Definitions

### Chometz = Ego

**Simple Equation:**
- Chometz represents ego
- Puffed up
- Inflated
- Self-importance

---

### Matzah = Submission

**Characteristics:**
- Letting go
- Being humble
- Submission
- Humility

---

## Pesach Main Idea

**What Pesach About:**
- Letting go
- Freedom
- Getting out of own restrictions
- Own perception
- Limitations put on self
- Something you can't do
- Can't reach
- Need to do
- Need to keep

---

### Defining Freedom

**Negative Definition:**
> "What is freedom? usually defined as negative, not slaved, not restricted, free."

**Positive Definition:**
> "Freedom is the act of reaching within ourselves, realizing who we r and not limiting ourselves to our outer part."

**Expanded:**
- Nothing wrong [with outer part]
- But we can do more

**Shabbos Parallel:**
> "Just like shabbos, the rest was an act of the 7th day, an act of itself, so too freedom is the act of looking within."

**Application:**
- Shabbos rest is active, not passive
- Freedom is active, not just absence of slavery
- Looking within is the act

---

## Going Out of Mitzrayim

> "Going out of mitzrayim, is setting free of limitations. We all prisoners but sit on key."

**Personal Application:**
> "Whatever ambission you have in yiddishkeit, spiritual growth, should b and can b conquered on pesach."

---

### True Celebration

**What Makes It Real:**
> "If food was hot, had matzah, not too much left over... Not celebrated properly, if you haven't left your mitzrayim, broken free from limitations."

**Not Just Physical:**
- Good food important
- But not the essence
- Must have spiritual liberation
- Must break your limitations

**Parenting Parallel:**
> "Just as in parenting not catigorize kids, the can b everything."

**Application:**
- Don't limit children
- They can be everything
- Same with ourselves
- Don't self-limit

---

## Step vs. Leap

**Step:**
- Still connected to previous space
- One foot on ground
- Gradual progression

**Leap:**
> "Leap both feet off the ground, into totally new place."

**Pesach Means:**
> "Pesach means to leap."

**Implication:**
- Complete transition
- Both feet off ground
- Totally new reality
- Not gradual growth

---

## Why Dangerous Place

### Danger #1: Amalek

> "Dangerous place to b, cuz what comes right after amalek"

**What is Amalek:**
> "Source of all negative traits? Ego."

**The Problem:**
> "When you make a real meaningful move, u feel very proud of yourself, without realizing that hashem helped u do it."

**Therefore:**
> "That y here at this time when moving forward in yiddishkeit, he goto have no chametz in mix"

**Application:**
- Making spiritual progress
- Natural to feel proud
- But that's ego (Amalek)
- Must avoid chometz (ego) at this time
- Chometz undermines the leap

---

### Danger #2: Foundation Stage

> "#2 when make a new platform of yiddishkeit, making new leap, new sense of spiritual self, need to have no ego in it, cuz it the foundation, you don't want chometz in that foundation."

**Why Critical:**
- Foundation determines everything
- New platform being built
- New sense of spiritual self
- Ego corrupts foundation
- Must be ego-free

---

## How Get Rid of Chometz?

### Two Ways

**Way #1: Our Effort**
> "Clean, search... Put in lots of your own effort"

**Physical Work:**
- Cleaning
- Searching
- Active labor
- Our responsibility

---

**Way #2: Revelation from Above**
> "Other way to get rid of chomotz, such a great revelation from above that you naturally humbled."

**What Happens:**
> "What happens pesach, OORigibaly pesach hashem was reveled in such a great way they were naturaly humbled."

**The Mechanism:**
> "The dough was unable to become chometz - not cuz they worked fast, it was unable to rise - no space for chometz, cuz hahsme was revelead so no scaope for ego"

**Why We Have Ego:**
> "We think we ego cuz hahsme hidden. When hashem revealed, so naturally inability to b chometz, no place for who."

**Original Pesach:**
- Hashem revealed so openly
- Naturally humbled
- Dough **unable** to rise
- Not because they hurried
- Because no space for ego
- Revelation left no room for ego

---

## In the Verse

**Punctuation Note:**
> "Lets see in the verse: we eat matzah cuz of ma."

**Aside:**
> "Typical change punctuation it diff. Guy questioning how serious trop, lend me 50$ and explain. When he says I owe u 50$??.."

*[Note: Reference to importance of correct reading/punctuation]*

---

### What's "Ma"?

**The Word:**
> "What is ma - ability to loose self, to b totally submitted to hashem, just like chochma, is undefined, just a spark of idea"

**Purpose:**
> "Why we eat matzah on pesach, in order for us to achieve level ma, to loose sence of ego in front of hashem."

---

### Four Sons Connection

**Chacham's Question:**
> "When we have four sons, chochom ma hu omer.. They all have the ma, whee is the submission"

**Analysis:**
- All sons have "ma" in their question
- Where is the submission?
- Wise son: "ma" (what)
- Question as submission

---

### Ma Nishtana

> "Also by ma nishtana, shoel - bowwor. Here the son bowwor ability to bitul."

**The Youngest:**
- Asks Ma Nishtana
- Shoel (asks)
- Shows he's a bor (simple)
- But bor shows ability to bitul (nullification)
- Asking = admitting you don't know
- Not knowing = humility

---

### Matzah = Ma

> "MMAtzah. Ability to submit to hashem"

**Connection:**
- Matzah contains "Ma"
- Ma = submission
- Eating matzah = achieving ma
- Humility embodied

---

## First Night vs. Rest of Pesach

**First Night:**
> "Just like back then incredible g-dly revelation no ego, so too today first night goto have matzah, let go of ego, rest of pesach is own work."

**Why Difference:**
> "Only when building smtn new needs get rid of ego, but last day of pesach can and should eat gebrochtz."

**Explanation:**
> "Cuz hahsme blow mind, all overwhlend to hashem, but now u goto work on yourself and build yourself up piece by piece to b that level"

---

### First Week of Omer

> "First week of the omer, is foundational, chesed work through yourself to build foundation and now u can let bit of chometz - goto b healthy build can't b total nobody, need Jewish pride, work with your self."

**Progression:**
- First night: Divine revelation, no ego
- Foundation week: Building on that revelation
- After foundation: Need healthy self
- Can't be "total nobody"
- Need Jewish pride
- Chometz (in moderation) now okay

---

### Chometz Timing

> "CCHometz only threat at foundation. Pesach time is the leap, when making smtn totally new."

**Other Times:**
> "Rosh hashana, is more smtn when make leap."

**Application:**
- Foundation moments need no chometz
- Pesach = foundation of year (freedom)
- Rosh Hashana = foundation of year (judgment)
- Both are "leap" moments
- Chometz threatens these foundations

---

**Source:** http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/article.html?h=892&o=2502120

**Purpose:** Teaching Haggadah with depth for those beyond basics

**Format:** Multiple teaching sections with stories

**Audience:** "Those who have already heard the basic Pirushim on the Haggadah but not yet accustomed to spend a whole hour on one Sicha in depth"

---

## Introduction from Author

**Opening Note:**
> "Dear Shluchim, This hand out below was from a somewhat different kind of class for those who have already heard the basic Pirushim on the Haggadah but not yet accustomed to spend a whole hour on one Sicha in depth."

---

### Four Aspects Discussed

**Structure:**
1. Dam-Tzfardeiah and Kadeish-Urchatz
2. The four questions
3. Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
4. The Rasha next to Chochom

---

### Author's Notes

**Self-Assessment:**
- "This section went over so so, as I could of used some more prep" (referring to four questions)
- "The other sections went over well"

**Formula:**
> "Add a couple of stories and your good to go."

**Closing:**
> "CHag Kasher Vsameiach."

---

## Section 1: Kadeish-Urchatz / Dam-Tzfardeiah

### The Principle

**Normal Order:**
> "Ordinarily you first need to get rid of the mold and then bring in the furniture."

**Pesach Exception:**
> "The order of the Haggadah is an inspiring lesson of exception to this rule!"

---

### Kadeish Before Urchatz

**The Sequence:**
> "The very first act of the Pesach Seder is Kiddush, sanctification. U'Rechatz, washing, comes afterwards."

**Usually:**
- Need to cleanse before sanctification
- Remove negative before adding positive
- Clean before holy

**On Pesach:**
> "God by his show of closeness to us at the time of redemption, enables us to be sanctified and He empowers us to achieve passion for Kedusha even before we clean up our act."

**Teaching:**
- G-d already prepared us for sanctification
- Divine closeness enables sanctification
- Passion for kedusha comes first
- Then cleaning follows

---

### Dam and Tzfardeiah (Blood and Frogs)

**Same Pattern:**
- First two plagues
- Blood before frogs
- Passion before removal

**Source:**
> "Rebbe's Haggadah on the first two Maakos"

**Teaching:**
- Sometimes passion for Kedusha comes even before Sur Meirah
- Sur Meirah (turn from evil) usually comes first
- But in special times, passion can precede it

---

### Kiddush Teaching

**Subtitle:**
> "Make a living, but don't forget to live"

**Purpose:**
> "We begin the Seder the same way we do other festivals and Shabbat, with a toast of Kiddush which formally sanctifies the day."

**Insight:**
> "The Kiddush this evening provides insight into the holiday of Pesach. It teaches us that G-d is in control of creation and of our destiny."

---

### Story: Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev

**The Scene:**
> "The great Chassidic master - Levi Yitzhak of Berditchev once looked out his window, and watched the bustling crowds as they rushed about their business."

**The Exchange:**
- He leaned out and asked: "Why are you rushing?"
- Man replied: "I'm running to work to make a living"

**Reb Levi Yitzchak's Response:**
> "What makes you so sure that your livelihood is in front of you so that you rush to catch up with it? What if it's behind you, running toward you? Maybe you should stop running and let it catch up to you!"

**Lesson:**
> "We can sometimes work so hard to make a living that we forget to live. We become a slave to work, not allowing the blessings we have accumulated catch up with us."

**Kiddush Application:**
> "Tonight as we make Kiddush, and sing the Shehechiyanu prayer, G-d is blessing us to take charge of our lives, fill it with goodness and appreciate our blessings."

---

## Section 2: Mah Nishtana - The Four Questions

### Rabbi Aaron of Stolin's Teaching

**The Text:**
> "'Here, the son asks' Said Rabbi Aaron of Stolin, 'Here' -- the night of the seder -- is an auspicious time for every 'son' and obviously every 'daughter' for that matter, to 'ask' directly from our Father in Heaven for all our needs, and to receive His blessings in abundance."

**Source:** Beit Aharon

**Application:**
- Auspicious time
- Direct asking from Father in Heaven
- For all needs
- Receive blessings in abundance
- Applies to sons and daughters

---

### Explaining Four Questions as Metaphor

**Note:**
> "Explaining the four questions as a metaphor for exile"

*[Author notes this section "went over so so" and needed more prep]*

---

## Section 3: Rabbi Elazar Ben Azarya

### The Statement

> "Rabbi Elazar Ben Azarya said I am like a 70-year-old man"

---

### Three Explanations

**1. Rabbinical Explanation:**
> "Our Rabbis explained that Rabbi Elazar was only eighteen at the time, yet he was 'like a 70-year-old man,' i.e., he had the maturity and wisdom of someone that age. Moreover, a miracle had occurred and his countenance mirrored his spiritual state."

**The Miracle:**
- Only 18 years old
- Maturity of 70
- Miracle: Appearance matched wisdom
- White hair/beard appeared

---

**2. Kabbalistic Explanation (Arizal):**
> "The sages of the Kabbalah, namely the holy Ari, state that when Rabbi Elazar's previous incarnation [Shmuel Hanavi who lived 52 years] are counted, he had indeed lived 70 years."

**The Math:**
- Current life: 18 years
- Previous incarnation (Shmuel HaNavi): 52 years
- Total: 70 years

**Teaching:**
> "This provides a lesson for each of us: the good we performed in previous incarnations enhances our divine service in this life."

---

**3. Discussion Point:**
> "Discussion of this empowering aspect of Gilgulim – reincarnation!"

**Empowering Message:**
- Previous good deeds count
- Cumulative spiritual growth
- Builds from life to life
- Nothing lost

**Source:**
> "Gemoro, Ramba"m, Arizal (gilgul of Shmuel) with lesson from the Sicha in the Rebbe's Haggadah of the empowerment of cumulative good."

---

## Section 4: The Four Sons

### The Question

**Title:**
> "How did the Rasha get a seat so close to the head of the table:"

**Issue:**
> "The Haggadah mentions the wicked son directly after the wise son."

---

### Three Reasons from Rebbe's Sichos

**Source:**
> "The Rebbes Sichos on the 3 reasons why the Rasha is next to the Chochom."

---

**Reason 1: For the Rasha**

> "Firstly, this order encourages the wicked son, teaching him that he also has the potential to become wise should he so desire."

**Message to Rasha:**
- You can change
- Potential to become wise
- Close to wisdom
- Just need to choose

---

**Reason 2: For the Chacham**

> "Secondly, it shows the wise son where he should lovingly concentrate his efforts. He should work with his wicked brother, and inspire him to reveal his potential."

**Responsibility:**
> "It is the wise son who is given this responsibility to reach out and bring out the 'One' in his wondering brother!"

**Message to Chacham:**
- Don't be detached
- Lovingly concentrate efforts
- Work with wicked brother
- Inspire him
- Bring out the good ("the One")

---

**Reason 3: Caution for the Chacham**

> "Lastly, it is a word of caution for the wise son, teaching him that he should not be overly proud or arrogant that he turned out OK, for there is only a slight distance between himself and his brother. If he does not continue to grow he could slip..."

**Warning:**
- Don't be proud
- Don't be arrogant
- Only slight distance between you
- Without continued growth, could slip
- Stay humble

---

### The Essential Oneness

**Deeper Layer:**
> "One wise, one wicked, one simple, and one who does not know how to ask: Echad, the essential oneness of our G-dly soul, remains present in all."

**Universal Truth:**
> "Even sons who are wicked or do not know how to ask possess oneness within their hearts."

**Application:**
- All four sons have Divine soul
- Echad (oneness) in everyone
- Even wicked
- Even those who don't know to ask
- Essential goodness never lost

---

## Conclusion: Next Year in Jerusalem

### Rebbe Rayatz's Teaching

**The Statement:**
> "Commenting on the closing prayer of the Pesach Seder, 'Next year in Jerusalem!', the Rebbe Rayatz once said:"

**The Message:**
> "One doesn't have to wait until next year. Rather, the Redemption is already brought into being immediately at the conclusion of the Seder. Then, as a matter of course, next year will be in Jerusalem."

**Meaning:**
- Not waiting
- Redemption happens NOW
- At conclusion of Seder
- Effect: Next year WILL be in Jerusalem
- Not hope, but certainty
- Action creates reality

---

## For Shluchim: Using This Outline

### Target Audience

**Described As:**
- Already heard basic Pirushim
- Not yet accustomed to spend whole hour on one Sicha
- Want depth without being overwhelmed
- Intermediate level

**Sweet Spot:**
- More than beginner
- Not yet advanced scholar
- Wants meaning, not just recitation
- Ready for concepts, not just stories

---

### Format Advantages

**Structure:**
- Four distinct sections
- Can use all or pick some
- Each stands alone
- Together create cohesive class

**Balance:**
- Teaching (concepts from Rebbe)
- Stories (Levi Yitzchak, Rebbe Rayatz)
- Practical application (Kiddush, questions, four sons)
- Inspiration (redemption, oneness)

---

### Author's Advice

**Simple Formula:**
> "Add a couple of stories and your good to go."

**Honest Assessment:**
- Some sections work better than others
- Four questions section needed more prep
- Other sections went over well
- Learn from experience

---

### Customization

**Can Add:**
- More stories for each section
- Additional sources
- Personal insights
- Local examples
- Visual aids

**Can Shorten:**
- Pick 2-3 sections instead of all 4
- Reduce depth on technical points
- Focus on one teaching per section
- Lighten for different audience

---

### Teaching Tips

**From This Outline:**

**1. Start Strong:**
- Kadeish-Urchatz concept compelling
- Levi Yitzchak story relatable
- Hooks audience immediately

**2. Build Progressively:**
- Four questions next (participation)
- Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya (depth)
- Four sons (practical application)

**3. End Powerfully:**
- Rebbe Rayatz on "Next Year"
- Creates hope and urgency
- Redemption is NOW
- Action-oriented close

---

### Class Format

**90-Minute Class:**
- 5 min: Introduction
- 20 min: Kadeish-Urchatz with story
- 15 min: Four questions
- 20 min: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
- 25 min: Four sons (3 reasons)
- 5 min: Next Year in Jerusalem close

**60-Minute Class:**
- Pick 3 of 4 sections
- Reduce depth slightly
- Keep stories
- Maintain structure

**30-Minute Dvar Torah:**
- Pick 1-2 sections
- Full story on one
- Brief on second
- Strong close

---

## Related Resources

**In This Collection:**
- File 1097: Matzah spiritual significance (philosophical teaching)
- File 1098: Chometz/matzah class notes (informal related)
- File 1095: Passover crash course laws (halachic foundation)
- File 1091: 12-step Passover preparation (community guide)
- File 1103: Passover jokes (lighter material to intersperse)

---

**Bottom Line:**

Haggadah class outline from Shluchim Exchange (shluchimexchange.com/en/article.html?h=892&o=2502120) for "somewhat different kind of class for those who have already heard basic Pirushim on Haggadah but not yet accustomed to spend whole hour on one Sicha in depth" discussing four aspects based on Rebbe's teachings with author noting four questions section "went over so so as I could of used some more prep" but "other sections went over well" with formula "add couple of stories and your good to go." **Section 1: Kadeish-Urchatz / Dam-Tzfardeiah** - principle "ordinarily you first need to get rid of mold and then bring in furniture" but "order of Haggadah is inspiring lesson of exception to this rule!" (very first act of Pesach Seder is Kiddush sanctification, U'Rechatz washing comes afterwards - usually need to cleanse before sanctification but on Pesach "God by his show of closeness to us at time of redemption enables us to be sanctified and He empowers us to achieve passion for Kedusha even before we clean up our act"); teaching from Rebbe's Haggadah on first two Maakos (plagues) that "sometimes passion for Kedusha comes even before Sur Meirah" (turn from evil usually comes first but in special times passion can precede); **Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev story:** Watched bustling crowds rushing, asked "why are you rushing?" man replied "running to work to make a living," Reb Levi Yitzchak responded "what makes you so sure that your livelihood is in front of you so that you rush to catch up with it? What if it's behind you running toward you? Maybe you should stop running and let it catch up to you!" (lesson: "we can sometimes work so hard to make a living that we forget to live, we become slave to work not allowing blessings we have accumulated catch up with us"); Kiddush application "tonight as we make Kiddush and sing Shehechiyanu prayer G-d is blessing us to take charge of our lives fill it with goodness and appreciate our blessings." **Section 2: Mah Nishtana - Four Questions** - Rabbi Aaron of Stolin teaching "'Here the son asks' - 'Here' the night of seder is auspicious time for every 'son' and obviously every 'daughter' for that matter to 'ask' directly from our Father in Heaven for all our needs and to receive His blessings in abundance" (Beit Aharon); note: explaining four questions as metaphor for exile (author notes this section needed more prep). **Section 3: Rabbi Elazar Ben Azarya** "I am like 70-year-old man" with three explanations: (1) Rabbinical: "Our Rabbis explained that Rabbi Elazar was only eighteen at time yet was 'like 70-year-old man' i.e. had maturity and wisdom of someone that age, moreover miracle had occurred and his countenance mirrored his spiritual state" (white hair/beard appeared); (2) Kabbalistic (Arizal): "Sages of Kabbalah namely holy Ari state that when Rabbi Elazar's previous incarnation [Shmuel Hanavi who lived 52 years] are counted he had indeed lived 70 years" (current life 18 + previous incarnation 52 = 70 total) teaching "this provides lesson for each of us: good we performed in previous incarnations enhances our divine service in this life;" (3) Discussion of "empowering aspect of Gilgulim - reincarnation!" (previous good deeds count, cumulative spiritual growth builds from life to life, nothing lost); source "Gemoro Rambam Arizal (gilgul of Shmuel) with lesson from Sicha in Rebbe's Haggadah of empowerment of cumulative good." **Section 4: Four Sons** - question "how did Rasha get seat so close to head of table" (Haggadah mentions wicked son directly after wise son); **Rebbe's Sichos three reasons:** (1) For Rasha: "This order encourages wicked son teaching him that he also has potential to become wise should he so desire" (you can change, potential to become wise, close to wisdom, just need to choose); (2) For Chacham: "Shows wise son where he should lovingly concentrate his efforts, he should work with his wicked brother and inspire him to reveal his potential - it is wise son who is given this responsibility to reach out and bring out the 'One' in his wondering brother!" (don't be detached, lovingly concentrate, inspire, bring out the good); (3) Caution for Chacham: "Word of caution for wise son teaching him that he should not be overly proud or arrogant that he turned out OK for there is only slight distance between himself and his brother, if he does not continue to grow he could slip..." (don't be proud/arrogant, only slight distance, without continued growth could slip, stay humble). **Essential oneness:** "One wise one wicked one simple and one who does not know how to ask: Echad the essential oneness of our G-dly soul remains present in all - even sons who are wicked or do not know how to ask possess oneness within their hearts" (all four sons have Divine soul, echad/oneness in everyone even wicked, essential goodness never lost). **Conclusion:** Rebbe Rayatz on "Next year in Jerusalem!" - "One doesn't have to wait until next year, rather Redemption is already brought into being immediately at conclusion of Seder, then as matter of course next year will be in Jerusalem" (not waiting, redemption happens NOW at conclusion of Seder, effect: next year WILL be in Jerusalem not hope but certainty, action creates reality). **For Shluchim:** Target audience intermediate level (already heard basic Pirushim, not yet accustomed to whole hour on one Sicha, wants depth without being overwhelmed); format advantages (four distinct sections can use all or pick some, each stands alone, together create cohesive class) balancing teaching/stories/practical application/inspiration; teaching tips: start strong with Kadeish-Urchatz and Levi Yitzchak story, build progressively through four questions/Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya/four sons, end powerfully with Rebbe Rayatz creating hope and urgency (redemption is NOW, action-oriented).
