# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Passover Jokes - "18 Minute Laughs"

## Note: Passover Content (Not Chanukah)

**Resource Type:** Humor collection

**Title:** "PASSOVER 18 MINUTE LAUGHS"

**Purpose:** Lighten mood, engage audience, break up serious teaching

**Format:** Short jokes and stories with Passover themes

**Note:** Some jokes repeated in the collection

---

## The Jokes

### 1. Dam Tzefardeyah (Unintelligent Frog)

**Q:** What do you call an unintelligent frog?

**A:** A Dam tzefardeyah!

**Type:** Wordplay on the plague
- Dam = blood (first plague)
- Tzefardeyah = frogs (second plague)
- Dam (also) = damn (curse/unintelligent)

---

### 2. Haggadah Wordplay

**Q:** Why do we have an Haggadah at Passover?

**A:** So we can Seder right words.

**Type:** Pun
- Seder = order of service
- Say-der = say the
- "Say the right words"

---

### 3. The Matzah Sandwich Exchange

**Setup:**
> "It was Passover and two Jewish attorneys, Saul and David, who worked downtown met at a food court to have lunch. Saul and David proceeded to produce matzah sandwiches from their briefcases and began to eat."

**Conflict:**
> "One of the waiters in the food court marched over and told them, 'You can't eat your own food in here!'"

**Punchline:**
> "Saul and David looked at each other, shrugged their shoulders, and then exchanged matzah sandwiches."

**Type:** Clever solution
- Rule: Can't eat your own food
- Loophole: Exchange, so it's not "your own"
- Lawyer humor
- Following letter not spirit of rule

---

### 4. The Blind Man and the Matzah

**Setup:**
> "A blind man is sitting on a park bench. A Rabbi sits down next to him. The Rabbi is chomping on a piece of matzoh. Taking pity on the blind man, he breaks off a piece and gives it to the blind man."

**Punchline:**
> "Several minutes later, the blind man turns, taps the Rabbi on the shoulder and asks, 'Who the heck wrote this?!!'"

**Type:** Misunderstanding
- Blind man reads by touch (Braille)
- Matzah has holes/texture
- Thinks it's written text
- Funny confusion

---

### 5. Abe and the Boss

**Setup:**
> "Abe goes to his boss and says 'we're doing some heavy house cleaning at home tomorrow for Pesach and my wife needs me to help with the attic and garage, moving and hauling stuff.'"

**Boss's Response:**
> "'We're shorthanded, Abe' the boss replies, 'I just can't give you the day off.'"

**Punchline:**
> "'Thanks, boss,' says Abe, 'I knew I could count on you.'"

**Type:** Reversal
- Expected: Abe disappointed
- Reality: Abe happy to be refused
- Wants to avoid cleaning
- Got excuse

---

### 6. Good Sermon Like Matzah (Version 1)

**Q:** How is a good sermon like a piece of matza?

**A:** They both should take less than 18 minutes!

**Type:** Self-deprecating rabbi humor
- 18 minutes = time for matzah to rise into chometz
- Long sermons = like chometz (inflated)
- Keep it brief
- Practical advice

**Note:** This joke appears twice in the collection (repeated)

---

### 7. Chopped Liver and Charoses Warning

**Setup:**
> "Just in time for this year, a group of leading medical people has published data indicating that seder participants should NOT partake of both chopped liver and charoses."

**Punchline:**
> "It is indicated that this combination can lead to Charoses of the Liver!"

**Type:** Pun
- Cirrhosis = liver disease
- Charoses = Passover food (apple/nut mixture)
- "Charoses of the liver"
- Medical humor

**Note:** This joke also appears twice in the collection (repeated)

---

### 8. Morris and the Divorce Threat

**Long Story Summary:**

**Setup:** Morris calls son Benny in NY:
> "Benny, I have something to tell you. However, I don't want to discuss it. I'm merely telling you because you're my oldest child, and I thought you ought to know. I've made up my mind, I'm divorcing Mama."

**Son's Reaction:** Shocked, tries to get information

**Morris's Response:** Won't discuss, too painful, 54 years together, has appointment with lawyer

**Son's Plea:**
> "Dad, don't do anything rash. I'm going to take the first flight down. Promise me that you won't do anything until I get there."

**Morris Agrees:** "Well, all right, I promise. Next week is Passover. I'll hold off seeing the lawyer until after the Seder."

**Daughter Calls:** Gets same news, also promises to fly down with her family

**The Reveal:**
> "After hanging up from his daughter, Morris turns to his wife and says, 'Well, it worked this time, but what are we going to do, to get them to come down next year?'"

**Type:** Elaborate scheme
- Manipulative parents
- Want kids to visit for Passover
- Fake divorce threat
- Gets results
- Already planning next year
- Relatable family dynamics

---

### 9. Moses and the Exodus Story

**Setup:**
> "A little boy once returned home from Hebrew school and his father asked, 'What did you learn today?'"

**Boy's Answer:**
> "The Rabbi told us how Moses led the children of Israel out of Egypt."

**Father:** "How?"

**Boy's Creative Version:**
> "Moses was a big strong man and he beat Pharoah up. Then while he was down, he got all the people together and ran towards the sea. When he got there, he has the Corps of Engineers build a huge pontoon bridge. Once they got on the other side, they blew up the bridge while the Egyptians were trying to cross."

**Father's Shock:**
> "Is that what the Rabbi taught you?"

**Punchline:**
> "The boy replied, 'No. But you'd never believe the story he DID tell us!'"

**Type:** Children's perspective
- Real story too fantastical
- Kid "improves" it with modern military
- Even made-up version more believable than truth
- Miracles hard to explain
- Kid's honesty

---

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Passover Seder Outline - Monica Study Group 2016

## Note: Passover Content (Not Chanukah)

**Resource Type:** Complete Seder guide for study group

**Year:** 2016

**Audience:** Monica study group (women's group)

**Purpose:** Interactive Seder with depth for each of 15 steps

**Format:** Step-by-step guide with stories, discussion questions, personal applications

---

## Opening Notes

**Preparation Reminders:**
> "Pesach guest who walked off with the bone - prepare your guests, prepare yourself for the night, make it interactive"

**The Mitzvah:**
> "The mitzvah of the night is V'higadta L'vincha and you shall tell your child, this is a night for children and the child inside of us to ask questions and break free from anything that limits us"

---

## How? The Seder - Organized Plan of Action

**Definition:**
> "Seder - organized plan of action"

**Purpose:**
> "The seder consists of 15 steps and each step is part of a process in becoming a free person."

**Symbolism:**
> "The moon take 15 days to grow to its fullest, pesach occurs on the 15th day of the month and the seder has 15 steps as guide for us to grow and reach personal freedom."

---

## 1. Kadesh (Sanctification)

### Details
- First of 4 cups
- Customary to have others pour for you - "we are like free people tonight"
- 3.4 ounces minimum requirement
- Try to drink all at once
- Leaning to the left

### Meaning of Sanctification

> "In the words of Kiddush we say that - '...sanctify also comes from the word - to separate (like groom and bride)'"

**Teaching:**
> "The Seder begins by recognizing in order for me to accomplish whatever I want to tonight, I have to first separate myself from my mundane, hum drum life, who am I, what is my mission on this world"

### Identity Question

**Ask:** "Who are we?"

**Answer:**
- A neshama
- A child of Avraham
- Story of Yankele the ganiv [thief]

> "I have the ability to be free from the limits of the natural world, where only our logic seems to function. Our g-dly soul is the first step to freedom."

---

## 2. Urchatz (Washing)

### Details
- 3 times on right, 3 times on left
- No blessing
- "This is how they did it in the temple"
- About to eat wet vegetable

### Meaning

> "The conclusion we have just made is something that we have resolved in our minds. However, to be of value, it needs to be brought into the reality of our physical existence."

**Symbolism:**
> "Idea of washing hands - hands represents the way we interact with the physical world"

---

## 3. Karpas (Vegetable in Salt Water)

### Details
- Dipping a veggie into salt water
- Say blessing HaAdamah
- Have in mind the maror you'll eat later
- "Eat up! You won't be getting some for a while!"

### Purpose

**Teaching:**
> "The Talmud teaches us that the custom of karpas has no reason. It is just there to provoke a question. Why are we dipping a vegetable in salt water?"

**Surface Explanation:**
- Salt water reminds us of tears shed while slaves in Egypt

**Essential Reason:**
- Simply to make us wonder
- Provoke questions

**Educational Value:**
> "More than we need to teach our children to learn, we need to teach them to ask questions. Brilliant book of Talmud is also q and a form"

**Freedom Message:**
> "In order to be free you have to challenge and question your previous assumptions. We have this bizarre ritual just to break us out of our comfort zone and ask, 'Hey', what and why am I doing what I do? Karpas your questions are an important part of becoming free."

### Discussion Question

> "Avodas perech - man did work of women did work of men - question: were you ever given a job that was pure torture simply because you didn't feel it suited your style, personality"

---

## 4. Yachatz (Breaking the Middle Matzah)

### Details
- Smaller piece - leave on table, "this is the poor man's bread" (they don't eat whole food)
- Larger piece for afikomen - hide or give
- Sefardim: Custom to tie it under kids' arms like they left Egypt

### Meaning

> "Breaking the middle matzo teaches that part of becoming free requires of us to break and shatter our comfortable and familiar habits."

**Slave Mentality:**
> "It's easier to take a person out of slavery than to take slavery out of a person"

**Story:** Beggar with brass door knockers

### The Pain of Change

> "We are married to our slave ideas and its hard to give them up - in this process there will be a breaking. I must expect that many ideas and beliefs that I am emotionally connected to will get shaken up - which can be painful."

### Pause for Reflection

> "Pause for a moment - what is an area of life, the voice of the pharaoh within you that may be limiting? A bad habit you have fallen into or way of thinking that you know is not helping?"

**Activity:** Watch freedom video

---

## 5. Maggid (Telling the Story)

### Readiness

> "After completing the first four steps, we are ready. Ready to delve into a story of the supernatural. Ready to remember leaving the Egypt of the past. Ready to leave the Egypt of our time."

### Chabad Custom - 4 Questions

**Note:**
> "Read about the custom first - value of customs, they keep our children tied to our tradition."

**Campus Observation:**
> "I see on campus, you could have a sign up for prayer, shake the lulav... but a bowl of chicken soup or an opportunity to make challa, something wakes up inside and they are comfortable to get involved Jewish - continue the customs of your FAMILY"

### How to Say Haggadah

- "Say the haggadah in a joyful tune"
- "Involve children"
- "Say it in first person, when we were slaves in Egypt..."

### 4 Sons

**Why the Order?**
- Chacham is near Rasha - so he can influence
- Rasha first - "because at least he has passion, the worst is apathy - I'm cool, couldn't care less!"

**Discuss:**
- Advantage of each son

**5th Son:**
> "Rebbe didn't want to leave an empty chair, fill the chair!!"

### Dayenu - Gratitude

[Express gratitude]

---

## 6. Rachtzah (Washing with Blessing)

### The Pattern

> "The order of the Seder is: Transcend, and then purify. Rise to a higher spiritual level, and draw that higher level into your physical life. Then do it again. Rise to a still higher level and draw it into your life. It is a process that goes on forever. It will only end when we reach the highest possible level of G-d. And He is infinite!"

**Continual Growth:**
> "Growing and learning never ends - the more you know the more you desire to learn some more"

---

## 7. Motzi (Blessing on Bread)

### Purpose

> "Our goal is not just to believe in miracles. We must also seek to see G-d in the process of the natural world."

### Story

**Boy from Hebrew School:**
> "If I would tell you..."

### Miracle Glasses

> "Pesach we recognize that miracles are the foundation of our nation - let's not dilute that! We need to wear miracle glasses and see them around us, big and small."

**Examples:**
- Monica called me
- I had a baby
- Time passed and then our group came together

> "Call it nature, call it a miracle! Nature is also miraculous"

**Personal Example:**
> "Since I have become pregnant Sarelka has become so independent. I guess, this is part of the miraculous system that G-d set up to have children slowly become independent."

---

## 8. Matzah (Eating Matzah)

### The Mitzvah of the Night

> "Eating Matza - the mitzvah of the night. This is what the seder is leading up to - what it's all about."

### What Matzah Represents

> "Matzo is food of faith and food of healing second night and we want to internalize it. The humility that matza represents is the first step in leaving our personal Egypt's and forging a relationships with G-d."

**Tangible Mitzvah:**
> "We don't just talk or meditate about humility but we tangibly eat it! And rid our homes, to the EXTREME of everything else."

### Amount and Care

> "Very careful to eat the right amount - it's spiritual medicine - make sure we eat the right amount: 1/2 to 3/4 matza"

**Personal Story:**
> "My grandfather the past couple of years, with the few teeth he had left and had huge issue with swallowing would painstakingly eat the matzo"

### Details
- Eat leaning to the left
- "Decorating pillow cases"

---

## 9. Maror (Bitter Herbs)

### Purpose

> "Having thought about the freedom from the limitations of the mind, we must now remember what psychological slavery is like."

**Examples:**
- Poor self esteem
- Desire to please

### Details
- Eat enough about small egg
- Wrap in romaine
- Dip but do not liberally apply the charoset

---

## 10. Korech (Sandwich)

### Meaning

> "The point is not to have the faith when everything is proceeding as planned. It is when there are obstacles, that we must rise to the occasion."

**Stories:**
- Fruma and Chanchie
- Shliach who bought the sunglasses and sunscreen on Lag B'Omer

---

## 11. Shulchan Orech (The Meal)

### Why Eat a Meal at Seder?

> "Why do eat a meal at a seder? If the point of seder is spiritual exercise of freedom why eat? Go to synagogue and pray!"

**Answer:**
> "Because every spiritual advance has to be bound to the physical - we don't leave our physical self at home, attend synagogue, have a spiritual exercise and return. We bring our physical side with us and imbue it with the ideas of seder night."

### Integration

> "The freedom that we have experienced tonight must not remain something which we feel only during holy-pursuits. We must weave it into all aspects of our lives. So we eat."

### Custom

> "Custom to start meal with boiled egg - remember egg is a sign of mourning and reminds us of the temple that was destroyed and sacrifices that we used to be able to bring there"

**Share 3 recipes**

---

## 12. Tzafun (Hidden - Finding the Afikomen)

### The Question

> "From where is the power going to come to leave mitzrayim today? Not from outside ourselves."

**Answer:**
> "Hidden within every Jew is the perfect faith in the supernatural and in G-d's infinite power. All we have to do is find it."

### After the Seder Experience

> "Hopefully after experiences much of the seder, eating matza, remembering how bitter it is to be slaves to anybody besides we g-d the hidden spark within every Jew comes out and we feel close to G-d in this world"

### Modern Application

**Story:** Shimona Tzuernuk - Coca Cola

> "From where do we find the power to fight a million dollars a minute of values? Believe in the soul. Nourish the soul with kosher food, torah, mitzvos, halacha, see the soul in others"

**Teen Example:**
- Prom
- "But to me..."

---

## 13. Berach (Blessing After Meal)

### Timing
- Pour cup before bentching
- Drink after

### Two and Two

> "We have drunk two cups celebrating our miraculous past. Now, we will drink two cups celebrating our miraculous future."

---

## 14. Hallel (Praise)

### Opening the Door

**First:** Open door for Eliyahu Hanavi

**Story:** Melamed and Eliyahu Hanavi, giving away salary etc.

> "For all this we praise G-d with Hallel."

---

## 15. Nirtzah (Acceptance)

### Waiting for G-d

> "Wait for G-d to accept our seder - to finish the process of freedom, G-d needs to do his part to liberate us"

> "Was it the best seder? It was the best one for this year 2016"

### Divine Partnership

> "Ultimately, we cannot truly leave Egypt on our own. After completing the Seder, we turn to G-d and ask him to accept our efforts and liberate us."

### Study Group Note

> "Conclude with note from kinus - lady said to stay as rebbetzin, I can do that most of the time but I remember when Shaya diagnosed, it came out in study group, crying because we have something special here, feel open a sense of trust, open arms whenever you need a hug so to remind myself and each of us to keep what comes out here private and maintain the special space this is."

### Conclusion

> "We end off our seder with L'shanah haba'ah b'Yerushalayim!!!"

---

## Additional Days

### Second Days of Pesach
- We light candles

### 7th Day
- Not celebrating downfall of Egyptians
- Remembering miracle of splitting of the sea

**Night that Sea Split:**
- Leave our doors unlocked
- Decorate synagogues with water/flowers
- Stay up the whole night as G-d did when we passed over
- Remember the song we sang at the sea

**Women's Faith:**
> "Only women had tambourines - reflection of the faith of their time - in the depth of despair, they packed the tambourines, they KNEW that G-d would save them"

**Our Generation:**
> "Our generation is the reincarnation of the souls of that generation - as women, we need to lead with the absolute knowledge and faith that the redemption will happen in our days as well"

### Second Day - Day of Moshiach

> "Mashal of preg [pregnancy], plane, engage only taking you to the next step. Redemption of Passover was only a step to take us to the redemption that we will experience TODAY in OUR TIMES"

**Baal Shem Tov:**
> "Instituted the Moshiach's Feast with matza and 4 cups of wine, leads into the end of Passover"

**Personal Note:**
> "Day of Moshiach - also my grandfather's yartzeit"

---

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah/General] Miriam - The Mother of Rebellion

## Note: Passover Content (Not Chanukah)

**Resource Type:** Teaching outline on Miriam

**Subtitle:** "The Feminist Lib Leader"

**Purpose:** Explore Miriam's role as leader, rebel, prophetess

**Audience:** Classes, divrei Torah, women's programs

**Format:** Structured outline with sources and applications

---

## Introduction: Miriam's Leadership

**Talmudic Teaching:**
> "There were three excellent leaders for Israel. They were Moses, Aaron and Miriam."

**Distinction:**
- Moses and Aaron: Leaders for all people
- Miriam: "The teacher of the women"

**Source:** Talmud, Taanit 9; Targum Mincha 6:4

---

## Historical Context

**Who is Miriam? Look at the Time Period:**

### The Brutality

**Biblical Description:**
> "And they [the Egyptians] embittered [vayemarreru, from the root mar] their lives with hard work" (Exodus 1:14)

**Nature of Brutality:**
- Both spiritually and physically
- Giving men the work of the women and vice versa
- Break their spirits
- Designed to demoralize

### The Decree

- Stargazers said to kill baby boys
- Pharaoh issued death decree
- Miriam's father, the respected leader, instructs all to divorce their wives

---

## Miriam's Name - Qualities of Character

### Mar = "Bitterness"

**Meaning:**
- She saw the bitterness of the people
- Felt it deeply
- Connected to their pain

### Meri = "Rebellion"

**Meaning:**
- Rebelled against the slave mentality
- Against the status quo
- Refused to accept despair
- Challenged assumptions

---

## Instances of Miriam's Courage / Rebellion

### 1. As a Midwife Summoned to Pharaoh

**The Story (Exodus 1:8-17):**

> "There arose a new king over Egypt...And he spoke to the Hebrew midwives, the name of one was Shifrah (Yocheved) and the name of the other Puah (Miriam)."

> "And he said, 'When you act as a midwife to the Hebrew women and see them on the birthing stool, if it is a son, you shall kill him, but if it is a daughter she shall live.'"

> "The midwives feared G-d and did not act as the king of Egypt commanded them...And it came to pass because the midwives feared G-d that He made them Houses..." [Kohanim and Leviim]

**Miriam's Response:**
- **Five years old** at the time
- First decree was to midwives to kill babies
- They didn't listen
- Miriam said: **"Woe to this man when G-d avenges him"**
- Pharaoh was furious!

**Courage:**
- Age 5 speaking truth to power
- Prophesied punishment
- Unafraid of consequences

---

### 2. Reprimanding Father's Divorce Decree

**The Situation:**
- Miriam's father (Amram, respected leader)
- Instructed all men to divorce wives
- Worse than Pharaoh's decree

**Miriam's Argument:**
> "She told the men you are doing worse than pharaoh, killing both girls and boys"

**Logic:**
- Pharaoh: Killing only boys
- Father's decree: No children at all (boys OR girls)
- More devastating impact

**Her Prophecy:**
> "She said a prophecy: 'my mother will give birth the leader of the Jewish people.'"

**Outcome:**
- Father listened
- Took back wife
- Others followed

---

### 3. Moshe's Birth - Faith Despite Doubt

**The Challenge:**
- Born 3 months early
- Parents said to her: **"Where is your prophecy??"**
- Looked hopeless
- Put him in basket

**Miriam's Response:**
> "Miriam stayed to watch"

**Against Slave Mentality:**
- "She was not ready to give up"
- "Waited to see what would happen"
- **DID NOT GIVE UP FAITH**
- Batya came, etc.
- Grew up in the palace

**Biblical Text (Exodus 2:3-4):**
> "The woman conceived and bore a son, and [when] she saw him that he was good..."

> "And when Yocheved could no longer hide him, she took for him an ark made of reeds...and put the child in it and laid it in the rushes by the river's bank. And his sister (Miriam) stood far away, to see what would be done to him."

---

## The Kior (Basin) in the Mishkan

### The Mirrors

**Miriam's Role:**
- Invigorated and strengthened Jewish women
- Told them not to give up
- Encouraged them to have **MIRRORS** with them
- Beautify themselves to attract husbands
- Be drawn together

**Credit:**
> "The credit of the continuity of the Jewish nation is attributed to the STRENGTH of the Jewish women - they CONQUERED THEIR DEPRESSION"

### Mishkan Donation

**The Offering:**
- Women brought mirrors
- Moshe hesitant to use it
- Seems vain...

**Hashem's Response:**
> "Hashem says no, use it for the kiyor [basin], because of what the women did for their husbands, for the continuity of the Jewish nation"

**Significance:**
- Mirrors built into holy vessels
- Women's initiative honored
- Faith and hope memorialized

---

## Shores of Red Sea

### After the Splitting

**The Events:**
- 10 plagues
- Leave Egypt
- Splitting of the sea
- Then: Sang praise to Hashem

**Biblical Text (Exodus 15:20-21):**
> "And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a tambourine in her hand; and all the women went out after her with tambourines, dancing. And Miriam answered them, 'Sing to the L-rd...'"

---

### The Tambourines - The Question

**What's Strange:**
> "Where did they get tambourines from??"

**Context:**
- Hasty exodus
- Left in rush
- Slaves with few possessions
- No time to pack luxuries

---

### The Answer

**Rashi (Exodus 15:20):**
> "The righteous women of that generation were confident that the Holy One Blessed be He would make miracles for them, so they prepared tambourines and dances."

**Miriam's Influence:**
- Never lost her vision
- Knew slavery would end
- Did not give in to slavery
- Did not lose hope
- **Inspired the women** to conquer their depression and to believe

---

### Miriam's Strength

**Legacy:**
> "This is the strength of Miriam - and a strength passed on to ALL Jewish women; to break out of our limitations, out of status quo"

**Reward:**
- Miriam's well traveled with them in desert
- When she had tzaraas
- Everyone waited 7 days for her
- Nation honored her as she honored them

---

## Inextinguishable Spark of Optimism

**Talmudic Teaching (Sotah 11b):**
> "In the merit of the righteous women of that generation, our forefathers were redeemed from Egypt."

**Why Their Merit:**
- In the merit of their faith
- They did not give up
- Even prepared for the day they would be redeemed
- **Knowing it would happen**

---

## Application: Emulating Miriam

### The Question

> "How can we emulate Miriam, a true feminist, and break out of comfort zones?"

---

### The Challenge

**Status Quo Comfort:**
> "It's always easier not to 'rock the boat', just stay as is..."

**But:**
> "We have the strength from Miriam to break out of our routine and do something greater...break out of our comfort zone"

---

### The Risk

**Reality:**
> "There's always risks...takes strength and courage to break out of what we usually do"

---

### The Method

**Process:**
> "Acknowledge the fear...then do what has to be done, and the strength grows."

**Steps:**
1. Acknowledge the fear
2. Do what has to be done anyway
3. The strength grows through action

---

## For Shluchim: Teaching This Material

### Structure Advantages

**Narrative Arc:**
1. Introduction (leadership trio)
2. Historical context (Egypt's brutality)
3. Name meaning (connection to character)
4. Stories of courage (chronological)
5. Lasting impact (mirrors, tambourines)
6. Application (modern women)

**Builds Well:**
- From context to character
- From past to present
- From story to application

---

### Key Messages

**For Women:**
- You have Miriam's strength
- Faith overcomes despair
- Rebellion against status quo is holy
- Breaking comfort zones is growth
- Your optimism can save the nation

**For All:**
- Question assumptions
- Don't accept slavery (physical or mental)
- Prepare for redemption
- Faith expressed in action
- Courage grows through use

---

### Teaching Approaches

**Chronological:**
- Miriam at 5 (midwife)
- Miriam as teen (father's decree, Moshe's birth)
- Miriam as adult (mirrors)
- Miriam at redemption (tambourines)
- Miriam in desert (well, tzaraas)

**Thematic:**
- Rebellion (against Pharaoh, against father, against despair)
- Faith (prophecy, waiting, tambourines)
- Leadership (women's teacher, inspiration)
- Legacy (merit, strength passed down)

**Question-Driven:**
- What made Miriam different?
- Where did tambourines come from?
- Why mirrors in Mishkan?
- How can we be like Miriam?

---

### Discussion Questions

**Personal Application:**
1. What "slave mentality" do you need to rebel against?
2. Where have you given up that you shouldn't have?
3. What tambourines are you preparing? (What redemption do you believe in?)
4. What comfort zone should you break out of?
5. What fears do you need to acknowledge and then act despite?

**Historical:**
1. Why was Miriam specifically "teacher of women"?
2. What was unique about the women's faith?
3. How did mirrors become holy vessels?
4. Why did everyone wait for Miriam?

---

### Feminist Angle

**"True Feminist":**
- Not about being like men
- About unique women's strength
- Faith, nurturing, persistence
- Conquering depression
- Building future despite present

**Modern Relevance:**
- Women's leadership
- Breaking glass ceilings
- Fighting despair
- Building despite obstacles
- Faith-based activism

---

### Visual Elements

**For Presentation:**
- Picture of Kior (basin)
- Tambourines
- Miriam's well (artistic depictions)
- Timeline of Miriam's life
- Map of exodus

---

## Related Resources

**In This Collection:**
- File 1108: Miriam and tambourines (complementary teaching, different angle)
- File 1106: Passover Seder outline (7th day includes women's tambourines)
- File 1097: Matzah spiritual (slave mentality vs freedom)
- File 1100: Haggadah class (freedom themes)

---

**Bottom Line:**

Teaching outline on Miriam "The Mother of Rebellion" as "feminist lib leader" exploring her role as leader/rebel/prophetess: **Talmudic teaching:** "There were three excellent leaders for Israel - Moses Aaron and Miriam" (Moses and Aaron leaders for all people, Miriam "teacher of the women" - Talmud Taanit 9, Targum Mincha 6:4). **Historical context:** Egypt embittered [vayemarreru from root mar] their lives with hard work (Exodus 1:14) both spiritually and physically giving men work of women and vice versa to break their spirits, stargazers said kill baby boys, Miriam's father respected leader instructs all to divorce wives. **Miriam's name qualities:** Mar = "bitterness" (she saw bitterness of people and felt it deeply connecting to their pain), Meri = "rebellion" (rebelled against slave mentality, against status quo, refused to accept despair, challenged assumptions). **Instances of courage:** (1) As midwife summoned to Pharaoh (Exodus 1:8-17) five years old when first decree was to midwives to kill babies they didn't listen, Miriam said "woe to this man when G-d avenges him" Pharaoh was furious (age 5 speaking truth to power, prophesied punishment, unafraid of consequences); (2) Reprimanding father's divorce decree when Miriam's father Amram instructed all men to divorce wives worse than Pharaoh's decree, Miriam told men "you are doing worse than pharaoh killing both girls and boys" (Pharaoh killing only boys but father's decree means no children at all boys OR girls more devastating impact), she said prophecy "my mother will give birth the leader of the Jewish people" (father listened took back wife others followed); (3) Moshe's birth faith despite doubt when born 3 months early parents said "where is your prophecy??" looked hopeless put him in basket but "Miriam stayed to watch - she was not ready to give up, waited to see what would happen - DID NOT GIVE UP FAITH" (Batya came grew up in palace - Exodus 2:3-4 "when Yocheved could no longer hide him took for him ark made of reeds...put child in it and laid it in rushes by river's bank, and his sister Miriam stood far away to see what would be done to him"). **The Kior (basin) in Mishkan:** Miriam invigorated and strengthened Jewish women told them not to give up, encouraged them to have MIRRORS with them and beautify themselves to attract husbands to be drawn together - "the credit of continuity of Jewish nation is attributed to STRENGTH of Jewish women - they CONQUERED THEIR DEPRESSION;" Mishkan donation women brought mirrors Moshe hesitant to use it seems vain but "Hashem says no use it for the kiyor because of what women did for their husbands for continuity of Jewish nation" (mirrors built into holy vessels, women's initiative honored, faith and hope memorialized). **Shores of Red Sea:** After 10 plagues/leave Egypt/splitting of sea sang praise to Hashem (Exodus 15:20-21) "And Miriam the prophetess sister of Aaron took tambourine in her hand and all women went out after her with tambourines dancing, and Miriam answered them 'Sing to the L-rd...'" - what's strange? "Where did they get tambourines from??" (hasty exodus, left in rush, slaves with few possessions, no time to pack luxuries); **Rashi Exodus 15:20:** "The righteous women of that generation were confident that Holy One Blessed be He would make miracles for them so they prepared tambourines and dances" (Miriam's influence: never lost vision, knew slavery would end, did not give in to slavery, did not lose hope, INSPIRED THE women to conquer their depression and to believe). **Miriam's strength:** "This is strength of Miriam - and strength passed on to ALL Jewish women; to break out of our limitations out of status quo" (reward: Miriam's well traveled with them in desert, when she had tzaraas everyone waited 7 days for her - nation honored her as she honored them). **Inextinguishable spark of optimism:** Talmud Sotah 11b "In merit of righteous women of that generation our forefathers were redeemed from Egypt" (in merit of their faith, they did not give up, even prepared for day they would be redeemed KNOWING it would happen). **Application emulating Miriam:** "How can we emulate Miriam a true feminist and break out of comfort zones? It's always easier not to 'rock the boat' just stay as is...but we have strength from Miriam to break out of our routine and do something greater...break out of our comfort zone; there's always risks...takes strength and courage to break out of what we usually do;" method: "Acknowledge the fear...then do what has to be done and the strength grows" (1. acknowledge fear, 2. do what has to be done anyway, 3. strength grows through action). **For Shluchim:** Narrative arc builds well from context to character, from past to present, from story to application; key messages for women (you have Miriam's strength, faith overcomes despair, rebellion against status quo is holy, breaking comfort zones is growth, your optimism can save the nation), for all (question assumptions, don't accept slavery physical or mental, prepare for redemption, faith expressed in action, courage grows through use); teaching approaches chronological (Miriam at 5/teen/adult/redemption/desert), thematic (rebellion/faith/leadership/legacy), or question-driven (what made Miriam different/where did tambourines come from/why mirrors in Mishkan/how can we be like Miriam); discussion questions personal application (what slave mentality need to rebel against/where have you given up/what tambourines are you preparing/what comfort zone should you break out of/what fears need to acknowledge and act despite), historical (why Miriam specifically teacher of women/what was unique about women's faith/how did mirrors become holy vessels/why did everyone wait for Miriam); "true feminist" not about being like men but unique women's strength (faith/nurturing/persistence, conquering depression, building future despite present) with modern relevance (women's leadership, breaking glass ceilings, fighting despair, building despite obstacles, faith-based activism). Related resources: File 1108 (Miriam and tambourines complementary teaching different angle), 1106 (Passover Seder outline 7th day includes women's tambourines), 1097 (matzah spiritual slave mentality vs freedom), 1100 (Haggadah class freedom themes). # [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Miriam and the Tambourines - Women's Event Speech

## Note: Passover Content (Not Chanukah)

**Resource Type:** Speech/teaching for women's event

**Purpose:** Inspire Jewish women through Miriam's example

**Format:** Narrative speech with activity (tambourine decorating)

**Tone:** Personal, inspirational, empowering

**Audience:** Jewish women's gathering/event

---

## Opening: The Context

**She grew up surrounded:**
- By slavery
- By people in despair
- Everywhere: talk of grim future for her people

**But still:**
> "From a young age, she believed."

---

## Introducing Miriam

**Names/Titles:**
- Miriam
- Miriam the midwife
- Miriam, sister of Moses
- Miriam, the prophetess

---

## Miriam's Character from Youth

**Obvious Difference:**
> "From a young age, it was obvious that Miriam was different. She had a sharp tongue and was not afraid to use it."

### The Midwife Incident

**Pharaoh's Command:**
- Commanded Miriam and her mother
- Make sure all baby boys thrown into Nile

**Miriam's Response:**
> "It was Miriam who answered back saying he'd be punished for such an evil decree."

**Character Revealed:**
> "Miriam was not a victim of her circumstances - Miriam was in control."

---

## After the Ten Plagues

**The Scene:**
> "After the ten plagues, the Jews finally leave Egypt and witness an awesome miracle of the splitting of the sea."

---

## The Torah Verse

**Biblical Text:**
> "Now picture the scene; They are coming out of slavery. They had barely 12 hours to pack and leave Egypt. They traveled a week in the desert. They crossed the sea."

---

## The Question

**The Puzzle:**
> "Where did Miriam and the women have tambourines to dance with?"

**Think About It:**
> "Imagine packing in a rush - do you go searching for a tambourine?"

> "Imagine their life in slavery; were there such luxuries as a tambourine?"

---

## The Men's Response

**Look at the verse about the men:**
> "No mention of musical instruments."

---

## Where Did Women Get These?

**Modern Impossibility:**
> "Where did the women get these musical instruments? I doubt there was a Target in the desert that they could've stopped in to pick some up; I'm pretty certain that Amazon Prime and Google Express had not yet begun their operations."

**The Significance:**
> "This verse alone tells us everything we need to know about Miriam."

---

## Miriam's Greatness

**What We Know:**
- Miriam was great
- She was special
- Miraculous water supply in desert was in her merit
- When she was afflicted, entire community waited one whole week just for her

**Through This Verse:**
> "It is through this verse that we can grasp what was so great about Miriam."

---

## Miriam's Faith

**Despite Circumstances:**
> "While the women were embittered in slavery, seeing no future, Miriam's faith in G-d would not be diminished. She believed. She trusted. And she knew G-d had not abandoned them."

---

## What Miriam Did

**Boosting Morale:**
> "And so she would boost the morale of the women; reminding them of Hashem's promises. filling them with faith in Hashem."

**The Tambourines:**
> "And she encouraged them to make tambourines. Because after all, if they expect great miracles, they'd want to have instruments to accompany their singing of praise to Hashem"

---

## The Paradox

**Their Reality:**
> "And so while their conditions were terrible and the situation bleak, they made tambourines. And their faith in G-d was strengthened."

**When the Time Came:**
> "And when the time came to sing praise to Hashem, they were ready. They were prepared, thanks to Miriam."

---

## The Source of This Faith

**The Question:**
> "Where did this deep strength, a faith that defied logic, come from?"

**The Answer:**
> "It is the deep faith that is in me, in you; in every Jewish women. They all had it; only Miriam helped them tap into it."

---

## Miriam's Vision

**Ability to See:**
> "Miriam was able to see past the present difficulties; Miriam's faith helped her rise above."

---

## Why We Gather

**Purpose of This Event:**
> "And today, we are all gathered here, me, and each one of you, to celebrate that Faith. Because it's a strength that lies in each one of us, waiting to be tapped into."

---

## Three Mitzvot - Tapping Into Faith

### 1. Shabbat Candles

> "When a women lights shabbat candles, ushering in the holiness of Shabbat, she is reaching that deep place of unshakeable faith."

### 2. Mikvah

> "When a woman fulfills the mitzvah of mikvah, the guidelines of family purity, she is reaching that deep place of unshakeable faith."

### 3. Challah

> "When a woman bakes bread that is enough dough to recite a special blessing on the dough, she is reaching that deep place of unshakeable faith."

---

## When We're In Touch With Faith

**Then:**
> "And when we are in touch with that faith, miracles happen."

**During Miriam's Time:**
> "During Miriam's time; it was the exodus of Egypt. Their faith made them worthy of such miracles."

**In Our Times:**
> "In our times, it's our personal exoduses; our personal freedoms of overcoming challenges and staying positive."

---

## The Eternal Message of the Tambourine

**Torah's Emphasis:**
> "And it is the tambourine that gives us this message. The tambourine that the torah felt was so important that it needed to be included in the writing of the written Torah; the torah did not leave that detail for a commentary to add; no, G-d himself felt it important to include in the actual text."

**Why Important:**
> "Because the tambourines the women danced with hold an eternal message for every woman, of all generations."

---

## We Can All Be Miriam

**The Potential:**
> "We can all be Miriam. We can all rise above our challenges. We all have the potential; and it is up to us to use it."

---

## Celebration

**What We Celebrate:**
> "Today we are here to celebrate. To celebrate Miriam, to celebrate Jewish unity. To celebrate the Jewish woman; to celebrate me and to celebrate you."

---

## The Activity

**Tambourine Decorating:**
> "We will each decorate a tambourine today to take home - keep it as your reminder, your proof. You have the strength like Miriam did; keep the tambourine in sight, on display, as a reminder to never give up."

---

## Closing: The Final Redemption

**Looking Forward:**
> "And when the final redemption with the arrival of Moshiach occurs, may it be speedily, it will be me and each one of you, dancing with our tambourines, rejoicing in happiness, proclaiming to all; we believed. We did not give up. And we were ready."

---

## For Shluchim: Event Planning

### This Speech Works For

**Events:**
- Women's Passover event
- Pre-Passover gathering
- Tambourine decorating workshop
- Women's circle
- Mother-daughter event
- Community celebration

**Timing:**
- Weeks before Passover
- During Sefirat HaOmer
- Shavuot (women receiving Torah)
- Anytime celebrating Jewish women

---

### Structure Analysis

**Opening (1-5 minutes):**
- Context: slavery, despair
- Miriam's character
- Not a victim, in control

**Build-Up (5-10 minutes):**
- After ten plagues
- The verse
- The question: Where did tambourines come from?
- Modern impossibility (Target/Amazon)

**Climax (10-15 minutes):**
- Miriam's faith
- What she did for women
- Source of faith in all of us
- Three mitzvot connection

**Application (5-10 minutes):**
- Miracles then and now
- Torah's emphasis on tambourine
- We can all be Miriam
- Celebration

**Activity & Close (5-10 minutes):**
- Tambourine decorating
- Keep as reminder
- Final redemption vision

**Total:** 30-50 minutes depending on pace

---

### Preparation Needed

**Materials:**
- Plain tambourines (one per participant)
- Decorating supplies:
  - Paint, markers, stickers
  - Ribbons
  - Gems, sequins
  - Glue
  - Glitter (optional)

**Space:**
- Tables for decorating
- Covering for tables
- Good lighting
- Cleanup supplies

**Tech:**
- Microphone if large group
- Music (optional background during decorating)
- Perhaps video/images of tambourines

---

### Engagement Ideas

**Before Speech:**
- Display decorated tambourine samples
- Music as people arrive
- Name tags

**During Speech:**
- Call and response
- Ask rhetorical questions
- Pause for effect
- Eye contact

**During Activity:**
- Circulate among tables
- Share stories
- Encourage creativity
- No "right way" - personal expression
- Background music (uplifting)

**After Activity:**
- Photo opportunity with tambourines
- Circle dance with tambourines
- Sing together
- Share what tambourine means to each person

---

### Variations

**Shorter Version (20 minutes):**
- Focus on: Question, Answer, Application
- Quick activity or send home to decorate

**Longer Version (90 minutes):**
- Add: More Miriam stories
- Deeper dive into three mitzvot
- More elaborate decorating
- Dancing/singing session
- Food and socializing

**Family Version:**
- Include daughters
- Mother-daughter bonding
- Simplified concepts
- More hands-on, less lecture

---

### Marketing Angles

**Event Title Ideas:**
- "Tambourines and Tea"
- "Faith Like Miriam"
- "Never Give Up: A Women's Celebration"
- "Decorating Hope: Tambourine Workshop"
- "Miriam's Message"

**Promotion:**
- Emphasize: Inspiration, creativity, community
- Show: Sample decorated tambourines
- Promise: Take home meaningful reminder
- Highlight: Celebrate Jewish women

---

### Follow-Up

**After Event:**
- Photo sharing (with permission)
- Thank you email
- Remind them to display tambourine
- Before Passover: "Remember your tambourine!"
- Next year: "Bring your tambourine to Seder!"

**Long-Term:**
- Annual tradition
- Growing collection
- Community tambourine dance at event
- Alumni photos with tambourines

---

### Adaptations for Different Audiences

**Ba'alot Teshuvah:**
- Emphasize: You have this strength too
- Explain: Three mitzvot clearly
- Welcome: Questions
- Non-judgmental about practice

**Established Community:**
- Deeper: Chassidic concepts
- Reference: More sources
- Challenge: Specific applications
- Build: On existing knowledge

**Mixed Observance:**
- Universal: Faith and strength themes
- Accessible: Miriam's story
- Practical: Personal challenges
- Inclusive: All welcome

**Teens/Young Adults:**
- Modern: Amazon/Target references
- Relevant: Social media, peer pressure
- Interactive: More activity time
- Upbeat: Energy and music

---

## Related Resources

**In This Collection:**
- File 1107: Miriam mother of rebellion (companion teaching, more structured)
- File 1106: Passover Seder outline (7th day women's tambourines)
- File 1097/1098: Matzah spiritual (freedom from limitations)
- File 1100: Haggadah class (redemption themes)

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Let My People Know - The Seder Seminar

## Note: Passover Content (Not Chanukah)

**Resource Type:** Seder guide/seminar handout

**Organization:** Chabad El Paso

**Contact:** 6615 Westwind Drive | 915.584.8218 | www.chabadelpaso.com

**Purpose:** Comprehensive Seder instruction with sources

**Format:** Step-by-step guide with Torah sources and halachic details

---

## Mitzvot of the Evening

**Four Primary Mitzvot:**
1. Eat Matzah
2. Eat Maror
3. Tell the Story (Haggadah)
4. Drink 4 cups of Wine

---

## The Seder Plate

### What You Need:

**Zeroah:** Roasted Chicken Neck

**Beitza:** Hardboiled Egg

**Maror:** Romaine Lettuce & Horseradish

**Charoset:** A Paste made of: Apples, Pears, Nuts & Wine

**Karpas:** Raw Onion or Cooked Potato

**Additional:** 3 Matzahs, Wine & A Festive Dinner

---

## Seder Outline - 15 Steps

### 1. Kadeish
- Recite Kiddush
- Drink first cup of wine
- Reclining on left side
- **Amount:** 3.5 fl oz

### 2. Urechatz
- Wash hands in the ritual fashion
- **Without a Blessing**

### 3. Karpas
- Dip vegetable in salt water
- Recite Blessing
- **Have Maror in mind**
- Eat vegetable

### 4. Yachatz
- Break middle Matzah
- **Smaller piece:** Back in middle of 2
- **Bigger piece:** Break into 5 for Afikomen

### 5. Magid
- Tell story of the Haggadah
- Children ask the 4 Questions
- **At the end:** Drink second cup of wine with Blessing, reclining on your left side

### 6. Rochtzoh
- Wash hands in the ritual fashion
- **Recite blessing:** Al Netillas Yadayim

### 7. Motzi
- Recite Blessing Hamotzi Lechem
- **Holding all 3 Matzahs in hand**

### 8. Matzah
- Blessing Al Achilas Matzah
- **Holding just 2 top Matzahs**
- Break off piece from the 2 top Matzahs
- Eat Matzah, reclining on your left side
- **Be sure to eat at least one ounce**

### 9. Maror
- Dip Maror in Charoset
- Blessing Al Achilas Maror
- **Do not recline**

### 10. Korech
- Take 3rd Matzah
- Say Kein Assa Hillel
- Eat Matzah and Maror together
- Reclining on your left side

### 11. Shulchan Orech
- Dinner is served
- **Begin with:** Egg dipped in salt water

### 12. Tzafun
- Eat afikoman
- Reclining on your left side
- **Be sure to eat at least one ounce**
- **Do not eat or drink afterwards**

### 13. Beirach
- Birkat Hamazon – Grace After Meals
- Afterwards, drink third cup with Blessing, reclining on your left side
- The Cup of Elijah is filled
- Open door in greeting

### 14. Hallel
- Songs of praise
- Afterwards, drink fourth cup with Blessing, reclining on your left side

### 15. Nirtzah
- Confidence that G-d accepts and will assist our efforts
- **LISHANA HABAH BIYERUSHALAYIM – NEXT YEAR IN JERUSALEM!**

---

## Torah Sources

### Deuteronomy 6:20-25
[Referenced for telling the story]

### Exodus 12:25-27
[Referenced for Pesach observance]

### Exodus 13:3-14
[Referenced for remembering the Exodus]

### Deuteronomy Chapter 26
[Referenced for first fruits declaration - template for Haggadah]

### Deuteronomy 16:3
**Bread of Affliction**

---

## Talmudic Sources

### Talmud, Pesachim 116a

**Samuel said:**
> "Bread of ['oni] [means] bread over which we recite ['onin] many words."

**It was taught likewise:**
> "'Bread of ['oni]' means bread over which we recite ['onin] many words."

**Another interpretation:**
> "'Bread of ['oni]': 'ani [poverty] is written: just as a beggar generally has a piece, so here too a piece [is taken]."

**Another interpretation:**
> "Just as a poor man fires [the oven] and his wife bakes, so here too, he heats and she bakes."

---

## Joshua - Chapter 24

### Hebrew Text with Translation

**Verses 2-4:**

Hebrew:
> ב וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֶל-כָּל-הָעָם כֹּה-אָמַר ה' אֱ-ל-ֹהֵ-י יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעֵבֶר הַנָּהָר יָשְׁבוּ אֲבוֹתֵיכֶם מֵעוֹלָם תֶּרַח אֲבִי אַבְרָהָם וַאֲבִי נָחוֹר וַיַּעַבְדוּ אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים. ג וָאֶקַּח אֶת-אֲבִיכֶם אֶת-אַבְרָהָם מֵעֵבֶר הַנָּהָר וָאוֹלֵךְ אֹתוֹ בְּכָל-אֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן וארב (וָאַרְבֶּה) אֶת-זַרְעוֹ וָאֶתֶּן-לוֹ אֶת-יִצְחָק. ד וָאֶתֵּן לְיִצְחָק אֶת-יַעֲקֹב וְאֶת-עֵשָׂו וָאֶתֵּן לְעֵשָׂו אֶת-הַר שֵׂעִיר לָרֶשֶׁת אוֹתוֹ וְיַעֲקֹב וּבָנָיו יָרְדוּ מִצְרָיִם.

Translation:
> "2. And Joshua said to the whole nation, 'Thus said the Lord God of Israel, "Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the river from earliest time, Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nahor; and they served other gods. 3. And I took your father Abraham from the other side of the river, and led him throughout all the land of Canaan, and multiplied his seed, and gave him Isaac. 4. And I gave to Isaac Jacob and Esau; and I gave to Esau Mount Seir to inherit it; and Jacob and his children went down into Egypt."'"

**Usage:** Beginning from degradation (idol worship) to praise (chosen by G-d)

---

## Jerusalem Talmud 10:1

### Four Cups Requirement

**Mishnah:**
> "[At the Seder those who serve] should not give him fewer than four cups of wine even if [the funds come] from the charity plate."

### Gemara - Source of Four Cups

**Rabbi Yohanan in name of Rabbi Benaiah:**
> "[They] correspond to the four redemptions [or acts of redemption, mentioned in reference to Egypt]:"

**Biblical Source - Exodus 6:6-7:**
> "Say, therefore, to the Israelite people: I am the Lord. **I will take you out** [from under the burdens of the Egyptians and deliver you from their bondage. **I will deliver you** [from their bondage]. **I will redeem you** with an outstretched arm and through extraordinary chastisements]. **And I will take you** to be my people,' etc."

**The Four Terms:**
1. "I will take out"
2. "I will deliver"
3. "I will redeem"
4. "I will take"

---

## Exodus 6:5-8

**Full Context:**
[Verses containing the four expressions of redemption]

---

## The Rambam's Laws of Chametz and Matza - Chapter Seven

### Halacha 1: The Mitzvah to Tell the Story

**Positive Commandment:**
> "It is a positive commandment of the Torah to relate the miracles and wonders wrought for our ancestors in Egypt on the night of the fifteenth of Nisan, as [Exodus 13:3] states: 'Remember this day, on which you left Egypt,' just as [Exodus 20:8] states: 'Remember the Sabbath day.'"

**When:**
> "From where [is it derived that this mitzvah is to be fulfilled on] the night of the fifteenth? The Torah teaches [Exodus 13:8]: 'And you shall tell your son on that day, saying: "It is because of this..."' [implying that the mitzvah is to be fulfilled] when matzah and maror are placed before you."

**Universal Obligation:**
> "[The mitzvah applies] even though one does not have a son. Even great Sages are obligated to tell about the Exodus from Egypt. Whoever elaborates concerning the events which occurred and took place is worthy of praise."

---

### Halacha 2: Teaching According to Understanding

**Obligation to Inform Sons:**
> "It is a mitzvah to inform one's sons even though they do not ask, as [Exodus 13:8] states: 'You shall tell your son.'"

**Teaching Method:**
> "A father should teach his son according to the son's knowledge:"

**How Applied:**

**If young or foolish:**
> "He should tell him: 'My son, in Egypt, we were all slaves like this maidservant or this slave. On this night, the Holy One, Blessed be He, redeemed us and took us out to freedom.'"

**If older and wise:**
> "He should inform him what happened to us in Egypt and the miracles wrought for us by Moses, our teacher; everything according to the son's knowledge."

---

### Halacha 3: Making Changes to Provoke Questions

**Purpose:**
> "He should make changes on this night so that the children will see and will [be motivated to] ask: 'Why is this night different from all other nights?' until he replies to them: 'This and this occurred; this and this took place.'"

**What Changes:**
- Give them roasted seeds and nuts
- Table should be taken away before they eat
- Matzots should be snatched from each other
- And the like

**Without a Son:**
> "When a person does not have a son, his wife should ask him. If he does not have a wife, [he and a colleague] should ask each other: 'Why is this night different?' This applies even if they are all wise."

**Alone:**
> "A person who is alone should ask himself: 'Why is this night different?'"

---

### Halacha 4: From Degradation to Praise

**Pattern:**
> "One must begin [the narrative describing our ancestors'] base [roots] and conclude with [their] praise."

**What This Means:**

**Begin:**
> "One begins relating how originally, in the age of Terach, our ancestors denied [God's existence] and strayed after vanity, pursuing idol worship."

**Conclude:**
> "One concludes with the true faith: how the Omnipresent has drawn us close to Him, separated us from the gentiles, and drawn us near to His Oneness."

**Similarly:**
> "One begins by stating that we were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt and [describing] all the evil done to us, and concludes with the miracles and wonders that were wrought upon us, and our freedom."

**Biblical Template:**
> "This [implies] that one should extrapolate [the passage beginning] from [Deuteronomy 26:5]: 'An Aramean sought to destroy my ancestor...' until one concludes the entire passage."

**Praise for Elaboration:**
> "Whoever adds and extends his extrapolation of this passage is praiseworthy."

---

### Halacha 5: Three Essential Matters

**Obligation:**
> "Whoever does not mention these three matters on the night of the fifteenth has not fulfilled his obligation. They are: the Paschal sacrifice, matzah, and maror."

**The Paschal Sacrifice:**
> "[It is eaten] because the Omnipresent passed over the houses of our ancestors in Egypt as [Exodus 12:27] states: 'And you shall say: "It is the Paschal sacrifice to God."'"

**The Bitter Herbs:**
> "[They are eaten] because the Egyptians embittered the lives of our ancestors in Egypt."

**The Matzah:**
> "[It is eaten] because of the redemption."

**Reference:**
> "These statements are all referred to as the Haggadah."

---

### Halacha 6: As If You Yourself Left Egypt

**Personal Experience:**
> "In each and every generation, a person must present himself as if he, himself, has now left the slavery of Egypt, as [Deuteronomy 6:23] states: 'He took us out from there.'"

**Torah Command:**
> "Regarding this manner, God commanded in the Torah: 'Remember that you were a slave [Deuteronomy 5:15]' - i.e., as if you, yourself, were a slave and went out to freedom and were redeemed."

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Splitting of the Sea - 7th Day Teaching

## Note: Passover Content (Not Chanukah)

**Resource Type:** Teaching for 7th day of Passover

**Source:** Shluchim Exchange forum

**URL:** http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/forum/viewtopic.php?t=546162

**Purpose:** Explain significance of splitting the sea miracle

**Audience:** Classes, divrei Torah, 7th day events

---

## The Question

**What We Celebrate:**
> "On the seventh day of Passover, we celebrate the miracle of the splitting of the sea."

**The Deeper Question:**
> "In Kabbalah, as well as in Chassidus, the question is asked as to why the necessity for such a grand miracle."

**Simple Explanations Insufficient:**
> "Were it to be just to save the Jewish people, or to kill the Egyptians, G-d had many other ways to do this."

---

## The Miracle Will Repeat

**Isaiah (-11:15):**
> "And the Lord shall dry up the tongue of the Egyptian Sea, and He shall lift His hand over the river with the strength of His wind, and He shall beat it into seven streams, and He shall lead [the exiles] with shoes."

**The Question:**
> "What does splitting water and passing through it have to do with the redemption from Egypt and then the final redemption?"

---

## Connection to Receiving Torah

### G-d's Promise to Moses

**When Told of Exodus:**
> "When G-d told Moses that G-d was going to take the Jewish people out of Egypt, G-d said, 'When you take the people out of Egypt, you will worship G-d on this mountain.'"

**Meaning:**
> "Everything which happened from leaving Egypt until receiving the Torah at Mt. Sinai, was happening either to bring the Jewish people out of Egypt, or to bring them to receiving the Torah."

**Purpose of Crossing the Sea:**
> "Crossing through the sea was for the purpose of bringing us to receiving the Torah."

---

## When Moshiach Comes

**Mishneh Torah, Laws of Teshuvah, Chapter 9, Law 2:**
> "He [Moshiach] will teach the entire nation and instruct them in the path of G-d."

**Then Too:**
> "The crossing of the waters will be in preparation of us receiving this new and deeper form of Torah knowledge."

---

## Two Levels: Hearing vs. Seeing

### Moses - Power of Hearing

**What Moses Brought:**
> "In Kabbalah we are taught that Moses brought us the power of hearing G-d within the Torah, as Moses said (-Deuteronomy 4:1), 'And now, O Israel, listen to the statutes.'"

**Moses's Request and Limitation:**
> "When Moses asked (-Exodus 33:18-22), 'Show me, now, Your glory!,' G-d responded with, 'You will not be able to see My face, for man shall not see Me and live.'"

---

### Moshiach - Power of Seeing

**Higher Level:**
> "Moshiach will bring us a higher level in which we will see G-d within His Torah, as the verse states (-Isaiah 40:5), 'And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh together shall see that the mouth of the Lord spoke.'"

**Therefore:**
> "When Moshiach comes, we will again go through the split waters."

---

## Sea Creatures vs. Land Creatures

### Kabbalistic Meaning

**Sea Creatures:**
> "According to Kabbalah and Chassidus, [sea creatures] represent the Hidden Worlds, such as the angels, which live within a conscientiousness of G-d being their life-force, with no Evil Inclination."

**Land Creatures:**
> "[Land creatures] represent the Revealed Worlds, in which we have an Evil Inclination, and often aren't conscious of G-d being our sole life-force."

---

### Hidden vs. Revealed Worlds

**Hidden Worlds:**
- Heaven
- Spiritual realms
- Conscious of G-d constantly
- No evil inclination

**Revealed Worlds:**
- Physical world (ultimate)
- Have evil inclination
- Often not conscious of G-d as sole life-force

---

## G-d's Desire: Torah in Physical World

**Specific Intent:**
> "G-d's desire was specifically to give the Torah to us physical people, souls within bodies, within a physical world."

**Superiority of Physical Mitzvot:**
> "Even more so, our sages tell us that the spiritual mitzvot that were performed by our forefathers are considered like a passing fragrance, while our physical mitzvot are the essence of Torah and mitzvot."

**Ultimate Experience:**
> "Thus, the desire of G-d is that we have the ultimate experience of G-d conscientiousness specifically here in the physical world."

---

## Soul and Body

**Another Layer:**
> "In some teachings, our soul represents the Hidden World, while our body represents the Revealed World, and G-d's desire is that the soul descend into the body, and only then receive the ultimate revelation, through G-d giving us the Torah."

---

## Breaking Down the Barrier

**What Had to Happen:**
> "However, in order for this to happen, the barrier between Heaven and Earth, between the Hidden World and the Revealed World, would have to come down."

**The Process:**
> "The land creatures of the Revealed World would have to first be able to walk through waters of the Hidden World, purifying them and opening them up to hearing G-d at Mount Sinai, and then again to be purified and opened by crossing the waters, in order to seeing G-d, when Moshiach comes."

---

## For Shluchim: Using This Teaching

### 7th Day Application

**Perfect For:**
- 7th day of Passover classes
- Evening of 7th day farbrengen
- Day of 7th day study session
- Pre-Shavuot connection

**Why 7th Day:**
- Celebrates splitting of sea
- Connects Exodus to Sinai
- Links past redemption to future
- Prepares for Shavuot (receiving Torah)

---

### Teaching Structure

**Opening (5 minutes):**
- Question: Why such grand miracle?
- G-d had other ways to save/destroy
- Must be deeper purpose

**Development (10-15 minutes):**
- Connection to receiving Torah
- Everything between Exodus and Sinai
- Crossing sea prepared us
- Moshiach will repeat (Isaiah)

**Core Concepts (10-15 minutes):**
- Moses: Hearing G-d (Deuteronomy 4:1)
- Moshiach: Seeing G-d (Isaiah 40:5)
- Sea creatures: Hidden Worlds (angels, no evil inclination)
- Land creatures: Revealed Worlds (us, evil inclination)
- G-d's desire: Torah in physical world

**Application (5-10 minutes):**
- Breaking down barrier
- Land creatures walk through waters
- First time: Prepared to hear (Sinai)
- Second time: Prepared to see (Moshiach)
- We are that process today

---

### Discussion Questions

**Understanding the Miracle:**
1. Why wasn't a simpler miracle sufficient?
2. What's unique about passing through water?
3. How does physical action prepare for spiritual revelation?

**Hearing vs. Seeing:**
1. What's the difference between hearing and seeing G-d?
2. Why was Moses limited to hearing?
3. How will Moshiach enable seeing?

**Hidden vs. Revealed:**
1. What are examples of Hidden Worlds today?
2. How do we experience Revealed Worlds?
3. Why is physical world superior despite evil inclination?

**Personal Application:**
1. How do we break barriers in our lives?
2. Where do we need to "cross waters"?
3. What prepares us to receive Torah more deeply?

---

### Connection to Shavuot

**Timeline:**
- 7th of Passover: Splitting of sea
- 49 days of Omer: Preparation
- Shavuot: Receiving Torah

**Teaching Flow:**
- 7th day: Prepared by crossing waters
- Omer: Refining ourselves
- Shavuot: Ready to receive

**Use This Teaching:**
- On 7th day: Explain how sea crossing prepared for Sinai
- During Omer: Remind of process
- Before Shavuot: Complete the connection

---

### Expansion Opportunities

**Can Add:**
- More about Hidden/Revealed Worlds
- Specific examples of angels' consciousness
- How physical mitzvot elevate spiritual
- Stories of Rebbes on 7th day
- Moshiach seudah connection
- Maimonides on Moshiach teaching Torah

**Can Reference:**
- Tanya on soul descending into body
- Zohar on splitting of sea
- Midrash on preparations for Sinai
- Prophets on future redemption

---

### Visual Aids

**For Presentation:**
- Diagram: Hidden Worlds vs. Revealed Worlds
- Timeline: Egypt → Sea → Sinai
- Comparison chart: Hearing vs. Seeing
- Map: Journey through sea to mountain
- Future: Waters split again (Isaiah)

---

### Different Audience Levels

**Beginners:**
- Focus on: Why sea had to split
- Simple: Prepared us for Torah
- Future: Will happen again with Moshiach

**Intermediate:**
- Add: Hearing vs. Seeing distinction
- Explain: Hidden and Revealed Worlds
- Connect: To personal spiritual journey

**Advanced:**
- Full: Kabbalistic concepts
- Deep: Soul/body parallel
- Chassidic: Breaking barriers
- Moshiach: New level of revelation

---

## Related Resources

**In This Collection:**
- File 1106: Passover Seder outline (7th day section mentions sea splitting, women's tambourines)
- File 1112: Moshiach Seudah (7th/8th day observance)
- File 1107/1108: Miriam teachings (women at sea)
- File 1100: Haggadah class (redemption themes)

---

**Bottom Line:**

Teaching for 7th day of Passover from Shluchim Exchange (forum viewtopic.php?t=546162) explaining significance of splitting sea miracle starting with question "on seventh day of Passover we celebrate miracle of splitting of sea" but "in Kabbalah as well as Chassidus question is asked as to why necessity for such grand miracle" because "were it to be just to save Jewish people or to kill Egyptians G-d had many other ways to do this." **Miracle will repeat:** Isaiah 11:15 "And Lord shall dry up tongue of Egyptian Sea and He shall lift His hand over river with strength of His wind and He shall beat it into seven streams and He shall lead exiles with shoes" - question: "what does splitting water and passing through it have to do with redemption from Egypt and then final redemption?" **Connection to receiving Torah:** When G-d told Moses going to take Jewish people out of Egypt said "when you take people out of Egypt you will worship G-d on this mountain" meaning "everything which happened from leaving Egypt until receiving Torah at Mt. Sinai was happening either to bring Jewish people out of Egypt or to bring them to receiving Torah" - "crossing through sea was for purpose of bringing us to receiving Torah." **When Moshiach comes:** Mishneh Torah Laws of Teshuvah Chapter 9 Law 2 "He [Moshiach] will teach entire nation and instruct them in path of G-d" then too "crossing of waters will be in preparation of us receiving this new and deeper form of Torah knowledge." **Two levels hearing vs seeing:** Moses brought us power of hearing G-d within Torah (Deuteronomy 4:1 "And now O Israel listen to statutes"), when Moses asked Exodus 33:18-22 "Show me now Your glory" G-d responded "You will not be able to see My face for man shall not see Me and live;" Moshiach will bring higher level in which we will see G-d within His Torah (Isaiah 40:5 "And glory of Lord shall be revealed and all flesh together shall see that mouth of Lord spoke"), therefore "when Moshiach comes we will again go through split waters." **Sea creatures vs land creatures kabbalistic meaning:** Sea creatures represent Hidden Worlds such as angels "which live within conscientiousness of G-d being their life-force with no Evil Inclination;" land creatures represent Revealed Worlds "in which we have Evil Inclination and often aren't conscious of G-d being our sole life-force" (Hidden Worlds = Heaven/spiritual realms conscious of G-d constantly no evil inclination, Revealed Worlds = physical world ultimate have evil inclination often not conscious of G-d as sole life-force). **G-d's desire Torah in physical world:** "G-d's desire was specifically to give Torah to us physical people souls within bodies within physical world;" "even more so our sages tell us that spiritual mitzvot that were performed by our forefathers are considered like passing fragrance while our physical mitzvot are essence of Torah and mitzvot" - "thus desire of G-d is that we have ultimate experience of G-d conscientiousness specifically here in physical world." **Soul and body:** "In some teachings our soul represents Hidden World while our body represents Revealed World and G-d's desire is that soul descend into body and only then receive ultimate revelation through G-d giving us Torah." **Breaking down barrier:** "In order for this to happen barrier between Heaven and Earth between Hidden World and Revealed World would have to come down - the land creatures of Revealed World would have to first be able to walk through waters of Hidden World purifying them and opening them up to hearing G-d at Mount Sinai and then again to be purified and opened by crossing waters in order to seeing G-d when Moshiach comes." **For Shluchim:** Perfect for 7th day Passover classes/evening farbrengen/day study session/pre-Shavuot connection (celebrates splitting of sea, connects Exodus to Sinai, links past redemption to future, prepares for Shavuot receiving Torah); teaching structure 40-50 minutes (opening 5 question why such grand miracle, development 10-15 connection to receiving Torah/everything between Exodus and Sinai/crossing sea prepared us/Moshiach will repeat Isaiah, core concepts 10-15 Moses hearing G-d/Moshiach seeing G-d/sea creatures Hidden Worlds/land creatures Revealed Worlds/G-d's desire Torah in physical world, application 5-10 breaking down barrier/land creatures walk through waters/first time prepared to hear Sinai/second time prepared to see Moshiach/we are that process today); connection to Shavuot timeline (7th Passover splitting of sea, 49 days Omer preparation, Shavuot receiving Torah) use teaching on 7th day/during Omer/before Shavuot; expansion opportunities can add more about Hidden/Revealed Worlds/specific examples angels' consciousness/how physical mitzvot elevate spiritual/stories of Rebbes on 7th day/Moshiach seudah connection/Maimonides on Moshiach teaching Torah, can reference Tanya on soul descending into body/Zohar on splitting sea/Midrash on preparations for Sinai/prophets on future redemption. Related resources: File 1106 (Passover Seder outline 7th day section mentions sea splitting women's tambourines), 1112 (Moshiach Seudah 7th/8th day observance), 1107/1108 (Miriam teachings women at sea), 1100 (Haggadah class redemption themes).
