# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Chabad Rebbes - Stories, Teachings, and Nigunim

## Note: Passover Content (Not Chanukah)

**Resource Type:** Collection of stories and teachings about Chabad Rebbes

**Format:** Seven Rebbes with associated nigunim and life lessons

**Purpose:** Teaching Chabad history, philosophy, and musical tradition

**Audience:** Classes, farbrengens, educational programs, Passover events

---

## Opening: The Power of Niggun

### Alter Rebbe's Teaching

**The Tongue and Melody:**
> "The tongue is the pen of the heart, but melody is the quill of the soul."

**Power of Niggun:**
> "A Niggun can pull one out of the deepest mire."

---

### Connection to Soul

> "A Jew is a human being in touch with his inner essence and possessed of the ability to unveil it, and bring it forth. How does one connect with one's inner self, one's highest levels of soul, above all, wisdom and comprehension, and then reveal it in a mundane, finite world? This can be accomplished through song."

*[thanks to A Simple Jew for this quote]*

---

### Rabbi Dov Ber's Teaching

> "Rabbi Dov Ber, the son and successor of Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, often used to say, 'My saintly father could penetrate into the innermost recesses of a Chassid's soul by either a word of Chassidus or a niggun.'"

---

## Historical Context: Baal Shem Tov's Vision

### Shalosh Tenuos (Three Movements)

**The Ascent:**
> "Approximately fifty years after the birth of the Baal Shem Tov, in the year 5507 -- according to a letter he wrote to his brother-in-law -- on the awesome day of Rosh Hashana, the Baal Shem Tov ascended to the supernal chamber of the Moshiach."

**The Question:**
> "He asked the Moshiach, 'When, master, will you come?'"

**The Answer:**
> "The reply: 'When your wellsprings will spread to the outside.'"

---

### The Mission

> "Ever since that Rosh Hashanah, the world has not been the same. Here we are, entering into our 265th year of spreading the wellsprings of the Ba'al Shem Tov, paving the way for Moshiach to fulfill his promise to the Bal Shem Tov."

**The Chain:**
- Rebbi Yisroel Ba'al Shem Tov
- R' DovBer - Mesritcher Maggid
- R' Shneur Zalman of Liadi - the Alter Rebbe

---

## 1. Alter Rebbe: Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi

### Niggun: Avienu Malkainu

---

### Napoleon and the Czar

**Historical Context:**
European Jewish leaders divided over Napoleon's campaign

**Those Who Supported Napoleon:**
- Rabbi Shlomo of Karlin
- Rabbi Israel, the Maggid of Kozhnitz
- Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Barditchev
- Rabbi Mendel of Rimanov

**Their Reasoning:**
> "The leaders of European Jewry were likewise divided. There were rabbis and Chassidic rebbes who eagerly awaited liberation by Napoleons armies. No longer would the Jewish people be locked into ghettos and deprived of their means of earning a livelihood; no longer would the state be allied with a religion hostile to the Jewish faith. Liberated from the persecution and poverty that had characterized Jewish life on European soil for a dozen centuries, the Jewish people would be free to deepen and intensify their bond with G-d in ways previously unimaginable. Indeed, there were those...who believed that a French victory would ready the world for the coming of Moshiach and the final redemption."

---

### Alter Rebbe's Position

**Disagreement:**
> "Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi disagreed. He said, if Bonaparte will be victorious, Jewish wealth will increase and prestige of the Jewish people will be raised; but their hearts will disintegrate and be distanced from their Father in Heaven. But if Alexandar will be victorious, although Israel's poverty will increase and their prestige will be lowered, their hearts will be joined, bound and unified with their Father in Heaven."

---

### The Contest

**Morning of Rosh Hashanah 5573 (1812-1813):**
> "Chassidim tell of a contest that took place on the morning of Rosh Hashanah between Rabbi Schneur Zalman and the Maggid of Kozhnitz to decide the outcome of Napoleons war against Russia."

**Kabbalistic Significance:**
> "According to Kabbalistic tradition, the sounding of the shofar on Rosh Hashanah effects G-ds coronation as king of the universe and the Divine involvement in human affairs for the coming year; each of these two rebbes therefore endeavored to be the first to sound the shofar in the fateful year of 5573 (1812-1813) and thereby influence the outcome of the war."

**The Race:**
- Maggid of Kozhnitz: Rose well before dawn, immersed in mikveh, began prayers at earliest permissible hour, prayed speedily, sounded shofar
- Alter Rebbe: Departed from common practice, sounded shofar at crack of dawn, **before** morning prayers

**The Result:**
> "'The Litvak (Lithuanian, as Rabbi Schneur Zalman was affectionately called by his colleagues) has bested us,' said Rabbi Israel of Kozhnitz to his disciples."

---

### Philosophy: No Easy Fix

> "The Alter Rebbe's philosophy is there is no easy fix in life. Positive change will only come through toiling on one's self. The promises of freedom with Napoleon would come with a cost that no one could afford, and would not last. Only through hard work, even if it means being stuck in olden days is what will ultimately prevail."

---

## 2. Mitteler Rebbe: Rabbi Dov Ber

### Niggun: Mitteler Rebbe Kapelye

---

### The Crying Baby Story

**Unusual Concentration:**
> "The Mitteler Rebbe was known for his unusual power of concentration. When he was engaged in study or prayer, he did not hear or see a thing around him."

**The Incident:**
> "Once, when Rabbi Dov Ber was studying, his baby sleeping in a nearby cot fell out of its cradle and began to cry. Rabbi Dov Ber did not hear the baby's cries and continued learning. But the infant's grandfather, Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi (the founder of Chabad Chasidism), who was in his room on an upper floor and was also learning at that time, did hear the baby's cries. He interrupted his studies, went downstairs, picked up the infant, soothed it and put it back in its cradle. Still, the infant's father did not hear or see what went on around him."

**The Teaching:**
> "Later on, Rabbi Schneur Zalman told his son: 'No matter how important the thing is in which a Jew is engaged, one must always hear the cry of a child.'"

---

### Applications

**For Parents:**
Must hear cry of their children

**For Teachers:**
Must hear cry of students

**For Children:**
Must hear cry of peers

**Universal:**
> "This story is applicable to parents, teachers and even children. We must always hear the cry of a child, whether that child is a child in years or knowledge or commitment to Judaism. Even when we are involved in important things, we must not neglect or ignore the cry of the child."

---

### The Inner Child

> "This applies, as well, to the child within each one of us. This spark of good and G-dliness, the wide-eyed and innocent trust and belief that the world can become a perfect place, that evil can be eradicated, that goodness can prevail, and that 'I' can be a part of it or perhaps even be the catalyst for realizing the world's potential, must be listened to and heeded."

---

## 3. Tzemach Tzedek: Rabbi Menachem Mendel

### Niggun: Niggun Hishtatchus

**Note:** Rebbe would spend much time praying at resting place of his holy mother, seen in deep meditative state singing this song

---

### The Devorah Leah Story

**Historical Context - 1792:**
> "The year was 1792 and the teachings of Chassidism were being disseminated very successfully. The Chassidic movement was growing rapidly and gaining strength by leaps and bounds. At the forefront of the movement's growth was the Alter Rebbe who served as a pillar of knowledge. It was a time that should have been filled with exultation and exuberance as Judaism became more meaningful to more and more Jews, as they embraced these revolutionary teachings."

**The Gray Cloud:**
> "Nevertheless, a gray cloud hung over the horizon. The Alter Rebbe, aware that in the spiritual worlds there existed strong opposition against him and the revelation of the deep secrets of the Torah, was filled with trepidation. He did all that he could to prevent a disastrous decree."

---

### Alter Rebbe's Efforts

**What He Did:**
- Sent carefully appointed messengers to gravesites of Baal Shem Tov and Maggid of Mezeritch to intercede
- Notified colleagues (students of Maggid) of dangerous time
- Asked Reb Nochum of Chernobyl for blessing
- Locked himself in study in prayer and supplication

**Result:**
> "Nevertheless, he sensed that all his attempts were to no avail."

---

### Devorah Leah's Response

**Her Understanding:**
> "One day, amidst his anxiety, the Alter Rebbe called for his daughter Devorah Leah. In the privacy of his study, he informed her about the very difficult times that lay ahead, and the strong heavenly opposition against revealing the innermost aspects of Chassidism. He described to her, in the gravest of tones, which he had seen a vision of the faces of the Maggid and the Baal Shem Tov, and they were extremely dark and clouded. Devorah Leah understood that her father's very life was in danger."

---

### The Plan

**Gathering Chassidim:**
> "Acting on her own initiative, Devorah Leah gathered together three of her father's senior Chassidim. She requested that they promise to fulfill all that she asked of them and swear not to reveal her requests to anyone. Only when they had agreed to these conditions, did she proceed."

**The Oath:**
> "Breaking down in tears, Devorah Leah begged them, 'I ask you to swear a solemn oath, one that cannot be annulled, that you will follow my request even if a human life is at stake.'"

**The Decision:**
> "Devorah Leah notified the Chassidim of the urgency of the present situation and the threat hanging over Reb Schneur Zalman's life. Resolutely, she stated, 'You three Chassidim will now constitute a Bet Din, a Court of Jewish Law. I have decided to give my own life in lieu of my father's. I will die and he will live.'"

---

### Public Declaration

**Eve of Rosh Hashanah:**
> "On the Eve of Rosh Hashanah of that year, after the afternoon prayers, Devorah Leah went into the small synagogue where her family and some elder Chassidim were engrossed in prayers. She walked towards the holy ark and loudly proclaimed, 'You are all witnesses before these Torah scrolls, that I, Devorah Leah, daughter of Sterna, accept upon myself, with a clear mind, to exchange lives with my father, Schneur Zalman, son of Rivkah. I, through my death, will be the atonement.'"

---

### First Night of Rosh Hashanah

**The Blessing:**
> "That night, the first night of Rosh Hashanah, the Alter Rebbe left his private room to seek out Devorah Leah. As she approached him, he began to bless her with the customary blessing of Leshana Tova... (you should be blessed with a good year.) She abruptly interrupted his blessing with, 'Father, leshana tova tikatev vetechatem – you should be inscribed and sealed for a good new year.' When he, in turn, was about to finish his blessing to her, she pleaded, 'Father, say no more!'"

---

### The Final Request

**After Rosh Hashanah:**
> "At the conclusion of Rosh Hashanah, the Alter Rebbe called for Devorah Leah and her husband, Rabbi Sholom Shachna. Rabbi Sholom broke down in tears, asking, 'What are we to do? Our young son, Menachem Mendel, is so special yet he is so young and tender. He has just celebrated his third birthday.'"

**Devorah Leah's Request:**
> "Devorah Leah's last request of her father was that he should personally involve himself with the duty of educating and raising her young and only son."

**The Promise:**
> "Reassuring her, the Alter Rebbe promised, 'Your son, Menachem [Hebrew for comfort], will be a nechama (comfort) to me, a nechama to you and a nechama to all of the Jewish people.'"

---

### The Fulfillment

**Third Day of Tishrei:**
> "The following day (tonight), on the third day of Tishrei, Devorah Leah's prayer came true. Her soul left her body and ascended to the heavens."

**The Legacy:**
> "Her little Menachem Mender grew to be one of the greatest Jewish leaders in his generation. After his uncle Rabbi Dov Ber's passing, he assumed the leadership of Chabad Chassidism and brought the movement to unparalleled growth. His own followers numbered well over a half-a-million and he was greatly respected and revered by all Jewry, Chassidic and non-Chassidic alike."

---

## 4. Rebbe Mahrash: Rabbi Shmuel

### Niggun: Litchachilah Aribar

---

### The Yechidus Story

**The Setting:**
> "Evening had fallen, and Rabbi Shmuel of Lubavitch was receiving those who came to seek his counsel in yechidus, the private meeting of souls between rebbe and chassid. Scarcely an hour had passed, and already the Rebbe was exhausted; he called a break and asked for a fresh change of clothes."

**Secretary's Observation:**
> "The Rebbe's secretary emerged from the room carrying the clothes which the Rebbe had removed. They were drenched in sweat. 'Master of the universe,' muttered the secretary, 'why does he exert himself so?! Every hour he needs a new change of clothes. Why does the Rebbe sweat so much?'"

---

### The Rebbe's Response

**Dismissal:**
> "The Rebbe's door opened, and Rabbi Shmuel stood in the doorway. 'Go home,' he said to his secretary. 'You have not the slightest understanding of my work. I will continue to pay your salary, but I no longer desire your services.'"

**The Explanation:**
> "'Don't you understand? In the past hour twenty people came to see me. Each of them poured out his soul to me and asked for my assistance in curing it of its spiritual ills. To relate to each one's dilemma, I have to see it through their eyes. So I must divest myself of my own personality and circumstances and clothe myself in theirs. Then, in order to answer them, I must re-assume my own persona - otherwise, why would they come to consult with me?'"

**The Question:**
> "'Did you ever attempt to change your clothes forty times an hour? If such physical dressing and undressing would exhaust you and bathe you in sweat, can you imagine what it involves to do so in the mental, emotional and spiritual sense?'"

---

### Philosophy: Litchachilah Aribar

**Meaning:**
> "Litchachilah Aribar means that one must transcend limitations."

**Application:**
> "We can never solve any problem by circumventing it. However, when one 'wrestles in mud' even if he wins, he may come up dirty. The Rebbe taught, cannot allow any physical limitation to get in our way of a solution, rather we must first commit ourselves mentally, emotionally and spiritually, and then we have the power to transcend ourselves to a higher place, where the problem is not a problem anymore."

---

## 5. Rebbe Rashab: Rabbi Sholom DovBer

### Niggun: Niggun Rostov

---

### The Child's Question

**The Visit (Age 4 or 5):**
> "On the occasion of his fourth or fifth birthday, Rabbi Sholom DovBer visited his grandfather, Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Lubavitch. Upon entering his grandfather's room, the child burst into tears."

**Why Crying:**
> "His teacher in cheder had taught them that week's Torah reading, Vayeira (Genesis 18:1-22:24), which begins, 'And G-d revealed himself to Abraham...' Why, wept the child, doesn't G-d reveal Himself to me?"

---

### The Grandfather's Answer

> "Rabbi Menachem Mendel replied: 'When a Jew, a tzaddik, realizes at the age of 99 that he must circumcise himself -- that he must continue to perfect himself -- he is worthy that G-d should reveal Himself to him.'"

---

### Two Extremes

**The Analysis:**
> "The child's question and the grandfather's explanation express two extremes, whose contrast and synthesis are a hallmark of the Rebbe Rashab's approach."

**The Child:**
> "Imagine: a five year old weeping because G-d doesn't reveal Himself to Him! To 'see' G-d -- to attain a consummate vision of the Truth of Truths -- is the ultimate goal of every spiritual quest. It is a goal that takes the greatest of the great at least a lifetime to achieve. Yet here is a child -- a very special child, but one who nonetheless is still at the very beginning of his spiritual journey -- who is disturbed, to the point of tears, by the fact that he has not yet attained this goal!"

**The 99-Year-Old:**
> "And on the other hand, we have a man who has 99 years of the most extraordinary spiritual achievements behind him, who recognizes that he is still not perfect -- that he must continue to change, grow and improve himself."

---

### The Synthesis

> "These two prototypes are not a conflicting vision of life, but a complementary and indispensable to each other. To strive for the ultimate, yet never feel that one has arrived. To have huge aspirations, yet remain humble and unassuming. To say: I want to, and can, do it all -- yet, no matter how much one has done, to know that there is still more to do."

---

## 6. Previous Rebbe: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak

### Niggun: The Bienoni

---

### The Gun Story

**Confrontation with Communists:**
> "In one of his confrontations with the communist authorities, the officers interrogating the Previous Lubavitcher Rebbe threatened with a gun, boasting of its power to influence people."

**The Response:**
> "The Previous Rebbe replied that the gun could only influence 'someone who has one world and many gods. I,' he continued, 'have one G-d and two worlds.'"

---

### Three Decades of Struggle

**Ten Years in Russia:**
> "The Previous Rebbe spent 10 years leading Chabad in Russia, struggling to preserve Judaism under the communists."

**Ten Years in Warsaw:**
> "The next ten years the Rebbe spent in Warsaw, struggling to preserve Judaism during the rise of the Nazis."

**Ten Years in America:**
> "The finial ten years of his life, he spent struggling to preserve Judaism in the land of opportunity, America."

---

### Like the Bienoni

> "But just like the Bienoni in the book of Tanya, there is no rest - but he never allows his struggles to overcome him."

---

## 7. The Rebbe: Rabbi Menachem Mendel

### Niggun: Anim Zemiros

---

### The Shofar Incident

**The Scene:**
> "On Rosh Hashana, one particular year, the Rebbe was blowing shofar as was his custom. There was some difficulty with the blowing of the shofar. The Rebbe tried for a long time and also tried blowing the second shofar that the Rebbe had with him, but with no success."

**The Chassid's Hachlota:**
> "In the crowd of the thousands of people assembled, stood a Chossid, who in those moments made a non-verbal hachlota (resolution), that he would take upon himself good deeds in order that the tekios should be successful. At that point, the Rebbe continued the tekios completing them successfully."

**The Message:**
> "After davening when the Rebbe was leaving the shul, walking through the two aisles of people, the Rebbe stopped and turned to this individual person in the crowd and said to him, 'Don't forget to fulfill your hachlota!'"

---

### The Dancing Jew

**The Story:**
> "It happened once in a European shtetl that on the day after Yom Kippur the community arrived to the synagogue for morning prayers, only to find a member of the community dancing around the podium at the center of the synagogue, singing Anim Zemiros with great fervor. It turned out that the Jew was so engrossed in the melody that he had danced the entire night, not noticing that the fast had ended and that he hadn't eaten for more than a day and a half!"

---

### Rebbe's Teaching - Simchat Torah 1961

**The Explanation:**
> "The Rebbe related this story and taught this melody on Simchat Torah, 1961. He explained that when a Jew completes the Yom Kippur fast he is joyous, having fulfilled G-d's commandment; however, he still feels a strong longing for the holiness of Yom Kippur."

**Application:**
> "To make this yom tov live with us the entire year, we all must take upon ourselves a mental hachlota!"

---

## Daled Bavos (Four Gates)

### The Holy Niggun

**Composer:**
> "A melody, niggun, composed by Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, the first Chabad Rebbe."

**Structure:**
> "The song has four stanzas, corresponding to the four spiritual worlds, Atzilut, B'riah, Yetzirah, and Assiyah."

**Purpose:**
> "Each stanza is intended to elevate the singer and listener to the next spiritual realm."

**Special Status:**
> "Due its holiness, this special melody is only sung on special occasions and dates."

---

## For Shluchim: Using This Resource

[Full teaching guide with applications for each section, discussion questions, farbrengen format, holiday connections, niggun teaching, visual aids, different audience approaches, and integration with Passover themes]

---

**Bottom Line:**

[Comprehensive summary of all seven Chabad Rebbes, their stories, teachings, and nigunim with full details about each Rebbe's philosophy and the overall message of spreading the wellsprings to bring Moshiach]

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] "What a Mess" - Moshiach Message

## Note: Passover Content (Not Chanukah)

**Resource Type:** Short inspirational teaching

**Author:** Rabbi Elisha Greenbaum

**Theme:** Resolving contradiction between promised redemption and current chaos

**Purpose:** Address doubts about Moshiach coming despite world appearing to deteriorate

**Format:** Essay with analogy

---

## The Contradiction

**What We're Told:**

> "You tell me that Moshiach is on his way and the world is standing on the brink of a whole new era of universal peace and tranquillity, but I don't see it."

> "You tell me that things are improving, that people are getting nicer and that good times will soon be here, but I beg to differ."

---

## What I See Instead

**The Reality:**

> "I see a mess. I see the greatest of our nation dying horrible deaths due to a tiny foreign virus. I see a world where 16 year old kids die of brain tumours and young mothers go to sleep and don't wake up. I see entire countries imploding. I see innocent people being accused of horrific crimes, while the real criminals bask in the false approval of a supine press."

**The Questions:**

> "What on earth is the world coming to and, even more frightening, where will we end up?"

> "But the Rebbe assured us that Moshiach is coming. But I can't see it. And the inherent contradiction is driving me mad. Who should I believe?"

---

## The Analogy: 10 Minutes Till Showtime

### The Scene Backstage

**Ever Produced or Acted in a Play?**

> "You've spent untold hours preparing the props and memorising lines. People who started out as strangers have practiced together till they feel that they know each other's personalities backwards. The audience is filing in and the curtain will soon be rising."

**But Then You Look Around and Panic:**

> "The actors are huddled to the side fighting over the script. The set designer is still daubing at the backdrops and there are sound and lighting cables and equipment strewn everywhere. Random pieces of costumes lie abandoned wherever you look and altogether it's a scene of utter chaos mixed with a healthy dose of last minute confusion."

**The Question:**

> "Will we ever be ready on time?"

---

### The Miracle

**As the Minutes Tick Closer:**

> "However, as the minutes tick closer, everything miraculously comes together. That which looked like a randomised accumulation of unpreparedness soon reveals itself as the building blocks of artistic accomplishment."

**The Inexplicable Success:**

> "You don't understand how, yet somehow it all comes good on the night."

---

## The Application

### Storm Before the Calm

**What We See Now:**

> "When we look around now and see only tragedy, petty infighting and bitterness, we're seeing the storm before the calm."

**What Will Happen:**

> "That depressing vista of the present will soon surrender to the promised perfection that awaits."

**Our Limited Perspective:**

> "It might look to us like an unsurmountable mess of loss and decay, but when the fog of confusion is allowed to clear, we'll look back and appreciate the order that lay concealed beneath the chaos."

---

### The Pieces Coming Together

**Current State:**

> "Until you put the pieces of history together and step back to see the final product, you've got nothing but a mess."

**When Moshiach Comes:**

> "But once Moshiach comes, and the seemingly random shards of apparent anarchy fall into place, we'll be able to see that all the chaos and confusion was really the building blocks of perfection."

**The Ultimate Understanding:**

> "Soon all the pain and suffering will be accounted for and we'll understand that life until now was just the precursor to building a permanent stage on which Hashem can perform."

---

## For Shluchim: Using This Teaching

### When to Use

**Perfect For:**
- Addressing doubts about Moshiach
- Times of crisis or tragedy
- When community feels discouraged
- Pre-Passover classes (redemption theme)
- Farbrengens on Geulah
- Email/bulletin inspiration

**Audience:**
- Skeptics who don't see redemption coming
- Those experiencing personal tragedy
- Community facing collective challenges
- Anyone questioning where the world is headed

---

### Teaching Structure

**Opening (2-3 minutes):**
- Voice the contradiction
- "You tell me Moshiach is coming, but I see a mess"
- Acknowledge real suffering and chaos
- Build tension: Who should I believe?

**The Analogy (3-5 minutes):**
- Theater production 10 minutes before curtain
- Describe the backstage chaos vividly
- The panic: "Will we ever be ready?"
- The miracle: Somehow it all comes together
- The building blocks were there all along

**The Application (3-5 minutes):**
- Current chaos = backstage before showtime
- Storm before the calm
- Pieces will come together
- Order concealed beneath chaos
- All will be accounted for and understood

**The Close (1-2 minutes):**
- "Building blocks of perfection"
- "Permanent stage on which Hashem can perform"
- Message of hope and faith
- Rebbe assured us

---

### Key Phrases to Emphasize

**The Contradiction:**
- "Inherent contradiction is driving me mad"
- "Who should I believe?"

**The Analogy:**
- "10 minutes till showtime"
- "Scene of utter chaos mixed with last minute confusion"
- "Somehow it all comes good on the night"

**The Resolution:**
- "Storm before the calm"
- "Order that lay concealed beneath the chaos"
- "Building blocks of perfection"
- "Permanent stage on which Hashem can perform"

---

### Adaptation Options

**Can Add:**
- Specific current events (with sensitivity)
- Personal stories of apparent chaos becoming clear
- Additional analogies (puzzle pieces, construction site, etc.)
- Torah sources on pre-Messianic birth pangs (chevlei Moshiach)
- Rebbe's teachings on signs of redemption

**Can Shorten:**
- Focus only on analogy and application
- Brief version: "Backstage chaos before curtain rises"
- One-liner: "We're 10 minutes till showtime"

**Can Expand:**
- Deeper exploration of apparent contradictions
- More examples of current world chaos
- Historical parallels (Egypt before redemption, etc.)
- Kabbalistic concepts (breaking vessels before repair)
- Personal action items (what to do while waiting)

---

### Tone Considerations

**Important:**
- Acknowledge real pain (don't minimize suffering)
- Validate the confusion and contradiction
- Balance realism with hope
- Avoid sounding dismissive of tragedies
- Use "we" not "you" (speaker shares the struggle)

**Rabbi Greenbaum's Approach:**
- Lists real tragedies specifically
- Doesn't sugar-coat the mess
- Builds genuine tension before resolution
- Analogy is relatable and concrete
- Ends with certainty, not just hope

---

### Discussion Questions

**Understanding the Contradiction:**
1. What makes the promise of redemption feel unbelievable today?
2. What specific "mess" do you see in your life or the world?
3. How does this contradiction affect your faith?

**The Analogy:**
1. Have you ever experienced last-minute chaos becoming success?
2. What are other examples of necessary chaos before creation?
3. How does the theater analogy help or not help you?

**Moving Forward:**
1. What changes if we're "10 minutes till showtime"?
2. How do we live with the tension while waiting?
3. What are the "building blocks" you can identify now?

---

### Related Teachings

**Connect To:**
- Chevlei Moshiach (birth pangs of Moshiach)
- Rebbe's assurances about imminent redemption
- "Darkness before dawn" teachings
- Kabbalistic concepts of shevirah (breaking) before tikkun (repair)
- Passover story (darkest before redemption)

---

### Distribution Formats

**Written:**
- Email subject: "What a Mess - or Is It?"
- Bulletin column with this title
- Social media post (shorter version)
- Printed card for distribution

**Spoken:**
- 10-minute dvar Torah
- 5-minute inspiration before Moshiach seudah
- Part of longer class on redemption
- Response to community tragedy

**Visual:**
- Slide with theater backstage chaos image
- Timeline graphic: backstage → curtain rises → performance
- Quote cards with key phrases

---

## Related Resources

**In This Collection:**
- File 1112: Moshiach Seudah booklet (ritual context)
- File 1111: Splitting of sea teaching (redemption past and future)
- File 1115: "Unfold" Seder guide (redemption themes)
- File 1110: "Let My People Know" (Exodus story)

---

**Bottom Line:**

Short inspirational essay "WHAT A MESS" by Rabbi Elisha Greenbaum addressing contradiction between Rebbe's assurance that Moshiach is coming and current world chaos - voices the doubt: "You tell me that Moshiach is on his way and world is standing on brink of whole new era of universal peace and tranquillity but I don't see it, you tell me that things are improving that people are getting nicer and that good times will soon be here but I beg to differ" and describes reality: "I see a mess - I see greatest of our nation dying horrible deaths due to tiny foreign virus, I see world where 16 year old kids die of brain tumours and young mothers go to sleep and don't wake up, I see entire countries imploding, I see innocent people being accused of horrific crimes while real criminals bask in false approval of supine press" with question "what on earth is world coming to and even more frightening where will we end up?" building tension "But Rebbe assured us that Moshiach is coming, but I can't see it, and inherent contradiction is driving me mad, who should I believe?" **Analogy - 10 minutes till showtime:** "Ever produced or acted in play? You've spent untold hours preparing props and memorising lines, people who started out as strangers have practiced together till they feel that they know each other's personalities backwards, audience is filing in and curtain will soon be rising" but panic when looking around "actors are huddled to the side fighting over script, set designer is still daubing at backdrops and there are sound and lighting cables and equipment strewn everywhere, random pieces of costumes lie abandoned wherever you look and altogether it's scene of utter chaos mixed with healthy dose of last minute confusion" question "will we ever be ready on time?" but miracle "as minutes tick closer everything miraculously comes together - that which looked like randomised accumulation of unpreparedness soon reveals itself as building blocks of artistic accomplishment, you don't understand how yet somehow it all comes good on the night." **Application:** "When we look around now and see only tragedy petty infighting and bitterness we're seeing storm before the calm, that depressing vista of present will soon surrender to promised perfection that awaits, it might look to us like unsurmountable mess of loss and decay but when fog of confusion is allowed to clear we'll look back and appreciate order that lay concealed beneath chaos" - "until you put pieces of history together and step back to see final product you've got nothing but a mess, but once Moshiach comes and seemingly random shards of apparent anarchy fall into place we'll be able to see that all chaos and confusion was really building blocks of perfection, soon all pain and suffering will be accounted for and we'll understand that life until now was just precursor to building permanent stage on which Hashem can perform." **For Shluchim:** Perfect for addressing doubts about Moshiach/times of crisis/when community feels discouraged/pre-Passover classes redemption theme/farbrengens on Geulah; teaching structure 10-15 minutes (opening voice the contradiction acknowledge real suffering, analogy theater production backstage chaos to miraculous success, application current chaos equals backstage before showtime/storm before calm/building blocks of perfection, close message of hope and faith Rebbe assured us); key phrases to emphasize "inherent contradiction is driving me mad," "10 minutes till showtime," "storm before the calm," "order that lay concealed beneath chaos," "building blocks of perfection," "permanent stage on which Hashem can perform"; important tone considerations: acknowledge real pain don't minimize suffering, validate confusion and contradiction, balance realism with hope, avoid sounding dismissive of tragedies, use "we" not "you" (speaker shares struggle), Rabbi Greenbaum lists real tragedies specifically/doesn't sugar-coat/builds genuine tension before resolution/analogy relatable and concrete/ends with certainty not just hope. Note: This Moshiach message appears in Chanukah directory.

# [Misc > For Writer > _5 Chanukah > General] Unfold: A Meaningful Seder - Comprehensive Guide

## Note: Passover Content (Not Chanukah)

**Resource Type:** Complete educational guide

**Title:** "Unfold - A Meaningful Seder" (בס"ד)

**Purpose:** Basis for Passover mitzvot, traditions, and conducting a proper Seder

**Format:** Two-part structured guide with Torah sources and practical instructions

**Audience:** Anyone conducting or learning about Passover Seder

---

## Content Overview

**Part I – Passover Night:**
- The basis for the Passover mitzvot and traditions
- I. The obligations for the Seder night
- II. Pesach, Matzah and Maror
- III. Recounting the story of the Exodus
- IV. The additional Mitzvot

**Part II – The Seder:**
- How to prepare and conduct a Seder from the first cup of wine until the last
- I. Introduction
- II. The Seder plate
- III. The structure and order of the Seder
- IV. Lel Shimurim ("The night which is guarded")

---

# Part I – Passover Night

## I. The Obligations for the Seder Night

### 1) Mitzvot from the Torah

**Four Biblical Commandments:**

1. **Pesach** (Passover offering)
2. **Matzah** (Unleavened bread)
3. **Maror** (Bitter herbs)
4. **Recounting the story of the Exodus**

---

### 2) Mitzvot from our Sages

**Four Rabbinic Ordinances:**

1. **Four cups of wine**
2. **Recline** (while eating and drinking)
3. **Charoset** (Apple-nut mixture)
4. **Hallel** (Psalms of praise)

---

## II. Pesach, Matzah and Maror

### 1) Exodus 12:1-20 - The Complete Text

**Verses 1-2 - The First Month:**

> 1 G-d spoke to Moshe and Aharon in the land of Egypt saying: 2 This month shall be the head of the month for you. It shall be the first of the months of the year.

---

**Verses 3-7 - Selecting and Slaughtering the Lamb:**

> 3 Speak to the entire community of Israel, saying: On the tenth of this month, every man must take a lamb for each extended family, a lamb for each household. 4 If the household is too small for a lamb, then he and a close neighbor can obtain a [lamb together], according to the number of people involved. Each person should be counted for the lamb according to his ability to eat.

> 5 You must have a flawless male lamb, in its first year. You may take either sheep or goats. 6 Hold it in safekeeping until the 14th day of this month.

> The entire community of Israel shall then slaughter [their sacrifices] in the afternoon. 7 They shall take some of its blood and put it on the two doorposts and on the lintel of the houses in which they will be eating it.

---

**Verses 8-11 - How to Eat the Pesach Offering:**

> 8 On that night, they shall eat the meat. **They should eat it roasted over fire, together with matzos and bitter herbs.**

> 9 Do not eat it undercooked or boiled in water, only roasted over the fire, its head with its legs and with its innards.

> 10 Do not leave any of it over until morning. Any part of it that is left over until morning shall be burned in fire.

> 11 This is how you shall eat it: Your waist should be belted, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand. You should eat it quickly. It is a Passover (Pesach) offering to G-d.

---

**Verses 12-14 - The Purpose and Memorial:**

> 12 I will pass through the land of Egypt on this night, and I will smite every first-born in the land of Egypt, both man and beast, and upon all the gods of Egypt I will perform acts of judgment. I [alone] am G-d.

> 13 The blood will be for you as a sign upon the houses where you are. I will see the blood and pass over you (Pasach). There will not be any deadly plague among you when I strike Egypt.

> 14 This day shall be for you as a memorial, and you shall celebrate it as a festival for G-d. For all generations you shall celebrate it as an eternal statute.

---

**Verses 15-20 - The Commandment of Matzah:**

> 15 Eat matzahs for seven days. But on the preceding day, you must have your homes cleared of all leaven. For whoever eats leaven from the first day until the seventh day will have his soul cut off from Israel.

> 16 The first day shall be a sacred holiday, and the seventh day shall [also] be a sacred holiday. No work may be done on these [days]. The only [work] that you may do is that which is needed so that everyone will be able to eat.

> 17 You shall guard the matzos, for on this very day I have brought your legions out of Egypt. You shall observe this day throughout your generations as an eternal statute. 18 In the first month, on the 14th day of the month in the evening, you shall eat matzahs, until the 21st day of the month in the evening. 19 For seven days, leaven shall not be found in your homes. If any person eats a leavening substance, his soul will be cut off from the community of Israel, whether he is a convert or a native of the land. 20 You shall not eat any leavening substance. In all the areas where you live, you shall eat matzahs.

---

### 2) Pesach Offering

**The Mitzvah:**

1. Eating the meat of the Pesach sacrifice is a Mitzvah, as Exodus [12:8] states:

> "On that night, they shall eat the meat. They should eat it roasted over fire, together with matzos and bitter herbs."

**Commemoration Today:**

2. To commemorate the Pesach offering, we are required to have meat on the Seder table (the **Zro'a**, shankbone).

---

### 3) Matzah

**The Biblical Obligation:**

1. Eating the matzah on the fifteenth of Nisan is a Mitzvah from the Torah, as Exodus [12:18] states:

> "In the evening, you shall eat matzah."

**When and Where:**

- This applies **in every place**, whether in the land of Israel or in the Diaspora
- And at **every time**, even when the Temple is destroyed
- Throughout the other days of the festival, eating matzah is left to one's choice

---

**Required Amount:**

2. One is required to eat at least a **kezayit** of Matzah:
   - A measurement formally described as the size of one olive
   - Traditionally determined as **one ounce or 25.6 grams**

**Timing:**

- The consumption of the required amount should be completed in **less than four minutes**

---

### 4) Maror (Bitter Herbs)

**The Torah's Command:**

1. According to the Torah, the eating of the bitter herbs is **not a mitzvah in its own right**: It is dependent on the consumption of the Pesach sacrifice.

- It is **one positive commandment** to eat the meat of the Pesach sacrifice together with matzah and bitter herbs
- However, the Sages established it as a mitzvah, instructing us to eat the bitter herbs alone on this night even if there is no Pesach sacrifice

---

**Which Vegetables:**

2. The bitter herbs referred to by the Torah are:
   - Romaine lettuce
   - Endives
   - Horseradish
   - Date ivy
   - Wormwood

- All of these five species of vegetable are called Maror
- However, it is popular to use either **Romaine lettuce** and/or **pure horseradish (chrein)**

---

**Required Amount:**

3. One is required to eat at least a **kezayit** of Maror:
   - A measurement formally described as the size of one olive
   - Traditionally determined as **one ounce, 25.6 grams**

**Flexibility (Since Rabbinic):**

- If one finds it difficult to consume this amount, one can suffice with a smaller measure of **two-thirds of an ounce**, since this is a rabbinic precept

**Timing:**

- The consumption should be completed in **less than four minutes**
- If this should prove difficult, one can extend the time to a maximum of **6 or 7 minutes**

---

### 5) A Passage from the Haggadah

**Rabban Gamliel's Statement:**

> Rabban Gamliel used to say: Whoever did not say [did not explain the reasons for] these three things on the night of Passover, has not fulfilled his obligation [in an ideal manner]. And these are: The Pesach offering, Matzah and Maror.

---

**Explaining Pesach:**

> The Pesach sacrifice that our fathers ate during the times of the Bet Hamikdash – for what reason did they do so? Because the Omnipresent passed over our fathers' houses in Egypt, as it is said [Exodus 12:27]: "You shall say, it is a Pesach-offering to the Lord because He passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt when He struck the Egyptians with a plague, and He saved our houses. And the people bowed and prostrated themselves."

---

**Explaining Matzah:**

> This matzah that we eat, is for what reason? Because the dough of our fathers did not have time to become leavened before the King of the Kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself to them and redeemed them. Thus it is said [Exodus 12:39]: "They baked matzah-cakes from the dough that they had brought out of Egypt, because it was not leavened; for they had been driven out of Egypt and could not delay, and they had also not prepared any [other] provisions."

---

**Explaining Maror:**

> This maror that we eat, is for what reason? Because the Egyptians embittered our fathers' lives in Egypt, as it is said [Exodus 1:14]: "They made their lives bitter with hard service, with mortar and with bricks, and with all manners of service in the field; all their service which they made them serve with rigor."

---

## III. Recounting the Story of the Exodus

### 1) Exodus 13:3-8

**Verse 3-4 - Remembering the Day:**

> 3 Moshe said to the people: Remember this day, when you went out of Egypt, from the house of bondage, for with a mighty hand G-d took you out of here. No leaven may be eaten. 4 Today you are going out, in the month of Aviv (spring).

---

**Verses 5-7 - The Future Land:**

> 5 When G-d will bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, the Hivites and Yebusites, which He swore to our ancestors to give you – a land flowing with milk and honey, you shall perform this ritual (Pesach) in this month. 6 For seven days, you shall eat matzahs, the seventh day is a festival for G-d.

> 7 Matzahs shall be eaten during the seven days, and no leaven that belongs to you shall be seen in your possession. No leaven that belongs to you shall be seen throughout your borders.

---

**Verse 8 - The Obligation to Tell:**

> 8 **You shall tell your son on that day, saying, "Because of this (these mitzvos of Pesach, Matzah and Maror) G-d did this for me when I went out of Egypt."**

---

### 2) "Vehigadeta Lebincha" - You Shall Tell Your Son

**The Positive Command:**

It is a **positive command from the Torah** to relate the miracles and wonders wrought for our ancestors in Egypt on the night of the fifteenth of Nissan, as Exodus [13:3] states:

> "Remember this day, on which you left Egypt."

---

**When? On the Night of the Fifteenth:**

From where is it derived that this Mitzvah is to be fulfilled on the night of the fifteenth? The Torah teaches [Exodus 13:8]:

> "And you shall tell your son on that day, saying: 'It is because of this…'"

Implying that the mitzvah is to be fulfilled **when matzah and maror are placed before you**.

---

**Who Must Tell:**

- The mitzvah applies **even though one does not have a son**
- **Even great Sages are obligated** to tell about the Exodus from Egypt
- **Whoever elaborates** on the events which occurred is worthy of praise

---

**How to Teach:**

It is a mitzvah to inform one's son **even though they do not ask**, as Exodus [13:8] states: "You shall tell your son."

- A father should **teach his son according to the son's knowledge**

---

**Making Changes to Prompt Questions:**

He should **make changes on this night** so that children will see and will be motivated to ask:

> "Why is this night different than all other nights?"

to which he replies:

> "This and this occurred; this and this took place."

**Which changes should be made?**
- He should give them **roasted seeds and nuts**
- The **table should be taken away** before they eat
- **Matzot should be snatched** from each other
- And the like

---

**If There Are No Children:**

- If a person does not have a son, **his wife should ask him**
- If he does not have a wife, **he and a colleague should ask each other**: "Why is this night different?"
- This applies **even if they are all wise**
- A person who is alone should **ask himself**: "Why is this night different?"

---

### 3) The Haggadah

**Why the Haggadah Was Composed:**

The Haggadah was composed for this reason.

**The Meaning of "Haggadah":**

The term **Haggadah** derives from:

1. Exodus [13:8]: **"Vehigadeta Lebincha"** (you shall tell your child)
2. The expression of **hoda'ah**, thanksgiving and praise to the Holy One, blessed be He, for taking us out of Egypt

---

## IV. The Additional Mitzvot

### 1) Four Cups of Wine

**The Basis:**

1. The four cups were instituted by our Sages to correspond to the **four expressions of redemption**:

> "I will take you out… I will save you… I will redeem you… I will take you for me" (Exodus 6:6-7)

---

**The Obligation:**

2. The Sages enacted that we drink four cups at the seder **in a manner of freedom**.

**Each Cup Has Its Purpose:**

Each one of the cups is a Mitzvah in itself, and requires its own blessing:

1. **First cup**: One recites the **Kiddush** pertaining to the day
2. **Second cup**: One recites the **Haggadah**
3. **Third cup**: One recites the **grace after meals**
4. **Fourth cup**: One concludes the **Hallel**

---

**Amount Required:**

3. Each cup must contain at least a **revi'it**:
   - Approximately **3.5 fluid ounces**

**How Much to Drink:**

- Ideally, one should **drink the whole cup** each time
- If this is difficult, one should drink **a little more than one half of a revi'it** (approximately 2 ounces)

---

### 2) To Recline

**The Principle:**

1. **In each and every generation, a person must present himself as if he himself has just left the slavery of Egypt**, as Deuteronomy [6:23] states:

> "He took us out from there"

Regarding this matter, G-d commanded in the Torah [Deuteronomy 5:15]:

> "Remember that you were a slave"

i.e., **as if you yourself were a slave** and went out to freedom and were redeemed.

**Therefore:**

Our Sages ordained that when a person feasts on this night, he must **eat and drink while he is reclining** in the manner of free men.

---

**When Must One Recline:**

2. When must one recline?
   - When **eating the matzah**
   - When **drinking the four cups of wine**

- It is praiseworthy if one reclines when eating and drinking at other times, but there is **no requirement**

---

**Which Side:**

3. We recline **on the left side**.

**Why Not Other Positions:**

- Lying on one's **right side, face or back**, is not regarded as reclining
- It is not a comfortable manner of eating and cannot be regarded as a symbol of freedom and liberation

**Safety Reason:**

- In addition, reclining on one's right side can be **dangerous**, lest the food go down the windpipe rather than the esophagus

---

### 3) Charoset

**The Obligation:**

1. The Sages ordained charoset as a Mitzvah.

**Two Commemorations:**

- This is to commemorate the **cement** with which our ancestors worked as slaves to construct buildings in Egypt
- It also commemorates the **apple trees** under which the Jewish women in Egypt gave birth without pain, away from the watchful eyes of the Egyptian authorities who were intent on killing their children

---

**How to Make Charoset:**

2. The Charoset can be made of:
   - Dates
   - Dried figs
   - Raisins
   - Apples
   - Nuts
   - Cinnamon
   - Ginger
   - Pomegranates
   - And other fruits which are metaphoric to the Jewish people in the Torah

**Preparation:**

- We **crush them** and add **vinegar or wine**
- And **mix them as straw is mixed into cement**

---

### 4) Hallel

**The Obligation:**

During the Seder, it is a mitzvah to recite the **Hallel** (praise of G-d).

**Source:**

- Hallel (Psalms 113-118) was recited while the Pesach sacrifice was being offered in the Beth Hamikdash
- And while it was eaten during the Seder
- Our sages explain that the Jews recited these verses of praise as they left Egypt

---

🙠  🙢

# Part II – The Seder

## I. Introduction

**From Sefer Maharil:**

> "Every one must conduct himself with **awe** and follow the instructions of the sages who arranged the precept of the Seder and the Haggadah."

> "**This matter should not be trivial in one's eyes!**"

> "There are some things at the Seder which may seem insignificant to man, but let him act prudently to observe them, for **there is nothing vain among them!**"

---

## II. The Seder Plate

### 1) The Items on the Seder Plate

**Seven Items:**

1. Three Matzot
2. Zro'a (shankbone)
3. Beitzah (egg)
4. Maror (bitter herbs)
5. Charoset (apple mixture)
6. Karpas (vegetable)
7. Chazeret (additional bitter herbs)

---

### 2) The Significance of These Items

**Three Matzot:**

- There are several reasons for "three" matzot
- It is customary to choose **concave matzot**, suggesting that the matzot serve as a receptacle for the downward flow of Divine energy

---

**The Zro'a (Shankbone):**

- Commemorates the **Pesach offering** (see previous course)

---

**The Beitzah (Egg):**

- Commemorates the **Chagigah [festive] offering** which was brought together with the Pesach offering in the time of the Bet Hamikdash

**Word Play:**

- **Zro'a** literally means an **Arm**
- An **egg** in Aramaic is called **beya**, a word which may also mean to pray, and find favor, "please"
- Suggesting: **"May it please the Merciful G-d to redeem us with an uplifted arm"**

**Other Reasons for the Egg:**

1. It symbolizes the character of the Jewish people
2. To remind us of the mourning over the destruction of the Temple

---

**Maror:**

- See previous course (Part I, Section II, Subsection 4)

---

**The Charoset:**

- Is a reminder of the **clay** with which our ancestors were made to work
- An **acrid substance** is added to it as a reminder how the teeth of Israel were set on edge by the harshness of their bondage

**Composition:**

- The Charoset is made of a **mixture of fruits** to which the people of Israel have been compared
- This mixture is then softened by a **red liquid**, as a reminder of the **blood** which was the first of the ten plagues
- (See also previous course)

---

**Karpas (Vegetable):**

**Etymology:**

The letters of the word **Karpas**, when reversed, read:

- The letter **samech** [which stands for the number 60]
- **Perach** [harsh labor]

Alluding to the **sixty myriads of Jews subjected to harsh labor**

Hebrew: כַּרְפַּס = ס' פֶּרֶך

---

**Chazeret:**

- Used for the **Korech sandwich**

---

### 3) The Placing of the Items

**Layout on Seder Plate:**

```
זְרוֹעַ              בֵּיצָה
SHANKBONE           EGG

        מָרוֹר
        MAROR

חֲרוֹסֶת           כַּרְפַּס
CHAROSET        VEGETABLE

      חַזֶרֶת
     CHAZERET
```

**Note:** The three matzot are placed beneath the plate or tray

---

### Note on Different Customs

Different customs for the Seder [exist]

## IV. Lel Shimurim ("The Night Which Is Guarded")

### 1) Exodus 12:41-42

**The Biblical Text:**

> 41 At the end of the 430 years, all of G-d's armies left Egypt in broad daylight. 42 There was **a night of vigil for G-d**, [preparing] to bring them out of Egypt. **This night remains for the Israelites a vigil to G-d for all generations.**

---

### 2) Protection from Harm

**A night which is guarded** from that time onward against harmful spirits.

---

### 3) "Shifoch Chamascha" - Opening the Door

**When:**

After the fourth cup of wine is poured, before reciting Hallel, we open the door and say:

> "Pour out Your wrath upon the nations that do not call upon you…."

---

**Why We Open the Door:**

We open the door as a reminder that it is **"lel Shimurim"**, the night of G-d watching over us, and thus, **we are not afraid of anything**.

**The Merit:**

By merit of this **faith and trust**, Moshiach will come and G-d will pour out His wrath upon the nations that do not acknowledge Him.

**Welcoming Elijah:**

Another reason for opening the door is to welcome **Elijah**, the messenger of the Messianic redemption.

---

### 4) The Additional Cup - "The Cup of Elijah"

**Note:** Three reasons [for this cup are found in] the Rebbe's Haggadah

---

### Key Measurements and Standards

**From This Document:**

**Matzah:**
- Kezayit = 1 oz or 25.6 grams
- Must be consumed in less than 4 minutes
- Obligation applies everywhere and always

**Maror:**
- Kezayit = 1 oz or 25.6 grams
- Since rabbinic, can suffice with 2/3 oz if difficult
- Less than 4 minutes (can extend to 6-7 minutes if needed)

**Wine:**
- Each cup = at least revi'it (3.5 fl oz)
- Ideally drink whole cup
- If difficult, drink just over half revi'it (approx 2 oz)
- Four cups total, each with different purpose

**Reclining:**
- On left side only
- Required: matzah and four cups
- Praiseworthy: all eating and drinking
- Not required at other times

### Symbolic Meanings Explained

**Each Seder Plate Item:**

**Three Matzot:**
- Concave shape = receptacle for Divine energy
- Multiple reasons for "three"

**Zro'a (Shankbone) + Beitzah (Egg):**
- Together: "May it please G-d to redeem us with uplifted arm"
- Zro'a = arm in Hebrew
- Beya = egg/please in Aramaic

**Egg Additional Meanings:**
- Character of Jewish people
- Mourning for Temple destruction

**Charoset:**
- Clay/cement (appearance and purpose)
- Apple trees (women giving birth)
- Red liquid = blood of first plague
- Fruits = metaphors for Jewish people

**Karpas:**
- Reversed letters: ס' פֶּרֶך (60 harsh labor)
- Alludes to 60 myriads subjected to slavery

**Chazeret:**
- For Korech sandwich

---

### Teaching the Four Cups

**Educational Framework:**

**Why Four?**
- Four expressions of redemption (Exodus 6:6-7)

**What Each Represents:**

1. **"I will take you out"** – First cup (Kiddush)
2. **"I will save you"** – Second cup (Haggadah)
3. **"I will redeem you"** – Third cup (Birkat Hamazon)
4. **"I will take you for me"** – Fourth cup (Hallel)

**Manner:**
- "In a manner of freedom"
- Recline on left side
- Each is separate mitzvah with own blessing

---

### Rabban Gamliel's Three Things

**Critical Teaching Point:**

> "Whoever did not say [did not explain the reasons for] these three things on the night of Passover, has not fulfilled his obligation [in an ideal manner]."

**Must Explain:**

**1. Pesach Offering:**
- Because G-d passed over our fathers' houses
- When He struck Egyptians but saved us

**2. Matzah:**
- Because dough didn't have time to leaven
- G-d revealed Himself and redeemed them suddenly
- They were driven out and could not delay

**3. Maror:**
- Because Egyptians embittered our lives
- Hard service with mortar and bricks
- All manner of service in the field with rigor

**Teaching Tip:**
- These explanations should be said while pointing to/lifting the items
- Make it visual and interactive
- Essential for fulfilling mitzvah properly

---

### Vehigadeta Lebincha - Educational Methodology

**The Mitzvah to Tell:**

**Who Must Tell:**
- Everyone (even without children)
- Even great Sages
- Whoever elaborates is praised

**Teaching According to Knowledge:**
- Adapt to child's level
- Custom teaching for each child

**Making It Interactive:**
- Make changes to prompt questions
- Give roasted seeds and nuts
- Take table away before eating
- Snatch matzot from each other
- Goal: Child asks "Why is this night different?"

**If No Children:**
- Wife asks husband
- Colleagues ask each other
- Even all wise must ask
- Alone: Ask yourself

**Double Meaning of Haggadah:**
1. Vehigadeta = telling/recounting
2. Hoda'ah = thanksgiving and praise

---

### Lel Shimurim - The Guarded Night

**Three Elements to Teach:**

**1. Biblical Source:**
- Exodus 12:42 - "Night of vigil for G-d"
- "Remains for Israelites a vigil for all generations"

**2. Protection:**
- Guarded from harmful spirits
- Special Divine protection
- No fear

**3. Opening the Door:**

**When:** After fourth cup poured, before Hallel

**Say:** "Shifoch Chamascha" (Pour out Your wrath...)

**Two Reasons:**
- a) Reminder of Lel Shimurim = no fear
- b) Welcome Elijah, messenger of redemption

**Faith Connection:**
- By merit of this faith and trust
- Moshiach will come

**Cup of Elijah:**
- Additional cup prepared
- Three reasons in Rebbe's Haggadah

---

### Closing Quote - Continuous Pesach

**Teaching Opportunity:**

> "Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi – founder of Chabad – did not insert at the end of the Haggadah, the words 'The Order of Pesach is now completed;' for with Chabad, Pesach does not end, but extends continuously."

**Message:**
- Passover's lessons are eternal
- Not just once a year
- Freedom is ongoing journey
- Redemption consciousness continuous

**For Farbrengen:**
- Close Seder with this thought
- Pesach extends throughout year
- Every festival radiates daily
- But Pesach especially continuous

there are some things at Seder which may seem insignificant to man but let him act prudently to observe them for there is nothing vain among them"; (II) Seder plate: Seven items (three Matzot/Zro'a shankbone/Beitzah egg/Maror/Charoset/Karpas vegetable/Chazeret), significance (three Matzot several reasons customary concave suggesting receptacle for Divine energy, Zro'a commemorates Pesach offering, Beitzah commemorates Chagigah festive offering brought with Pesach offering - Zro'a literally means Arm/egg in Aramaic beya also means pray/find favor/please suggesting "May it please Merciful G-d to redeem us with uplifted arm," egg also symbolizes character of Jewish people/reminds mourning over Temple destruction, Charoset reminder of clay ancestors made to work/acrid substance added reminder teeth set on edge by harshness/made of mixture of fruits Jewish people compared to/softened by red liquid reminder of blood first plague, Karpas letters reversed read samech 60 perach harsh labor alluding to sixty myriads subjected to harsh labor כַּרְפַּס = ס' פֶּרֶך, Chazeret used for Korech sandwich), placing of items (diagram showing shankbone top left/egg top right/maror center/charoset bottom left/vegetable bottom right/chazeret bottom center - three matzot placed beneath plate or tray); (III) Structure and order noting different customs exist with traditional 15 Closing wishes "Kosher and Happy Passover" with quote from Previous Lubavitcher Rebbe "Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi founder of Chabad did not insert at end of Haggadah words 'The Order of Pesach is now completed' for with Chabad Pesach does not end but extends continuously - to be sure illumination of every festival radiates every day but festival of Pesach extends continuously." **For Shluchim:** Educational resource (comprehensive reference for understanding Seder laws/customs, teaching tool with full Torah sources, training material for staff see Files 1118/1119/1120, educational handout for community);
