# Model Matzah Bakery - Practical Implementation Guide

**Type**: Program Overview and Resource Guide
**Topic**: Running Model Matzah Bakery as pre-Pesach program
**Format**: Condensed practical instructions with resource links
**Related**: File 1175 (detailed theatrical version)

## Program Overview

Model matzah bakry [sic] is a "go to before pesach" program. "Its a easy program do make and it teaches the kids not just how to make matzah also the story of yezias mitraim [Exodus from Egypt]"

## Most Common Show Format

1. Showing wheat stalks
2. Milling them
3. Making the dough
4. Giving it out for each to make their own matzah

## Oven Options and Challenges

**When Bringing Your Own Oven**:
- Expensive because need portable one
- Must plug into 110 outlet
- Must bake matzas fast ("so u dont have to be there a whole day")
- Problem: "there has been times that the oven caused the smoke alrm to go off"
- **Solution**: "if u give to there kmitchen then its there headache"

**Alternative Oven Options**:
- Good toaster oven with tile on bottom to make baking faster
- Smaller commercial ovens (~$100) "work good"
- Portable stove top - place matzah on it (remember to tovel)

**Note**: "The cheap [pizza] ovens most say they are not good"

## Program Variations

"If going to the same location for a few years or bored of the same act there is for different acts that could be done for the first part then go into the matzah baking"

## Video Resources

**Model Matzah Presentation Example**:
- https://www.chabad.org/multimedia/video_cdo/aid/1481872/jewish/Model-Matzah-Bakery.htm

**Educational Video** ("Matzah, What's Up With It?"):
- http://www.chabad.org/kids/article.asp?AID=269485
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3XMZBCoq4NY&pp=ygUTTW9kZWxfTWF0emFoX0Jha2VyeQ%3D%3D

## Kemach + Mayim Station

"There is someone that has a backdrop that one could buy, or on sukkah depot or sometihnd liie that there is the booths"

## Wheat Stalks

**Challenge**: "Hard to find online ones that have the kernels inside most on amazon dont ave anything inside"

**Best Source**: http://JewishYouthPrograms.com/shop/crafts/model-matzah-bakery

## Wheat Kernels

Available on Amazon

## Flour Recipes

**Recipe Option 1**:
- Two cups regular flour
- One cup whole wheat flour
- One cup water

**Recipe Option 2**:
- 3 1/4 white flour
- 3/4 cups whole-wheat flour
- 1 1/3 cup water

## Paper for Rolling

Can get big rolls of thick parchment paper

## Aprons & Hats

With the matzah bakery logo on it can get from the shluchim selling websites

## For Shluchim: Quick Implementation Tips

### Key Practical Insight

**Venue Kitchen Strategy**: The critical insight here is using the venue's kitchen/oven rather than bringing portable. This:
- Shifts smoke alarm liability to venue
- Eliminates portable oven expense
- Faster baking with proper oven
- Less equipment to transport
- Builds venue relationship

### Resource Priorities

**Essential Purchases**:
1. Wheat stalks with kernels (JewishYouthPrograms.com - only good source)
2. Flour (any grocery)
3. Parchment paper (bulk rolls)
4. Aprons/hats with logo (Shluchim websites) - creates professional look

**Can Get Free/Cheap**:
- Wheat kernels (Amazon, inexpensive)
- Venue's oven (coordinate with venue)
- Water (venue)
- Bowls/mixing equipment (borrow or venue)

### Avoiding Common Pitfalls

**Don't Buy**:
- "Cheap pizza ovens" - reportedly not good
- Wheat stalks without kernels (Amazon ones) - hollow/fake looking
- Expensive portable oven if venue has kitchen

**Do Test**:
- Venue oven temperature and baking time
- Smoke alarm sensitivity before event
- Recipe proportions for your specific flour

### Program Evolution

If running annually at same location, vary the first part (story/introduction) to keep it fresh while maintaining the core wheat-to-matzah process.

### Video Strategy

- Show Chabad.org video to kids as introduction or conclusion
- Use for volunteer training (watch what successful program looks like)
- Share links with parents before event (builds excitement, sets expectations)

## Bottom Line

This condensed Model Matzah Bakery implementation guide emphasizes practical execution, identifying it as a "go to before pesach" program that's "easy to make" teaching children "not just how to make matzah also the story of yezias mitraim [Exodus]" through most common format of showing wheat stalks → milling → making dough → individual matzah making, with critical practical insight recommending use of venue's kitchen/oven rather than bringing portable equipment because portable ovens are expensive, require 110 outlet, must bake fast to avoid all-day commitment, and "there has been times that the oven caused the smoke alrm to go off" leading to recommendation "if u give to there kmitchen then its there headache" shifting liability and eliminating expense, while alternative oven options include good toaster oven with tile at bottom for faster baking, smaller commercial ovens (~$100) that "work good," or portable stove top (must tovel) with warning that "cheap [pizza] ovens most say they are not good." Resource guidance highlights wheat stalks as hardest to source because "hard to find online ones that have the kernels inside most on amazon dont ave anything inside" with best source being JewishYouthPrograms.com/shop/crafts/model-matzah-bakery, while wheat kernels available on Amazon, custom aprons/hats with logo from Shluchim websites, and parchment paper in big rolls, providing two flour recipe options (Option 1: 2 cups regular/1 cup whole wheat/1 cup water; Option 2: 3¼ white/¾ whole-wheat/1⅓ cup water). Video resources include model presentation at chabad.org/multimedia showing successful program example for training and parent preview, plus educational "Matzah, What's Up With It?" videos for kids on Chabad.org and YouTube, with Kemach + Mayim station backdrop available from "someone" or Sukkah Depot "or sometihnd liie that," and program variation tip that "if going to the same location for a few years or bored of the same act there is for different acts that could be done for the first part then go into the matzah baking" keeping program fresh. For Shluchim, the venue kitchen strategy is critical insight shifting smoke alarm liability, eliminating portable oven expense ($100-500 savings), enabling faster baking with proper equipment, reducing transportation burden, and building venue relationship, with resource priorities focusing essential purchases on wheat stalks with kernels (only JewishYouthPrograms.com has good ones), flour, parchment paper, and logo aprons/hats (professional appearance), while getting free/cheap wheat kernels from Amazon, venue oven through coordination, venue water, and borrowed/venue bowls, avoiding cheap pizza ovens (reportedly poor quality), hollow Amazon wheat stalks, and expensive portable ovens when venue has kitchen, testing venue oven temperature/timing and smoke alarm sensitivity before event plus recipe proportions for specific flour, evolving program by varying story/introduction annually while maintaining core process, and using videos for participant introduction/conclusion, volunteer training to see successful model, and parent preview building excitement and setting expectations, ultimately providing Shluchim with practical, cost-effective approach to implementing engaging pre-Pesach children's program that educates about Exodus while creating hands-on mitzvah experience without excessive equipment investment or logistical complexity.

# Shluchim Forum: Water-to-Flour Ratio for Model Matzah Bakery

**Type**: Shluchim Exchange Forum Discussion
**Topic**: Correct flour and water proportions for model matzah bakery
**Date**: March 17, 2017
**Source**: http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/forum/viewtopic.php?t=515274
**Key Question**: "Do you know the ratio?"

## Original Question - Avrohom Rimler, Plattsburgh, NY

**Question**: "ratio water to flour for model matzah bakery? Do you know the ratio?"

**Context**: Shliach preparing for model matzah bakery needs correct proportions

**Contact**: Rabbi Avrohom Rimler, Chabad of Plattsburgh, www.PSJews.com, 518-565-0677

## Response #1: Yitzchok Bergstein, Oak Park, IL

**Ratio Provided**: "just less than 50% water than you are of flour"

**Example**: 4 cups flour to 1.75 cups water

**Mathematical Breakdown**:
- 1.75 ÷ 4 = 0.4375 (43.75% water relative to flour)
- Slightly less than 50% as stated

## Response #2: Eli Dovid Strasberg, Media, PA

**Detailed Recipe**:
- 4 cups flour (approx. 2/3 white flour and 1/3 whole wheat)
- 1.5 cups water
- Yields: "enough for about 30 smaller-medium sized matzos"

**Ratio Calculation**:
- 1.5 ÷ 4 = 0.375 (37.5% water relative to flour)

**Important Caveat**: "More water than that, and it sticks"

**Critical Skill Note**: "(only catch is you need to know how to mix well)"

**Flour Composition**:
- 2/3 white = 2.67 cups white
- 1/3 whole wheat = 1.33 cups whole wheat

## Response #3: Yisroel Hecht, Sunnyvale, CA

**Practical System for Traveling Programs**:

"I would add that for those who do doing ongoing, traveling programs, what has worked well for me was to work it out backwards."

**Method**:
1. **Start with water**: Get small bottle of bottled water (~15oz)
2. **Calculate flour**: Figure out how much flour is needed "in comparison"
3. **Benefits**:
   - "Saves spills"
   - "Time refilling water"
   - "Problems if the water spills after you measure (there are bottles at hand)"

**Pre-Prep Strategy**:
- "Get cheap plastic containers and prefill the flour for as many as 10 programs in advance"
- "Beats making a mess measuring before programs"
- "Beats carrying around open flour bags"

## For Shluchim: Ratio Analysis and Implementation

### Comparing the Three Approaches

**Bergstein Method** (4 cups : 1.75 cups):
- Ratio: 43.75% water to flour
- Wetter dough
- Potentially easier to work with (more pliable)
- Risk: May be too sticky if not mixed well

**Strasberg Method** (4 cups : 1.5 cups):
- Ratio: 37.5% water to flour
- Dryer dough
- "More water than that, and it sticks"
- Requires good mixing technique
- Proven yield: 30 smaller-medium matzos

**Consensus Range**: 37.5% - 43.75% water relative to flour

### Recommended Starting Point

**For First-Time Programs**:
- Start with Strasberg's ratio (4:1.5 = 37.5%)
- Safer (less sticky)
- Can add water if too dry
- Harder to fix if too wet

**As You Gain Experience**:
- Can experiment toward 40-44% water
- More pliable dough may be easier for kids
- But requires better mixing technique

### Flour Type Matters

**Strasberg's Composition** (2/3 white, 1/3 whole wheat):
- White flour: More gluten, can handle more water
- Whole wheat: Absorbs more water, dryer result
- Balance provides workability plus authentic appearance
- Whole wheat gives brownish color (more "authentic" looking)

**If Using All White**:
- May need slightly less water
- Will be lighter colored

**If Using All Whole Wheat**:
- May need slightly more water
- Will be darker, denser

### The "Know How to Mix Well" Factor

Strasberg's caveat is critical: achieving proper consistency requires mixing technique.

**Proper Mixing**:
1. Create well in center of flour
2. Add water gradually to well
3. Mix from center outward
4. Knead briefly until cohesive (but under 18 minutes per matzah custom)
5. Dough should be smooth, not sticky, not cracking

**Signs of Problems**:
- Too sticky: Add flour tablespoon at a time
- Too crumbly: Add water teaspoon at a time
- Proper: Forms ball, slight tackle but doesn't stick to hands

### Hecht's Traveling Program Innovation

**Brilliant for Regular Programs**:

**Water Strategy**:
- Buy cases of small bottled water (16.9 oz standard, or find 15oz)
- One bottle = one batch's water
- No measuring, no spilling during transport
- Always fresh water
- Bottles stack/store easily

**Flour Pre-Prep**:
- Buy cheap plastic containers with lids (dollar store)
- Pre-measure flour for each program
- Label: "Program 1," "Program 2," etc.
- Stack in storage
- Grab and go

**Benefits**:
- Setup time at venue: ~2 minutes (open container, open water bottle)
- No mess at venue
- No transporting open flour bags
- No forgotten measuring cups
- Professional, organized appearance

**Calculation for Hecht Method**:
If using 15 oz water bottle:
- 15 oz = 1.875 cups
- At Strasberg ratio (37.5%): 1.875 ÷ 0.375 = 5 cups flour
- At Bergstein ratio (43.75%): 1.875 ÷ 0.4375 = 4.29 cups flour

**Recommendation**: Round to 5 cups flour per 15oz water bottle (37.5% ratio)

### Scaling for Different Group Sizes

**For 30 kids** (Strasberg's yield):
- 4 cups flour + 1.5 cups water
- Or: 5 cups flour + 15oz water bottle

**For 60 kids**:
- 8 cups flour + 3 cups water
- Or: 10 cups flour + two 15oz water bottles

**For 100 kids**:
- 13.3 cups flour + 5 cups water
- Or: 16-17 cups flour + three 15oz water bottles

### Testing Before Event

**Critical**: Test your specific flour with your chosen ratio AT LEAST one week before event

**Testing Process**:
1. Make small batch (1 cup flour, 0.375 cups water)
2. Mix, knead, roll
3. Note consistency
4. Adjust ratio if needed
5. Document for future years

**Variables Affecting Results**:
- Flour brand (protein content varies)
- Humidity (affects flour moisture)
- Altitude (affects dough texture)
- Water temperature (room temp works best)

### Storage of Pre-Made Dough

**Generally Not Recommended**:
- Dough should be made fresh
- Can't refrigerate (condensation = water contact over time)
- Matzah must be made from fresh-mixed dough

**Exception**:
- Can pre-mix for demo portion (show how it's done)
- Then make fresh batch for kids to use

## Bottom Line

This March 2017 Shluchim Exchange forum discussion addresses the critical water-to-flour ratio for model matzah bakery programs, with Avrohom Rimler (Plattsburgh, NY) asking "Do you know the ratio?" receiving three experienced responses: Yitzchok Bergstein (Oak Park, IL) recommends "just less than 50% water than you are of flour" giving example of 4 cups flour to 1.75 cups water (43.75% ratio); Eli Dovid Strasberg (Media, PA) provides detailed recipe of 4 cups flour (approximately ⅔ white and ⅓ whole wheat) to 1.5 cups water yielding "about 30 smaller-medium sized matzos" (37.5% ratio) with critical caveat that "more water than that, and it sticks" and success requires "you need to know how to mix well"; and Yisroel Hecht (Sunnyvale, CA) offers brilliant traveling program innovation of "work it out backwards" starting with small bottled water (~15oz) then calculating needed flour, which "saves spills, time refilling water, problems if the water spills after you measure (there are bottles at hand)" plus pre-filling cheap plastic containers with flour "for as many as 10 programs in advance" which "beats making a mess measuring before programs and beats carrying around open flour bags." For Shluchim implementation, comparing approaches reveals consensus range of 37.5-43.75% water relative to flour with recommendation to start with Strasberg's safer dryer ratio (37.5%) for first-time programs since "more water than that, and it sticks" and it's easier to add water if too dry than fix too-wet dough, while experienced programs can experiment toward 40-44% water producing more pliable dough requiring better mixing technique; Strasberg's flour composition (⅔ white ⅓ whole wheat) balances white flour's gluten/water-handling capacity with whole wheat's absorption and authentic brownish color, requiring adjustment if using all-white (slightly less water, lighter color) or all whole-wheat (slightly more water, darker/denser); the "know how to mix well" factor emphasizes proper technique of creating flour well, adding water gradually to center, mixing outward, kneading briefly (under 18 minutes per custom) until smooth/cohesive but not sticky or cracking, troubleshooting by adding flour tablespoon-at-a-time if too sticky or water teaspoon-at-a-time if too crumbly, with proper dough forming ball having slight tackle without sticking to hands; Hecht's traveling program innovation proves brilliant for regular programs using cases of small bottled water (15-16.9oz) as pre-measured water requiring no measuring/spilling during transport while providing fresh water and easy stacking/storage, combined with pre-measuring flour in cheap labeled plastic containers creating grab-and-go system with ~2-minute venue setup, zero mess, no forgotten measuring cups, and professional organized appearance, calculating to 5 cups flour per 15oz water bottle at Strasberg ratio or 4.29 cups at Bergstein ratio; scaling for group sizes from 30 kids (4 cups flour + 1.5 cups water or 5 cups + 15oz bottle) to 60 kids (8 cups + 3 cups or 10 cups + two bottles) to 100 kids (13.3 cups + 5 cups or 16-17 cups + three bottles); critical pre-event testing of specific flour with chosen ratio at least one week before making small batch (1 cup flour + 0.375 cups water) to note consistency and adjust for variables including flour brand protein content, humidity affecting flour moisture, altitude affecting dough texture, and water temperature (room temp optimal), documenting for future years; and avoiding pre-made dough storage (must be fresh-mixed, can't refrigerate due to condensation water contact) except demo portion showing process before making fresh batch for participant use, ultimately providing Shluchim with evidence-based ratio range, practical mixing technique guidance, innovative pre-prep system for traveling programs, scaling calculations, testing protocol, and troubleshooting framework ensuring successful hands-on matzah-making experience for children where dough consistency enables proper rolling and baking without excessive sticking or crumbling that would frustrate young participants and undermine educational objective.


---
**End of Document 198**
---

# Forum: Using Regular Electric Oven on Broil for Model Matzah Bakery

**Source**: http://www.shluchimexchange.com/en/forum/viewtopic.php?t=443204
**Topic**: Can regular electric oven on broil be used instead of pizza oven?
**Date**: April 2014

## Question
"Has anyone ever used a regular electric oven on broil to bake the matzohs? Will it pass? I just decided to do a model bakery last minute and would like to see if I can get away without getting a pizza oven."

## Responses

**Response 1 (Yahoo Mail on Android)**:
"I have done many matzah bakeries where the oven did not have time to reach full heat and it worked fine."

**Response 2 (Nosson Potash, S. Francisco, CA - April 1, 2014)**:
"I have done it and it works. Takes longer to bake so make sure the matzah is very thin."

**Response 3 (Rabbi Mendel Hendel, Chabad of Greece)**:
"We did it and it works. Put it on maximum heat, and also have some Matza prepared in advance because it takes longer to bake. Hatzlocho"

## Bottom Line
Consensus: Regular electric oven on broil works for model matzah bakery though takes longer than pizza oven, requiring very thin matzah and preparing batches in advance to manage longer baking time, useful for last-minute programs without pizza oven access.


---
**End of Document 199**
---

# Big Book - Merkos 302 Complete Database

**Document Type**: Comprehensive Excel Database
**Sheets**: 21 tabs covering all Merkos 302 programs
**Format**: Structured data with program details, statistics, and information

## Overview

This Excel workbook contains comprehensive data about all Merkos 302 programs and initiatives. 
Each sheet corresponds to a major program division with detailed information including establishment dates, 
slogans, mission statements, program details, statistics, and operational information.

## Sheet Summary

1. **CTeen**: 1004 rows × 29 columns
2. **CKids**: 1004 rows × 29 columns
3. **CYP**: 1004 rows × 28 columns
4. **JNET**: 1004 rows × 26 columns
5. **Chazak**: 1004 rows × 26 columns
6. **Mitzvah Society**: 1004 rows × 26 columns
7. **Chabad on Call**: 1004 rows × 26 columns
8. **Chabad Tomorrow**: 1004 rows × 26 columns
9. **Moshiach Office**: 1004 rows × 26 columns

###Key Information

**Moisad**: JNET - The Jewish Learning Network

**Established**: 2006.0

**Slogan**: Any place. Any topic. Any time.

**Tagline**: Study, learn and debate your Jewish heritage on your schedule in person, online, or on the phone.

**Mission**: The Jewish Learning Network was established in 2006 to fulfill the Lubavitcher Rebbe's instruction to encourage all Jews to set fixed times for Torah study. “One should strive as much as possible, and more, to influence every single Jew, regardless of his location or circumstances, to designate a set time for Torah study. When one encounters a Jew in the street, one should ask him if he has already set a time for Torah study. If he has, one should influence him to increase further—ideally, by influencing him to become a teacher himself.” - The Rebbe (Hisva’aduyos 5745, Vol. 1, pp. 461-2)

# Merkos 302 Moisdos & Programs - Complete Catalog

**Document Type**: Comprehensive Program Catalog
**Organization**: Merkos L'Inyonei Chinuch, Suite 302
**Pages**: 48 pages
**Purpose**: Resource guide for Shluchim showcasing all available programs and support services

## Executive Summary

This comprehensive catalog details over 100 programs and resources offered by Merkos 302 to support Shluchim (Chabad emissaries) worldwide in their mission. The organization's stated goal is singular: "to help shluchim complete the last phase of their shlichus by preparing their makom hashlichus to be mekabel pnei Moshiach Tzidkeinu."

## Letter from Rabbi Mendy Kotlarsky

**Key Message**: Merkos 302 began with a single Kinus hachlatah 15 years ago and has grown to over 100 programs responding to Kinus hachlatos and pressing needs of Shluchim. The mission is to serve the Shluchim's mission until the shlichus is complete with the hisgalus of Melech HaMoshiach.

---

## MAJOR PROGRAM DIVISIONS

### 1. CKIDS - CHABAD CHILDREN'S NETWORK
**Established**: 2011

**Mission**: Help Shluchim reach every Jewish child through expansion of educational institutions by creating advanced curricula, experiential programming, teacher training, professional branding, competitions, trips, and shabbatons.

**Programs**:

#### CKids Hebrew School
Child-centered, innovative educational program teaching Jewish life events, holidays, reading Hebrew, and developing pride in Jewish identity.

#### JewQ
International Torah competition encouraging children to learn about, review, and take tests on the fundamentals of Yiddishkeit.

#### JewQ's GameZone
Online game site where children play fun and educational Jewish games, gaining Torah knowledge and excitement for Yiddishkeit.

#### CKids Shabbaton
Unforgettable three-day extravaganza in Crown Heights bringing together Jewish children from around the country to inspire pride in their Yiddishkeit.

#### CKids CGI Overnight
Three CKids Gan Israel Overnight Camps providing life-changing summer experiences. Hundreds of children from CKids Hebrew Schools have joined. Camps are independently run and fundraised by individual directors.

#### Staff Training
Empowering training for camp counselors, head counselors, and directors.

#### CKids CGI Day Camp
New cutting-edge customized curricula, creative programs and activities, staff training and placements, and networking so children wait all year to return to Camp Gan Israel.

#### CKids Tzivos Hashem Brigade
Network for Chabad House children encouraging every child to be an active member in Hashem's army through motivational point system, rewards, and rank promotions.

#### CKids Club
Educational, family-style programs that can be run independently or during Hebrew school or after-school programs with individualized boxes that help Shluchim take programs to the next level.

#### Advanced Curriculum Development
Skillful curriculum development for camps, schools, and programs to teach about Yiddishkeit in a meaningful and engaging way.

#### Kinusim
Yearly kinnus for youth directors to participate in training and enlightening lectures to improve their schools and camps.

#### Jewish Birthdays
Customizable, digital birthday packages sent to hundreds of children worldwide.

#### CKids Mezuzah Bank
In partnership with Yad Menachem: For every mezuzah a shliach puts up on a family home, CKids provides an additional mezuzah for a child's bedroom doorpost.

#### Holiday Tool Boxes
Specially created kit with everything students need to create a fun, exciting, and unforgettable family yom tov experience in their homes.

#### Tefillah Publications
Specialized siddurim and machzorim where students can write their own meditations and thoughts in invisible ink.

**For New Shluchim**:
- Hebrew School with engaging curricula
- JewQ can be used in or out of Hebrew School
- CKids Club for one-time events
- CKids CGI Daycamp enrichment

---

### 2. CTEEN - CHABAD TEEN NETWORK
**Established**: 2008

**Mission**: Reach every Jewish teen—to touch their souls and nurture the Jewish spark. Comprehensive schedule of social, educational, and humanitarian programming in a nurturing environment fusing fun, friendship, mitzvah observance, and engaging Torah study helps teens find purpose, learn integrity, and gain confidence.

**Programs**:

#### CTeen U
College-accredited courses exploring tenets of Judaism taught by local Shluchim.

#### Mitzvah Ambassadors
Nationwide movement of teens who support and encourage peers to learn about and observe mitzvos.

#### CTeen Xtreme
Unique traveling camp for high school girls and boys fostering appreciation for Yiddishkeit with adventure and exciting trips.

#### CTeen Heritage Quest
Awe-inspiring 22-day journey through major Jewish sites in Poland and Israel.

#### CTeen Israel Journey
Journey through time as teens experience the rich history of the Holy Land and find its relevance in daily lives.

#### CTeen Leadership
Creating the next generation of Jewish leaders by empowering teens to take active roles in their communities and beyond.

#### TGIS (Thank G-d It's Shabbos)
International CTeen TGIS event uniting all CTeen chapters worldwide to keep one Shabbos together with inspiration, memorable experiences, and a 24-hour global learn-a-thon.

#### CTeen Shabbaton
Transformative weekend convention for Jewish teens from around the world.

#### CTeen High School Clubs
Kosher Food Club Curriculum delivered in school giving students experience with kosher food and cuisine, sparking discussion on health and humanitarian work.

#### Campus Connect
Teens become acquainted with Chabad on Campus before entering college, easing transition to future "home away from home."

#### Torah Buddies
CTeeners paired with Lubavitch teens their own age for weekly over-the-phone study.

#### Jewish Heritage Night
CTeen chapters unite monumental display of Jewish pride with favorite American pastime by lighting menorahs at local sports games (pirsumei nissa).

#### Regionals
Regional shabbatons and trips coordinated between chapters within same geographic region providing opportunity to meet and befriend other Jewish teens.

#### CTeen Connection
Teens share their talents and voices in a fun forum created for teens, by teens.

#### Mitzvah Bank
Provides teens with Judaic items including tefillin, Shabbat candles, tzitzit, siddurim, charity boxes, and mezuzot.

#### CTeen Lounges
CTeen sponsors lounges giving teens their own space to form and lead communities where they can lead, create, and engage as independent individuals.

#### Yeshiva Grants
Prestigious, merit-based award providing financial assistance for outstanding young men and women who wish to pursue a year of Torah study.

#### Road Trips
Helping teens arrange three-day road trips during summer vacation with their local shliach.

#### CTeen Jr
Bridge between Hebrew School and CTeen, offering preteens educational, humanitarian, and social activities.

#### CTeen Mitzvah Booths
[Program for community engagement]

#### Shluchim Resources and Coaching
Resources and guidance to implement CTeen's programs, reduce costs, and become more effective.

---

### 3. CYP - CHABAD YOUNG PROFESSIONALS
**Established**: 2014

**Mission**: Partnership with 165+ Shluchim worldwide providing pivotal shlichus for reaching young adults at crossroads of individual destiny and Jewish continuity. Provides global Jewish community for post-college, pre-suburb demographic inspiring each individual to think Jewish, feel Jewish, and marry Jewish.

**Programs**:

#### Met@Chabad
Three primary components: educating young singles to date for marriage, connecting them with ground-breaking technology and human support, and preparing young couples for chuppah and building strong Jewish homes.

#### The CYP Kinus
Shluchim from CYP Chabad Houses worldwide gather in beautiful, relaxing destination to exchange ideas, gain insight, and grow.

#### CYP New Shluchim
Helping new Shluchim receive seed grants to move to town and establish new center dedicated to needs of today's young adults.

#### CYP Mitzvah Ambassadors
Empowers young Jews in community to own their Judaism and share mitzvah with a friend.

#### CYP Encounter: Crown Heights
Annual Shabbaton bringing hundreds of young Jews and their Shluchim together for transformative, inspiring, captivating Shabbos experience in Crown Heights.

#### CYP Regional Shabbatons
Immersive experience providing YPs opportunity to form deeper and more personal connection with their Shluchim while forming relationships with fellow YPs within larger network.

#### CYP Chabad Houses
Providing Shluchim with monthly event package including tochendik'e concept and theme and everything needed to host professional and thought-out event for young adults.

#### CYP Academy
Specially curated learning experiences bringing Torah's eternal lessons to today's busy young professional.

#### CYP Partners' Summit
Summit connects leaders from around the globe making difference in local Jewish communities and celebrates partnerships that have given rise to revolutionary growth in young Jewish life.

**For New Shluchim**:
- CYP New Shluchim: aid in securing grants to open CYP program
- CYP Chabad House: fully prepared, monthly event package

---

### 4. CHABAD ON CALL
**Established**: 2015

**Mission**: Alleviate pain, loneliness, and despair in hospital settings by genuinely addressing emotional and spiritual needs of patients and families. Chabad representatives provide visitations, chaplaincy requests, spiritual needs, consolation, comfort, and inspiration.

**Programs**:

#### Chaplaincy Training
Course granting hospital recognized certification, giving tools to work with those coping with life-altering situations.

#### Cultural Sensitivity
"Cultural Awareness" professional curriculum helping hospital staff better support and serve their Jewish patients.

#### Hospital Resources
Resources guide through every step of journey within medical community. Many downloadable for free or minimal cost. Popular items include Tehillim and pop-up pushka.

#### New Shluchim Placement
Helping Shluchim whose main focus is servicing hospitals to maximize potential and provide seed grants to expand this area of shlichus.

#### Seder To Go
Complete seder experience in a box for Jewish patients.

#### Website
ChabadOnCall.com provides online hospital directory, educational courses, and variety of practical resources for medical professionals and patients.

#### Hospitality Suite
Creating series of Bikkur Cholim lounges and apartments near major medical centers.

#### Chicken Soup Conference
Professional training and opportunities to brainstorm, discuss, and develop ideas with other chaplains.

#### Shluchim Refuah
Confidential rofeh yedid network for Shluchim to help through medical and mental health challenges according to Rebbe's guidance.

---

### 5. JNET - JEWISH LEARNING NETWORK
**Established**: 2006

**Mission**: Provide business people, students, and homemakers with opportunity to take time from busy work week to study Torah. Volunteers bring warmth of Torah and Judaism to people whose situations restrict them from acquiring it in other ways.

**Programs**:

#### Chavrusa Program
JNet carefully matches baalei batim with members of Anash for weekly Torah study sessions on topic of their choice. Sessions typically half hour once a week. Many chavrusas have continued learning weekly for many years, guiding one another to true spiritual growth.

#### Learning Material
JNet partners with JLI, Kehot, and private individuals to produce and subsidize books and online content helping chavrusas easily find something meaningful to study. Extensive online resource page with links to websites.

#### JNet Connection Magazine
Monthly pamphlet describing incredible impact weekly learning has had on individual's journey in life. Distributed in Chabad houses and shuls worldwide and sent digitally to all JNet members.

#### Annual Volunteer Appreciation Dinner
JNet hosts annual appreciation dinner for volunteers with great food and entertainment, celebrating accomplishments of chavrusas over past year.

---

### 6. MERKOS SHLICHUS
**Established**: 1943

**Mission**: Worldwide student-visitation programs dispatching young rabbis to small, isolated communities around globe to spread Jewish awareness and knowledge of Torah and mitzvos.

**Programs**:

#### Pesach Merkos Shlichus
Bochurim matched with Shluchim worldwide to assist in preparing for Pesach and running a seder.

#### Summer Merkos Shlichus
Bochurim sent to small communities to connect with Jews and teach about Yiddishkeit.

#### Shavuos Merkos Shlichus
Shluchim in small areas can have bochurim come for Shavuos to infuse their kids with chassidishe chayus, assist with Aseres Hadibros readings, and help with shlichus.

---

### 7. CHABAD TOMORROW
**Established**: 2015

**Mission**: Assist Shluchim worldwide in working with supporters on legacy gifts. Provides broad array of marketing materials and advice about planned giving.

**Programs**:

#### Legacy Challenge
Helping ensure community's future by providing Shluchim with $10,000 Legacy Challenge grant.

---

### 8. MITZVAH SOCIETY
**Established**: 2019

**Mission**: Provide every shliach with tools to mobilize community members as active partners in avodas hashlichus. Every community member empowered to share joy and practice of Judaism with family, friends, and neighbors in beautiful, elegant, user-friendly manner.

**Programs**:

#### Mitzvah Experience
[Community mobilization program]

#### Mezuzah it Forward
[Mezuzah outreach initiative]

---

### 9. MOSHIACH OFFICE
**Established**: 2020

**Mission**: Provide global awareness and education regarding unique generation we live in. Through initiatives, educational campaigns, and media materials, work to inspire and empower people to answer Rebbe's call for our times.

**Programs**:

#### Tut Altz Kids
Fundamental sichos and maamarim of Rebbe and Rambam's teachings about Moshiach brought down to elementary level in curricula, games, and programs making Geula a reality for children.

#### Moshiach Curriculum
Engaging, clearly translated, and annotated sichos and maamarim about Moshiach. In-depth explorations develop Moshiach mindset and make living with Geula a reality.

#### Kinus Companion
"Vision Conscious" and "Welcome Home" programs provide thorough guide into shlichus today, based on Rebbe's sichos to men's and women's kinusim.

#### Resource Hub
Tutaltz.com/store has everything Geula related at your fingertips. Inspiring podcasts, broadcasts, and learning booklets available anytime, anywhere, with various lengths and intensities to suit schedule.

Global farbrengens with thousands of participants reflecting on striving to meet Rebbe's standards of shlichus with Geulah.

### 14. KEREN HASHLUCHIM (THE SHLUCHIM FUND)

**Mission**: In conjunction with visionary philanthropists, provides financial support to Shluchim during major life cycle events and in times of emergency and crisis, as well as assists in development and expansion of shlichus and shlichus opportunities.

**Programs**:

#### Simcha Fund
Provides grants to alleviate financial burden accompanying joyful milestones, including new births, bar mitzvahs, and marriage of a child.

#### Crisis and Emergency Support
Provides critical assistance to Shluchim affected by natural disasters, national unrest, economic collapse, serious illness, and other crises.

#### Yom Tov Fund
Provides Shluchim with assistance for personal needs and communal events for yomim tovim of Tishrei, Pesach, and Shavuos.

#### Mikvah Fund
Facilitates grants for building and restoration of mikvaos in Shluchim's communities.

#### Building Fund
Provides Shluchim with seed grants to build and expand their Chabad Houses.

#### New Shluchim Grant
Provides seed grants that set up Shluchim for early success and long-term sustainability in their work.

#### Emergency Loans
Keren Sholom Ber and Sara Esther Gemach established with gracious grant by Rabbi Sholom Ber Sanowicz to help Shluchim with short-term emergency loans. Currently available for Shluchim residing in USA.

#### Meromim Building Loans
Meromim Chul offers Shluchim interest-free loans to help establish or expand Chabad centers around the world.

#### Sefer Torah Gemach
Bais Yisroel Torah Gemach lends primary and secondary Sifrei Torah to Shluchim for up to two years, assisting Chabad Houses ready to start minyan but do not have own Torah.

**For New Shluchim**:
- New Shluchim Grant: obtaining grants to kickstart shlichus

**Established**: 2007

Pairing yaldei haShluchim ages 8-13 with mature, knowledgeable, Chassidishe bochurim and girls for hour a week of over-the-phone chavrusa learning.

Motivates and incentivizes hundreds of yaldei haShluchim to spend free time learning and reciting Mishnayos baal peh to purify the air.

Weekly two-hour interactive program providing hundreds of yaldei haShluchim with Chassidishe social opportunities.

Daily learning encounter giving yaldei haShluchim opportunity to create friends while learning.

Enabling Shluchim's children to participate in global Chidon competition.

### 16. YALDEI SHLUCHEI HAREBBE (YSH)
**Established**: 2009

**Mission**: Shluchim who experience having child who is different often feel very alone. YSH provides financial support and appropriate programming for families of Shluchim raising children with different needs. By offering opportunities for service coordination, advocacy, financial assistance, and family and respite support, helps Shluchim continue serving Jews in their community.

**Programs**:

#### Family Care Coordination
Maintain ongoing contact with families and assist in identifying long- and short-term needs of child and family.

#### School and Camp Placement and Grants
Yaldei advises parents regarding school and camp placement for child and provides special grant subsidies for special-ed tuitions.

#### Therapy and Equipment Grants
YSH provides and assists with finding and funding expensive therapies and medical and home-accessibility equipment.

#### Mental Health Grants
Makes referrals and absorbs some costs involved in obtaining professional therapy for family members of special needs children.

#### Project Care and Project Smile
Design and send birthday gifts to parents and every child in family, letting them know they are cared for and not alone on challenging journey.

#### Respite Retreats and Grants
Offers and promotes various respite programs providing regular and at-will opportunities for parents to take break and recharge batteries, as well as covering costs during parents' break.

#### Networking
Coordinates peer-to-peer support contact network between parents facing similar challenges.

#### Yom Tov Packages
Sends care packages for yomim tovim to help keep kids entertained and deliver joy to entire family.

## For Shluchim

**Key Takeaways**:

1. **Comprehensive Support**: Merkos 302 offers 100+ programs covering every aspect of shlichus from children's education to young professionals, from hospital chaplaincy to legacy planning.

2. **Flexible Solutions**: Programs are designed to be flexible for every Chabad House with dedicated team standing by to help find right programs for each community.

3. **Continuous Development**: Merkos 302 constantly striving to advance programs. Shluchim feedback is critical in this process.

4. **New Shluchim Resources**: Each major program division has specific resources marked "For New Shluchim" to help those just starting their shlichus journey.

5. **Financial Support**: Keren Hashluchim provides various grants and loans for simchas, emergencies, building projects, and ongoing operations.

6. **Professional Development**: Training seminars, courses, farbrengens, and coaching available across multiple programs.

7. **Network Building**: Multiple initiatives facilitate connections between Shluchim for sharing best practices, support, and collaboration.

## Bottom Line for Shluchim

This catalog represents the infrastructure supporting global Chabad shlichus. From the moment a young couple considers going on shlichus through decades of building and expanding their community, Merkos 302 provides tools, funding, training, networking, and support. The breadth of offerings demonstrates that Shluchim are not alone in their mission - they have an entire organization backing them with resources specifically designed to help them succeed in preparing their communities to greet Moshiach.

Whether a Shliach needs curriculum for Hebrew school, grants for building projects, respite support for special needs children, training for hospital chaplaincy, or simply connection with fellow Shluchim, Merkos 302 has established a program to meet that need. The organization's commitment to responding to each year's Kinus hachlatos ensures that the support continues to evolve based on real needs in the field.
